abaeis nicippe.name: Orange-tip
abaeis nicippe.desc: Orange-tip (Abaeis nicippe): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

abies.name: Fir and conifer forest
abies.desc: Conifer forest covers the high slopes where the monkeys live and gives seeds, shade and winter shelter.

abies alba.name: Silver fir
abies alba.desc: A conifer that grows with beech in the mixed beech-fir stands that cover much of the Poloniny uplands.

abies balsamea.name: Balsam fir
abies balsamea.desc: A northern conifer of the spruce-fir forest that covers most of the park's vegetated land. Deer, hares and squirrels all feed on it.

abies fargesii.name: Farges's fir
abies fargesii.desc: A conifer of the cool upper slopes. Conifer forest at higher elevations shelters the wildlife of the Qionglai range.

abies fraseri.name: Fraser fir
abies fraseri.desc: Grows near the highest summits. The balsam woolly adelgid killed most mature firs from the 1960s on, though young firs are regrowing on some peaks.

abies grandis.name: Giant Fir
abies grandis.desc: Giant Fir (Abies grandis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

abies lasiocarpa.name: Subalpine fir
abies lasiocarpa.desc: Grows at and just below the tree line. Its seeds feed birds and squirrels, and its clumps trap snow and help form meadows.

abies magnifica.name: Red fir
abies magnifica.desc: A tall fir of the snowy Cascade slopes, and a common conifer in the park forests.

abies nordmanniana.name: Nordmann fir
abies nordmanniana.desc: A tall mountain conifer growing at roughly 900 to 2,200 m. The Caucasus reserve was founded in 1924 partly to protect its giant firs.

abies religiosa.name: Oyamel fir
abies religiosa.desc: A cloud-forest conifer of central Mexican mountains. Overwintering monarchs gather in its forests, and UNESCO says keeping the standing forest and its microclimates is the key management need.

abies spectabilis, juniperus.name: Fir and juniper
abies spectabilis, juniperus.desc: Conifers of the subalpine forest, which Wikipedia says holds fir, birch and rhododendron above about 3,000 m.

abronia fragrans.name: Heart's-delight
abronia fragrans.desc: Heart's-delight (Abronia fragrans): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

abrothrix olivaceus.name: Olive grass mouse
abrothrix olivaceus.desc: A small rodent of steppe and forest edge, eating seeds, plants and insects. It is staple prey for foxes and raptors.

abrus precatorius.name: Crab's eye vine
abrus precatorius.desc: A climbing legume recorded on the island. GloBI lists it as food for the Common Blue butterfly.

acacia aneura.name: Mulga
acacia aneura.desc: A shrub or small tree of arid Australia that gives its name to the mulga woodlands. Listed as a dominant tree of the park.

acacia dealbata.name: Silver wattle
acacia dealbata.desc: A wattle that colonises gaps and burnt ground at forest edges; black cockatoos are recorded eating its seeds.

acacia koa.name: Koa
acacia koa.desc: A native forest tree whose leaves feed caterpillars and other insects, and whose crowns shelter forest birds.

acacia ligulata.name: Dune wattle
acacia ligulata.desc: A common scrub of coastal dunes and sandplains. Banded hare-wallabies favour thickets of it for shelter, and its seeds and foliage feed other animals.

acalypha radians.name: Cardinal feather
acalypha radians.desc: Cardinal feather (Acalypha radians): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

acanthacris ruficornis.name: Garden locust
acanthacris ruficornis.desc: A large grasshopper that chews grasses and other plants and feeds reptiles and birds.

acanthaster planci.name: Crown-of-thorns starfish
acanthaster planci.desc: A starfish that eats hard coral polyps. Outbreaks can strip large areas of living coral.

acanthis flammea.name: Common redpoll
acanthis flammea.desc: A small finch that eats seeds and shoots. GloBI records it eating grasses and horsetail.

acanthocercus annectans.name: Eritrean ridgeback agama
acanthocercus annectans.desc: A rock-dwelling lizard that eats insects and is itself prey for snakes and raptors.

acanthodactylus boskianus.name: Bosc's fringe-toed lizard
acanthodactylus boskianus.desc: A fast, insect-eating lizard of sandy and gravelly ground. Lizards are a major food for birds and snakes here.

acanthogammarus and relatives.name: Baikal amphipods
acanthogammarus and relatives.desc: A very diverse endemic group. Some are mostly carnivorous, others eat detritus, and the high oxygen of the lake is linked to the giant size of some.

acanthosicyos horridus.name: Nara melon
acanthosicyos horridus.desc: A spiny, leafless melon plant of coastal dunes that fruits for animals and people. Its roots tap deep water.

acanthuridae.name: Surgeonfish
acanthuridae.desc: Grazes algae in schools so seaweed does not overgrow corals.

acanthurus.name: Surgeonfish
acanthurus.desc: Schooling fish that graze algae around coral reefs.

accipiter cooperii.name: Cooper's hawk
accipiter cooperii.desc: A bird-hunting hawk that nests in urban parks. Robins and starlings are the most commonly reported prey, with doves and house sparrows also taken.

accipiter nisus.name: Eurasian sparrowhawk
accipiter nisus.desc: A woodland hawk that hunts small birds such as finches and tits.

accipiter rufitorques.name: Fiji goshawk
accipiter rufitorques.desc: Fiji's top forest raptor; it takes birds up to pigeon size, reptiles, insects and rodents.

accipiter striatus.name: Sharp-shinned hawk
accipiter striatus.desc: A small woodland hawk that hunts birds and small mammals, including red squirrels.

acer.name: Maples & other broadleaf trees
acer.desc: Maples, limes and other broadleaf trees mixed into the forest, offering leaves, twigs and bark to browsers.

acer circinatum.name: Vine maple
acer circinatum.desc: Vine maple (Acer circinatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 66 times near the park in GBIF.

acer davidii.name: Father David's maple
acer davidii.desc: A broadleaf tree of the mid-elevation mixed forest; leaves and buds feed browsers.

acer macrophyllum.name: Pacific maple
acer macrophyllum.desc: Pacific maple (Acer macrophyllum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

acer negundo.name: Ashleaf Maple
acer negundo.desc: Ashleaf Maple (Acer negundo): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

acer pensylvanicum.name: Striped maple
acer pensylvanicum.desc: Moosewood (Acer pensylvanicum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 36 times near the park in GBIF.

acer platanoides.name: Norway maple
acer platanoides.desc: Norway maple (Acer platanoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 891 times near the park in GBIF.

acer rubrum.name: Red maple
acer rubrum.desc: A common hardwood of the park's mixed forest and wetlands. Its twigs and leaves are browsed by deer and hares.

acer saccharinum.name: Red Maple
acer saccharinum.desc: Red Maple (Acer saccharinum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

acer saccharum.name: Sugar maple
acer saccharum.desc: Sugar maple (Acer saccharum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

acer spicatum.name: Mountain maple
acer spicatum.desc: A shrubby understory maple, also called moose maple. Moose, hares and beavers browse it.

acer spp..name: Maples & other street trees
acer spp..desc: Maples, along with ash and other street trees, shade neighborhoods and feed leaf-eating insects, with buds and seeds for squirrels.

acharia stimulea.name: Saddleback Caterpillar Moth
acharia stimulea.desc: Saddleback Caterpillar Moth (Acharia stimulea): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 42 times near the park in GBIF.

achillea millefolium.name: Yarrow
achillea millefolium.desc: Yarrow (Achillea millefolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

achlys triphylla.name: Deerfoot
achlys triphylla.desc: Deerfoot (Achlys triphylla): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.

achnatherum hymenoides.name: Indian ricegrass
achnatherum hymenoides.desc: A tufted desert grass of sandy soils that is listed among the common plants of Arches. Its seeds are food for desert rodents.

achyrachaena mollis.name: Blow wives
achyrachaena mollis.desc: Blow wives (Achyrachaena mollis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

acidic forest soil.name: Acidic forest soil
acidic forest soil.desc: Needle litter makes cool, acidic soils that break down slowly.

acidic peat soil.name: Acidic peat soil
acidic peat soil.desc: Buttongrass moor grows on damp, nutrient-poor, acidic peat soils in western Tasmania.

acinonyx jubatus.name: Cheetah
acinonyx jubatus.desc: Sprints after gazelles on open plains, often losing kills to larger predators.

acinonyx jubatus hecki.name: Saharan cheetah
acinonyx jubatus hecki.desc: A critically endangered cheetah that hunts desert antelope and gazelles and gets water from its prey.

acleisanthes longiflora.name: Angel trumpet
acleisanthes longiflora.desc: Angel trumpet (Acleisanthes longiflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

acmella repens.name: Oppositeleaf spotflower
acmella repens.desc: Oppositeleaf spotflower (Acmella repens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

acomys dimidiatus.name: Spiny mouse
acomys dimidiatus.desc: A rocky-desert rodent that eats seeds and small invertebrates and is prey for foxes and owls.

acraea.name: Acraea butterflies
acraea.desc: A large genus of butterflies, many species recorded in the Nyungwe area. Adults visit flowers for nectar.

acrantophis madagascariensis.name: Madagascar ground boa
acrantophis madagascariensis.desc: A ground-dwelling constrictor that preys on ring-tailed lemurs and other small animals.

acrididae.name: Grasshoppers
acrididae.desc: Plant-eating insects that feed on grasses. They are prey for lizards, birds and small mammals.

acrocephalus griseldis.name: Basra reed warbler
acrocephalus griseldis.desc: Breeds in dense reed and papyrus beds of the Tigris-Euphrates system. Drainage nearly destroyed its habitat and it is endangered.

acrocodia indica.name: Malayan tapir
acrocodia indica.desc: Solitary herbivore that eats shoots and leaves from over a hundred plant species; recorded repeatedly in the reserve.

acromyrmex versicolor.name: Desert Leaf-cutter Ant
acromyrmex versicolor.desc: Desert Leaf-cutter Ant (Acromyrmex versicolor): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

acronicta americana.name: American Dagger Moth
acronicta americana.desc: American Dagger Moth (Acronicta americana): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

acronicta insita.name: Large Gray Dagger
acronicta insita.desc: Large Gray Dagger (Acronicta insita): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

acronicta longa.name: Long-winged Dagger
acronicta longa.desc: Long-winged Dagger (Acronicta longa): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

acropora.name: Reef-building corals
acropora.desc: Branching corals build the reef structure. They catch plankton and shelter many fish.

acropora palmata.name: Elkhorn coral
acropora palmata.desc: Branching reef-builder of the shallow reef crest. It takes in food from plankton as well as from its algal partners.

acropora spp..name: Reef-building coral
acropora spp..desc: Builds the limestone reef that shelters thousands of other species. It bleaches when warm water drives out its algae.

actias luna.name: Luna Moth
actias luna.desc: A large moth whose caterpillars feed on the leaves of trees such as sweetgum. It is often recorded around the park.

actinopterygii.name: Forest river fish
actinopterygii.desc: Salonga holds dozens of fish species. They feed on insects and other small animals and are the main food of dwarf crocodiles in the Congo basin.

adansonia digitata.name: Baobab
adansonia digitata.desc: A huge, long-lived tree of dry savanna, recorded in the park.

adansonia grandidieri.name: Grandidier's baobab
adansonia grandidieri.desc: Giant water-storing tree of seasonal dry forest. Its flowers open at dusk and are pollinated by hawk moths and nocturnal lemurs.

addax nasomaculatus.name: Addax
addax nasomaculatus.desc: A critically endangered antelope that grazes desert grasses and browses shrubs, and can go a very long time without drinking.

adenostoma fasciculatum.name: Chamise
adenostoma fasciculatum.desc: A fire-adapted shrub that makes up much of the park chaparral. Wikipedia says it resprouts from its base after fire and its seeds germinate after burns.

adesmia cancellata.name: Pitted beetle
adesmia cancellata.desc: A darkling beetle of arid Middle Eastern habitats, recorded in the Al Reem area. It is food for lizards, birds and shrikes.

adiantum aleuticum.name: Aleutian maidenhair
adiantum aleuticum.desc: Aleutian maidenhair (Adiantum aleuticum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

adiantum capillus-veneris.name: Maidenhair Fern
adiantum capillus-veneris.desc: Maidenhair Fern (Adiantum capillus-veneris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

adiantum pedatum.name: Maidenfern
adiantum pedatum.desc: Maidenfern (Adiantum pedatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 35 times near the park in GBIF.

aedes vexans.name: Vexans Mosquito
aedes vexans.desc: Vexans Mosquito (Aedes vexans): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 45 times near the park in GBIF.

aegilops.name: Steppe grasses
aegilops.desc: Wild goatgrasses and other grasses grow on the dry steppe and meadows, which together are a large part of the reserve.

aegypius monachus.name: Cinereous vulture
aegypius monachus.desc: A huge vulture that feeds mostly on carrion, such as dead wild and domestic hoofed animals, and also takes marmots.

aeorestes semotus.name: ʻŌpeʻapeʻa (Hawaiian hoary bat)
aeorestes semotus.desc: The native land mammal. It is a generalist insect eater that mainly takes moths and beetles, in open areas and in forest.

aepyceros melampus.name: Impala
aepyceros melampus.desc: A very common antelope, eaten by lions, leopards, wild dogs and hyenas.

aesculus pavia.name: Red Buckeye
aesculus pavia.desc: Red Buckeye (Aesculus pavia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.

aethopyga temminckii.name: Temminck's sunbird
aethopyga temminckii.desc: A small nectar-feeding bird of Bornean mountain forest, among the most recorded birds near the park.

aetobatus narinari.name: Spotted eagle ray
aetobatus narinari.desc: Ray that crushes conch and other shelled prey on sandy flats near the reef.

aframomum.name: Aframomum herbs
aframomum.desc: Ground-layer herbs of the ginger family. On Afi Mountain they made up most of the diet of Cross River gorillas.

afropavo congensis.name: Congo peafowl
afropavo congensis.desc: Endemic to the Congo Basin and found in both old and regrowing forest in Salonga. Eats fruit, insects, spiders, snails and worms.

afruca tangeri.name: West African fiddler crab
afruca tangeri.desc: Burrowing crab of muddy flats that feeds on organic matter in the sediment and is itself prey for birds and octopus.

agama agama.name: Common agama
agama agama.desc: A sun-loving lizard that eats mainly ants, grasshoppers, beetles and termites. Males hold territories around trees or rocks.

agama atra.name: Southern rock agama
agama atra.desc: A rock-dwelling lizard that feeds mainly on insects and is prey for raptors.

agapostemon texanus.name: Texas Agapostemon
agapostemon texanus.desc: Texas Agapostemon (Agapostemon texanus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

agave lechuguilla.name: Lechuguilla
agave lechuguilla.desc: An indicator plant of the Chihuahuan Desert that spreads by underground offshoots into large colonies. Collared peccaries eat much of it in some areas.

agave palmeri.name: Century plant
agave palmeri.desc: Century plant (Agave palmeri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 113 times near the park in GBIF.

agave parryi.name: Parry's agave
agave parryi.desc: Parry's agave (Agave parryi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 91 times near the park in GBIF.

agelaius phoeniceus.name: Red-winged Blackbird
agelaius phoeniceus.desc: Red-winged Blackbird (Agelaius phoeniceus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4,275 times near the park in GBIF.

agkistrodon conanti.name: Florida cottonmouth
agkistrodon conanti.desc: A venomous water snake that eats frogs, fish and other small animals around swamp water.

agkistrodon contortrix.name: Copperhead
agkistrodon contortrix.desc: Copperhead (Agkistrodon contortrix): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

agkistrodon piscivorus.name: Cottonmouth
agkistrodon piscivorus.desc: Cottonmouth (Agkistrodon piscivorus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 23 times near the park in GBIF.

aglaia.name: Rainforest fruit trees
aglaia.desc: Fruiting trees such as Aglaia, whose fruits are recorded as eaten by macaques, fruit bats and civets.

aglaia elliptica.name: Segera
aglaia elliptica.desc: A rainforest tree well recorded near the park. GloBI has a record of the Asian palm civet eating its fruit.

aglais io.name: Peacock butterfly
aglais io.desc: A butterfly well recorded near the mountain. Its caterpillars feed on nettles.

aglais urticae.name: Small tortoiseshell
aglais urticae.desc: A common butterfly whose caterpillars feed on nettle leaves; adults drink nectar from many flowers.

agrostis stolonifera.name: Creeping Bent
agrostis stolonifera.desc: Creeping Bent (Agrostis stolonifera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.

aguadas and bajos.name: Aguadas and bajos
aguadas and bajos.desc: The area has little permanent surface water, so seasonal ponds and swampy low spots are vital wildlife water sources.

ahaetulla nasuta.name: Green vine snake
ahaetulla nasuta.desc: A slender tree snake that eats lizards and frogs. GloBI records show it eating red-vented bulbuls.

ailanthus altissima.name: Tree of heaven
ailanthus altissima.desc: Tree of heaven (Ailanthus altissima): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 389 times near the park in GBIF.

ailuropoda melanoleuca.name: Giant panda
ailuropoda melanoleuca.desc: About 99% of the diet is bamboo. This site holds a large share of the wild population. Adults have few predators, but cubs and sub-adults can be taken.

ailurus fulgens.name: Red panda
ailurus fulgens.desc: Eats mainly bamboo leaves, plus fruit, blossoms and acorns. Leopards are its only documented predator.

aix sponsa.name: Wood Duck
aix sponsa.desc: Wood Duck (Aix sponsa): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.

akodon cursor.name: Cursor grass mouse
akodon cursor.desc: A common small forest rodent, one of the most frequently recorded mammals here. It feeds on seeds, fruit and insects.

alcelaphus buselaphus.name: Western hartebeest
alcelaphus buselaphus.desc: A large grass-eating antelope of open savanna, taken by leopards and hyenas.

alces alces.name: Moose
alces alces.desc: Moose (Alces alces): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

alces americanus.name: Moose
alces americanus.desc: Moose (Alces americanus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

aldabrachelys gigantea.name: Aldabra giant tortoise
aldabrachelys gigantea.desc: About 100,000 live here, the largest population anywhere. They eat grasses, leaves and woody stems, and like elephants they shape the landscape.

alectoris chukar.name: Chukar
alectoris chukar.desc: A ground-nesting partridge of dry rocky slopes that eats seeds and plant matter.

alectura lathami.name: Australian brushturkey
alectura lathami.desc: Builds a large nest mound of rotting leaf litter. Its eggs are a favourite food of goannas, snakes and dingoes.

algae.name: Reef algae
algae.desc: Algae growing on reef rock feed turtles, parrotfish and surgeonfish. They spread when corals die.

algae and cyanobacteria.name: Phytoplankton
algae and cyanobacteria.desc: Drifting algae in the shallow lagoon. Nutrient-rich water has led to confirmed algal blooms there.

algae, cyanobacteria and microbes.name: Periphyton
algae, cyanobacteria and microbes.desc: A living mat of algae and microbes on submerged plants and surfaces. In the Everglades it grows where sawgrass is sparse and feeds larval insects and amphibians.

algal turf and macroalgae.name: Reef algae and macroalgae
algal turf and macroalgae.desc: Algae growing on reef rock and sand. Grazers such as parrotfish and conch keep it from smothering corals.

aliger gigas.name: Queen conch
aliger gigas.desc: A large snail that grazes algae and seagrass films on sandy flats and meadows.

alkaline soils.name: Alkaline soils
alkaline soils.desc: Salty, alkaline soils on the Great Plain keep much of the puszta treeless and favour salt-tolerant grasses and herbs.

allactaga sibirica.name: Mongolian five-toed jerboa
allactaga sibirica.desc: A hopping desert rodent that eats seeds and plants and is hunted by foxes, falcons and eagles.

alle alle.name: Little auk
alle alle.desc: A sparrow-sized seabird nesting in huge scree-slope colonies, feeding chiefly on copepods. Its colonies are raided by Arctic foxes and glaucous gulls.

allenrolfea occidentalis.name: Iodine-bush
allenrolfea occidentalis.desc: Iodine-bush (Allenrolfea occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

alliaria petiolata.name: Garlic Mustard
alliaria petiolata.desc: Garlic mustard (Alliaria petiolata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 336 times near the park in GBIF.

alligator mississippiensis.name: American alligator
alligator mississippiensis.desc: Digs gator holes that keep water through the dry season, giving fish and other animals a refuge. An opportunistic top predator.

allium falcifolium.name: Scytheleaf onion
allium falcifolium.desc: Scytheleaf onion (Allium falcifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

allium stellatum.name: Autumn onion
allium stellatum.desc: Autumn onion (Allium stellatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

allium tolmiei.name: Tolmie's onion
allium tolmiei.desc: Tolmie's onion (Allium tolmiei): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.

allocasuarina decaisneana.name: Desert oak
allocasuarina decaisneana.desc: A tall, drought-tolerant tree of the sand dunes and sandplains of central Australia, frequently recorded around the park.

allochrocebus lhoesti.name: L'Hoest's monkey
allochrocebus lhoesti.desc: Mostly plant eater of fruit, leaves, roots and mushrooms, occasionally eggs and small animals. Favours dense undergrowth in mountain forest.

alluvial soil & nutrients.name: Alluvial soil & nutrients
alluvial soil & nutrients.desc: River-borne silt and leaf litter build the rich, wet soils of the floodplain.

alnus alnobetula.name: Green alder
alnus alnobetula.desc: A shrub that colonises ground left bare by retreating ice. Alders host nitrogen-fixing root bacteria that enrich young soils.

alnus glutinosa.name: Common alder
alnus glutinosa.desc: Alders and willows form the deciduous wet forest on the Colchic plain, rooted in waterlogged soil.

aloe perryi.name: Socotrine aloe
aloe perryi.desc: A succulent of Socotra's dry slopes and cliffs, with bright flower spikes that offer nectar to birds.

aloidendron eminens.name: Somali tree aloe
aloidendron eminens.desc: A tall tree aloe, one of the most frequently recorded plants of the Erigavo highlands in GBIF data.

alopochen aegyptiaca.name: Egyptian goose
alopochen aegyptiaca.desc: A grazing waterbird of river banks and pools. Eaten by pythons.

alosa pseudoharengus.name: Alewife
alosa pseudoharengus.desc: An invasive herring that eats zooplankton. It became the main prey for stocked salmon and trout.

alosa sapidissima.name: American shad
alosa sapidissima.desc: A plankton-feeding fish that runs up the Connecticut River to spawn. Striped bass are its main predator and harbor seals take some.

alouatta caraya.name: Black howler
alouatta caraya.desc: A mostly leaf-eating, tree-living monkey. GloBI records it eating caranday palm.

alouatta macconnelli.name: Guyanan red howler
alouatta macconnelli.desc: A howler monkey native to Guyana and neighbouring countries, living in the forest canopy.

alouatta palliata.name: Mantled howler
alouatta palliata.desc: A leaf-eating monkey that also takes fruit, especially figs, and helps spread and germinate seeds.

alouatta spp..name: Howler monkey
alouatta spp..desc: Eats leaves, flowers and fruit, and announces its territory with a roar that carries for miles.

alpine soil.name: Alpine soil
alpine soil.desc: Thin mountain soils hold the nutrients that meadow plants and dwarf shrubs draw on.

alpine soils.name: Alpine soils
alpine soils.desc: Thin soils on rock and moraine supply nutrients to alpine plants and are topped up as dead matter is broken down.

alternanthera philoxeroides.name: Alligatorweed
alternanthera philoxeroides.desc: Alligatorweed (Alternanthera philoxeroides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

alticola argentatus.name: Silver mountain vole
alticola argentatus.desc: A small rodent of rocky mountain ground, recorded near the park. It eats plant material and is prey for foxes and snakes.

alypia octomaculata.name: Eight-spotted Forester
alypia octomaculata.desc: Eight-spotted Forester (Alypia octomaculata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

amazona aestiva.name: Turquoise-fronted parrot
amazona aestiva.desc: A parrot of Chaco woodland that eats seeds and fruit.

amazona vittata.name: Puerto Rican parrot
amazona vittata.desc: Critically endangered. Eats flowers, fruit, leaves and bark, and nests in tree cavities, favouring palo colorado trees. Hurricanes have repeatedly cut its numbers.

amblyopsis spelaea.name: Northern cavefish
amblyopsis spelaea.desc: An eyeless fish of caves in Kentucky and southern Indiana. Related cavefish eat small crustaceans, so crayfish are likely prey.

amblyrhynchus cristatus.name: Marine iguana
amblyrhynchus cristatus.desc: The only sea-going lizard. It feeds almost entirely on red and green seaweed, and populations crash when El Niño kills off its algae.

ambrosia dumosa.name: White bursage
ambrosia dumosa.desc: A low shrub that often grows alongside creosote bush across the desert floor.

ambrosia trifida.name: Perennial Ragweed
ambrosia trifida.desc: Perennial Ragweed (Ambrosia trifida): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

amelanchier alnifolia.name: Saskatoon serviceberry
amelanchier alnifolia.desc: A berry-bearing shrub of open slopes. Bears, birds and browsing ungulates use its fruit and leaves.

amelanchier arborea.name: Allegheny Serviceberry
amelanchier arborea.desc: Allegheny Serviceberry (Amelanchier arborea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

amelanchier utahensis.name: Utah serviceberry
amelanchier utahensis.desc: Utah serviceberry (Amelanchier utahensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

amia calva.name: Bowfin
amia calva.desc: A predatory fish that copes with the acidic, low-oxygen tannic water. The refuge names it among its common fish.

ammelaphus imberbis.name: Lesser kudu
ammelaphus imberbis.desc: A shy browser of thornbush and dense cover. Tree and shrub foliage makes up most of its diet, and it is found across most of Somalia.

ammodramus savannarum.name: Grasshopper Sparrow
ammodramus savannarum.desc: Grasshopper Sparrow (Ammodramus savannarum): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1,333 times near the park in GBIF.

ammodytes americanus.name: American sand lance
ammodytes americanus.desc: A small schooling fish that eats plankton and is a key prey of seals, whales and seabirds.

ammodytes personatus.name: Pacific sand lance
ammodytes personatus.desc: A small schooling fish that eats zooplankton and is prey for many seabirds, fish and marine mammals.

ammomanes deserti.name: Desert lark
ammomanes deserti.desc: Eats seeds and insects, with more insects in the breeding season. A common small bird that predators of the desert hunt.

ammophila arenaria.name: European marram grass
ammophila arenaria.desc: A tough dune grass whose roots bind loose sand on the beach and foredunes.

ammophila breviligulata.name: American beachgrass
ammophila breviligulata.desc: A beach grass native to Great Lakes shores. Wikipedia says its genus builds coastal dunes and stabilises the sand with creeping rhizomes.

ammospermophilus harrisii.name: Harris' antelope squirrel
ammospermophilus harrisii.desc: Harris' antelope squirrel (Ammospermophilus harrisii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 37 times near the park in GBIF.

ammospermophilus leucurus.name: White-tailed antelope squirrel
ammospermophilus leucurus.desc: A day-active omnivore that eats mostly plants and seeds, plus arthropods. Raptors, canids and snakes prey on it.

ammotragus lervia.name: Barbary sheep (aoudad)
ammotragus lervia.desc: A North African wild sheep introduced to the Southwest and heavily recorded near the park. It grazes and browses desert plants, competing with native herbivores.

amorpha canescens.name: Leadplant
amorpha canescens.desc: A deep-rooted prairie shrub in the pea family, listed among the hills' characteristic flowering plants and visited by bumble bees.

amorpha fruticosa.name: Desert false indigo
amorpha fruticosa.desc: Desert false indigo (Amorpha fruticosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

amphibolis antarctica.name: Wire weed
amphibolis antarctica.desc: A seagrass of southern and western Australian coasts that forms extensive meadows in shallow water on sand, gravel and rock.

amphipoda.name: Amphipods and small crustaceans
amphipoda.desc: Small crustaceans that live among the kelp and feed on its tissue and drift. Food for small fish.

amsonia hubrichtii.name: Hubricht's bluestar
amsonia hubrichtii.desc: Hubricht's bluestar (Amsonia hubrichtii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.

amsonia tabernaemontana.name: Texas-star
amsonia tabernaemontana.desc: Texas-star (Amsonia tabernaemontana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

anabas testudineus.name: Climbing perch
anabas testudineus.desc: A hardy small fish of ponds, swamps and paddies; prey for otters and many wading birds.

anableps anableps.name: Four-eyed fish
anableps anableps.desc: Surface-dwelling fish of the brackish waters of the swamp, with eyes adapted to look above and below the water.

anabrus simplex.name: Mormon cricket
anabrus simplex.desc: A flightless shrub-dwelling katydid that eats plants and is eaten by bears and birds.

anaphalis margaritacea.name: Pearly everlasting
anaphalis margaritacea.desc: Common pearlyeverlasting (Anaphalis margaritacea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

anas platyrhynchos.name: Mallard
anas platyrhynchos.desc: Eats seeds from moist-soil plants and other plant foods in flooded fields and backwaters.

anax parthenope.name: Lesser emperor
anax parthenope.desc: Large dragonfly of still and slow water that catches other insects in flight; its larvae live in the water.

anchistea virginica.name: Virginia chain fern
anchistea virginica.desc: Virginia chain fern (Anchistea virginica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 44 times near the park in GBIF.

anchoa mitchilli.name: Bay anchovy
anchoa mitchilli.desc: A small schooling fish that eats zooplankton and is a key forage fish for larger fish and birds.

andersonglossum virginianum.name: Giant-forget-me-not
andersonglossum virginianum.desc: Giant-forget-me-not (Andersonglossum virginianum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

andrena erigeniae.name: Spring Beauty Andrena
andrena erigeniae.desc: Spring Beauty Andrena (Andrena erigeniae): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 40 times near the park in GBIF.

andricus quercusflocci.name: Andricus quercusflocci
andricus quercusflocci.desc: Andricus quercusflocci (Andricus quercusflocci): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

andropogon.name: Bluestem grasses
andropogon.desc: Tall bunch grasses are among the common grass genera of the savanna and feed grazers through the wet season.

andropogon canaliculatus.name: Bluestem grass
andropogon canaliculatus.desc: A bunchgrass of the open savanna. Grasses like this carpet the plains and feed the park's grazers.

andropogon gayanus.name: Gamba grass
andropogon gayanus.desc: A tall tussock grass of West African savannas, recorded often near the park. It is a staple of grazers and carries the dry-season fires.

andropogon gerardi.name: Big bluestem
andropogon gerardi.desc: A tall dominant prairie grass. The MDC says prairie species such as prairie-chickens and Henslow's sparrows indirectly depend on it, and it is excellent forage for livestock.

anemonastrum canadense.name: Canada anemone
anemonastrum canadense.desc: Canada anemone (Anemonastrum canadense): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

anemone cylindrica.name: Candle anemone
anemone cylindrica.desc: Candle anemone (Anemone cylindrica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

anemone oregana.name: Blue windflower
anemone oregana.desc: Blue windflower (Anemone oregana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 45 times near the park in GBIF.

anemone quinquefolia.name: Wood Anemone
anemone quinquefolia.desc: Wood Anemone (Anemone quinquefolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

anemone virginiana.name: Thimbleweed
anemone virginiana.desc: Thimbleweed (Anemone virginiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

angiopteris evecta.name: Tree fern
angiopteris evecta.desc: A large fern of the damp forest floor and stream edges, shading the ground and sheltering small animals.

anguilla anguilla.name: European eel
anguilla anguilla.desc: Eats worms, fish, molluscs and crustaceans. Critically endangered, with numbers reaching Europe down by about 90% since the 1970s.

anhinga melanogaster.name: Oriental darter
anhinga melanogaster.desc: Swims with only its neck above water and spears fish; nests in mixed waterbird colonies in trees standing in water.

anodorhynchus hyacinthinus.name: Hyacinth macaw
anodorhynchus hyacinthinus.desc: A giant parrot that in the Pantanal feeds almost entirely on nuts of the acuri and bocaiuva palms.

anogeissus pendula.name: Dhok
anogeissus pendula.desc: Wikipedia calls it the characteristic tree of Ranthambore. It looks dry and brown in summer but greens up after a little rain.

anolis carolinensis.name: Green anole
anolis carolinensis.desc: GREEN ANOLE (Anolis carolinensis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1,043 times near the park in GBIF.

anolis chlorocyanus.name: Hispaniolan green anole
anolis chlorocyanus.desc: A tree-dwelling lizard that hunts insects such as ants on trunks and foliage.

anolis distichus.name: Bark anole
anolis distichus.desc: A small lizard on trunks and branches that hunts insects and other arthropods.

anolis equestris.name: Knight anole
anolis equestris.desc: Large Cuban tree lizard of forest and mangrove that eats insects, snails and fruit, and sometimes small vertebrates.

anolis fuscoauratus.name: Brown-eared anole
anolis fuscoauratus.desc: A small forest lizard that eats insects. The blunthead treesnake is recorded in GloBI eating it.

anolis gundlachi.name: Gundlach's anole
anolis gundlachi.desc: A common forest anole that eats small invertebrates. Young Puerto Rican boas feed mainly on anoles.

anolis lineatopus.name: Stripefoot anole
anolis lineatopus.desc: A common Jamaican lizard that hunts insects, including ants, and is itself eaten by snakes and mongooses.

anolis townsendi.name: Cocos anole
anolis townsendi.desc: An endemic lizard of Cocos Island, one of the most recorded animals there, that hunts small insects.

anopheles aquasalis.name: Salt-marsh mosquito
anopheles aquasalis.desc: A mosquito whose larvae develop in brackish water; its larvae and adults are prey for fish and insect-eating bats.

anous stolidus.name: Brown noddy
anous stolidus.desc: A tropical seabird that nests on the atoll islets and catches small fish at the sea surface.

anser albifrons.name: Greater white-fronted goose
anser albifrons.desc: A winter visitor that grazes grasses, clover and dandelion in open fields.

anser anser.name: Greylag goose
anser anser.desc: A large grazing goose of wetland and meadows that eats reed shoots and grasses.

anser brachyrhynchus.name: Pink-footed goose
anser brachyrhynchus.desc: Breeds in the Icelandic highlands, using wetlands near the glacier, and eats tundra plants in summer. The Arctic fox is its main land predator.

anser caerulescens.name: Snow goose
anser caerulescens.desc: Nests on the tundra in summer and grazes sedges.

anseranas semipalmata.name: Magpie goose
anseranas semipalmata.desc: Floodplain bird that eats grass seeds, grass blades and spike-rush bulbs. It is the most recorded bird near the park and a seasonal food for people and crocodiles.

antarctic convergence.name: Antarctic Convergence
antarctic convergence.desc: The Southern Ocean boundary where cold and warmer waters meet, which concentrates plankton and the fish and squid that feed on it.

antheraea polyphemus.name: Polyphemus Moth
antheraea polyphemus.desc: Polyphemus Moth (Antheraea polyphemus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

anthophora urbana.name: Urbane Digger Bee
anthophora urbana.desc: Urbane Digger Bee (Anthophora urbana): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

anthornis melanura.name: New Zealand bellbird
anthornis melanura.desc: A common forest bird that feeds on nectar, fruit and insects.

anthracoceros albirostris.name: Oriental pied hornbill
anthracoceros albirostris.desc: A large forest bird that eats figs and other fruit as well as lizards and insects, and so spreads fig seeds.

anthropoides virgo.name: Demoiselle crane
anthropoides virgo.desc: A small crane nesting on the steppe and wetland edge, eating seeds, shoots and insects. Recorded often near the lake.

antidesma montanum.name: Antidesma
antidesma montanum.desc: A forest tree recorded near the park whose small fruits are eaten by macaques, according to GloBI records.

antidorcas marsupialis.name: Springbok
antidorcas marsupialis.desc: A small antelope of arid plains that grazes and browses and needs little free water.

antilocapra americana.name: Pronghorn
antilocapra americana.desc: Pronghorn (Antilocapra americana): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

antrozous pallidus.name: Pallid bat
antrozous pallidus.desc: Pallid bat (Antrozous pallidus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

aphelocoma californica.name: California scrub-jay
aphelocoma californica.desc: California scrub-jay (Aphelocoma californica): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 698 times near the park in GBIF.

aphelocoma woodhouseii.name: Woodhouse's scrub-jay
aphelocoma woodhouseii.desc: A common oak-scrub bird that eats acorns, seeds and insects, and is among the most recorded birds here.

apis dorsata.name: Giant honey bee
apis dorsata.desc: A wild bee that hangs open combs from high branches and feeds on flower nectar. It is one of the best-recorded insects near the park.

apis mellifera.name: Western honey bee
apis mellifera.desc: Western honey bee (Apis mellifera): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

aplodinotus grunniens.name: Freshwater drum
aplodinotus grunniens.desc: Crushes mussels and eats insect larvae and, later in the year, young gizzard shad.

apocynum androsaemifolium.name: Bitterroot
apocynum androsaemifolium.desc: Bitterroot (Apocynum androsaemifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

apodemus agrarius.name: Striped field mouse
apodemus agrarius.desc: A small rodent of fields and forest edges that eats seeds and plant material. It is prey for stoats, gulls and wolves.

apodemus draco.name: South China field mouse
apodemus draco.desc: A well-recorded forest rodent of the Hengduan mountains and a staple small prey for carnivores.

apodemus flavicollis.name: Yellow-necked mouse
apodemus flavicollis.desc: A forest rodent that eats seeds and is a main prey of wildcats in the Carpathians.

apodemus sylvaticus.name: Wood mouse
apodemus sylvaticus.desc: A small woodland rodent that eats seeds and fruit, and is food for foxes, martens and snakes.

apodemus uralensis.name: Ural field mouse
apodemus uralensis.desc: Small ground-dwelling rodent recorded near the park; a staple prey for herons, harriers and mammals.

aporosaura anchietae.name: Sand-diving lizard
aporosaura anchietae.desc: A dune lizard that dives into sand to escape heat and enemies. It eats wind-blown seeds and insects and is itself prey for snakes.

aptenodytes patagonicus.name: King penguin
aptenodytes patagonicus.desc: Breeds in large colonies at Kerguelen, about 240,000 to 280,000 pairs. Eats mostly lanternfish and squid.

apteryx australis.name: Southern brown kiwi
apteryx australis.desc: Flightless forest bird found almost entirely in Fiordland and nearby areas; it probes soil for invertebrates.

aquarius cordifolius.name: Creeping burhead
aquarius cordifolius.desc: Creeping burhead (Aquarius cordifolius): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

aquatic macrophytes.name: Floodplain plants & algae
aquatic macrophytes.desc: Floating meadows and algae in flooded forest that feed capybaras and fish.

aquifer water.name: Aquifer water
aquifer water.desc: The Kirkwood-Cohansey aquifer under the Barrens feeds its bogs, swamps and vernal pools.

aquila adalberti.name: Spanish imperial eagle
aquila adalberti.desc: An endangered eagle that eats rabbits and, where rabbits are scarce, water birds such as coots and ducks.

aquila audax.name: Wedge-tailed eagle
aquila audax.desc: A large eagle that takes rabbits, young kangaroos, lizards and birds, and feeds on carrion and roadkill.

aquila audax fleayi.name: Tasmanian wedge-tailed eagle
aquila audax fleayi.desc: A large endangered eagle that takes wallabies, possums and rabbits, and feeds on carrion in winter.

aquila chrysaetos.name: Golden eagle
aquila chrysaetos.desc: Large raptor that takes marmots and, from general knowledge, pikas and game birds.

aquila fasciata.name: Bonelli's eagle
aquila fasciata.desc: Cyprus diet studies show it taking chukar, pigeons, black rats, jackdaws and lizards, mostly caught alive.

aquila nipalensis.name: Steppe eagle
aquila nipalensis.desc: A large eagle of open country that hunts ground squirrels, marmots, voles and hares.

aquila rapax.name: Tawny eagle
aquila rapax.desc: A raptor that hunts and also feeds at carcasses; it is known to take young springbok.

aquila verreauxii.name: Verreaux's eagle
aquila verreauxii.desc: A hyrax specialist: in many areas hyraxes make up most of its diet, so its range follows theirs.

aquilegia canadensis.name: Wild columbine
aquilegia canadensis.desc: Wild columbine (Aquilegia canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

aquilegia coerulea.name: Colorado columbine
aquilegia coerulea.desc: Colorado columbine (Aquilegia coerulea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 89 times near the park in GBIF.

aquilegia micrantha.name: Alcove columbine
aquilegia micrantha.desc: Alcove columbine (Aquilegia micrantha): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

ara ambiguus.name: Great green macaw
ara ambiguus.desc: A large parrot that cracks hard nuts. It relies heavily on almendro trees and Indio Maiz is a main refuge for it.

ara macao.name: Scarlet macaw
ara macao.desc: Cracks open hard seeds and fruits high in the canopy.

aramus guarauna.name: Limpkin
aramus guarauna.desc: A wading bird that specializes in extracting apple snails from their shells.

arapaima gigas.name: Arapaima
arapaima gigas.desc: One of the largest freshwater fish. It breathes air and eats other fish.

arbutus menziesii.name: Pacific madrone
arbutus menziesii.desc: Pacific madrone (Arbutus menziesii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 31 times near the park in GBIF.

arctocephalus australis.name: South American fur seal
arctocephalus australis.desc: Breeds on the Islas de Torres. Eats fish such as anchovies and squid, and is hunted by sharks, orcas and sea lions.

arctocephalus gazella.name: Antarctic fur seal
arctocephalus gazella.desc: Eats krill, among other prey. Its pups are taken by leopard seals.

arctocephalus pusillus.name: Cape fur seal
arctocephalus pusillus.desc: Large colonies breed on the Namib coast and feed on fish at sea. Their pups and carcasses feed jackals, hyenas and lions on land.

arctonyx collaris.name: Greater hog badger
arctonyx collaris.desc: A rooting forest omnivore that feeds on invertebrates and plant matter in leaf litter.

arctostaphylos glauca.name: Bigberry manzanita
arctostaphylos glauca.desc: A chaparral shrub with berry-like fruit. Wikipedia says its seeds need exposure to fire before they germinate.

arctostaphylos nevadensis.name: Pinemat manzanita
arctostaphylos nevadensis.desc: A low evergreen shrub whose berries are eaten by Sierra Nevada red foxes when in season.

arctostaphylos patula.name: Greenleaf manzanita
arctostaphylos patula.desc: A shrub of mid-elevation forest and chaparral whose flowers feed bumble bees and whose berries are food for wildlife.

arctostaphylos pungens.name: Pointleaf manzanita
arctostaphylos pungens.desc: Pointleaf manzanita (Arctostaphylos pungens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 173 times near the park in GBIF.

arctostaphylos uva-ursi.name: Bearberry
arctostaphylos uva-ursi.desc: Bearberry (Arctostaphylos uva-ursi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 43 times near the park in GBIF.

arctostaphylos viscida.name: WHITELEAF MANZANITA
arctostaphylos viscida.desc: WHITELEAF MANZANITA (Arctostaphylos viscida): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 90 times near the park in GBIF.

ardea alba.name: Great Egret
ardea alba.desc: A tall wader that stalks fish, frogs, crayfish and insects in shallow water. It also takes young alligators.

ardea cinerea.name: Grey heron
ardea cinerea.desc: Wading predator of frogs, small mammals, coots and fish; GloBI also records it taking coypu. The European eel page lists herons as eel predators.

ardea herodias.name: Great blue heron
ardea herodias.desc: Wades the shallows spearing fish. The NPS notes herons depend on fish.

ardea melanocephala.name: Black-headed heron
ardea melanocephala.desc: A heron that hunts in open grassland and at water edges, eating frogs, reptiles and small animals.

ardea purpurea.name: Purple heron
ardea purpurea.desc: A reed-bed wader that stalks fish and frogs in shallow water.

ardenna carneipes.name: Flesh-footed shearwater
ardenna carneipes.desc: A burrow-nesting seabird. Lord Howe holds about 22,000 breeding pairs, though numbers on the island have been declining.

ardenna pacifica.name: Wedge-tailed shearwater
ardenna pacifica.desc: A seabird that nests in burrows on Lord Howe and hunts fish, squid and crustaceans at sea, diving to depths of up to 66 m.

arenaria and calidris spp..name: Migratory shorebirds
arenaria and calidris spp..desc: Nest on the tundra for a few summer weeks, feeding on insects, seeds and eggs. Many then fly to coasts and reef flats as far south as Australia.

arenga obtusifolia.name: Arenga palm
arenga obtusifolia.desc: A fast-growing palm that shades the forest floor and reduces the food available to rhinos, so authorities work to remove it.

arenicola marina.name: Lugworm
arenicola marina.desc: A burrowing worm that swallows sand and digests the organic matter in it. Its coiled casts are visible at low tide.

argemone polyanthemos.name: Plains prickly-poppy
argemone polyanthemos.desc: Annual pricklypoppy (Argemone polyanthemos): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 35 times near the park in GBIF.

argia vivida.name: Vivid Dancer
argia vivida.desc: Vivid Dancer (Argia vivida): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 31 times near the park in GBIF.

argyrochosma dealbata.name: Powdery false cloak fern
argyrochosma dealbata.desc: Powdery false cloak fern (Argyrochosma dealbata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

argyroxiphium sandwicense.name: Haleakalā silversword
argyroxiphium sandwicense.desc: A silver-leaved plant found only on Haleakalā, above about 2,100 m. It is federally threatened, and introduced hoofed animals are a major reason it declined.

arilus cristatus.name: Wheel Bug
arilus cristatus.desc: Wheel Bug (Arilus cristatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

ariolimax columbianus.name: Pacific banana slug
ariolimax columbianus.desc: A big forest-floor slug that eats leaves, moss, dung and dead plant matter, and recycles them into soil. Snakes and small mammals sometimes eat it.

arizona elegans.name: Glossy snake
arizona elegans.desc: A nocturnal desert snake. GloBI records show it eating kangaroo rats, deer mice and lizards.

arnoglossum plantagineum.name: Arnoglossum
arnoglossum plantagineum.desc: Arnoglossum (Arnoglossum plantagineum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

artemia.name: Brine shrimp
artemia.desc: Tiny crustaceans of salt lakes and brine ponds. Their tolerance of very salty water helps them escape most fish predators.

artemisia.name: Wormwoods
artemisia.desc: Aromatic shrubby Artemisia species grow on the dry slopes. A tarragon relative is a recorded food plant of the Old World swallowtail.

artemisia absinthium.name: Absinth sagewort
artemisia absinthium.desc: Absinth sagewort (Artemisia absinthium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

artemisia annua.name: Annual Mugwort
artemisia annua.desc: Annual Mugwort (Artemisia annua): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

artemisia californica.name: California sagebrush
artemisia californica.desc: A common shrub of the coastal scrub on the islands; its flowers and seeds feed insects and small animals.

artemisia filifolia.name: Sand sagebrush
artemisia filifolia.desc: Sand sagebrush (Artemisia filifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.

artemisia herba-alba.name: White wormwood
artemisia herba-alba.desc: A low grey shrub of dry steppe and a main climax plant of the Syrian Desert. It is good fodder, mainly for sheep.

artemisia stelleriana.name: Oldwoman
artemisia stelleriana.desc: Oldwoman (Artemisia stelleriana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

artemisia tridentata.name: Big sagebrush
artemisia tridentata.desc: An aromatic shrub of dry rim flats. Mule deer eat it, along with bitterbrush and oak.

artemisiospiza nevadensis.name: Sagebrush Sparrow
artemisiospiza nevadensis.desc: Sagebrush Sparrow (Artemisiospiza nevadensis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 138 times near the park in GBIF.

arthropoda.name: Forest arthropods
arthropoda.desc: Millipedes, beetles, crickets, ants and other invertebrates of the leaf litter and canopy, eating leaves and litter.

arthrospira.name: Spirulina algae
arthrospira.desc: A blue-green alga that thrives in very alkaline water and is the main food of lesser flamingos on East African soda lakes.

artibeus jamaicensis.name: Jamaican fruit bat
artibeus jamaicensis.desc: The most-recorded mammal near the site; it feeds on fruit such as figs and carries seeds through the forest at night.

artibeus lituratus.name: Great fruit-eating bat
artibeus lituratus.desc: A fruit bat that feeds on figs and other fruit and carries the seeds away at night.

artocarpus altilis.name: Breadfruit
artocarpus altilis.desc: A large fruiting tree of villages and forest edges. Its fruit is eaten by flying foxes and rats.

arundinaria gigantea.name: Giant cane
arundinaria gigantea.desc: Giant cane (Arundinaria gigantea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

arvicanthis.name: Grass rats
arvicanthis.desc: Diurnal grass-eating rodents of open ground. Records near the park include Blick's and Ethiopian grass rats, which the wolf is recorded eating.

arvicanthis abyssinicus.name: Abyssinian grass rat
arvicanthis abyssinicus.desc: A rodent of the highland grasslands and the main prey of the Ethiopian wolf in Simien.

arvicanthis niloticus.name: African grass rat
arvicanthis niloticus.desc: Common rodent of grassy, damp ground and an important prey item for many predators in the region.

arvicola amphibius.name: European water vole
arvicola amphibius.desc: Burrowing rodent of banks and wet meadows that feeds on reeds, sedges and grasses and is prey for many predators.

asarum marmoratum.name: Marbled wildginger
asarum marmoratum.desc: Marbled wildginger (Asarum marmoratum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 47 times near the park in GBIF.

ascia monuste.name: Great Southern white
ascia monuste.desc: Great Southern white (Ascia monuste): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 67 times near the park in GBIF.

asclepias.desc: The only plant monarch caterpillars eat. It grows far to the north, and herbicide use on Corn Belt crops has destroyed much of it.

asclepias asperula.name: Antelope horns

asclepias exaltata.name: Tall milkweed

asclepias incarnata.name: Swamp Milkweed
asclepias incarnata.desc: Swamp Milkweed (Asclepias incarnata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

asclepias oenotheroides.desc: Prairie milkweed (Asclepias oenotheroides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

asclepias perennis.name: Smooth-seed milkweed

asclepias speciosa.name: Greek milkweed
asclepias speciosa.desc: Greek milkweed (Asclepias speciosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

asclepias spp..name: Milkweed
asclepias spp..desc: A prairie wildflower whose nectar feeds butterflies. The MDC lists Mead's milkweed as a prairie species at risk.

asclepias subverticillata.name: Horsetail milkweed
asclepias subverticillata.desc: Horsetail milkweed (Asclepias subverticillata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

asclepias syriaca.name: Common Milkweed
asclepias syriaca.desc: Common Milkweed (Asclepias syriaca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

asclepias tuberosa.name: Butterfly Milkweed
asclepias tuberosa.desc: Butterfly Milkweed (Asclepias tuberosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

asclepias viridiflora.name: Green antelopehorn milkweed
asclepias viridiflora.desc: Green antelopehorn milkweed (Asclepias viridiflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 23 times near the park in GBIF.

asclepias viridis.name: Antelope-horns
asclepias viridis.desc: Antelope-horns (Asclepias viridis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 23 times near the park in GBIF.

ascophyllum nodosum.name: Rockweed
ascophyllum nodosum.desc: A brown seaweed that covers rocks in the tidal zone. Wikipedia notes that its chemical defenses deter grazing snails.

asimina triloba.name: Pawpaw
asimina triloba.desc: Pawpaw (Asimina triloba): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 121 times near the park in GBIF.

asio flammeus.name: Pueo (short-eared owl)
asio flammeus.desc: A hunting owl of open country. GloBI records list it eating rodents and small birds near the park.

asio stygius.name: Stygian owl
asio stygius.desc: A night hunter of forest and caves, named by Wikipedia as a natural predator of the solenodon.

asota alienata.name: Tiger moth
asota alienata.desc: A moth recorded on Santo. Caterpillars of this genus are known to feed on fig leaves, and adults are prey for bats and birds.

aspidotis densa.name: Indian's dream
aspidotis densa.desc: Indian's dream (Aspidotis densa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

asplenium.name: Understory ferns and herbs
asplenium.desc: Ferns such as spleenwort and other low plants carpet the shaded limestone forest floor. Spleenwort is recorded in the diet of the saola.

asplenium platyneuron.name: Ebony Spleenwort
asplenium platyneuron.desc: Ebony Spleenwort (Asplenium platyneuron): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

asplenium resiliens.name: Blackstem spleenwort
asplenium resiliens.desc: Blackstem spleenwort (Asplenium resiliens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

asplenium rhizophyllum.name: Walking fern
asplenium rhizophyllum.desc: Walking fern (Asplenium rhizophyllum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.

asterocampa celtis.name: Hackberry Emperor
asterocampa celtis.desc: Hackberry Emperor (Asterocampa celtis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

asterocampa clyton.name: Tawny Emperor
asterocampa clyton.desc: Tawny Emperor (Asterocampa clyton): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

astragalus bisulcatus.name: Two-groove milk-vetch
astragalus bisulcatus.desc: Two-groove milk-vetch (Astragalus bisulcatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

astragalus caricinus.name: Buckwheat milkvetch
astragalus caricinus.desc: Buckwheat milkvetch (Astragalus caricinus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

astragalus ceramicus.name: Painted milk-vetch
astragalus ceramicus.desc: Painted milk-vetch (Astragalus ceramicus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

astragalus crassicarpus.name: Ground-plum
astragalus crassicarpus.desc: Ground-plum (Astragalus crassicarpus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

astragalus distortus.name: Ozark milk-vetch
astragalus distortus.desc: Ozark milk-vetch (Astragalus distortus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

astragalus filipes.name: Basalt milkvetch
astragalus filipes.desc: Basalt milkvetch (Astragalus filipes): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

astragalus miser.name: Timber milkvetch
astragalus miser.desc: Timber milkvetch (Astragalus miser): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

astragalus missouriensis.name: Missouri milkvetch
astragalus missouriensis.desc: Missouri milkvetch (Astragalus missouriensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 31 times near the park in GBIF.

astragalus praelongus.name: Stinking milk-vetch
astragalus praelongus.desc: Stinking milk-vetch (Astragalus praelongus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 28 times near the park in GBIF.

astragalus purshii.name: Pursh milk-vetch
astragalus purshii.desc: Pursh milk-vetch (Astragalus purshii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

astragalus rhizanthus.name: Milkvetch
astragalus rhizanthus.desc: A legume of the stony alpine ground. Legumes are food plants for the caterpillars of clouded yellow butterflies.

astragalus spatulatus.name: Draba milk-vetch
astragalus spatulatus.desc: Draba milk-vetch (Astragalus spatulatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

astragalus subcinereus.name: Siler's milk-vetch
astragalus subcinereus.desc: Siler's milk-vetch (Astragalus subcinereus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 41 times near the park in GBIF.

astragalus toanus.name: Toano milkvetch
astragalus toanus.desc: Toano milkvetch (Astragalus toanus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

astrapia splendidissima.name: Splendid astrapia
astrapia splendidissima.desc: A bird-of-paradise of montane forest that eats mostly fruit, especially Schefflera and Pandanus, plus insects and small lizards and frogs.

astrocaryum standleyanum.name: Black palm
astrocaryum standleyanum.desc: A spiny lowland palm of Pacific Central America whose large seeds are eaten and buried by forest rodents.

astrochelys radiata.name: Radiated tortoise
astrochelys radiata.desc: Grazing tortoise of the southern spiny thickets that feeds on plants.

ateles geoffroyi.name: Geoffroy's spider monkey
ateles geoffroyi.desc: Fruit takes most of its feeding time, with leaves, flowers and insects as extras. Jaguars and pumas are its main adult predators.

ateles paniscus.name: Red-faced spider monkey
ateles paniscus.desc: A large canopy primate that eats mostly fruit and young leaves, plus some insects. A prey of harpy eagles.

athene cunicularia.name: Burrowing owl
athene cunicularia.desc: Nests underground and is associated with prairie dog colonies. Hunts small mammals, birds, frogs and insects.

athene noctua.name: Little owl
athene noctua.desc: A small owl of open dry country that hunts small birds, rodents and insects, often at dusk.

atheris nitschei.name: Great Lakes bush viper
atheris nitschei.desc: A tree-dwelling viper of Albertine Rift forests, recorded eating Temminck's mouse.

atlantic rain.name: Atlantic rain
atlantic rain.desc: Wet Atlantic weather feeds the plants of the thin soils and the Burren's seasonal lakes.

atlantic rainfall.name: Atlantic rainfall
atlantic rainfall.desc: Mountains block moist Atlantic air, giving very heavy rain, roughly 1,600 mm a year low down and about 3,200 mm on the heights.

atractosteus spatula.name: Alligator gar
atractosteus spatula.desc: An ambush predator of slow river backwaters and brackish marsh. Eats mainly shad and other fish, and blue crabs in brackish water.

atriplex argentea.name: Saltbush
atriplex argentea.desc: Saltbush (Atriplex argentea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

atriplex canescens.name: Four-wing saltbush
atriplex canescens.desc: A tough, salt-tolerant shrub well recorded near the park. Its leaves and seeds feed many grazers and browsers.

atriplex gardneri.name: Gardner's saltbush
atriplex gardneri.desc: Gardner's saltbush (Atriplex gardneri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

atriplex halimus.name: Shrubby orache
atriplex halimus.desc: A salt-tolerant evergreen shrub of dry, saline ground that provides browse in arid areas.

atriplex lampa.name: Saltbush
atriplex lampa.desc: A salt-tolerant shrub of dry ground that suits the salty soils. Maras are reported to eat it.

atriplex micrantha.name: Twoscale Saltbush
atriplex micrantha.desc: Twoscale Saltbush (Atriplex micrantha): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

atriplex parishii.name: Parish's saltbush
atriplex parishii.desc: Parish's saltbush (Atriplex parishii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

atriplex prostrata.name: Spear-leaved Orache
atriplex prostrata.desc: Spear-leaved Orache (Atriplex prostrata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

atta.name: Leafcutter ants
atta.desc: Cut leaves to feed fungus gardens. Wikipedia says nests reach densities of up to 4,000 per hectare in the Cerrado.

atta cephalotes.name: Leafcutter ants
atta cephalotes.desc: Carry leaf fragments to underground gardens of fungus, which they eat.

attalea phalerata.name: Acuri palm
attalea phalerata.desc: A palm whose very hard nuts are the main food of hyacinth macaws in the Pantanal. Collared peccaries and many birds also eat its fruit.

augochlora pura.name: Pure Green Augochlora
augochlora pura.desc: Pure Green Augochlora (Augochlora pura): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

augochlorella aurata.name: Golden Sweat Bee
augochlorella aurata.desc: Golden Sweat Bee (Augochlorella aurata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 216 times near the park in GBIF.

aulacoseira baicalensis.name: Diatoms (Aulacoseira)
aulacoseira baicalensis.desc: Microscopic glassy algae that bloom in and under the ice. Over 400 diatom species live in Baikal, and about half are found nowhere else.

auriparus flaviceps.name: Verdin
auriparus flaviceps.desc: Verdin (Auriparus flaviceps): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1,590 times near the park in GBIF.

austrostipa.name: Spear grasses
austrostipa.desc: Tussock grasses of the sandy mainland and island country, grazed and seeded on by ground-dwelling mammals.

autumn-winter rain.name: Autumn-winter rain
autumn-winter rain.desc: Rainfall drives the flooding of the marshes. Wikipedia notes that very low water in January 2024 gave the lowest bird count on record.

avena.name: Wild oats and grasses
avena.desc: Grasses of clearings, forest edges and farmland, recorded in large numbers near the forest.

avena sterilis.name: Wild oat
avena sterilis.desc: A wild annual grass of the Mediterranean and steppe zones that sprouts after winter rain and feeds grazers and seed eaters.

avenella flexuosa.name: Wavy hair-grass
avenella flexuosa.desc: A fine grass of acidic, sandy forest soils and open ground, where it grows in tufts.

avicennia germinans.name: Black mangrove
avicennia germinans.desc: Black mangrove (Avicennia germinans): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 30 times near the park in GBIF.

avicennia marina.name: Grey mangrove
avicennia marina.desc: One of the few mangroves of arid Red Sea shores; its aerial roots trap sediment and it excretes salt through its leaves.

awash river inflow.name: Awash River inflow
awash river inflow.desc: The Awash is the lake's main source of water. It has no outflow, so salts build up and the level swings with river supply.

axis axis.name: Chital
axis axis.desc: The main large prey of the Sundarbans tiger. Browses and grazes on the forest floor.

axis porcinus.name: Hog deer
axis porcinus.desc: A small deer of the floodplain grasslands, recorded as prey of tigers and leopards.

axonopus, paspalum.name: Cerrado grasses
axonopus, paspalum.desc: Grasses form most of the herb layer of the open savanna, which Wikipedia says typically reaches about 60 cm. Golden carpetgrass is well recorded here.

aythya valisineria.name: Canvasback
aythya valisineria.desc: A diving duck that migrates along the Mississippi Flyway. It eats tubers, buds, seeds, snails and insect larvae, favoring wild celery. The FWS says the upper river supports up to half the world's canvasbacks.

azolla cristata.name: Atlantic azolla
azolla cristata.desc: Atlantic azolla (Azolla cristata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

azolla filiculoides.name: Water Fern
azolla filiculoides.desc: Water Fern (Azolla filiculoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

azorella compacta.name: Yareta
azorella compacta.desc: A dense, cushion-forming evergreen of the high Andes that grows only a centimetre or so a year. Local people burn it for fuel, which is hard for it to withstand.

azorella selago.name: Cushion azorella
azorella selago.desc: Compact cushion plant common in the islands fellfield and rocky ground, and eaten by introduced rabbits.

baccaurea parviflora.name: Baccaurea trees
baccaurea parviflora.desc: Understory fruit tree recorded in the reserve; its fruit is eaten by macaques and mouse-deer according to GloBI records.

baccharis halimifolia.name: Groundsel tree
baccharis halimifolia.desc: Groundsel tree (Baccharis halimifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 98 times near the park in GBIF.

baccharis pilularis.name: Coyote Brush
baccharis pilularis.desc: Coyote Brush (Baccharis pilularis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 714 times near the park in GBIF.

bacillariophyceae.name: Phytoplankton
bacillariophyceae.desc: Microscopic drifting algae, including diatoms, that capture sunlight in the bay and fjord waters and feed the marine food chain.

bacillariophyceae and other microalgae.name: Phytoplankton and algae
bacillariophyceae and other microalgae.desc: Drifting microscopic algae, including about 20 endemic algae species in Ohrid, feed the zooplankton and snails.

bacillariophyta.name: Marsh algae & diatoms
bacillariophyta.desc: Microscopic algae in the shallow marsh water. Flamingos filter algae and diatoms from the mud and water.

bacillariophyta (diatoms).name: Stream algae
bacillariophyta (diatoms).desc: Films of diatoms on stream stones. They feed the mayflies and other grazers that trout depend on.

bacteria and fungi.name: Decomposers
bacteria and fungi.desc: Break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil.

bacteria, fungi and worms.name: Decomposers
bacteria, fungi and worms.desc: Break down mangrove leaf litter, dead seagrass and carcasses, returning nutrients to the bay.

bacteria, worms, snails.name: Bacteria & decomposers
bacteria, worms, snails.desc: Break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the water. Decaying blooms use up oxygen.

badland and clay soils.name: Badland and clay soils
badland and clay soils.desc: Erodible clay soils of the Painted Desert hold little water and nutrients, so the grassland on better soils is a prized, slow-recovering resource.

badlands soil.name: Badlands soil
badlands soil.desc: Nutrients in the soil feed the grasses and shrubs.

baeolophus bicolor.name: Tufted Titmouse
baeolophus bicolor.desc: Tufted Titmouse (Baeolophus bicolor): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3,910 times near the park in GBIF.

baikiaea plurijuga.name: Zambezi teak
baikiaea plurijuga.desc: A dry-woodland tree. Wikipedia says dense stands of it once covered the Chobe riverfront before elephants thinned them.

balaeniceps rex.name: Shoebill
balaeniceps rex.desc: A giant wading bird for which the Sudd is a major stronghold; it hunts large fish such as lungfish in papyrus swamp.

balaenoptera musculus.name: Blue whale
balaenoptera musculus.desc: The largest animal; feeds on krill by filtering swarms.

balearica pavonina.name: Black crowned crane
balearica pavonina.desc: A wetland crane that feeds on seeds, insects and small animals in grasslands and shallow water of the Sudd.

balsamorhiza careyana.name: Carey's balsamroot
balsamorhiza careyana.desc: Carey's balsamroot (Balsamorhiza careyana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

bambusoideae.name: Bamboo & forest grasses
bambusoideae.desc: Grasses and bamboo grow in clearings, gaps and secondary growth. Grass is a regular food of large deer such as sambar.

baptisia australis.name: Baptisia
baptisia australis.desc: Baptisia (Baptisia australis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

barringtonia acutangula.name: Flooded-forest tree
barringtonia acutangula.desc: A tree of the seasonally flooded forest that rings the lake and shelters young fish when the water rises.

barringtonia edulis.name: Cutnut
barringtonia edulis.desc: An evergreen tree of humid forests found only in Fiji and Vanuatu. Moths and bats pollinate its flowers and its seeds are edible.

basilinna leucotis.name: White-eared hummingbird
basilinna leucotis.desc: A very commonly recorded bird of the highland forests, feeding on nectar from sages and other flowers.

battus philenor.name: Blue Swallowtail
battus philenor.desc: Blue Swallowtail (Battus philenor): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

bay nutrients.name: Bay nutrients
bay nutrients.desc: Nutrients released from dead plants and animals feed seagrass, mangroves and algae again.

bay water and tides.name: Bay water and tides
bay water and tides.desc: Salt water from San Lorenzo Bay floods the mangrove roots and carries the plankton and small fish the seabirds depend on.

benguela current algae.name: Phytoplankton
benguela current algae.desc: Drifting algae in the cold, productive Benguela Current, the base of the offshore food chain.

berberis microphylla.name: Calafate
berberis microphylla.desc: A spiny shrub of the steppe and forest edge that bears dark berries in summer.

bertholletia excelsa.name: Brazil nut tree
bertholletia excelsa.desc: A towering canopy tree whose hard-shelled seeds are opened only by agoutis.

bettongia lesueur.name: Boodie
bettongia lesueur.desc: Burrowing bettong that eats seeds, roots, fungi, grasses and more. Its digging turns over soil and spreads seeds and fungi.

betula alleghaniensis.name: Yellow birch
betula alleghaniensis.desc: A major tree of the Green Mountains hardwood forest. Browsed by deer and eaten by beavers, porcupines and red squirrels.

betula ermanii.name: Erman's birch
betula ermanii.desc: A birch that forms the tree line on the mountain, growing where conifers thin out below the tundra.

betula papyrifera.name: Paper birch
betula papyrifera.desc: A pale-barked northern hardwood recorded in the park; browsed by deer, hares and beavers and a common pioneer after disturbance.

betula pendula.name: Silver birch
betula pendula.desc: A pioneer tree of clearings and disturbed ground, browsed by roe deer and gnawed by beavers.

betula pubescens.name: Mountain birch
betula pubescens.desc: A pale-barked tree that forms the open woodland on the lower mountain slopes. Moose and hares eat its twigs and buds.

betula tianschanica.name: Tien Shan birch
betula tianschanica.desc: A shrubby birch of sheltered Pamir valleys, one of the few tree-like plants in the park.

bidens alba.name: Beggarticks
bidens alba.desc: A common wildflower of open ground. GloBI records it as food for the eastern lubber grasshopper.

birgus latro.name: Coconut crab
birgus latro.desc: The largest land arthropod. It eats fruit and carrion and also kills tortoise hatchlings and other crabs. Adults have almost no predators.

bison bison.name: American bison
bison bison.desc: About 50 bison were released in 1963 and the herd has grown to over 1,200. They graze grasses such as western wheatgrass.

bison bonasus.name: European bison
bison bonasus.desc: Europe's heaviest land animal eats grasses, herbs and tree bark and leaves. The forest holds the largest free-living herd, restored after reintroduction in 1929.

bistorta vivipara.name: Alpine bistort
bistorta vivipara.desc: A small tundra herb whose leaves and bulbils are eaten by birds such as the rock ptarmigan.

bitis nasicornis.name: Rhinoceros viper
bitis nasicornis.desc: A forest viper recorded in the Nimba circle. GloBI records it eating the striped grass mouse.

bitis peringueyi.name: Peringuey's adder
bitis peringueyi.desc: A small sidewinding viper that buries itself in sand and ambushes lizards. Dune lizards with high water content help it get water.

bivalves and polychaetes.name: Bottom clams & worms
bivalves and polychaetes.desc: Seafloor dwellers that feed on plankton and detritus. Summer low-oxygen zones kill them, which removes a key food source for blue crabs.

bivalvia.name: Seafloor clams
bivalvia.desc: Bottom-living clams and other bivalves. Pacific walruses prefer them, and benthic invertebrates make up most of the walrus diet.

black sea rain.name: Black Sea rain
black sea rain.desc: Moist air from the Black Sea coast waters the northern slopes and supports their forests.

blackwater and rain.name: Blackwater and rain
blackwater and rain.desc: The swamp depends on rainfall, and decaying plants stain the water tea-coloured. The Suwannee and St. Marys rivers drain it.

blarina brevicauda.name: Northern short-tailed shrew
blarina brevicauda.desc: Northern short-tailed shrew (Blarina brevicauda): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

blastocerus dichotomus.name: Marsh deer
blastocerus dichotomus.desc: South America's largest deer lives only in shallow marsh. The reserve is a stronghold for this Vulnerable species, which eats mostly aquatic plants.

blephilia ciliata.name: Downy wood-mint
blephilia ciliata.desc: Downy wood-mint (Blephilia ciliata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

boa constrictor.name: Boa constrictor
boa constrictor.desc: Ambushes agoutis, birds and small mammals.

boa imperator.name: Boa constrictor
boa imperator.desc: A constricting snake. GloBI records it eating fruit bats, agoutis, black iguanas and gray foxes.

bocconia frutescens.name: Parrot weed
bocconia frutescens.desc: A fast-growing shrub of forest openings whose seeds are eaten by small birds.

boisea trivittata.name: Boxelder Bug
boisea trivittata.desc: Boxelder Bug (Boisea trivittata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 91 times near the park in GBIF.

bolbometopon muricatum.name: Bumphead parrotfish
bolbometopon muricatum.desc: A large reef fish that scrapes and crunches live coral and algae; its feeding produces coral sand and clears space on the reef.

bolboschoenus maritimus.name: Sea Club-rush
bolboschoenus maritimus.desc: Sea Club-rush (Bolboschoenus maritimus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

boleophthalmus boddarti.name: Mudskipper
boleophthalmus boddarti.desc: Fish that crawls over mudflats at low tide scraping green algae, and is also found in Kuwait Sulaibikhat Bay.

boloria selene.name: Small Pearl-bordered Fritillary
boloria selene.desc: Small Pearl-bordered Fritillary (Boloria selene): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus.name: Bumble bees
bombus.desc: Many bumble bee species are recorded in the park. They feed on nectar and pollen from fireweed and other wildflowers.

bombus affinis.name: Rusty-patched Bumble Bee
bombus affinis.desc: Rusty-patched Bumble Bee (Bombus affinis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus auricomus.name: Black And Gold Bumble Bee
bombus auricomus.desc: Black And Gold Bumble Bee (Bombus auricomus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus bifarius.name: Black-notched Bumble Bee
bombus bifarius.desc: Black-notched Bumble Bee (Bombus bifarius): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 90 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus bimaculatus.name: Two-spotted Bumble Bee
