bombus bimaculatus.desc: Two-spotted Bumble Bee (Bombus bimaculatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 57 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus borealis.name: Northern Amber Bumble Bee
bombus borealis.desc: Northern Amber Bumble Bee (Bombus borealis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 135 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus centralis.name: Central Bumble Bee
bombus centralis.desc: Central Bumble Bee (Bombus centralis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus crotchii.name: Crotch Bumble Bee
bombus crotchii.desc: Crotch Bumble Bee (Bombus crotchii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus fervidus.name: Yellow Bumble Bee
bombus fervidus.desc: Yellow Bumble Bee (Bombus fervidus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus festivus.name: Festive bumble bee
bombus festivus.desc: A bumble bee recorded often in the area. It collects nectar and pollen from mountain flowers.

bombus flavifrons.name: Yellow Head Bumble Bee
bombus flavifrons.desc: Yellow Head Bumble Bee (Bombus flavifrons): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus fraternus.name: Southern Plains Bumble Bee
bombus fraternus.desc: Southern Plains Bumble Bee (Bombus fraternus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus griseocollis.name: Brown-belted Bumble Bee
bombus griseocollis.desc: Brown-belted Bumble Bee (Bombus griseocollis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus huntii.name: Hunt Bumble Bee
bombus huntii.desc: A bumble bee that gathers nectar and pollen from mountain wildflowers, and is a pollinator.

bombus impatiens.name: Common Eastern Bumble Bee
bombus impatiens.desc: Common Eastern Bumble Bee (Bombus impatiens): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 112 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus melanopygus.name: Black Tail Bumble Bee
bombus melanopygus.desc: Black Tail Bumble Bee (Bombus melanopygus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus mixtus.name: Fuzzy-horned Bumble Bee
bombus mixtus.desc: Fuzzy-horned Bumble Bee (Bombus mixtus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus nevadensis.name: Nevada Bumble Bee
bombus nevadensis.desc: Nevada Bumble Bee (Bombus nevadensis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus occidentalis.name: Western Bumble Bee
bombus occidentalis.desc: Western Bumble Bee (Bombus occidentalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus pascuorum.name: Common carder bee
bombus pascuorum.desc: A bumblebee that feeds on nectar and pollen from many flowers, including bird's-foot-trefoil and devil's-bit scabious.

bombus pensylvanicus.name: Bumble bee
bombus pensylvanicus.desc: Bumble bee (Bombus pensylvanicus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus rufocinctus.name: Red-belted bumble bee
bombus rufocinctus.desc: Red-belted bumble bee (Bombus rufocinctus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 53 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus sandersoni.name: Sanderson Bumble Bee
bombus sandersoni.desc: Sanderson Bumble Bee (Bombus sandersoni): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus sylvicola.name: Forest Bumble Bee
bombus sylvicola.desc: Forest Bumble Bee (Bombus sylvicola): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus ternarius.name: Tri-colored Bumble Bee
bombus ternarius.desc: Tri-colored bumble bee (Bombus ternarius): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus terricola.name: Yellow-banded bumble bee
bombus terricola.desc: Collects nectar and pollen from forest and meadow flowers such as raspberry, fireweed and yarrow.

bombus vagans.name: Half-black Bumble Bee
bombus vagans.desc: Half-black Bumble Bee (Bombus vagans): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus vosnesenskii.name: Vosnesensky Bumble Bee
bombus vosnesenskii.desc: A bumble bee recorded often on the islands; it feeds on nectar and pollen of scrub flowers.

bombycilla cedrorum.name: Cedar Waxwing
bombycilla cedrorum.desc: Cedar Waxwing (Bombycilla cedrorum): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

borassus flabellifer.name: Lontar palm
borassus flabellifer.desc: The palm that gives the dry savanna its scattered skyline. Its fallen fruit feed ground-dwelling animals.

boreal forest soil.name: Boreal forest soil
boreal forest soil.desc: Mostly acidic, thin soils under pine and spruce; the park also has herb-rich patches on more nutrient-rich ground.

boreogadus saida.name: Arctic cod
boreogadus saida.desc: A small fish that links copepods to seals, whales and seabirds.

borrichia frutescens.name: Bushy seaoxeye
borrichia frutescens.desc: Bushy seaoxeye (Borrichia frutescens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 39 times near the park in GBIF.

bos gaurus.name: Gaur (seladang)
bos gaurus.desc: Massive wild ox of Peninsular Malaysia that eats grasses and browse and is a main prey of the Malayan tiger.

bos grunniens.name: Yak
bos grunniens.desc: Grazing livestock herded in the high valleys, which overlap heavily with wild herbivores for pasture.

bos javanicus.name: Banteng
bos javanicus.desc: Wild cattle that compete with rhinos for feeding grounds in the park. Recorded prey of leopards and dholes.

bos taurus.name: Cow
bos taurus.desc: Dark, semi-wild cattle that roam the marshes under the care of gardians and supply the bulls for the local bull-running tradition.

boselaphus tragocamelus.name: Nilgai
boselaphus tragocamelus.desc: Asia's largest antelope. Records show tigers, leopards and striped hyenas feeding on it.

boswellia elongata.name: Socotra frankincense
boswellia elongata.desc: A resin tree found only on Socotra, growing in dry forest and shrubland. It is listed as Endangered.

bothrops asper.name: Terciopelo
bothrops asper.desc: A large pit viper that ambushes rodents and lizards on the forest floor.

bothrops atrox.name: Fer-de-lance
bothrops atrox.desc: A venomous pit viper of lowland forest. GloBI records it eating the lizard Kentropyx calcarata.

bothrops jararaca.name: Jararaca
bothrops jararaca.desc: A venomous pit viper of the Atlantic Forest, ambushing small mammals and frogs. It is the most recorded snake in the area.

botrychium matricariifolium.name: Matricary Grapefern
botrychium matricariifolium.desc: Matricary Grapefern (Botrychium matricariifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

botrychium michiganense.name: Michigan moonwort
botrychium michiganense.desc: Michigan moonwort (Botrychium michiganense): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

bottom-water oxygen.name: Bottom-water oxygen
bottom-water oxygen.desc: In summer the layered water traps oxygen-poor water near the bottom, where dissolved oxygen can drop to near zero.

bourreria succulenta.name: Pigeon berry
bourreria succulenta.desc: A coastal scrub shrub with fruit. GloBI records show white-crowned pigeons eating its fruit.

bouteloua.name: Desert grasses
bouteloua.desc: Grama grasses of the grasslands on the park's igneous and limestone soils and along the river. Their seeds and leaves feed rodents, doves, rabbits and deer.

bouteloua eriopoda.name: Woolly foot grama
bouteloua eriopoda.desc: Woolly foot grama (Bouteloua eriopoda): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 133 times near the park in GBIF.

bouteloua gracilis.name: Blue grama
bouteloua gracilis.desc: A short prairie grass that prairie dogs eat in spring and summer.

brachyteles arachnoides.name: Southern muriqui
brachyteles arachnoides.desc: The largest primate in the Americas, eating mainly fruit plus leaves and flowers. Wikipedia says it has a major role in seed dispersal.

brachyura.name: Crabs
brachyura.desc: Crabs of mudflats and mangroves feed on algae, leaf litter and dead matter and are prey for waders, fish and herons.

brackish coastal water.name: Brackish coastal water
brackish coastal water.desc: Salty water along the southern coast and lagoons supports mangroves, which tolerate salt.

brackish lagoon water.name: Brackish lagoon water
brackish lagoon water.desc: A shallow, low-salinity lagoon cut off from the Adriatic by a sand strip, rich in algae and dense aquatic plants.

bradypus variegatus.name: Brown-throated sloth
bradypus variegatus.desc: Moves slowly through the canopy browsing leaves, and comes down about once a week.

brahmaputra floods.name: Brahmaputra floods
brahmaputra floods.desc: Floods can cover most of the park for days, drive animals to higher ground and leave fresh silt and new grass behind.

braided channels & sandbars.name: Braided channels & sandbars
braided channels & sandbars.desc: The broad, shallow, braided river with shifting sandbars is the open roosting habitat cranes use at night.

branta bernicla.name: Brant goose
branta bernicla.desc: A small sea goose whose winter diet centres on eelgrass, with sea lettuce and marsh plants as alternatives.

branta canadensis.name: Canada goose
branta canadensis.desc: Canada goose (Branta canadensis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 145 times near the park in GBIF.

branta leucopsis.name: Barnacle goose
branta leucopsis.desc: Breeds in Svalbard and winters on the Solway Firth. Goslings leap from cliff nests and often fall to Arctic foxes.

branta sandvicensis.name: Nēnē (Hawaiian goose)
branta sandvicensis.desc: An endangered goose that eats leaves, seeds and fruit of grasses and shrubs. It died out in the park and was reintroduced in 1962.

brephidium exilis.name: Western pygmy blue butterfly
brephidium exilis.desc: Western pygmy blue butterfly (Brephidium exilis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

brevoortia patronus.name: Gulf menhaden
brevoortia patronus.desc: A filter feeder. Wikipedia says juveniles eat mainly phytoplankton and adults mainly zooplankton. A major forage fish for the Gulf.

brevoortia tyrannus.name: Atlantic menhaden
brevoortia tyrannus.desc: A schooling filter feeder that strains plankton from the water. Striped bass, bluefish, ospreys, eagles and dolphins all eat it.

bridelia ferruginea.name: Bridelia
bridelia ferruginea.desc: A common savanna woodland tree whose fruit and leaves are eaten by duikers, baboons, warthogs and kob in GloBI records.

bromeliaceae.name: Bromeliads
bromeliaceae.desc: Cloud-forest plants growing on trees and slopes. Their leaf hearts are a main food of the spectacled bear.

bromus inermis.name: Hungarian Brome
bromus inermis.desc: Hungarian Brome (Bromus inermis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

bronchocela cristatella.name: Green crested lizard
bronchocela cristatella.desc: A slender tree lizard that hunts insects among the foliage and is in turn eaten by birds and snakes.

brosimum alicastrum.name: Ramon (breadnut)
brosimum alicastrum.desc: One of the dominant trees of the Maya forest. Its fruits and seeds feed many animals, and birds and bats help spread the seeds.

brosimum lactescens.name: Milk tree
brosimum lactescens.desc: A lowland forest tree whose fruit is recorded in GloBI as food for many birds and monkeys here, from macaws to woolly and howler monkeys.

broussonetia papyrifera.name: Wauke
broussonetia papyrifera.desc: Wauke (Broussonetia papyrifera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 37 times near the park in GBIF.

brunnichia ovata.name: American buckwheat vine
brunnichia ovata.desc: American buckwheat vine (Brunnichia ovata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

bryophyta.name: Mosses
bryophyta.desc: Mosses, with algae and bacteria, give tufa a surface to build on. They help trigger the limestone deposits that form the barriers.

bryophyta, polypodiopsida.name: Mosses and ferns
bryophyta, polypodiopsida.desc: Mosses coat trunks and branches and ferns carpet the floor in the damp understory.

bubalus arnee.name: Wild water buffalo
bubalus arnee.desc: Grazes grasses and sedges in wet grasslands and swamps. Adults are preyed on by tigers.

bubalus bubalis.name: Feral water buffalo
bubalus bubalis.desc: Introduced grazer that damaged floodplains and wetlands before most were removed. Carcasses feed kites and crows, and crocodiles also take buffalo.

bubo ascalaphus.name: Pharaoh eagle-owl
bubo ascalaphus.desc: A large nocturnal owl that hunts small desert mammals and has been recorded taking fennec fox pups.

bubo blakistoni.name: Blakiston's fish owl
bubo blakistoni.desc: A very large owl of old riverside forest that hunts fish, including salmon, plus frogs and small mammals. It needs rivers that stay partly unfrozen in winter.

bubo scandiacus.name: Snowy owl
bubo scandiacus.desc: Hunts lemmings by day and lays more eggs in years when lemmings are plentiful.

bubo virginianus.name: Great horned owl
bubo virginianus.desc: Named among the reserve's wildlife. A night hunter of small mammals such as mice.

buceros bicornis.name: Great hornbill
buceros bicornis.desc: Eats mostly fruit, especially figs, and gets its water from fruit. Also catches small animals. A seed disperser for many forest trees.

buceros rhinoceros.name: Rhinoceros hornbill
buceros rhinoceros.desc: A large forest hornbill whose diet is mostly fruit, plus insects, small reptiles and rodents. GloBI records show it eating figs.

buchnera americana.name: American bluehearts
buchnera americana.desc: American bluehearts (Buchnera americana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 23 times near the park in GBIF.

budorcas taxicolor.name: Sichuan takin
budorcas taxicolor.desc: A heavy goat-antelope that browses leaves and grasses and eats bamboo shoots and flowers. It retreats into thick bamboo when alarmed.

bufo bufo.name: Common toad
bufo bufo.desc: An amphibian that spends most of the year on land eating beetles and other invertebrates.

bulbostylis capillaris.name: Densetuft Hairsedge
bulbostylis capillaris.desc: Densetuft Hairsedge (Bulbostylis capillaris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

burkea africana.name: Burkea
burkea africana.desc: One of the characteristic trees of the park woodland, and a species elephants injure often.

burnsius communis.name: Common Checkered Skipper
burnsius communis.desc: Common Checkered Skipper (Burnsius communis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

bursera simaruba.name: Gumbo-limbo
bursera simaruba.desc: Gumbo-limbo is a typical tree of the dry to moist forest that covers the island hills. Deer and iguanas browse such foliage.

buteo augur.name: Augur buzzard
buteo augur.desc: A raptor commonly recorded on the plateau. It mainly eats small ground mammals such as rats and mole-rats, and reptiles.

buteo buteo.name: Common buzzard
buteo buteo.desc: A raptor of forest edges and meadows that hunts rodents and other small animals.

buteo galapagoensis.name: Galápagos hawk
buteo galapagoensis.desc: The islands' top land predator. It eats insects, lizards, rodents, small birds and young iguanas and tortoises, and scavenges carrion.

buteo jamaicensis.name: Red-tailed hawk
buteo jamaicensis.desc: Red-tailed Hawk (Buteo jamaicensis): a top predator in this web. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

buteo japonicus.name: Eastern buzzard
buteo japonicus.desc: Bird of prey, the top flying predator on the islands, taking lizards, rodents and seabirds.

buteo oreophilus.name: Mountain buzzard
buteo oreophilus.desc: A raptor of montane forest, listed for Kibira; it hunts small mammals, reptiles and insects from perches.

buteo platypterus.name: Broad-winged Hawk
buteo platypterus.desc: Broad-winged Hawk (Buteo platypterus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 622 times near the park in GBIF.

buteo platypterus brunnescens.name: Puerto Rican broad-winged hawk
buteo platypterus brunnescens.desc: A rare forest hawk found in El Yunque's tabonuco forest. Raptors including hawks are listed among natural predators of the parrot.

buteo ridgwayi.name: Ridgway's hawk
buteo ridgwayi.desc: A critically endangered Hispaniolan raptor that takes mostly reptiles, plus birds, bats, rodents and frogs. The park holds one of its few surviving wild populations.

buteo rufinus.name: Long-legged buzzard
buteo rufinus.desc: A steppe buzzard that takes mainly rodents and ground squirrels, plus many reptiles, birds and insects.

buteo rufofuscus.name: Jackal buzzard
buteo rufofuscus.desc: A mountain raptor that hunts small mammals, snakes and lizards, and eats carrion outside the breeding season.

buteo socotraensis.name: Socotra buzzard
buteo socotraensis.desc: An island-only buzzard that nests on cliffs and hunts mainly reptiles and large invertebrates.

buteo solitarius.name: ʻIo (Hawaiian hawk)
buteo solitarius.desc: Endemic hawk that breeds only on the Big Island, in ʻōhiʻa forest. It now eats rats, lizards, game birds and insects, hunting mostly from a perch.

buteo swainsoni.name: Swainson's Hawk
buteo swainsoni.desc: Swainson's Hawk (Buteo swainsoni): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1,608 times near the park in GBIF.

buteogallus meridionalis.name: Savanna hawk
buteogallus meridionalis.desc: A hawk of open country that hunts reptiles, small mammals and other prey from perches.

butomus umbellatus.name: Flowering-rush
butomus umbellatus.desc: Flowering-rush (Butomus umbellatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 59 times near the park in GBIF.

bycanistes fistulator.name: Piping hornbill
bycanistes fistulator.desc: A noisy canopy hornbill, among the best-recorded birds around the park, that mainly eats forest fruit.

caenurgia chloropha.name: Vetch Looper Moth
caenurgia chloropha.desc: Vetch Looper Moth (Caenurgia chloropha): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

caesio.name: Fusiliers
caesio.desc: Schooling fish that feed on zooplankton in the water above the reef, and are prey for larger predators.

caiman crocodilus.name: Spectacled caiman
caiman crocodilus.desc: Caiman of calm waters in Trinidad and Tobago; adults take fish, crabs and snails, birds and mammals.

caiman yacare.name: Yacare caiman
caiman yacare.desc: A semi-aquatic reptile of lakes and wetlands. It eats mainly snails and fish, sometimes larger prey such as capybara, and is itself taken by jaguars.

cakile edentula.name: American searocket
cakile edentula.desc: American searocket (Cakile edentula): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

cakile maritima.name: Sea rocket
cakile maritima.desc: A salt-tolerant pioneer plant of beaches and foredunes, recorded near Cabo Polonio.

calamagrostis canadensis.name: Bluejoint reedgrass
calamagrostis canadensis.desc: A tall moist-ground grass recorded in the park area; a grazing food for bison.

calamus.name: Rattan palms
calamus.desc: Climbing palms of the forest understory. Wikipedia lists rattan among the park plants that are overharvested.

calanoides and relatives.name: Copepods
calanoides and relatives.desc: Small crustacean grazers of phytoplankton. Krill also eat them.

calanus finmarchicus.name: Copepods
calanus finmarchicus.desc: Small crustaceans that graze phytoplankton in the Gulf of Maine and are food for herring.

calanus glacialis.name: Arctic copepods
calanus glacialis.desc: Rich in fat, they link the algae bloom to fish, seabirds and whales.

calcarius lapponicus.name: Lapland longspur
calcarius lapponicus.desc: A tundra songbird that eats seeds and plants and, in summer, insects. A very commonly recorded bird here.

calidris alpina.name: Dunlin
calidris alpina.desc: Small wintering shorebird that probes mudflats in flocks for molluscs, worms and crustaceans.

calidris canutus.name: Red knot
calidris canutus.desc: Probes for buried shellfish and swallows them whole. It breeds on Arctic tundra and stops over on coastal mudflats such as the Wadden Sea.

callicarpa americana.name: American beauty-berry
callicarpa americana.desc: A shrub with bright purple berries that birds and mammals eat in autumn.

calligonum.name: Calligonum shrubs
calligonum.desc: Sand-loving shrubs with thin, nearly leafless stems that grow on dunes of the Karakum.

callinectes sapidus.name: Blue crab
callinectes sapidus.desc: An omnivore that eats clams, mussels, oysters, worms, small fish and eelgrass, and also scavenges. Striped bass are among its predators.

calliopsis andreniformis.name: Eastern Miner Bee
calliopsis andreniformis.desc: Eastern Miner Bee (Calliopsis andreniformis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 167 times near the park in GBIF.

callipepla californica.name: California Quail
callipepla californica.desc: A ground-living bird that feeds on seeds, leaves and berries, and is hunted by hawks, snakes and cats.

callipepla gambelii.name: Gambel's quail
callipepla gambelii.desc: A ground bird that eats seeds, leaves and mesquite beans and is prey for hawks and snakes.

callirhoe involucrata.name: Purple poppy-mallow
callirhoe involucrata.desc: Purple poppy-mallow (Callirhoe involucrata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

callosciurus erythraeus.name: Pallas's squirrel
callosciurus erythraeus.desc: A tree squirrel of forests below about 3,000 m that eats seeds, fruit, leaves and flowers, and is regular prey of forest raptors.

callosciurus finlaysonii.name: Finlayson's squirrel
callosciurus finlaysonii.desc: A common tree squirrel. GloBI records it eating jambolan fruit and other fruit.

callosciurus prevostii.name: Prevost's squirrel
callosciurus prevostii.desc: A colourful tree squirrel that eats fruit, seeds and some insects. It is one of the most recorded mammals near the park.

callospermophilus lateralis.name: Golden-mantled ground squirrel
callospermophilus lateralis.desc: Eats seeds, plants and fungi in mountain forests and meadows, and is prey for eagles and carnivores.

calluna vulgaris.name: Heather
calluna vulgaris.desc: A low evergreen shrub of mountain heaths, eaten by deer and chamois.

calocedrus decurrens.name: Californian Incense-cedar
calocedrus decurrens.desc: Californian Incense-cedar (Calocedrus decurrens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 226 times near the park in GBIF.

calocedrus macrolepis.name: Calocedrus (cypress) forest
calocedrus macrolepis.desc: A stand of these conifers covers about 50 km2 of the park on limestone, and Wikipedia says most of the trees are thought to be 500 to 600 years old.

calochortus gunnisonii.name: Gunnison's mariposa lily
calochortus gunnisonii.desc: Gunnison's mariposa lily (Calochortus gunnisonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

calochortus lyallii.name: Lyall's mariposa lily
calochortus lyallii.desc: Lyall's mariposa lily (Calochortus lyallii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 90 times near the park in GBIF.

calochortus macrocarpus.name: Greenband mariposa lily
calochortus macrocarpus.desc: Greenband mariposa lily (Calochortus macrocarpus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

calochortus nuttallii.name: Sego-lily
calochortus nuttallii.desc: Sego-lily (Calochortus nuttallii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

calochortus tolmiei.name: WHITE PUSSY EARS
calochortus tolmiei.desc: WHITE PUSSY EARS (Calochortus tolmiei): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 73 times near the park in GBIF.

calopogon tuberosus.name: Tuberous grasspink
calopogon tuberosus.desc: Tuberous grasspink (Calopogon tuberosus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 73 times near the park in GBIF.

calotes calotes.name: Green forest lizard
calotes calotes.desc: A common agamid lizard of the wet zone that feeds on insects.

calotes versicolor.name: Variable agama
calotes versicolor.desc: An insect-eating lizard of forest edges and gardens. Birds and snakes prey on it.

calypte costae.name: Costa's Hummingbird
calypte costae.desc: Costa's Hummingbird (Calypte costae): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 88 times near the park in GBIF.

cambaridae and orconectes spp..name: Crayfish
cambaridae and orconectes spp..desc: Scavenging omnivores of stream bottoms. The MDC says crayfish are the main food of Ozark hellbenders and are eaten by smallmouth bass.

camelus dromedarius.name: Dromedary
camelus dromedarius.desc: Domestic camels graze and browse coastal shrubs and mangroves along the Arabian coast; a few records fall in the circle.

camelus ferus.name: Wild Bactrian camel
camelus ferus.desc: A critically endangered camel of the Gobi that survives on sparse desert plants and can drink salty water.

camnula pellucida.name: Clear-winged Grasshopper
camnula pellucida.desc: Clear-winged Grasshopper (Camnula pellucida): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

campanula rotundifolia.name: Harebell
campanula rotundifolia.desc: Harebell (Campanula rotundifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

campanulastrum americanum.name: American bellflower
campanulastrum americanum.desc: American bellflower (Campanulastrum americanum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

campephilus magellanicus.name: Magellanic woodpecker
campephilus magellanicus.desc: A big woodpecker of mature southern beech forest that eats mainly wood-boring grubs and beetles, plus spiders.

canal freshwater.name: Canal freshwater
canal freshwater.desc: Canals that drain the Everglades send fresh water, sediment and pollutants into the bay and shift its salinity.

canbya aurea.name: Golden pygmypoppy
canbya aurea.desc: Golden pygmypoppy (Canbya aurea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

candoia bibroni.name: Pacific boa
candoia bibroni.desc: A forest snake recorded on Espiritu Santo that eats birds, lizards, rodents and bats; the island has no native land mammal predators.

canis adustus.name: Side-striped jackal
canis adustus.desc: An omnivorous canid that takes small prey, fruit and carrion. It is present in the park.

canis aureus.name: Golden jackal
canis aureus.desc: An opportunistic hunter and scavenger, recorded eating deer and wild boar.

canis dingo.name: Dingo
canis dingo.desc: Top land predator that hunts wallabies, rodents, birds and young buffalo. Dingo predation is a major cause of quoll losses.

canis familiaris.name: Highland wild dog
canis familiaris.desc: Wild dogs live near the base of Puncak Jaya at roughly 3,900 to 4,200 m. New Guinea wild dogs eat marsupials, rodents, birds and fruit, and are said to steal eagle kills.

canis latrans.name: Coyote
canis latrans.desc: Coyote (Canis latrans): a top predator in this web. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

canis lupaster.name: African golden wolf
canis lupaster.desc: A generalist canid that eats rodents, hares and carrion. Ethiopian wolves usually win encounters with it, though it is not a rodent specialist.

canis lupus.name: Gray wolf
canis lupus.desc: Packs hunt moose, caribou and beaver, mainly taking calves and weak animals, and sometimes hares.

canis lupus arctos.name: Arctic wolf
canis lupus arctos.desc: Follows caribou and muskox herds and hunts lemmings in summer.

canis lupus chanco.name: Himalayan wolf
canis lupus chanco.desc: Hunts bharal and marmots, and takes livestock where herds overlap its range.

canis simensis.name: Ethiopian wolf
canis simensis.desc: Rodent specialist. In Bale it hunts mostly big-headed mole-rats. Bale holds the largest population of this endangered canid.

cannabis sativa.name: Hemp
cannabis sativa.desc: Hemp (Cannabis sativa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

canyon soil and sediment.name: Canyon soil and sediment
canyon soil and sediment.desc: Thin sandy soils and river-borne sediment give plants a place to root across the canyon floor and mesas.

canyon springs.name: Canyon springs
canyon springs.desc: The range is mostly limestone with little surface water, so seeps, springs and McKittrick Creek sustain the canyon trees.

cap blanc upwelling.name: Cap Blanc upwelling
cap blanc upwelling.desc: Permanent upwelling at Cap Blanc brings nutrients that help make these waters among the richest fishing grounds in the region.

capra aegagrus.name: Bezoar ibex
capra aegagrus.desc: A wild goat of rocky mountain slopes that feeds on plants. It is a main prey of the big cats and wolves of the region.

capra caucasica.name: West Caucasian tur
capra caucasica.desc: A wild goat found only in the western half of the Caucasus, living on steep, rocky mountain slopes and meadows.

capra hircus.name: Feral goat
capra hircus.desc: Introduced goats strip vegetation and compete with tortoises for grazing. They were removed from Santiago by 2006.

capra ibex.name: Alpine ibex
capra ibex.desc: A steep-ground grazer living mostly between 1,800 and 3,300 m. It was nearly wiped out by hunting and has been restored by reintroductions.

capra nubiana.name: Nubian ibex
capra nubiana.desc: A cliff-dwelling wild goat that eats grasses and acacia leaves. Captive breeding and reintroduction rebuilt its Jordan population, and Dana is a stronghold.

capra pyrenaica.name: Spanish ibex
capra pyrenaica.desc: Wild goat that returned to the mountains after the Gerês ibex died out in the 1890s; about 100 animals by 2011.

capra sibirica.name: Siberian ibex
capra sibirica.desc: A wild goat of steep rocky slopes that eats grasses and herbs, and twigs and needles in winter. Snow leopards and wolves prey on it.

capra walie.name: Walia ibex
capra walie.desc: An endemic wild goat of steep cliffs that browses shrubs, herbs, lichens and grasses; Simien is its main stronghold.

capreolus capreolus.name: European roe deer
capreolus capreolus.desc: A small browsing deer that eats shoots and leaves of oak, spruce and bilberry. It is a favoured prey of lynx where common.

capreolus pygargus.name: Siberian roe deer
capreolus pygargus.desc: A small deer of forest-steppe that browses herbs and woody shoots; wolves and snow leopards prey on it.

capricornis sumatraensis.name: Mainland serow
capricornis sumatraensis.desc: A goat-antelope of steep, rocky forest that browses leaves and herbs. Wikipedia lists it in the park, and bears are reported to kill serow.

capricornis swinhoei.name: Formosan serow
capricornis swinhoei.desc: A goat-antelope of steep rock and forest that eats leaves, vines, ferns and ground herbs, and licks minerals from cliffs.

capromys pilorides.name: Desmarest's hutia
capromys pilorides.desc: Large tree-dwelling rodent eating mostly bark, leaves and fruit. Common where mangroves are abundant and a key prey item.

caracal aurata.name: African golden cat
caracal aurata.desc: A forest cat that hunts tree hyraxes and rodents, and also takes birds, small monkeys and duikers.

caracal caracal.name: Caracal
caracal caracal.desc: A medium-sized cat that hunts hyraxes, rodents and mongooses. GloBI records it with many species from this site.

caracara plancus.name: Southern caracara
caracara plancus.desc: A bold raptor and scavenger of open country. GloBI records it eating hares, birds and carrion.

caranx ignobilis.name: Giant trevally
caranx ignobilis.desc: Patrols the reef edge, hunting fish in groups.

carcharhinus amblyrhynchos.name: Grey reef shark
carcharhinus amblyrhynchos.desc: A reef shark that hunts reef fish. The lagoons hold healthy populations of top predators.

carcharhinus galapagensis.name: Galápagos shark
carcharhinus galapagensis.desc: A large reef shark of the islands. It eats fish and is among the sharks that hunt sea lions and occasionally marine iguanas.

carcharhinus leucas.name: Bull shark
carcharhinus leucas.desc: A coastal shark that enters estuaries and river mouths and eats fish and dolphins.

carcharhinus limbatus.name: Blacktip shark
carcharhinus limbatus.desc: Coastal shark that hunts schooling fish such as mullet and sardines. Sharks and rays in the park are under heavy fishing pressure.

carcharhinus melanopterus.name: Blacktip reef shark
carcharhinus melanopterus.desc: A shallow reef shark that eats small bony fish, squid and crabs.

carcharhinus perezi.name: Caribbean reef shark
carcharhinus perezi.desc: Top reef predator of bony fishes and rays. Overfishing has reduced its numbers off Belize.

carcharodon carcharias.name: Great white shark
carcharodon carcharias.desc: Preys mainly on seals and sea lions off California. Bites sea otters often but usually does not eat them.

carcinus maenas.name: Shore crab
carcinus maenas.desc: An omnivore that eats bivalves, worms, small crustaceans and eelgrass seeds. It will also eat other crabs.

cardamine concatenata.name: Cut-leaf toothcup
cardamine concatenata.desc: Cut-leaf toothcup (Cardamine concatenata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

cardinalis cardinalis.name: Northern Cardinal
cardinalis cardinalis.desc: Northern Cardinal (Cardinalis cardinalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 79 times near the park in GBIF.

cardisoma carnifex.name: Land crabs
cardisoma carnifex.desc: Burrowing crabs of the mangrove and scrub fringe that eat leaf litter. They also prey on young tortoises.

caretta caretta.name: Loggerhead sea turtle
caretta caretta.desc: Yakushima is the largest nesting ground for loggerheads in the North Pacific. Adults eat jellyfish and shellfish; eggs and hatchlings are eaten by crabs, crows and raccoon dogs.

carex.name: Sedges
carex.desc: Grass-like plants of meadows and coastal flats. Wikipedia lists sedges among the main foods of brown bears.

carex albicans.name: Whitetinge Sedge
carex albicans.desc: Whitetinge Sedge (Carex albicans): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

carex and salix arctica.name: Sedges & dwarf willow
carex and salix arctica.desc: Low tundra plants that grow quickly during the short summer.

carex aquatilis.name: Sedges
carex aquatilis.desc: Grass-like plants that form much of the tundra and wet meadow cover. GloBI records caribou eating water sedge.

carex arkansana.name: Arkansas sedge
carex arkansana.desc: Arkansas sedge (Carex arkansana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

carex atrata.name: Alpine sedges and herbs
carex atrata.desc: Sedges and flowering herbs grow in the high meadows and tundra above the trees and feed grazers and seed eaters.

carex aureolensis.name: Broad-scaled sedge
carex aureolensis.desc: Broad-scaled sedge (Carex aureolensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

carex bicolor.name: Bicoloured sedge
carex bicolor.desc: Small sedge of damp ground near meltwater and snowbeds. GloBI records roe deer and red deer feeding on it.

carex bigelowii.name: Bigelow's sedge
carex bigelowii.desc: A common tundra sedge. Sedges and grasses are the main summer forage for the island's grazing animals.

carex canescens.name: White Sedge
carex canescens.desc: White Sedge (Carex canescens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

carex concinna.name: Low northern sedge
carex concinna.desc: A grass-like sedge of open ground, eaten by Dall sheep and ground squirrels.

carex deasyi.name: Deasy's sedge
carex deasyi.desc: A sedge among the most recorded plants near the plateau. Sedges are staple food for marmots and ibex in the alpine meadows.

carex duriuscula.name: Needleleaf sedge
carex duriuscula.desc: Needleleaf sedge (Carex duriuscula): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

carex fissa.name: Hammock sedge
carex fissa.desc: Hammock sedge (Carex fissa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

carex grayi.name: Gray's Sedge
carex grayi.desc: Gray's Sedge (Carex grayi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

carex interior.name: Inland Sedge
carex interior.desc: Inland Sedge (Carex interior): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

carex laeviconica.name: Smooth-cone sedge
carex laeviconica.desc: Smooth-cone sedge (Carex laeviconica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

carex microptera.name: Ovalhead sedge
carex microptera.desc: Ovalhead sedge (Carex microptera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

carex molesta.name: Field oval sedge
carex molesta.desc: Field oval sedge (Carex molesta): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

carex pachystachya.name: Chamisso sedge
carex pachystachya.desc: Chamisso sedge (Carex pachystachya): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

carex pellita.name: Woolly sedge
carex pellita.desc: Woolly sedge (Carex pellita): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

carex pensylvanica.name: Pennsylvania Sedge
carex pensylvanica.desc: Pennsylvania Sedge (Carex pensylvanica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

carex praegracilis.name: Clustered field sedge
carex praegracilis.desc: Clustered field sedge (Carex praegracilis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

carex retrorsa.name: Knotsheath sedge
carex retrorsa.desc: Knotsheath sedge (Carex retrorsa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

carex scabrata.name: Eastern rough sedge
carex scabrata.desc: Eastern rough sedge (Carex scabrata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

carex tribuloides.name: Blunt broom sedge
carex tribuloides.desc: Blunt broom sedge (Carex tribuloides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

carex trichocarpa.name: Hairy-fruit sedge
carex trichocarpa.desc: Hairy-fruit sedge (Carex trichocarpa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

carex utriculata.name: Northwest Territory sedge
carex utriculata.desc: Northwest Territory sedge (Carex utriculata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

cariama cristata.name: Red-legged seriema
cariama cristata.desc: A grassland bird that eats arthropods such as ants, grasshoppers and beetles, plus lizards, snakes and small mammals. Common in the Cerrado.

carlia bicarinata.name: Rainbow skink
carlia bicarinata.desc: A small skink recorded often in the area and endemic to Papua New Guinea. Small lizards like this are prey for kookaburras, pythons and monitors.

carnegiea gigantea.name: Saguaro
carnegiea gigantea.desc: The park's namesake giant cactus. It stores rainwater, flowers feed bats, bees and birds, and its fruit feeds doves; woodpecker holes become homes for other birds.

carollia perspicillata.name: Seba's short-tailed bat
carollia perspicillata.desc: The most recorded mammal in the GBIF data near the park. It eats fruit and helps spread seeds.

carpinus betulus.name: Hornbeam
carpinus betulus.desc: A common broadleaf tree of the mixed forest, recorded often in the area. Its shoots and bark are browsed by deer and bison.

caryota urens.name: Jaggery palm
caryota urens.desc: A fishtail palm recorded in the reserve; local people tap its sap, and its fruit and flowers feed forest animals.

caspian moisture and rain.name: Caspian moisture and rain
caspian moisture and rain.desc: The Alborz range catches moist air from the Caspian Sea, giving the northern slopes far more rain than the dry country to the south.

cassiope tetragona.name: Arctic bell-heather
cassiope tetragona.desc: A small evergreen heath shrub of tundra. GloBI records Arctic hares feeding on it.

castanea dentata.name: American chestnut
castanea dentata.desc: Once a major forest tree, nearly wiped out by chestnut blight in the 1930s. It still sprouts from old roots but usually dies back before maturing.

castanea ozarkensis.name: Ozark chinkapin
castanea ozarkensis.desc: Ozark chinkapin (Castanea ozarkensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

castanopsis.name: Chestnut-oaks
castanopsis.desc: Evergreen nut-bearing trees of Southeast Asian hill forest. Their nuts are a mast food for bears and other animals.

castilleja chromosa.name: Desert paintbrush
castilleja chromosa.desc: Desert paintbrush (Castilleja chromosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

castilleja coccinea.name: Scarlet Indian paintbrush
castilleja coccinea.desc: Scarlet Indian paintbrush (Castilleja coccinea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.

castilleja exserta.name: Exserted Indian paintbrush
castilleja exserta.desc: Exserted Indian paintbrush (Castilleja exserta): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

castilleja flava.name: Yellow paintbrush
castilleja flava.desc: Yellow paintbrush (Castilleja flava): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

castilleja indivisa.name: Texas paintbrush
castilleja indivisa.desc: Texas paintbrush (Castilleja indivisa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 118 times near the park in GBIF.

castilleja integra.name: Squawfeather
castilleja integra.desc: Squawfeather (Castilleja integra): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

castilleja linariifolia.name: Wyoming paintbrush
castilleja linariifolia.desc: Wyoming paintbrush (Castilleja linariifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

castor canadensis.name: American beaver
castor canadensis.desc: American beaver (Castor canadensis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

castor fiber.name: Eurasian beaver
castor fiber.desc: Gnaws trees and dams streams, creating wetlands. It feeds on bark and shoots of woody plants such as birch.

casuarius casuarius.name: Southern cassowary
casuarius casuarius.desc: Forages on the forest floor for fallen fruit and seeds, including palms, and also takes fungi, insects, snails, small animals and carrion. Listed as threatened in the park.

cataglyphis bombycina.name: Saharan silver ant
cataglyphis bombycina.desc: Dashes out for only minutes in midday heat to scavenge animals killed by the heat, and then returns to its nest.

catagonus wagneri.name: Chacoan peccary
catagonus wagneri.desc: A large wild pig of the dry Chaco that feeds heavily on cacti and other tough plants. Once thought extinct, it is now known from the Chaco.

caterpillars, beetles and others.name: Leaf-eating insects
caterpillars, beetles and others.desc: Caterpillars, beetles and other plant-feeding insects. They are the main food link between plants and insect-eating birds.

cathartes aura.name: Turkey vulture
cathartes aura.desc: Turkey Vulture (Cathartes aura): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.

catharus ustulatus.name: Swainson's Thrush
catharus ustulatus.desc: Swainson's Thrush (Catharus ustulatus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1,886 times near the park in GBIF.

catopuma temminckii.name: Asian golden cat
catopuma temminckii.desc: A medium forest cat listed among the reserve's wildlife. It takes birds and small mammals.

cavia aperea.name: Brazilian guinea pig
cavia aperea.desc: A small wild cavy of grassy ground, eaten by foxes and cats according to GloBI records.

ceanothus.name: Ceanothus
ceanothus.desc: A shrub of the mixed conifer zone that mule deer browse. Many species are adapted to regrow or germinate after fire.

ceanothus integerrimus.name: Deerbrush ceanothus
ceanothus integerrimus.desc: Deerbrush ceanothus (Ceanothus integerrimus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

ceanothus lemmonii.name: LEMMON'S CEANOTHUS
ceanothus lemmonii.desc: LEMMON'S CEANOTHUS (Ceanothus lemmonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 67 times near the park in GBIF.

ceanothus spinosus.name: Greenbark ceanothus
ceanothus spinosus.desc: Greenbark ceanothus (Ceanothus spinosus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 42 times near the park in GBIF.

cecropia.name: Cecropia & other forest trees
cecropia.desc: Forest fills the hollows and lines the rivers, supplying leaves, fruit and dead wood to sloths, tapirs, termites and bats.

cecropia pachystachya.name: Ambay pumpwood
cecropia pachystachya.desc: A fast-growing pioneer tree of forest edges and clearings. It is among the best-recorded plants near the park and is eaten by tapirs and capuchins in GloBI records.

cecropia schreberiana.name: Pumpwood (yagrumo)
cecropia schreberiana.desc: A fast-growing pioneer tree that recolonizes hurricane-damaged ground. Birds and bats eat its fruit and spread the seeds.

cecropia spp..name: Cecropia
cecropia spp..desc: A fast-growing gap tree. Sloths browse its leaves, and ants live in its hollow stems.

cedrus libani.name: Cedar of Lebanon
cedrus libani.desc: The reserve's signature conifer, forming forests on the slopes of Mount Barouk. Goat browsing on young trees hinders its natural regeneration.

ceiba pentandra.name: Kapok
ceiba pentandra.desc: One of the tallest emergent trees. Its flowers feed bats and monkeys, and its leaves feed leafcutter ants.

celtis iguanaea.name: Iguana hackberry
celtis iguanaea.desc: A hackberry shrub or tree. Its fruit is widely eaten by forest mammals and birds in GloBI records.

celtis laevigata.name: Sugar hackberry
celtis laevigata.desc: Sugar hackberry (Celtis laevigata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

celtis occidentalis.name: Hackberry
celtis occidentalis.desc: Hackberry (Celtis occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

celtis reticulata.name: Netleaf hackberry
celtis reticulata.desc: Netleaf hackberry (Celtis reticulata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 81 times near the park in GBIF.

cenchrus ciliaris.name: Buffel grass
cenchrus ciliaris.desc: Drought-tolerant bunch grass of wadis and lowland plains, grazed when rain brings new growth.

centaurea stoebe.name: Panicled Knapweed
centaurea stoebe.desc: Panicled Knapweed (Centaurea stoebe): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

centronyx henslowii.name: Henslow's sparrow
centronyx henslowii.desc: A secretive sparrow the MDC says cannot persist without big bluestem prairie. Eats insects and seeds.

centrosema virginianum.name: Spurred Butterfly Pea
centrosema virginianum.desc: Spurred Butterfly Pea (Centrosema virginianum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 29 times near the park in GBIF.

centrostephanus rodgersii.name: Long-spined sea urchin
centrostephanus rodgersii.desc: A large dark urchin that grazes algae on rocky reef. Marine park surveys found it increasing about threefold between 2006 and 2010.

cephalanthus occidentalis.name: Button-willow
cephalanthus occidentalis.desc: Button-willow (Cephalanthus occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

cephalophus dorsalis.name: Bay duiker
cephalophus dorsalis.desc: A small forest antelope that feeds on fallen fruit and leaves on the forest floor. It is prey for leopards and crowned eagles.

cephalophus niger.name: Black duiker
cephalophus niger.desc: A small forest antelope of the undergrowth that eats fallen fruit and leaves.

cephalophus nigrifrons.name: Black-fronted duiker
cephalophus nigrifrons.desc: A small forest antelope that mostly browses leaves and plant shoots, and also eats fruit.

cephalophus rufilatus.name: Red-flanked duiker
cephalophus rufilatus.desc: A small antelope of savanna woodland and forest edges that eats foliage, fallen fruit, seeds and blossoms.

cephalophus spp..name: Forest duikers
cephalophus spp..desc: Small forest antelope that eat fruit and leaves and are common prey for leopards, golden cats, eagles and apes.

cephalophus zebra.name: Zebra duiker
cephalophus zebra.desc: A small forest antelope that eats fruit, leaves and seeds and can crack hard fruit shells. It is a threatened species of the Upper Guinea forests.

cerambycidae.name: Longhorn beetles
cerambycidae.desc: Wood-boring beetle larvae chew into trunks and stems, and adults feed on nectar and fruit. Several species are recorded nearby.

cerastes cerastes.name: Horned viper
cerastes cerastes.desc: An ambush snake that buries itself in sand and strikes small rodents and lizards.

cerastes gasperettii.name: Arabian horned viper
cerastes gasperettii.desc: A sand-dwelling viper whose diet is thought to be mainly rodents, with beetles and lizards as smaller prey.

cerastoderma edule.name: Common cockle
cerastoderma edule.desc: A shallow-burrowing bivalve that filters food from the water. Red knots and oystercatchers both take it.

ceratina dupla.name: Doubled Ceratina
ceratina dupla.desc: Doubled Ceratina (Ceratina dupla): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 198 times near the park in GBIF.

ceratina mikmaqi.name: Mikmaq Small Carpenter
ceratina mikmaqi.desc: Mikmaq Small Carpenter (Ceratina mikmaqi): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 131 times near the park in GBIF.

ceratina strenua.name: Nimble Ceratina
ceratina strenua.desc: Nimble Ceratina (Ceratina strenua): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 105 times near the park in GBIF.

ceratiola ericoides.name: Florida-rosemary
ceratiola ericoides.desc: Florida-rosemary (Ceratiola ericoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

ceratogymna atrata.name: Black-casqued hornbill
ceratogymna atrata.desc: A large forest hornbill, the most recorded of the big birds near the reserve, that eats fruit and spreads seeds.

ceratogymna elata.name: Yellow-casqued hornbill
ceratogymna elata.desc: A large canopy hornbill, the most-recorded bird near Gola. It lives in family groups and is listed as Vulnerable.

ceratotherium simum.name: White rhinoceros
ceratotherium simum.desc: A heavy grazer of the short grass layer. Wikipedia lists it among the park herbivores.

cercis canadensis.name: Eastern Redbud
cercis canadensis.desc: Eastern Redbud (Cercis canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

cercocarpus intricatus.name: Dwarf mountain mahogany
cercocarpus intricatus.desc: Dwarf mountain mahogany (Cercocarpus intricatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 29 times near the park in GBIF.

cercocarpus ledifolius.name: Curl-leaf mountain-mahogany
cercocarpus ledifolius.desc: A tough evergreen shrub of dry slopes that mule deer browse, especially in winter.

cercocarpus montanus.name: Mountain mahogany
cercocarpus montanus.desc: A tough rocky-slope shrub that elk and deer browse heavily, often keeping it short.

cercocebus atys.name: Sooty mangabey
cercocebus atys.desc: A ground-and-canopy monkey of West African forest. GloBI records show it feeding on several Taï forest fruits.

cercopithecus cephus.name: Moustached guenon
cercopithecus cephus.desc: A small forest monkey that eats fruit and insects; GloBI records it feeding on Strombosia fruit near the park.

cercopithecus diana.name: Diana monkey
cercopithecus diana.desc: Eats mainly fruit, flowers and leaves in all levels of the canopy. Its predator-specific alarm calls are understood by other forest species.

cercopithecus lhoesti.name: L'Hoest's monkey
cercopithecus lhoesti.desc: A forest guenon recorded in Kibira that feeds mostly on fruit and other plant material.

cercopithecus mitis.name: Blue monkey
cercopithecus mitis.desc: A common forest monkey that eats fruit and leaves, including cherry and pittosporum fruit.

cercopithecus nictitans.name: Greater spot-nosed monkey
cercopithecus nictitans.desc: A tree-living guenon recorded near the reserve that eats mainly fruit and is hunted by eagles, leopards and chimpanzees.

cercyonis pegala.name: Common Wood-nymph
cercyonis pegala.desc: Common Wood-nymph (Cercyonis pegala): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

cerdocyon thous.name: Crab-eating fox
cerdocyon thous.desc: An opportunistic canid that eats fruit, insects and small vertebrates.

cereus hildmannianus.name: Hedge cactus
cereus hildmannianus.desc: A tall cactus of the coastal scrub whose fruit is eaten by birds and lizards.

cereus insularis.name: Noronha cactus
cereus insularis.desc: A tall columnar cactus recorded very often on the island. It copes with the dry season and provides cover and fruit.

certhia brachydactyla.name: Short-toed treecreeper
certhia brachydactyla.desc: Small bark-creeping bird recorded in large numbers; GloBI records it eating butterflies such as the large white.

cervus canadensis.name: Elk
cervus canadensis.desc: Mostly grazes native grasses but also browses shrubs. Bears and coyotes take calves, and cougars take adults.

cervus canadensis roosevelti.name: Roosevelt elk
cervus canadensis roosevelti.desc: Browses shrubs and grazes grasses, and eats conifer seedlings in winter. Olympic protected much of its range.

cervus canadensis xanthopygus.name: Manchurian wapiti
cervus canadensis xanthopygus.desc: Adapted to mixed deciduous forest. Tiger distribution has been found to follow wapiti distribution closely.

cervus elaphus.name: Elk
cervus elaphus.desc: Elk (Cervus elaphus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

cervus elaphus maral.name: Caspian red deer
cervus elaphus maral.desc: A large deer that eats grasses and leaves. The leopard is its main predator, and wolves and bears take fewer.

cervus nippon.name: Sika deer
cervus nippon.desc: Sika Deer (Cervus nippon): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 219 times near the park in GBIF.

ceryle rudis.name: Pied kingfisher
ceryle rudis.desc: A fish-eating bird that hovers over open water and dives for small fish.

cethosia cydippe.name: Eastern red lacewing
cethosia cydippe.desc: A butterfly whose caterpillars feed on passion-flower vines. GloBI records it feeding on Passiflora aurantia.

cetonia aurata.name: Rose chafer
cetonia aurata.desc: A metallic green beetle. Its larvae live in rotting wood and humus, and adults visit flowers.

chaerephon plicatus.name: Wrinkle-lipped bat
chaerephon plicatus.desc: Lives in large cave colonies and flies out to feed on night-flying insects. Its droppings enrich cave and soil nutrients.

chaetadelpha wheeleri.name: Dune wirelettuce
chaetadelpha wheeleri.desc: Dune wirelettuce (Chaetadelpha wheeleri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

chaetoceros.name: Phytoplankton
chaetoceros.desc: Microscopic algae drifting in the bay. They use sunlight and dissolved nutrients and feed the plankton, oysters and fish that fill the water.

chaetodipus baileyi.name: Bailey's pocket mouse
chaetodipus baileyi.desc: Bailey's pocket mouse (Chaetodipus baileyi): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

chaetodontidae.name: Butterflyfish
chaetodontidae.desc: Nips at coral polyps and small invertebrates.

chaetura pelagica.name: Chimney swift
chaetura pelagica.desc: Catches flying insects in the air and nests in chimneys. Peregrines and some other raptors catch adults in flight.

chalcomitra balfouri.name: Socotra sunbird
chalcomitra balfouri.desc: An endemic bird that feeds on nectar and insects, and helps pollinate Socotra's flowering plants.

chalcosoma moellenkampi.name: Three-horned rhinoceros beetle
chalcosoma moellenkampi.desc: A large beetle of the montane forest. Rhinoceros beetle larvae of this kind develop in rotting wood; adults are prey for forest birds and frogs.

chamaea fasciata.name: Wrentit
chamaea fasciata.desc: Wrentit (Chamaea fasciata): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 61 times near the park in GBIF.

chamaebatiaria millefolium.name: Desert sweet
chamaebatiaria millefolium.desc: Desert sweet (Chamaebatiaria millefolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 228 times near the park in GBIF.

chamaecrista fasciculata.name: Golden Cassia
chamaecrista fasciculata.desc: Golden Cassia (Chamaecrista fasciculata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

chamaeleo monachus.name: Socotra chameleon
chamaeleo monachus.desc: An island endemic that lives in scrub and along seasonal stream beds, catching insects.

chamaeleonidae.name: Chameleons
chamaeleonidae.desc: Slow-moving lizards that catch insects with a sticky tongue and are eaten by lemurs, raptors and the fossa.

chamaenerion angustifolium.name: Fireweed
chamaenerion angustifolium.desc: A tall pink wildflower of open and disturbed ground that deer and pikas eat.

channa micropeltes.name: Giant snakehead
channa micropeltes.desc: A voracious freshwater predator that eats nearly anything small enough to fit in its mouth and can gulp air in poor water.

chaoborus edulis.name: Lake fly (kungu)
chaoborus edulis.desc: Its larvae eat zooplankton and are food for fish. Adult swarms feed birds and are harvested by people.

chara.name: Stoneworts and pondweeds
chara.desc: Underwater plants and algae that carpet the lake bed below the reeds. Slate-colored coots feed on them, especially Chara.

characiformes.name: Characin fishes
characiformes.desc: Piranha and relatives, the main food of giant otters in Amazon rivers and oxbow lakes.

charadrius vociferus.name: Killdeer
charadrius vociferus.desc: Killdeer (Charadrius vociferus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 505 times near the park in GBIF.

charina bottae.name: Northern rubber boa
charina bottae.desc: Northern Rubber Boa (Charina bottae): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

charonia tritonis.name: Giant triton
charonia tritonis.desc: A large sea snail that eats crown-of-thorns starfish.

chasiempis sandwichensis.name: Hawaiʻi ʻelepaio
chasiempis sandwichensis.desc: A native flycatcher that hunts insects in the forest, and is prey for introduced cats and rats.

chasmanthium latifolium.name: Broadleaf chasmanthium
chasmanthium latifolium.desc: Broadleaf chasmanthium (Chasmanthium latifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

chauliognathus pensylvanicus.name: Soldier Beetle
chauliognathus pensylvanicus.desc: Soldier Beetle (Chauliognathus pensylvanicus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

chauna torquata.name: Southern screamer
chauna torquata.desc: A goose-like wetland bird that grazes leaves, stems and seeds of aquatic plants in marshes and flooded meadows.

cheilinus undulatus.name: Napoleon wrasse
cheilinus undulatus.desc: A large, endangered reef wrasse that eats molluscs, crustaceans, fish and toxic prey including crown-of-thorns starfish.

cheilopogon.name: Flyingfish
cheilopogon.desc: Open-water fish that feed on plankton and glide above the surface to escape predators. A classic prey of frigatebirds.

chelonia mydas.name: Green sea turtle
chelonia mydas.desc: Adults graze seagrass and algae in shallow water. Tiger sharks are their main predator.

chelonoidis species.name: Galápagos giant tortoise
chelonoidis species.desc: A huge herbivore that eats cactus, grasses, leaves and lichens and gets much of its water from Opuntia and dew. Long-lived adults have no natural predators.

chenopodium album.name: Fat-hen
chenopodium album.desc: Fat-hen (Chenopodium album): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 47 times near the park in GBIF.

chilabothrus angulifer.name: Cuban boa
chilabothrus angulifer.desc: Large constrictor; top land predator in Cuba, eating mostly mammals and birds, including hutias and fruit bats.

chilabothrus subflavus.name: Jamaican boa
chilabothrus subflavus.desc: Jamaica's top native predator. It kills by constriction and eats birds, bats and lizards, and hunts from ambush in vines and bromeliads.

chimaphila maculata.name: Striped Prince's Pine
chimaphila maculata.desc: Pipsissewa (Chimaphila maculata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 108 times near the park in GBIF.

chimaphila umbellata.name: Pipsissewa
chimaphila umbellata.desc: Pipsissewa (Chimaphila umbellata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

chindwin headwaters.name: Chindwin headwaters
chindwin headwaters.desc: The Tanai and other streams drain the valley and form the head of the Chindwin River, watering the lowlands.

chiococca alba.name: West Indian milkberry
chiococca alba.desc: A shrub or climber with small white berries. GloBI records show bats, doves, thrushes and other birds eating its fruit.

chionochloa.name: Snow tussock
chionochloa.desc: Tall alpine tussock grasses. Their leaves are the main food of takahe and are also grazed by red deer.

chionochloa rubra.name: Red tussock
chionochloa rubra.desc: Dominant tall tussock of the volcanic plateau, growing on pumice soils. Its flower heads host fly larvae and moth caterpillars.

chionomys nivalis.name: European snow vole
chionomys nivalis.desc: Small rodent of rocky alpine ground that eats grasses and other plants.

chironomidae.name: Midge larvae
chironomidae.desc: Aquatic insect larvae in lagoon mud and shallows. Flamingos and ibises list insect larvae such as chironomids among their food.

chironomus.name: Non-biting midges
chironomus.desc: Midge larvae live in the mud and water of the delta and are eaten by dragonflies, damselflies, fish and frogs.

chiroxiphia linearis.name: Long-tailed manakin
chiroxiphia linearis.desc: The most recorded bird near the site. It eats small fruits such as those of alligatorwood and wax mallow.

chloephaga hybrida.name: Kelp goose
chloephaga hybrida.desc: A shoreline goose of southern South America that grazes seaweed on rocky coasts. It was one of the most recorded birds here.

chloephaga melanoptera.name: Andean goose
chloephaga melanoptera.desc: A large goose of high grassland, bogs and lake shores, living almost entirely above 3,000 m. It eats mostly grasses.

chloephaga picta.name: Upland goose
chloephaga picta.desc: A grazing goose of grassland and wet meadows, one of the best-recorded birds around the park.

chlorocebus sabaeus.name: Green monkey
chlorocebus sabaeus.desc: A common, widely recorded monkey of the area that feeds on fruit and other plant foods.

chlorodrepanis virens.name: Hawaiʻi ʻamakihi
chlorodrepanis virens.desc: A native honeycreeper that drinks nectar from ʻōhiʻa and māmane flowers and hunts insects and spiders. It is among the most recorded birds near the park.

chlorogalum pomeridianum.name: Amole
chlorogalum pomeridianum.desc: Amole (Chlorogalum pomeridianum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 51 times near the park in GBIF.

chlosyne gorgone.name: Gorgone Checkerspot
chlosyne gorgone.desc: Gorgone Checkerspot (Chlosyne gorgone): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

chlosyne palla.name: Northern Checkerspot
chlosyne palla.desc: Northern Checkerspot (Chlosyne palla): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

choeropsis liberiensis.name: Pygmy hippopotamus
choeropsis liberiensis.desc: A secretive forest hippo that eats ferns, herbs and fallen fruit. Wikipedia lists Taï as one of the few areas holding it in Côte d'Ivoire.

choloepus didactylus.name: Linnaeus's two-toed sloth
choloepus didactylus.desc: A slow leaf-eater of the canopy. In the harpy eagle article sloths are the most important prey group.

chorispora tenella.name: Bluemustard
chorispora tenella.desc: Bluemustard (Chorispora tenella): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

choristoneura fumiferana.name: Spruce budworm
choristoneura fumiferana.desc: A moth whose caterpillars feed on conifer needles. Outbreaks defoliate large areas of forest and feed many nesting warblers.

chorthippus biguttulus.name: Bow-winged grasshopper
chorthippus biguttulus.desc: A very common grassland grasshopper, a main summer food for choughs and other insect eaters.

chroicocephalus serranus.name: Andean gull
chroicocephalus serranus.desc: An opportunistic feeder at highland lakes, taking insects, amphibians, small fish and sometimes waterbird eggs and chicks.

chromolaena odorata.name: Siam weed
chromolaena odorata.desc: A fast-spreading invasive shrub of disturbed ground. GloBI has records of elephants eating it.

chrysanympha formosa.name: Formosa Looper
chrysanympha formosa.desc: Formosa Looper (Chrysanympha formosa): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 52 times near the park in GBIF.

chrysaora quinquecirrha.name: Sea nettle
chrysaora quinquecirrha.desc: A stinging jellyfish of the bay's summer waters that feeds on zooplankton.

chrysobalanus icaco.name: Cocoplum
chrysobalanus icaco.desc: A coastal and wetland shrub whose fruit is eaten by bats and fruit-eating birds in GloBI records.

chrysocyon brachyurus.name: Maned wolf
chrysocyon brachyurus.desc: An omnivore that eats mostly plant matter, especially wolf apple, plus armadillos, rodents and birds. Its dung helps leafcutter fungus gardens and seed germination.

chunga burmeisteri.name: Black-legged seriema
chunga burmeisteri.desc: A long-legged ground bird of the Chaco that hunts insects, snakes and other small animals.

chuquiraga.name: Chuquiraga shrubs
chuquiraga.desc: Spiny evergreen shrubs of dry Patagonian steppe. GBIF records several species around the peninsula.

chylismia.name: Desert wildflowers
chylismia.desc: Annual flowers such as browneyes burst out after good rains and provide leaves and nectar for many desert animals.

cibotium glaucum.name: Hāpuʻu tree fern
cibotium glaucum.desc: A native tree fern of the wet forest understory, growing slowly to a few metres tall.

cicadella viridis.name: Green leafhopper
cicadella viridis.desc: Sap-feeding insect that lives on sedges, rushes and other herbs of damp ground.

cichlids, catfish and others.name: River fish
cichlids, catfish and others.desc: River fish feed on invertebrates and organic matter and take up nutrients from hippo dung. Crocodiles eat them.

cichorium intybus.name: Chicory
cichorium intybus.desc: Chicory (Cichorium intybus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

cicindela theatina.name: Great Sand Dunes tiger beetle
cicindela theatina.desc: A predatory beetle found only on sparsely vegetated sand in this park. Its whole range lies inside the protected park.

ciconia ciconia.name: White stork
ciconia ciconia.desc: Hunts frogs, reptiles, small mammals and crayfish in marsh and pasture, and is a summer visitor that winters in Africa.

cinclus cinclus.name: White-throated dipper
cinclus cinclus.desc: Walks into fast streams to feed on caddis larvae, shrimps and other invertebrates, and sometimes on small fish.

cinnyris chalybeus.name: Southern double-collared sunbird
cinnyris chalybeus.desc: A small nectar-feeding bird, one of the most recorded birds near the site, that visits heath and protea flowers.

cinnyris regius.name: Regal sunbird
cinnyris regius.desc: An Albertine Rift endemic sunbird that feeds on nectar from montane flowers.

circaetus gallicus.name: Short-toed snake eagle
circaetus gallicus.desc: A raptor that specialises in catching snakes, and is recorded often around the gorge.

circus aeruginosus.name: Western marsh harrier
circus aeruginosus.desc: Raptor that hunts over the flats in winter and has been recorded taking shorebirds such as red knot.

circus approximans.name: Swamp harrier
circus approximans.desc: Bird of prey recorded eating possums and rabbits; it hunts and scavenges across open ground.

circus cyaneus.name: Hen Harrier
circus cyaneus.desc: Hen Harrier (Circus cyaneus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 44 times near the park in GBIF.

circus hudsonius.name: Northern harrier
circus hudsonius.desc: Glides low over the grass hunting voles and small birds.

cirsium arvense.name: Creeping Thistle
cirsium arvense.desc: Creeping Thistle (Cirsium arvense): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.

cirsium horridulum.name: Yellow thistle
cirsium horridulum.desc: Yellow thistle (Cirsium horridulum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 62 times near the park in GBIF.

cirsium pitcheri.name: Pitcher's thistle
cirsium pitcheri.desc: Pitcher's thistle (Cirsium pitcheri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.

cirsium wheeleri.name: Wheeler's thistle
cirsium wheeleri.desc: Wheeler's thistle (Cirsium wheeleri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.

cissus verticillata.name: Seasonvine
cissus verticillata.desc: A climbing vine whose fruit and foliage are eaten by several forest animals.

cistus salviifolius.name: Rockrose scrub
cistus salviifolius.desc: Sage-leaved rockrose, one of many shrubs of the dry scrub, grazed by red deer and other herbivores.

citheronia regalis.name: Hickory Horned Devil
citheronia regalis.desc: Hickory Horned Devil (Citheronia regalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

citrus trifoliata.name: Chinese bitter orange
citrus trifoliata.desc: Chinese bitter orange (Citrus trifoliata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

civettictis civetta.name: African civet
civettictis civetta.desc: A nocturnal omnivore that eats rodents, insects, millipedes, small reptiles, carrion and fruit.

cladium jamaicense.name: Sawgrass
cladium jamaicense.desc: Dominates the marshes and grows best in slow-moving water. Dense stands hold few animals, but alligators nest in them.

cladocera and copepods.name: Zooplankton
cladocera and copepods.desc: Tiny animals that graze algae and feed paddlefish, gizzard shad and silver carp.

cladonia.name: Lichens
cladonia.desc: Slow-growing ground lichens, including reindeer lichen, are a staple winter food for caribou, which dig down through snow to reach them.

cladonia rangiferina.name: Reindeer lichen
cladonia rangiferina.desc: A slow-growing winter food for caribou.

cladonia, sphagnum and others.name: Lichens & mosses
cladonia, sphagnum and others.desc: Ground cover of the forest floor and peatland. Woodland caribou rely on lichens, especially in winter.

clarkia cylindrica.name: Speckled clarkia
clarkia cylindrica.desc: Speckled clarkia (Clarkia cylindrica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.

clarkia pulchella.name: Pinkfairies
clarkia pulchella.desc: Pinkfairies (Clarkia pulchella): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

clay floodplain soil.name: Clay floodplain soil
clay floodplain soil.desc: Heavy, poorly draining clays hold floodwater and trap sediment and nutrients that feed the swamp plants.

clay licks.name: Clay licks
clay licks.desc: Exposed riverbank clay where parrots and some mammals come to eat soil. Reasons are still debated.

claytonia sibirica.name: Candy-striped Claytonia
claytonia sibirica.desc: Candy-striped Claytonia (Claytonia sibirica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 547 times near the park in GBIF.

claytonia virginica.name: Spring beauty
claytonia virginica.desc: Spring beauty (Claytonia virginica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 41 times near the park in GBIF.

clear fast streams.name: Clear fast streams
clear fast streams.desc: Cold, oxygen-rich mountain streams with permanent flow are the home of aquatic insect larvae and of the desman.

clear mountain streams.name: Clear mountain streams
clear mountain streams.desc: Cold, fast, clean streams drain the granite uplands and support trout, otters and the rare Pyrenean desman.

clear, low-nutrient water.name: Clear, low-nutrient water
clear, low-nutrient water.desc: Ohrid is oligotrophic, with very low phosphorus and clarity to about 22 m, which suits its many endemic species.

clematis drummondii.name: Texas virgin's bower
clematis drummondii.desc: Texas virgin's bower (Clematis drummondii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

clematis fremontii.name: Fremont's clematis
clematis fremontii.desc: Fremont's clematis (Clematis fremontii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.

clematis terniflora.name: Sweet Autumn Clematis
clematis terniflora.desc: Sweet Autumn Clematis (Clematis terniflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 23 times near the park in GBIF.

cleomella lutea.name: Spiny Caper
cleomella lutea.desc: Spiny Caper (Cleomella lutea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

cleomella serrulata.name: Rocky Mountain Beeweed
cleomella serrulata.desc: Rocky Mountain Beeweed (Cleomella serrulata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 252 times near the park in GBIF.

clethrionomys glareolus.name: Bank vole
clethrionomys glareolus.desc: A small rodent of woodland floors eating seeds, berries and green plants; prey of wildcats and adders.

clinopodium talladeganum.name: Talladega Wild Basil
clinopodium talladeganum.desc: Talladega Wild Basil (Clinopodium talladeganum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 47 times near the park in GBIF.

clintonia borealis.name: Bluebead
clintonia borealis.desc: Bluebead (Clintonia borealis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

clitoria mariana.name: Butterfly-pea
clitoria mariana.desc: Butterfly-pea (Clitoria mariana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

cloud and mist.name: Cloud and mist
cloud and mist.desc: Cloud wraps the montane forest and moorland, giving moisture to fog-dependent mosses and trees.

cloud and rain.name: Cloud and rain
cloud and rain.desc: Moist air rising over the high peaks feeds the humid broadleaf cloud forest and the streams that drain the massif.

clupea harengus.name: Atlantic herring
clupea harengus.desc: A schooling fish that eats copepods. It is food for seals and many seabirds.

clupea pallasii.name: Pacific herring
clupea pallasii.desc: A schooling fish that feeds on plankton and is eaten by whales, seals, birds and salmon-eating predators.

clupeidae.name: Small schooling fish
clupeidae.desc: Herring-like fish of warm bays that graze plankton. Pelicans elsewhere in the Caribbean rely on such fish.

cnidoscolus stimulosus.name: Bull-nettle
cnidoscolus stimulosus.desc: Bull-nettle (Cnidoscolus stimulosus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 48 times near the park in GBIF.

coastal fog.name: Coastal fog
coastal fog.desc: Cold Benguela Current air makes thick fog for much of the year. Plants and beetles drink from it where almost no rain falls.

coastal sand dunes.name: Coastal sand dunes
coastal sand dunes.desc: A sandy barrier separates the lagoon from the sea; salt-tolerant plants and later pines settle and stabilise it.

coastal summer fog.name: Coastal summer fog
coastal summer fog.desc: Wikipedia says fog supplies a large share of the water redwoods use, and that its summer consistency matters more to tree health than rainfall.

coccinella septempunctata.name: Seven-spot Ladybird
coccinella septempunctata.desc: Seven-spot Ladybird (Coccinella septempunctata): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

coccoloba uvifera.name: Seagrape
coccoloba uvifera.desc: Seagrape (Coccoloba uvifera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 67 times near the park in GBIF.

coccothraustes coccothraustes.name: Hawfinch
coccothraustes coccothraustes.desc: A heavy-billed finch able to crack hard seeds and fruit stones, including hornbeam and beech seeds.

coccyzus longirostris.name: Hispaniolan lizard-cuckoo
coccyzus longirostris.desc: A large forest cuckoo that hunts lizards and other small animals in the canopy.

cocos nucifera.name: Coconut palm
cocos nucifera.desc: A coastal palm found around the shores of the islands. Flying foxes and rats eat its fruit.

coenonympha california.name: Common Ringlet
coenonympha california.desc: Common Ringlet (Coenonympha california): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

coenonympha tullia.name: Large Heath
coenonympha tullia.desc: Large Heath (Coenonympha tullia): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

coereba flaveola.name: Bananaquit
coereba flaveola.desc: The most recorded bird near the park; a small nectar, fruit and insect eater that GloBI records feeding on Miconia fruit.

colaptes auratus.name: Northern Flicker
colaptes auratus.desc: Northern Flicker (Colaptes auratus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 228 times near the park in GBIF.

cold and winter snow.name: Cold and winter snow
cold and winter snow.desc: High summits are cold, and snow can lie on the peaks in winter. Cold sets the upper limit of trees and shapes the subalpine shrubs and cane.

cold deep water.name: Cold deep water
cold deep water.desc: Cold bottom water below the thermocline is the home of Mysis, Diporeia and lake trout.

cold dry continental climate.name: Cold dry continental climate
cold dry continental climate.desc: Cold winters and dry air shape the semi-desert, steppe and spruce zones, so water supply sets where plants can grow.

cold forest and steppe soil.name: Cold forest and steppe soil
cold forest and steppe soil.desc: Young glacial soils that recycle nutrients slowly in the cold.

cold gulf of maine water.name: Cold Gulf of Maine water
cold gulf of maine water.desc: Cold, nutrient-bearing water along the coast feeds plankton and seaweed.

cold nights & frost.name: Cold nights & frost
cold nights & frost.desc: On the high plateaus frost kills forest seedlings, which helps keep grassland open between shola patches.

cold nutrient-rich water.name: Cold nutrient-rich water
cold nutrient-rich water.desc: Cool, nutrient-bearing Atlantic water feeds plankton, and plankton feed the fish that the seals depend on.

cold soils and nutrients.name: Cold soils and nutrients
cold soils and nutrients.desc: Permafrost and cold slow decay, so nutrients recycle slowly. Salmon carcasses add marine nitrogen along streams.

cold, nutrient-rich current.name: Cold, nutrient-rich current
cold, nutrient-rich current.desc: Cold water of the Falkland Current flows north along the Patagonian Shelf and carries nutrients that feed plankton and kelp.

cold, nutrient-rich gulf waters.name: Cold, nutrient-rich gulf waters
cold, nutrient-rich gulf waters.desc: The sheltered gulfs of the peninsula hold the plankton and fish that the whales, seals and penguins depend on.

cold, nutrient-rich water.name: Cold, nutrient-rich water
