cold, nutrient-rich water.desc: Cold water holds nutrients that feed spring blooms when sunlight returns.

cold, short growing season.name: Cold, short growing season
cold, short growing season.desc: Harsh weather and a brief summer shape which plants can grow and when animals can feed.

cold, snowy winters.name: Cold, snowy winters
cold, snowy winters.desc: Deep cold and snow shape which plants survive and push animals such as ibex to lower slopes in winter.

coleogyne ramosissima.name: Blackbrush
coleogyne ramosissima.desc: A dense, dark shrub that is among the most recorded plants of the park and a common cover on its higher, drier ground.

coleoptera.name: Wood-boring beetles
coleoptera.desc: Beetle grubs tunnelling in trees. They are the main food of the Magellanic woodpecker.

colias fieldii.name: Dark clouded yellow
colias fieldii.desc: A butterfly whose caterpillars feed on legumes. Many butterflies fly over the plateau meadows in spring and summer.

colias philodice.name: Clouded Sulphur
colias philodice.desc: Clouded Sulphur (Colias philodice): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

collembola.name: Leaf-litter invertebrates
collembola.desc: Springtails, mites and other tiny animals of the leaf litter that feed on decaying leaves and fungi.

colletes kincaidii.name: Kincaid's Cellophane Bee
colletes kincaidii.desc: Kincaid's Cellophane Bee (Colletes kincaidii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 55 times near the park in GBIF.

collinsia verna.name: Spring blue eyed Mary
collinsia verna.desc: Spring blue eyed Mary (Collinsia verna): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

collomia linearis.name: Narrow-leaf mountain-trumpet
collomia linearis.desc: Narrow-leaf mountain-trumpet (Collomia linearis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

colobus angolensis.name: Ruwenzori colobus
colobus angolensis.desc: A leaf-eating monkey of the park. It also takes fruit and flowers, and its digestion lets it use food other primates cannot.

colobus guereza.name: Mantled guereza
colobus guereza.desc: A leaf-eating black-and-white monkey with a multi-chambered stomach for digesting tough plant matter.

colobus satanas.name: Black colobus
colobus satanas.desc: A leaf- and seed-eating monkey of Central African forest, named among the primates of Monte Alen National Park.

colophospermum mopane.name: Mopane
colophospermum mopane.desc: The most common tree in Etosha, making up most of its trees. Elephants, giraffes and antelopes browse the leaves.

colossoma macropomum.name: Tambaqui
colossoma macropomum.desc: A big fish that swims into flooded forest to eat fallen fruit and seeds.

columba arquatrix.name: Rameron pigeon
columba arquatrix.desc: A fruit-eating forest pigeon. GloBI records it eating African juniper.

columba janthina.name: Japanese wood pigeon
columba janthina.desc: A dark pigeon of island forests that feeds mainly on fruits, berries, leaves, buds and conifer seeds.

columba livia.name: Rock Pigeon
columba livia.desc: Rock Pigeon (Columba livia): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2,362 times near the park in GBIF.

columba palumbus.name: Common wood pigeon
columba palumbus.desc: A large pigeon that feeds mostly on seeds, buds and berries.

comephorus spp..name: Golomyanka (oilfish)
comephorus spp..desc: Translucent, live-bearing deep-water fish and the most numerous fish in the lake. They rise toward the surface at night to feed on copepods and amphipods.

commelina erecta.name: Erect Dayflower
commelina erecta.desc: Erect Dayflower (Commelina erecta): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

commelina virginica.name: Virginia Dayflower
commelina virginica.desc: Virginia Dayflower (Commelina virginica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

comptonia peregrina.name: Sweet Fern
comptonia peregrina.desc: Sweet Fern (Comptonia peregrina): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

conifers, shrubs and berries.name: Taiga shore forest
conifers, shrubs and berries.desc: Forest and shrub cover around the lake that feeds and shelters shore animals such as bears and sables.

connecticut river discharge.name: River flow
connecticut river discharge.desc: Spring floods bring fresh water, silt and nutrients down to the estuary and Long Island Sound.

connochaetes taurinus.name: Blue wildebeest
connochaetes taurinus.desc: More than a million migrate in a loop around the ecosystem, following the rains and the new grass.

conoclinium coelestinum.name: Blue mistflower
conoclinium coelestinum.desc: Blue mistflower (Conoclinium coelestinum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

conophthorus ponderosae.name: Lodgepole cone beetle
conophthorus ponderosae.desc: Lodgepole cone beetle (Conophthorus ponderosae): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

conraua goliath.name: Goliath frog
conraua goliath.desc: The largest frog in the world; it lives in fast rivers in the southern part of the park and is protected from hunting. It eats insects and other small animals.

convolvulus arvensis.name: Field Bindweed
convolvulus arvensis.desc: Field Bindweed (Convolvulus arvensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

cool maritime climate.name: Cool maritime climate
cool maritime climate.desc: A cool, wet oceanic climate suits cool temperate rainforest, which can regenerate without large catastrophic events.

cool mountain air.name: Cool mountain air
cool mountain air.desc: Temperature falls with height, so forest type changes from lowland to montane oak, rhododendron and conifer zones.

cool nutrient-rich ocean water.name: Cool nutrient-rich ocean water
cool nutrient-rich ocean water.desc: Cool, nutrient-bearing water from the open Pacific supports plankton, kelp and the animals that feed on them.

cool nutrient-rich water.name: Cool nutrient-rich water
cool nutrient-rich water.desc: Cold, nutrient-bearing water from the deep ocean feeds the algae and plankton of the bay.

cool ocean nutrients.name: Cool ocean nutrients
cool ocean nutrients.desc: Cool, nutrient-rich water from the Pacific feeds plankton blooms along the coast. This is general ecology and illustrative.

cool upland air.name: Cool upland air
cool upland air.desc: Cooler air at high elevation keeps mosquitoes and avian malaria down, so it is a refuge for native forest birds.

cool water temperature.name: Cool water temperature
cool water temperature.desc: Giant kelp does best in cool water, mostly below about 21 C. Warm El Nino water has been known to kill it.

cool, wet mountain climate.name: Cool, wet mountain climate
cool, wet mountain climate.desc: Rain and snow on the Carpathian slopes keep the beech and fir forest moist.

copadichromis.name: Utaka
copadichromis.desc: Open-water cichlids that feed in schools on zooplankton.

copepoda.name: Zooplankton
copepoda.desc: Tiny animals of the plankton that graze phytoplankton and feed corals and fish.

copepoda and relatives.name: Zooplankton
copepoda and relatives.desc: Tiny animals that graze algae in the lakes. Sockeye salmon feed extensively on them.

copepods and larvae.name: Zooplankton
copepods and larvae.desc: Tiny animals that graze phytoplankton. Young menhaden and bay anchovies feed on them.

copepods and water fleas.name: Zooplankton
copepods and water fleas.desc: Tiny animals that graze algae. Alewife and juvenile fish eat them, and so do filtering mussels.

copernicia alba.name: Caranday palm
copernicia alba.desc: A fan palm of seasonally flooded plains. GloBI records its fruit or foliage eaten by howler monkeys, maned wolves and many birds.

coragyps atratus.name: Black vulture
coragyps atratus.desc: Black Vulture (Coragyps atratus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

corallorhiza wisteriana.name: Spring coralroot
corallorhiza wisteriana.desc: Spring coralroot (Corallorhiza wisteriana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

corallus hortulana.name: Amazon tree boa
corallus hortulana.desc: Eats a wide range of prey, including frogs, lizards, birds and mammals such as bats. GloBI records it eating a sac-winged bat.

corallus ruschenbergerii.name: Trinidad tree boa
corallus ruschenbergerii.desc: Tree-climbing snake reported in the swamp. GloBI records it eating green iguanas.

coregonus clupeaformis.name: Lake whitefish
coregonus clupeaformis.desc: Young fish eat plankton and larger ones eat bottom animals like snails and mussels. Its condition fell as Diporeia declined.

coregonus migratorius.name: Omul
coregonus migratorius.desc: An endemic whitefish and the lake's main commercial fish. It eats zooplankton, algae and some small fish, and spawns in the rivers feeding the lake.

coreopsis rosea.name: Pink Tickseed
coreopsis rosea.desc: Pink Tickseed (Coreopsis rosea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

corispermum villosum.name: Hairy bugseed
corispermum villosum.desc: Hairy bugseed (Corispermum villosum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

cornufer vitiensis.name: Fiji tree frog
cornufer vitiensis.desc: A small native frog of forest floors and streams, hunting insects at night.

cornus canadensis.name: Canadian Bunchberry
cornus canadensis.desc: Bunchberry dogwood (Cornus canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 57 times near the park in GBIF.

cornus florida.name: Flowering Dogwood
cornus florida.desc: Flowering Dogwood (Cornus florida): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

cornus mas.name: Cornelian cherry
cornus mas.desc: A shrub or small tree of forest edges and clearings with early spring flowers and edible red fruit.

cornus nuttallii.name: Nuttall's dogwood
cornus nuttallii.desc: Nuttall's dogwood (Cornus nuttallii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

cornus unalaschkensis.name: Unalaska bunchberry
cornus unalaschkensis.desc: Unalaska bunchberry (Cornus unalaschkensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.

coronilla varia.name: Crown Vetch
coronilla varia.desc: Crown Vetch (Coronilla varia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

corvus albicollis.name: White-necked raven
corvus albicollis.desc: Large crow named on the park page as a bird of the mountain; it scavenges carrion and eats insects.

corvus brachyrhynchos.name: American Crow
corvus brachyrhynchos.desc: American Crow (Corvus brachyrhynchos): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.

corvus corax.name: Common raven
corvus corax.desc: Common Raven (Corvus corax): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 447 times near the park in GBIF.

corvus cornix.name: Hooded crow
corvus cornix.desc: An opportunistic bird that cleans up carrion left by larger predators.

corvus corone.name: Carrion crow
corvus corone.desc: Omnivorous scavenger and predator of small animals; also eats berries and seeds.

corvus crassirostris.name: Thick-billed raven
corvus crassirostris.desc: A large highland raven that is commonly seen in the park.

corvus cryptoleucus.name: Chihuahuan raven
corvus cryptoleucus.desc: A scavenging crow that eats insects, small animals and carrion in open desert country.

corvus macrorhynchos.name: Large-billed crow
corvus macrorhynchos.desc: An opportunistic bird that feeds at carcasses; one GloBI record shows it eating chital.

corvus orru.name: Torresian crow
corvus orru.desc: Opportunistic scavenger and omnivore, often at carcasses.

corvus ruficollis.name: Brown-necked raven
corvus ruficollis.desc: A desert raven that scavenges carcasses and hunts small animals and eggs.

corvus tasmanicus.name: Forest raven
corvus tasmanicus.desc: The most-recorded bird near the site. It feeds on carrion such as dead wallabies and pademelons.

corydalis scouleri.name: Scoulers corydalis
corydalis scouleri.desc: Scoulers corydalis (Corydalis scouleri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.

corylus americana.name: American Hazelnut
corylus americana.desc: American Hazelnut (Corylus americana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

corylus avellana.name: Common hazel
corylus avellana.desc: A very widely recorded understory shrub whose nuts are eaten by boar, squirrels and mice.

corylus colurna.name: Turkish hazel
corylus colurna.desc: A Tertiary relict tree named by Wikipedia among the park's notable plants. Its nuts are food for small forest animals.

corylus cornuta.name: Beaked Hazel
corylus cornuta.desc: Beaked Hazel (Corylus cornuta): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

corymbia papuana.name: Ghost gum
corymbia papuana.desc: A eucalypt of open, grassy woodland. Its pale cream flowers appear around October to November and, as a Myrtaceae tree, offer nectar and pollen to birds and bats.

corynorhinus townsendii.name: Townsend's big-eared bat
corynorhinus townsendii.desc: Wikipedia says it feeds almost entirely on moths. Pinnacles lists it as breeding in its talus caves, which close during pupping season.

corythaeola cristata.name: Great blue turaco
corythaeola cristata.desc: A large forest bird that eats fruit, flowers and leaves, and spreads seeds in its droppings.

costus scaber.name: Spiral ginger
costus scaber.desc: A forest-understorey plant with showy flowers; GloBI records show birds such as the bananaquit feeding on it.

cotinis nitida.name: Common Green June Beetle
cotinis nitida.desc: Common Green June Beetle (Cotinis nitida): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 35 times near the park in GBIF.

cottocomephorus spp..name: Baikal sculpins
cottocomephorus spp..desc: Small endemic bottom and open-water fish. Baikal seals eat them, especially in autumn.

cotula coronopifolia.name: Buttonweed
cotula coronopifolia.desc: Buttonweed (Cotula coronopifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

coula edulis.name: Coula nut tree
coula edulis.desc: A rainforest tree with very hard nuts. Taï chimpanzees crack such nuts open with stones and branches.

crangon crangon.name: Brown shrimp
crangon crangon.desc: A small shrimp that moves onto the flats to feed. Young plaice eat shrimp, and seals take them occasionally.

craspedocephalus malabaricus.name: Malabar pit viper
craspedocephalus malabaricus.desc: An ambush snake of Ghats forests that takes frogs, lizards and small mammals.

crassostrea.name: Oysters
crassostrea.desc: Filter-feeding molluscs. Wikipedia lists oysters among the shellfish of the bay, and they strain phytoplankton from the water.

crassostrea virginica.name: Eastern oyster
crassostrea virginica.desc: A filter feeder that strains plankton from the water, clearing it as it feeds. Its reefs give hard surfaces and shelter to many other species.

crataegus crus-galli.name: Cockspurthorn
crataegus crus-galli.desc: Cockspurthorn (Crataegus crus-galli): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

crataegus viridis.name: Southernthorn
crataegus viridis.desc: Southernthorn (Crataegus viridis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

crater lake water.name: Crater Lake water
crater lake water.desc: A very deep caldera lake with no streams flowing in or out; its water comes from rain and snow falling directly on it.

crepis occidentalis.name: Gray hawk's-beard
crepis occidentalis.desc: Gray hawk's-beard (Crepis occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

cricetomys gambianus.name: Gambian pouched rat
cricetomys gambianus.desc: A large forest-edge rodent that eats fruit, nuts and other plant matter and is prey for many carnivores.

cricetulus migratorius.name: Gray dwarf hamster
cricetulus migratorius.desc: A small seed- and plant-eating rodent recorded near the park. GloBI records red foxes eating it.

cricetus cricetus.name: European hamster
cricetus cricetus.desc: A burrowing rodent of grassland and fields that eats seeds and plants and is taken by foxes and many raptors.

crocodylus acutus.name: American crocodile
crocodylus acutus.desc: A threatened mangrove-shore predator found in Biscayne Bay; adults eat fish, crabs and small mammals.

crocodylus johnstoni.name: Freshwater crocodile
crocodylus johnstoni.desc: Smaller crocodile of billabongs and creeks. It eats insects and fish, and ambushes larger prey like wallabies. Cane toads have hit its numbers hard.

crocodylus niloticus.name: Nile crocodile
crocodylus niloticus.desc: Ambushes fish and animals at the water's edge, including hippo calves. Wikipedia notes crocodiles may threaten gorillas at Mbeli Bai.

crocodylus palustris.name: Mugger crocodile
crocodylus palustris.desc: Eats mainly fish but also snakes, birds and mammals up to chital size. Shares the Rapti and Narayani with gharials.

crocodylus porosus.name: Saltwater crocodile
crocodylus porosus.desc: An ambush predator that eats mud crabs, fish and large mammals such as deer and boar.

crocodylus rhombifer.name: Cuban crocodile
crocodylus rhombifer.desc: Endemic crocodile whose only wild population is in Zapata Swamp. Adults eat small mammals, fish and turtles.

crocodylus siamensis.name: Siamese crocodile
crocodylus siamensis.desc: Critically endangered freshwater crocodile that eats fish and snakes plus amphibians and small mammals.

crocodylus suchus.name: West African crocodile
crocodylus suchus.desc: Large reptile reported in large numbers in the sanctuary; it is mainly a fish-eating ambush predator of the river and lakes.

crocothemis servilia.name: Scarlet skimmer
crocothemis servilia.desc: A dragonfly recorded in the marshes, hunting smaller flying insects over open water.

crocuta crocuta.name: Spotted hyena
crocuta crocuta.desc: A powerful hunter in its own right, as well as a scavenger of lion kills.

cromwell current and humboldt current.name: Cold upwelling
cromwell current and humboldt current.desc: Seamounts push the nutrient-rich Cromwell Current upward near the islands. El Niño shuts this upwelling off and warms the water.

crossarchus obscurus.name: Common kusimanse
crossarchus obscurus.desc: A small social mongoose of West African forest floors that forages for insects and other small animals.

crossopteryx febrifuga.name: African bark
crossopteryx febrifuga.desc: A small savanna tree. GloBI records show baboons, duikers, elephants and civets using it as food.

crotalus adamanteus.name: EASTERN DIAMONDBACK RATTLESNAKE
crotalus adamanteus.desc: EASTERN DIAMONDBACK RATTLESNAKE (Crotalus adamanteus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

crotalus atrox.name: Western diamondback rattlesnake
crotalus atrox.desc: Ambush predator of rodents, rabbits and birds. Young snakes are eaten by roadrunners, and coyotes also take it.

crotalus cerastes.name: Sidewinder
crotalus cerastes.desc: A small desert rattlesnake that hunts rodents and lizards, moving by a looping sidewinding motion over sand.

crotalus horridus.name: Timber rattlesnake
crotalus horridus.desc: Ambush predator of deciduous forest that winters in limestone crevices. Eats mostly small mammals, especially mice.

crotalus lutosus.name: Great Basin rattlesnake
crotalus lutosus.desc: A venomous snake listed among the park's reptiles that hunts small rodents and lizards.

crotalus oreganus.name: Western rattlesnake
crotalus oreganus.desc: A pit viper of rocky ground (the Arches form is the Grand Canyon rattlesnake). It eats small mammals such as cottontails and lizards.

crotalus triseriatus.name: Mexican dusky rattlesnake
crotalus triseriatus.desc: A small high-elevation rattlesnake whose recorded prey includes lizards, frogs and small mammals such as the volcano mouse.

crotalus viridis.name: Prairie rattlesnake
crotalus viridis.desc: A venomous snake that preys on small mammals, including prairie dogs, and shelters in burrows.

crotaphytus collaris.name: Collared lizard
crotaphytus collaris.desc: A big-headed lizard of rocky desert ground that hunts insects and smaller lizards. Hawks and rattlesnakes eat it.

croton dioicus.name: Grassland croton
croton dioicus.desc: Grassland croton (Croton dioicus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

croton punctatus.name: Beach croton
croton punctatus.desc: Beach croton (Croton punctatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

croton socotranus.name: Socotra croton
croton socotranus.desc: A common shrub of Socotra's dry shrubland, part of the low cover that insects and grazers use.

cryptobranchus alleganiensis bishopi.name: Ozark hellbender
cryptobranchus alleganiensis bishopi.desc: A big aquatic salamander of cool, rocky rivers in the White and Black river systems. Mostly eats crayfish. Silt, disease and poor water quality are threats.

cryptocarya.name: Laurels
cryptocarya.desc: Trees of the laurel family, among the most recorded plants in the area (Cryptocarya moschata). Their fleshy fruits are eaten by forest animals.

cryptomeria japonica.name: Yakusugi cedar
cryptomeria japonica.desc: Japanese cedar that grows very old on the island; the ancient trees called yakusugi are a hallmark of the forest and shelter many mosses and ferns.

cryptoprocta ferox.name: Fossa
cryptoprocta ferox.desc: Madagascar's largest land predator. Lemurs make up over half of its diet, plus tenrecs, lizards, birds and rodents.

ctenium aromaticum.name: Toothache grass
ctenium aromaticum.desc: Toothache grass (Ctenium aromaticum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 78 times near the park in GBIF.

ctenomys opimus.name: Highland tuco-tuco
ctenomys opimus.desc: A burrowing rodent of the puna, regularly recorded in the area. It eats roots and plants; the link to its predators is general ecology.

ctenomys pearsoni.name: Pearson's tuco-tuco
ctenomys pearsoni.desc: A burrowing rodent and the dominant vertebrate of the Cabo Polonio dunes.

ctenophorus nuchalis.name: Central netted dragon
ctenophorus nuchalis.desc: A common agamid lizard of the sandplain that eats insects, and is itself taken by hawks, falcons and goannas.

cucurbita foetidissima.name: Prairie gourd
cucurbita foetidissima.desc: Buffalo gourd (Cucurbita foetidissima): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 41 times near the park in GBIF.

culex pipiens.name: Northern house mosquito
culex pipiens.desc: Larvae develop in standing water and feed on algae and organic particles; adults are prey for frogs and other animals.

culex tarsalis.name: Western encephalitis mosquito
culex tarsalis.desc: Western encephalitis mosquito (Culex tarsalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 43 times near the park in GBIF.

cullenia exarillata.name: Cullenia
cullenia exarillata.desc: A tall rainforest tree of Silent Valley. Wikipedia says the lion-tailed macaque's presence there depends on its flowering.

cuniculus paca.name: Lowland paca
cuniculus paca.desc: A large nocturnal rodent that eats fruit, seeds and leaves; illegal hunting has reduced it in the region.

cuon alpinus.name: Dhole
cuon alpinus.desc: A pack-hunting wild dog that takes medium and large deer such as sambar and muntjac, mostly avoiding the tiger's largest prey.

cupania americana.name: Wild ackee
cupania americana.desc: A fruiting forest tree whose fruits are taken by thrushes, pigeons and bananaquits.

cuyahoga river & wetlands.name: Cuyahoga River & wetlands
cuyahoga river & wetlands.desc: The river runs through the park and feeds floodplains, marshes and beaver ponds that many species rely on.

cyanobacteria.name: Algae and cyanobacteria
cyanobacteria.desc: Films of algae coat stones and tufa in the lakes and streams and are grazed by insect larvae and small crustaceans.

cyanobacteria, lichen and moss.name: Biological soil crust
cyanobacteria, lichen and moss.desc: A living skin of cyanobacteria, fungi, lichen, moss and algae that protects sandy desert soil from erosion.

cyanocitta cristata.name: Blue Jay
cyanocitta cristata.desc: Blue Jay (Cyanocitta cristata): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

cyanocitta stelleri.name: Steller's Jay
cyanocitta stelleri.desc: Steller's Jay (Cyanocitta stelleri): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 490 times near the park in GBIF.

cyathea.name: Tree ferns
cyathea.desc: Tall tree ferns are a hallmark of the wet, misty mountain forest, and many other ferns and epiphytes grow in the same cloud-soaked habitat.

cyclura cychlura.name: Northern Bahamian rock iguana
cyclura cychlura.desc: A mostly plant-eating lizard of coastal scrub and beaches. The Exuma population is threatened by feral animals and development.

cygnus buccinator.name: Trumpeter/Tundra Swan
cygnus buccinator.desc: Trumpeter/Tundra Swan (Cygnus buccinator): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 679 times near the park in GBIF.

cygnus olor.name: Mute swan
cygnus olor.desc: Large waterbird that grazes on water plants, including water-lily and waterweed, in shallow wetlands.

cylindropuntia acanthocarpa.name: Buckhorn cholla
cylindropuntia acanthocarpa.desc: Buckhorn cholla (Cylindropuntia acanthocarpa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.

cylindropuntia echinocarpa.name: Cholla cactus
cylindropuntia echinocarpa.desc: A spiny cactus of the lower desert whose pads and fruit are food for tortoises and other desert animals.

cylindropuntia fosbergii.name: Cylindropuntia fosbergii
cylindropuntia fosbergii.desc: Cylindropuntia fosbergii (Cylindropuntia fosbergii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

cylindropuntia imbricata.name: Tree cholla
cylindropuntia imbricata.desc: A tall branching cactus of desert slopes and flats. Cholla and prickly pear are a major food of woodrats.

cylindropuntia leptocaulis.name: Christmas cactus
cylindropuntia leptocaulis.desc: Christmas cactus (Cylindropuntia leptocaulis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 35 times near the park in GBIF.

cymodocea nodosa.name: Slender seagrass
cymodocea nodosa.desc: Seagrass of shallow sandy bottoms in the eastern Atlantic, forming meadows alongside dwarf eelgrass.

cynips quercusfolii.name: Oak leaf gall wasp
cynips quercusfolii.desc: A tiny wasp whose larvae develop inside round galls on the underside of oak leaves.

cynodon.name: Floodplain grasses
cynodon.desc: Grasslands among the woodland and on the seasonally flooded plains feed zebra, antelopes, buffalo and hippos.

cynodon and digitaria spp..name: Short grasses
cynodon and digitaria spp..desc: Short, nutritious grasses on the southern plains that wildebeest and gazelles head for each rainy season.

cynodon dactylon.name: Bermuda grass
cynodon dactylon.desc: Short creeping grass that can carpet open ground and river margins, grazed by hippos, buffalo and other grazers.

cynoglossum officinale.name: Hound's-tongue
cynoglossum officinale.desc: Hound's-tongue (Cynoglossum officinale): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

cynomys gunnisoni.name: Gunnison's prairie dog
cynomys gunnisoni.desc: Lives in colonies and eats mostly grasses and herbs. Its burrowing loosens soil and creates habitat, and many predators hunt it.

cynomys leucurus.name: White-tailed prairie dog
cynomys leucurus.desc: White-tailed prairie dog (Cynomys leucurus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 131 times near the park in GBIF.

cynomys ludovicianus.name: Black-tailed prairie dog
cynomys ludovicianus.desc: Eats mostly grasses and is called an ecosystem engineer. Its colonies feed and shelter ferrets and burrowing owls.

cynomys parvidens.name: Utah prairie dog
cynomys parvidens.desc: A threatened burrowing rodent reintroduced to the park. Wikipedia calls it a keystone species because its burrowing mixes soil and its burrows shelter other animals.

cynopterus brachyotis.name: Lesser short-nosed fruit bat
cynopterus brachyotis.desc: A fruit bat recorded eating Allophylus fruit; spreads seeds as it feeds.

cynoscion nebulosus.name: Spotted seatrout
cynoscion nebulosus.desc: Hunts shrimp, anchovies and small fish in bays and marsh edges.

cyperaceae.name: Swamp sedges and aquatic grasses
cyperaceae.desc: Sedges and reeds along flooded edges and clearings. They are staple food for the sitatunga.

cyperus mesochorus.name: Midland flatsedge
cyperus mesochorus.desc: Midland flatsedge (Cyperus mesochorus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

cyperus papyrus.name: Papyrus
cyperus papyrus.desc: Thick papyrus swamp once dominated the Hula marsh, and a reintroduced stand grows in the reserve today.

cyprinidae.name: River fish
cyprinidae.desc: The Rapti-Narayani river system has over a hundred fish species, which feed gharials and mugger crocodiles.

cyprinus carpio.name: Common carp
cyprinus carpio.desc: Bottom-feeding fish of warm, slow water. In Europe it is a favoured prey of the great white pelican.

cypripedium acaule.name: Lady's-Slipper Orchid
cypripedium acaule.desc: Pink lady's-slipper (Cypripedium acaule): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 71 times near the park in GBIF.

cypripedium parviflorum.name: Lesser Yellow Lady's Slipper
cypripedium parviflorum.desc: Lesser Yellow Lady's Slipper (Cypripedium parviflorum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

cypripedium reginae.name: Showy Lady's-Slipper
cypripedium reginae.desc: Showy Lady's-Slipper (Cypripedium reginae): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

cypseloides senex.name: Great dusky swift
cypseloides senex.desc: Catches insects in the air and nests on cliffs beside or behind waterfalls, flying through the spray of falls such as Iguazu.

cyrilla racemiflora.name: Swamp Cyrilla
cyrilla racemiflora.desc: Swamp Cyrilla (Cyrilla racemiflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.

cystopteris fragilis.name: Brittle bladder fern
cystopteris fragilis.desc: Brittle bladder fern (Cystopteris fragilis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

dacelo leachii.name: Blue-winged kookaburra
dacelo leachii.desc: Eats ground animals such as insects, lizards and frogs. GloBI records it eating cane toads.

dacelo novaeguineae.name: Laughing kookaburra
dacelo novaeguineae.desc: Takes snakes, lizards, frogs and insects, swooping from a perch.

dacryodes edulis.name: Eben tree
dacryodes edulis.desc: A common rainforest tree of the Gabon region whose oily fruit is eaten by chimpanzees and other animals; GBIF records its relatives (Pachylobus) as the most-recorded plants near the park.

dacryodes excelsa.name: Tabonuco
dacryodes excelsa.desc: Dominant tree of the lower tabonuco forest zone at El Yunque. Its trunk cavities can serve as nest sites for the Puerto Rican parrot.

dalea villosa.name: Silky prairie-clover
dalea villosa.desc: Silky prairie-clover (Dalea villosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

dama dama.name: Fallow deer
dama dama.desc: A smaller deer present in the park. Young fallow deer are sometimes taken by the Iberian lynx.

damaliscus lunatus.name: Tiang
damaliscus lunatus.desc: A grazing antelope that migrates with kob and gazelle across South Sudan plains.

damaliscus pygargus.name: Bontebok
damaliscus pygargus.desc: A grazing antelope of the Cape lowlands, recorded often near the site.

danaus gilippus.name: Queen
danaus gilippus.desc: Queen (Danaus gilippus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

danaus plexippus.name: Monarch butterfly
danaus plexippus.desc: Monarch butterfly (Danaus plexippus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

danube floodwater.name: Danube floodwater
danube floodwater.desc: The river splits into three main branches and spreads over a very low, flat plain, keeping the lakes, channels and reed beds flooded.

danube river.name: Danube river
danube river.desc: The Danube cuts the long Iron Gates gorge here. Dams raised the river and formed a large reservoir with new wetlands along its edge.

daphnia.name: Zooplankton
daphnia.desc: Tiny animals drifting in lakes that graze algae and are the main food of sockeye in fresh water.

dark-water rivers.name: Dark-water rivers
dark-water rivers.desc: Many Gran Sabana rivers are acidic and tea-colored from humic acids and tannins; forests line their banks.

dasineura investita.name: Wood Nettle Gall Midge
dasineura investita.desc: Wood Nettle Gall Midge (Dasineura investita): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

dasiphora fruticosa.name: Shrubby cinquefoil
dasiphora fruticosa.desc: A low shrub of mountain meadows and rocky ground; GloBI records bears and other animals feeding on it.

dasycercus.name: Mulgara
dasycercus.desc: A burrowing marsupial carnivore of spinifex deserts that eats mainly insects, as well as reptiles and small mammals. Listed as vulnerable in the park.

dasyochloa pulchella.name: Fluffgrass
dasyochloa pulchella.desc: Fluffgrass (Dasyochloa pulchella): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 42 times near the park in GBIF.

dasyprocta azarae.name: Azara's agouti
dasyprocta azarae.desc: A forest rodent that eats palm fruit and seeds, and often buries them, which can start new palms.

dasyprocta fuliginosa.name: Black agouti
dasyprocta fuliginosa.desc: A forest rodent that eats fruit and seeds. It is prey for jaguars, ocelots and harpy eagles.

dasyprocta leporina.name: Red-rumped agouti
dasyprocta leporina.desc: A rodent that eats mostly seeds, fruit pulp, leaves and roots, and disperses the seeds of some trees by carrying them off.

dasyprocta punctata.name: Central American agouti
dasyprocta punctata.desc: Eats fruit and seeds and buries surplus seeds for later, which helps spread forest trees.

dasyprocta spp..name: Agouti
dasyprocta spp..desc: Gnaws open Brazil nuts and buries spares, planting new trees.

dasypus novemcinctus.name: Nine-banded armadillo
dasypus novemcinctus.desc: Digs for insects such as ants and termites. It is prey for maned wolves, ocelots and big cats in GloBI records.

dasyurus albopunctatus.name: New Guinea quoll
dasyurus albopunctatus.desc: A climbing marsupial hunter of forests up to about 3,300 m. It takes birds, rats, other marsupials, reptiles and insects, and also scavenges.

dasyurus hallucatus.name: Northern quoll
dasyurus hallucatus.desc: Small carnivorous marsupial that eats invertebrates, small mammals, lizards and frogs. Cane toads have caused steep local declines in Kakadu.

dasyurus maculatus.name: Spotted-tailed quoll
dasyurus maculatus.desc: Tasmania's top hunting mammal, living in rainforest and wet forest and taking possums, pademelons, wombats and crayfish.

dasyurus viverrinus.name: Eastern quoll
dasyurus viverrinus.desc: A small spotted marsupial carnivore that hunts possums and smaller wallabies and takes carrion.

datura wrightii.name: Sacred datura
datura wrightii.desc: Sacred datura (Datura wrightii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 67 times near the park in GBIF.

daucus carota.name: Queen Anne's Lace
daucus carota.desc: Queen Anne's Lace (Daucus carota): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

davilla kunthii.name: Davilla liana
davilla kunthii.desc: A woody climber whose fruits feed a range of birds in GloBI feeding records.

deadwood and forest soil.name: Deadwood and forest soil
deadwood and forest soil.desc: Almost half the forest wood is dead, far more than in managed forests, and it slowly returns nutrients to the soil.

decapoda.name: Reef crustaceans
decapoda.desc: Crabs, shrimps and similar animals living among the algae and coral, an important food for many reef fishes.

decomposer community.name: Fungi and bacteria
decomposer community.desc: Break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil.

decomposers.name: Decomposers
decomposers.desc: Fungi, bacteria and insects break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil.

deep cold lakes.name: Deep cold lakes
deep cold lakes.desc: Over 25,000 lakes, many hundreds of metres deep, fill the plateau valleys and hold a large store of Russian fresh water.

deep oxygenated water.name: Deep oxygenated water
deep oxygenated water.desc: Unlike many deep lakes, Baikal keeps oxygen at depth, which lets animals live throughout the water column.

deep prairie soil.name: Deep prairie soil
deep prairie soil.desc: Dense roots hold the soil, with big bluestem roots saturating the top two feet and reaching about twelve feet deep, per the MDC.

delphinapterus leucas.name: Beluga
delphinapterus leucas.desc: A white whale that hunts cod and other fish in shallow Arctic waters.

delphinium barbeyi.name: Subalpine larkspur
delphinium barbeyi.desc: Subalpine larkspur (Delphinium barbeyi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 33 times near the park in GBIF.

delphinium tricorne.name: Dwarf larkspur
delphinium tricorne.desc: Dwarf larkspur (Delphinium tricorne): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

delta silt & nutrients.name: Delta silt & nutrients
delta silt & nutrients.desc: The Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna deliver mud and nutrients that feed the forest and the tidal flats.

delta silt and nutrients.name: Delta silt and nutrients
delta silt and nutrients.desc: Sediment from the Tigris-Euphrates river system built the muddy delta coast of the northern Gulf, and river water carries nutrients to the bays.

dendrelaphis caudolineatus.name: Striped bronzeback
dendrelaphis caudolineatus.desc: A slender tree snake. GloBI records it eating the common tree frog and a skink.

dendrelaphis punctulatus.name: Common tree snake
dendrelaphis punctulatus.desc: Feeds on frogs, skinks and other small reptiles.

dendroaspis jamesoni.name: Jameson's mamba
dendroaspis jamesoni.desc: A tree-living venomous snake recorded near the park that hunts birds, small mammals and lizards.

dendrobates leucomelas.name: Bumblebee poison dart frog
dendrobates leucomelas.desc: A small yellow-and-black frog of the Gran Sabana region that eats tiny insects, especially ants, on the forest floor.

dendrobates tinctorius.name: Dyeing poison frog
dendrobates tinctorius.desc: A bold-patterned poison frog of leaf litter that eats small invertebrates such as ants.

dendrocitta cinerascens.name: Bornean treepie
dendrocitta cinerascens.desc: The most recorded bird near the park; an omnivorous crow relative that takes fruit and small animals.

dendrocopos leucotos.name: White-backed woodpecker
dendrocopos leucotos.desc: Feeds mainly on wood-boring beetles and larvae and needs plenty of standing and fallen dead wood in mature broadleaf forest.

dendrocopos major.name: Great spotted woodpecker
dendrocopos major.desc: Takes seeds and insects and, in GloBI records, small birds and nestlings.

dendroctonus ponderosae.name: Mountain pine beetle
dendroctonus ponderosae.desc: A bark beetle that kills conifers. The park page says warmer winters let it survive and reproduce faster, raising tree mortality.

dendrocygna viduata.name: White-faced whistling duck
dendrocygna viduata.desc: Abundant wetland duck recorded eating cattail; it feeds on plant matter in shallow water.

dendrohyrax arboreus.name: Southern tree hyrax
dendrohyrax arboreus.desc: A nocturnal, tree-living hyrax of the forest belt, browsing leaves and twigs.

dendrohyrax validus.name: Kilimanjaro tree hyrax
dendrohyrax validus.desc: Leaf-eater of the foothill and montane forest, reaching about 3,000 m on Kilimanjaro. Leopards and crowned eagles prey on it.

dendrolagus bennettianus.name: Bennett's tree-kangaroo
dendrolagus bennettianus.desc: Eats leaves of dozens of rainforest plants, especially umbrella tree, in a small range north of Cooktown.

dendrolagus mbaiso.name: Dingiso
dendrolagus mbaiso.desc: A tree-kangaroo of subalpine forest and shrubland at about 3,250 to 4,200 m, mostly living on the ground. Endangered, mainly because of hunting and habitat loss.

dendropanax caucanus.name: Dendropanax tree
dendropanax caucanus.desc: A forest tree whose fruit is recorded in GloBI as food for monkeys, toucans and other birds.

dendrosenecio keniodendron.name: Giant groundsel
dendrosenecio keniodendron.desc: A tree-like rosette plant of the high alpine valleys. Its leaves fold over the central bud at night, keeping it above freezing.

dendrosenecio kilimanjari.name: Giant groundsel
dendrosenecio kilimanjari.desc: Giant groundsel endemic to the mountain, growing below about 4,000 m.

dendrosicyos socotranus.name: Cucumber tree
dendrosicyos socotranus.desc: The only tree in the gourd family. It stores water in its swollen trunk to survive long dry spells.

deparia acrostichoides.name: Silver false spleenwort
deparia acrostichoides.desc: Silver false spleenwort (Deparia acrostichoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

dericorys.name: Saxaul locusts
dericorys.desc: Locusts of this genus are recorded as pests of saxaul in Turkmenistan and neighbouring countries.

deschampsia cespitosa.name: Tufted hairgrass
deschampsia cespitosa.desc: A tussock grass of the island's warmer, drier valleys, where steppe-like meadows grow. Muskoxen prefer grasses when they are plentiful.

desert soil.name: Desert soil
desert soil.desc: Thin soils of igneous and limestone origin. Nutrients return to them from dead plants and animals.

desert soil & nutrients.name: Desert soil & nutrients
desert soil & nutrients.desc: Sandy, thin soil that holds nutrients plants draw on, topped by the crust.

desert soil and nutrients.name: Desert soil and nutrients
desert soil and nutrients.desc: Thin rocky soils hold the minerals and organic matter that annual plants use after winter rains.

desert sunlight.name: Desert sunlight
desert sunlight.desc: Intense sun powers desert plants, but heat sends many animals underground for the day.

diadasia australis.name: Diadasia australis
diadasia australis.desc: Diadasia australis (Diadasia australis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 338 times near the park in GBIF.

diadema antillarum.name: Long-spined sea urchin
diadema antillarum.desc: A spiny urchin that grazes algae on reef surfaces.

dialium.name: Velvet tamarind trees
dialium.desc: Forest trees whose fruit is eaten by bonobos. Seeds that pass through a bonobo can germinate better, and some Dialium seem to rely on that.

diama dam.name: Diama Dam
diama dam.desc: Operating since 1988, the downstream dam changed the water balance and salinity, and invasive reeds and floating plants spread afterwards.

dianthera americana.name: American water-willow
dianthera americana.desc: American water-willow (Dianthera americana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

dianthus armeria.name: Deptford Pink
dianthus armeria.desc: Deptford Pink (Dianthus armeria): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

diatoms and dinoflagellates.name: Phytoplankton
diatoms and dinoflagellates.desc: Drifting algae that bloom where river nutrients arrive. When a bloom dies and sinks, bacteria break it down and use up oxygen.

diatoms and flagellates.name: Phytoplankton
diatoms and flagellates.desc: Drifting algae that bloom in open water and near the ice edge. Growth is often limited by a shortage of iron.

diatoms and green algae.name: Phytoplankton and algae
diatoms and green algae.desc: Microscopic algae in the open water and on the lake bottom. They feed the lake's small grazers and filter feeders.

diatoms and other algae.name: Phytoplankton
diatoms and other algae.desc: Drifting algae that feed the bay's filter feeders and zooplankton. Too many nutrients cause blooms that block light and use up oxygen when they die and decay.

diatoms living in and under ice.latin: Diatoms living in and under ice
diatoms living in and under ice.name: Sea-ice algae
diatoms living in and under ice.desc: Algae growing in channels and on the underside of sea ice, a spring food supply for krill.

dicentra cucullaria.name: Dutchman's-breeches
dicentra cucullaria.desc: Dutchman's-breeches (Dicentra cucullaria): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

dicerorhinus sumatrensis.name: Sumatran rhinoceros
dicerorhinus sumatrensis.desc: A critically small population lives in the park. Wikipedia reports a 2011 camera-trap survey and an estimate of no more than 27 animals.

diceros bicornis.name: Black rhinoceros
diceros bicornis.desc: A selective browser that strips leaves and twigs with its prehensile lip, favouring acacias. Etosha is a major stronghold for the species.

dichanthelium acuminatum.name: Tapered Rosette Grass
dichanthelium acuminatum.desc: Tapered Rosette Grass (Dichanthelium acuminatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

dichanthelium linearifolium.name: Narrowleaf Witchgrass
dichanthelium linearifolium.desc: Narrowleaf Witchgrass (Dichanthelium linearifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

dichanthelium scoparium.name: Velvety Panic Grass
dichanthelium scoparium.desc: Velvety Panic Grass (Dichanthelium scoparium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

dichanthelium sphaerocarpon.name: Roundfruit Panicgrass
dichanthelium sphaerocarpon.desc: Roundfruit Panicgrass (Dichanthelium sphaerocarpon): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

dichrostachys cinerea.name: Sicklebush
dichrostachys cinerea.desc: A thorny shrub of African savanna. GloBI records many local browsers eating it, including impala, elephant, warthog and waterbuck.

dicksonia antarctica.name: Soft tree fern
dicksonia antarctica.desc: A tree fern that forms an open, park-like understorey in many rainforest stands.

dicotyles tajacu.name: Collared peccary
dicotyles tajacu.desc: Called javelina locally. Feeds on cactus such as prickly pear and is taken by cougars and eaten as carrion by vultures in GloBI records.

dicranopteris linearis.name: Forkedfern
dicranopteris linearis.desc: A tangle-forming fern of forest clearings and openings, recorded in the Gola area. Ferns and herbs are staple foods of the pygmy hippo.

dicrostonyx groenlandicus.name: Collared lemming
dicrostonyx groenlandicus.desc: Tunnels under the snow all winter. Its boom-and-bust numbers drive owls and foxes.

dicrostonyx vinogradovi.name: Wrangel Island collared lemming
dicrostonyx vinogradovi.desc: The island has unusually dense lemming populations. Lemmings are the key prey of Arctic foxes, snowy owls and wolverines.

dicrurus adsimilis.name: Fork-tailed drongo
dicrurus adsimilis.desc: A black insect-eating bird, recorded in GBIF data near the reserve. It hunts flying insects from perches.

dicrurus lophorinus.name: Sri Lanka drongo
dicrurus lophorinus.desc: An insect-eating bird that hunts from open perches. Related drongos are noisy members of the mixed-species flocks that Sinharaja is known for.

didelphis aurita.name: Big-eared opossum
didelphis aurita.desc: An omnivorous marsupial that eats fruit and small animals. GloBI records show it eating many of the same fruits as other forest animals.

didelphis virginiana.name: Virginia opossum
didelphis virginiana.desc: Virginia opossum (Didelphis virginiana): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

didiereaceae.name: Spiny forest plants
didiereaceae.desc: Woody, spiny, drought-adapted plants of the south-west that are only distantly related to cacti.

dieunomia nevadensis.name: Nevada Nomia
dieunomia nevadensis.desc: Nevada Nomia (Dieunomia nevadensis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

dillenia indica.name: Elephant apple
dillenia indica.desc: A fruiting tree of the open woodland. A GloBI record shows Asian elephants eating it.

dinaromys bogdanovi.name: Balkan snow vole
dinaromys bogdanovi.desc: A rock-dwelling rodent of the Dinaric mountains that eats plants. Small mammals like this feed foxes, eagles and bears.

dione vanillae.name: Gulf Fritillary
dione vanillae.desc: Gulf Fritillary (Dione vanillae): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 64 times near the park in GBIF.

diospyros.name: Ebony trees
diospyros.desc: A genus of forest trees with fleshy fruit and hard dense wood; Diospyros conocarpa is among the most recorded plants near the reserve.

diospyros cauliflora.name: Ebony relatives
diospyros cauliflora.desc: Understory tree of the ebony genus recorded in the reserve; its fruit is eaten by mouse-deer in GloBI records.

diospyros lotus.name: Date plum
diospyros lotus.desc: A fruit tree of the Hyrcanian forest. Its fruit is eaten by birds and mammals.

diospyros mespiliformis.name: African ebony
diospyros mespiliformis.desc: A savanna and riverine tree whose fruit and leaves are recorded in the diets of antelope, elephants, warthogs and baboons.

diospyros virginiana.name: Eastern Persimmon
diospyros virginiana.desc: Eastern Persimmon (Diospyros virginiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

diphasiastrum digitatum.name: Fan Clubmoss
diphasiastrum digitatum.desc: Fan Clubmoss (Diphasiastrum digitatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 27 times near the park in GBIF.

diplacus aurantiacus.name: Bush monkey-flower
diplacus aurantiacus.desc: Bush monkey-flower (Diplacus aurantiacus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 99 times near the park in GBIF.

dipodomys compactus.name: Gulf Coast Kangaroo Rat
dipodomys compactus.desc: Gulf Coast Kangaroo Rat (Dipodomys compactus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

dipodomys deserti.name: Desert kangaroo rat
dipodomys deserti.desc: A seed-eater that lives in sand burrows. NPS notes it gets all its water from its food and never needs to drink.

dipodomys merriami.name: Merriam's kangaroo rat
dipodomys merriami.desc: Eats mostly seeds and stores them in its burrow. It rarely drinks, getting water from its food and its humid burrow.

dipodomys ordii.name: Ord's kangaroo rat
dipodomys ordii.desc: A nocturnal seed-eater that stores seeds in burrows and gets most of its water from its food. Coyotes, bobcats, owls and snakes eat it.

dipodomys venustus.name: Narrow-faced kangaroo rat
dipodomys venustus.desc: A nocturnal seed-eating rodent of chaparral slopes, and an important prey animal for snakes, cats and canids.

diporeia hoyi.name: Diporeia
diporeia hoyi.desc: A native lake-bottom amphipod that fell sharply from the 1990s, which invasive mussels are thought to have caused.

dipterocarpaceae.name: Dipterocarp trees
dipterocarpaceae.desc: Tall hardwood trees that dominate much of the lowland rainforest of Sumatra and shape the forest structure.

dipterocarpus.name: Dipterocarp trees
dipterocarpus.desc: Tall emergent and canopy trees that dominate lowland rainforest in Peninsular Malaysia and shape the structure of the forest.

dipterocarpus zeylanicus.name: Hora dipterocarp
dipterocarpus zeylanicus.desc: A giant endemic rainforest tree, up to about 40 to 45 m tall, with winged seeds carried by wind. It grows in the wet lowlands including Sinharaja, where dipterocarps dominate the valleys and lower slopes.

dipteryx oleifera.name: Almendro (mountain almond)
dipteryx oleifera.desc: A tall rainforest tree with hard nuts. Its seeds are the core food and the main nesting tree of the great green macaw.

dipus sagitta.name: Northern three-toed jerboa
dipus sagitta.desc: A small hopping rodent of sandy ground that shelters in burrows. Foxes, shrikes and snakes take it.

dirca palustris.name: Leatherwood
dirca palustris.desc: Leatherwood (Dirca palustris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

dissolved nutrients.name: Dissolved nutrients
dissolved nutrients.desc: River inflow and recycled nutrients feed algal growth in the lake.

dissostichus mawsoni.name: Antarctic toothfish
dissostichus mawsoni.desc: Large fish that eats shrimp, silverfish and other fish. Weddell seals and orcas eat big adults.

distichlis spicata.name: Inland Saltgrass
distichlis spicata.desc: Inland Saltgrass (Distichlis spicata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

diverse microalgae.name: Phytoplankton
diverse microalgae.desc: Blooms in open water as ice retreats, feeding zooplankton and the sea floor.

dja river and swamps.name: Dja River and swamps
dja river and swamps.desc: The Dja River loops around almost the whole reserve, forming its natural boundary, and its banks and swamps hold water-loving plants and animals.

dodecatheon meadia.name: Common shootingstar
dodecatheon meadia.desc: Common shootingstar (Dodecatheon meadia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 41 times near the park in GBIF.

dolichophis jugularis.name: Large whip snake
dolichophis jugularis.desc: A fast, large snake; GloBI records it eating mice. Hunted by jackals, foxes and snake eagles.

dolichotis patagonum.name: Patagonian mara
dolichotis patagonum.desc: A large cavy that eats mostly grasses and shrubs such as Atriplex lampa and Lycium. Foxes and birds of prey hunt the young.

dorcopsis luctuosa.name: Gray dorcopsis
dorcopsis luctuosa.desc: A forest wallaby of southern New Guinea that lives in forest and disturbed ground such as old gardens. It browses vegetation.

dorcopsis muelleri.name: Brown dorcopsis
dorcopsis muelleri.desc: A forest wallaby of lowland and hill rainforest that feeds on plant matter on the forest floor. Forest wallabies are a main prey of the Papuan eagle.

dorosoma cepedianum.name: Gizzard shad
dorosoma cepedianum.desc: A filter-feeding fish and the most important forage fish in the river. Herons, cormorants, pelicans, ospreys, eagles and catfish all eat it.

doryteuthis gahi.name: Patagonian squid
doryteuthis gahi.desc: A small squid fished in Falklands waters and an important prey for seabirds, seals and fish.

downingia bicornuta.name: Doublehorn calicoflower
downingia bicornuta.desc: Doublehorn calicoflower (Downingia bicornuta): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

downingia pulchella.name: Flatface calicoflower
downingia pulchella.desc: Flatface calicoflower (Downingia pulchella): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

dracaena cinnabari.name: Dragon's blood tree
dracaena cinnabari.desc: An umbrella-crowned tree whose red resin is famous. Goats stop seedlings from growing, so many stands are ageing with little new growth.

dreissena bugensis, d. polymorpha.name: Quagga & zebra mussels
dreissena bugensis, d. polymorpha.desc: Invasive filter feeders that strip plankton from the water and clear it. They are now the main drain on the lake's food supply.

drepanis coccinea.name: ʻIʻiwi
drepanis coccinea.desc: A scarlet honeycreeper with a long curved bill, recorded in GloBI feeding on ʻōhiʻa flowers.

drepanotermes.name: Harvester termites
drepanotermes.desc: Termites eat dead plant material such as grass and wood, recycling nutrients in arid soils, and are food for ants, lizards and many others.

drift detritus.name: Wind-blown plant debris
drift detritus.desc: Dry plant matter carried by wind from the interior feeds dune invertebrates, which in turn support reptiles.

drift sea ice.name: Drift sea ice
drift sea ice.desc: Ice from the Sea of Okhotsk is carried south each winter and reaches Shiretoko. As it melts in spring it releases nutrients that help start the plankton bloom.

drifting algae.name: Phytoplankton
drifting algae.desc: Microscopic algae that bloom where cold, nutrient-rich water is pushed up around the islands. They feed the zooplankton and small fish that the marine food web rests on.

drifting sand and dunes.name: Drifting sand and dunes
drifting sand and dunes.desc: The spit is a long sand ridge with some of Europe's highest moving dunes. Sand shapes which plants can grow and where forest can take hold.

dromas ardeola.name: Crab-plover
dromas ardeola.desc: A crab specialist that nests in burrows in sandy banks; Bubiyan reportedly hosts the largest breeding colony in the world.

drosera capillaris.name: Pink sundew
drosera capillaris.desc: Pink sundew (Drosera capillaris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 84 times near the park in GBIF.

drosera intermedia.name: Oblong-leaved Sundew
drosera intermedia.desc: Oblong-leaved Sundew (Drosera intermedia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 42 times near the park in GBIF.

drought and fire.name: Drought and fire
drought and fire.desc: Cycles of drought and fire have shaped the wetland, shifting plants and pushing fish into deeper water.

dry westerly wind & low rain.name: Dry westerly wind & low rain
dry westerly wind & low rain.desc: The peninsula is a cold desert with roughly 240 mm of rain a year and winds mainly from the west, which keeps the vegetation low and shrubby.

dry-season fire.name: Dry-season fire
dry-season fire.desc: Savanna vegetation here is adapted to periodic fire, which helps keep trees from taking over open grassland.

dryas octopetala.name: Mountain avens
dryas octopetala.desc: A low, mat-forming tundra wildflower that is one of the well-recorded plants of the coast.

dryobates pubescens.name: Downy Woodpecker
dryobates pubescens.desc: Downy Woodpecker (Dryobates pubescens): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 3,386 times near the park in GBIF.

dryocopus pileatus.name: Pileated Woodpecker
dryocopus pileatus.desc: Pileated Woodpecker (Dryocopus pileatus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 257 times near the park in GBIF.

dryolimnas cuvieri.name: Aldabra rail
dryolimnas cuvieri.desc: The last flightless bird of the Indian Ocean region, a flightless form of the white-throated rail found here.

dryophytes andersonii.name: Pine Barrens treefrog
dryophytes andersonii.desc: Breeds in shallow acidic pools, and the New Jersey Pine Barrens hold its largest populations. It is a threatened species in the state.

dryopteris marginalis.name: Marginal Fern
dryopteris marginalis.desc: Marginal Fern (Dryopteris marginalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

drypetes deplanchei.name: Yellow tulipwood
drypetes deplanchei.desc: A fruiting native forest tree recorded very often on the island in GBIF data. It is part of the native forest canopy.

duabanga.name: Forest canopy trees
duabanga.desc: Semi-evergreen and deciduous forest trees such as lampati make up the forest cover of the northern park, feeding leaf and fruit eaters.

ducula aenea.name: Green imperial pigeon
ducula aenea.desc: A large fruit-eating pigeon of forest canopy that swallows fruit whole, especially figs.

ducula latrans.name: Barking imperial pigeon
ducula latrans.desc: A large fruit-eating pigeon that swallows big fruits, giving trees a way to spread seeds.

ducula pacifica.name: Pacific imperial pigeon
ducula pacifica.desc: A fruit-eating pigeon that feeds on many fruit species and passes seeds through undamaged, making it an important seed disperser.

ducula pistrinaria.name: Island imperial pigeon
ducula pistrinaria.desc: A large fruit pigeon of Pacific island forests and coasts that feeds on fruit such as figs.

ducula rosacea.name: Pink-headed imperial pigeon
ducula rosacea.desc: A large fruit pigeon of Lesser Sunda forests, rated near threatened, and listed among the park's notable birds.

dugong dugon.name: Dugong
dugong dugon.desc: A large marine mammal that feeds almost entirely on seagrass.

dumetella carolinensis.name: Gray Catbird
dumetella carolinensis.desc: Winter visitor that eats fruit and insects in thickets, including scarletbush and West Indian milkberry.

dunaliella.name: Lagoon microalgae
dunaliella.desc: Microscopic algae, including salt-loving types, grow in sunlit lagoons. Brine shrimp feed on planktonic algae; flamingos also take diatoms and blue-green algae.

dunaliella salina.name: Pink lagoon algae
dunaliella salina.desc: Salt-loving algae that tint Laguna Colorada pink to red. They feed the plankton that the flamingos filter from the water.

dune sand.name: Dune sand
dune sand.desc: The Gran Desierto de Altar is North America's largest field of active sand dunes, a loose, fast-draining habitat for burrowers and specialised plants.

dupontia fisheri.name: Tundra grass
dupontia fisheri.desc: A grass of wet Arctic tundra, one of the grasses and sedges that grazing reindeer and geese use in summer.

duttaphrynus melanostictus.name: Asian common toad
duttaphrynus melanostictus.desc: A common amphibian that eats insects. GloBI records water monitors eating it.

eacles imperialis.name: Imperial Moth
eacles imperialis.desc: Imperial Moth (Eacles imperialis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 23 times near the park in GBIF.

east australian current.name: East Australian Current
east australian current.desc: Warm water carried south by this current lets the most southerly true coral reef grow, and mixes tropical and temperate marine life.

echinacea angustifolia.name: Prairie wildflowers
echinacea angustifolia.desc: Coneflowers, globemallow and other forbs add diversity to the grassland and feed pronghorn and prairie dogs.

echinacea pallida.name: Pale echinacea
echinacea pallida.desc: Pale echinacea (Echinacea pallida): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

echinacea paradoxa.name: Bush's purple-coneflower
echinacea paradoxa.desc: Bush's purple-coneflower (Echinacea paradoxa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.

echinacea simulata.name: Wavy leaf purple coneflower
echinacea simulata.desc: Wavy leaf purple coneflower (Echinacea simulata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

echinacea, silphium and others.name: Prairie wildflowers
echinacea, silphium and others.desc: Coneflowers, rosinweeds and many other flowering plants that feed pollinators and browsers.

echinocactus horizonthalonius.name: Eagle-claw cactus
echinocactus horizonthalonius.desc: Eagle-claw cactus (Echinocactus horizonthalonius): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

echinocactus polycephalus.name: Cottontop barrel cactus
echinocactus polycephalus.desc: Cottontop barrel cactus (Echinocactus polycephalus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 76 times near the park in GBIF.

echinocereus bakeri.name: Baker Kingcup Cactus
echinocereus bakeri.desc: Baker Kingcup Cactus (Echinocereus bakeri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 27 times near the park in GBIF.

echinocereus coccineus.name: Scarlet hedgehog cactus
echinocereus coccineus.desc: Scarlet hedgehog cactus (Echinocereus coccineus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 203 times near the park in GBIF.

echinocereus engelmannii.name: Engelmann's hedgehog cactus
echinocereus engelmannii.desc: Engelmann's hedgehog cactus (Echinocereus engelmannii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 92 times near the park in GBIF.

echinocereus fasciculatus.name: Bundle hedgehog
echinocereus fasciculatus.desc: Bundle hedgehog (Echinocereus fasciculatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

echinocereus reichenbachii.name: Classen's cactus
echinocereus reichenbachii.desc: Lace hedgehog cactus (Echinocereus reichenbachii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 80 times near the park in GBIF.

echinocereus triglochidiatus.name: Claretcup
echinocereus triglochidiatus.desc: Claretcup (Echinocereus triglochidiatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 173 times near the park in GBIF.

echinocereus viridiflorus.name: Nylon hedgehog cactus
echinocereus viridiflorus.desc: Nylon hedgehog cactus (Echinocereus viridiflorus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

echinochloa.name: Wild millet grasses
echinochloa.desc: Floodplain grasses that spread over the semi-flooded plains as water rises, forming rich seasonal pasture.

echinocystis lobata.name: Wild balsam apple
echinocystis lobata.desc: Wild balsam apple (Echinocystis lobata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

echinopepon bigelovii.name: Desert starvine
echinopepon bigelovii.desc: Desert starvine (Echinopepon bigelovii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

echium vulgare.name: Viper's Bugloss
echium vulgare.desc: Viper's Bugloss (Echium vulgare): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

eelgrass and widgeon grass.name: Underwater grasses
eelgrass and widgeon grass.desc: Submerged grass beds that give food and shelter, add oxygen and clear the water. Eelgrass in the southern bay has shrunk by more than half since the early 1970s.

egretta caerulea.name: Little blue heron
egretta caerulea.desc: A wading heron that hunts by sight for fish and crabs; in some mangroves crabs make up most of its diet.

egretta garzetta.name: Little egret
egretta garzetta.desc: The most recorded bird around the lagoon; it stalks shallows for fish, amphibians and insects.

egretta gularis.name: Western reef heron
egretta gularis.desc: Wades in shallows for fish, crustaceans and molluscs; on coasts mudskippers are a regular part of its diet.

egretta sacra.name: Pacific reef heron
egretta sacra.desc: The second most-recorded bird near the bay. It wades along rocky shores and eats small fish and crustaceans.

eidolon helvum.name: Straw-coloured fruit bat
eidolon helvum.desc: A fruit bat that eats fruit, flowers and nectar. It spreads seeds and is the main disperser of the African teak tree.

elaeagnus angustifolia.name: Russian Olive
elaeagnus angustifolia.desc: Russian Olive (Elaeagnus angustifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

elaeagnus umbellata.name: Spreading Oleaster
elaeagnus umbellata.desc: Spreading Oleaster (Elaeagnus umbellata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

elaeis guineensis.name: Oil palm
elaeis guineensis.desc: A palm whose fruit feeds many animals. GBIF records show it in the area, and palm-nut vultures, chimpanzees and monkeys are all recorded eating it.

elaeocarpus sylvestris.name: Japanese blueberry tree
elaeocarpus sylvestris.desc: A common forest tree whose fruits are eaten by island birds such as the Japanese white-eye.

elaphe dione.name: Steppe rat snake
elaphe dione.desc: Widespread snake of grasslands, shrubland and rocky ground up to about 3,580 m, taking small vertebrates.

electrona carlsbergi.name: Lanternfish
electrona carlsbergi.desc: Small, abundant deep-sea fish that rise toward the surface at night and are the staple food of king penguins and many other predators.

eleocharis dulcis.name: Spike-rush & sedges
eleocharis dulcis.desc: Wetland sedge whose bulbs (corms) are eaten by magpie geese in the dry season. It grows in shallow water and mud on the floodplains.

eleocharis obtusa.name: Blunt Spikerush
eleocharis obtusa.desc: Blunt Spikerush (Eleocharis obtusa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

eleocharis palustris.name: Common Spike-rush
eleocharis palustris.desc: Common Spike-rush (Eleocharis palustris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

eleodes.name: Darkling beetles
eleodes.desc: Ground beetles of desert country that feed on plant material and detritus and are common food for small predators.

eleodes armata.name: Armored stink beetle
eleodes armata.desc: Flightless darkling beetle that scavenges plant litter and is a common ground insect on desert sand.

eleodes hirtipennis.name: Darkling beetle
eleodes hirtipennis.desc: Eleodes beetles mostly eat plant and animal debris, scavenging at night. They spray a foul liquid, yet coyotes and owls still eat them.

elephas maximus.name: Asian elephant
elephas maximus.desc: A huge grazer and browser of grass, leaves and bark that moves through forest and grassland.

eleutherodactylus.name: Robber frogs
eleutherodactylus.desc: Small, direct-developing forest frogs that eat arthropods in leaf litter and are recorded in the park.

eleutherodactylus coqui.name: Common coquí
eleutherodactylus coqui.desc: A nocturnal sit-and-wait frog that mainly eats arthropods and can reach very high densities. It lays eggs on land and has no tadpole stage.

elkalyce comyntas.name: Elkalyce comyntas
elkalyce comyntas.desc: Elkalyce comyntas (Elkalyce comyntas): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

ellisia nyctelea.name: False Babyblueeyes
ellisia nyctelea.desc: False Babyblueeyes (Ellisia nyctelea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

elymus glaucus.name: Blue wild rye
elymus glaucus.desc: Blue wild rye (Elymus glaucus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 23 times near the park in GBIF.

elymus smithii.name: Western Wheat Grass
elymus smithii.desc: Western Wheat Grass (Elymus smithii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

emoia concolor.name: Fiji green emo skink
emoia concolor.desc: A native skink, a small lizard of Fiji forests that eats small invertebrates.

emoia cyanura.name: Copper-tailed skink
emoia cyanura.desc: A common small Pacific skink that hunts small invertebrates on the forest floor and in clearings.

empetrum nigrum.name: Black crowberry
empetrum nigrum.desc: A low evergreen tundra shrub with black berries that ptarmigan, caribou and other animals eat, as recorded in GloBI.

empetrum rubrum.name: Diddle-dee
empetrum rubrum.desc: A low evergreen shrub of heath and above the tree line; GloBI records upland geese eating it.

empidonax minimus.name: Least Flycatcher
empidonax minimus.desc: Least Flycatcher (Empidonax minimus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 45 times near the park in GBIF.

enallagma civile.name: Familiar Bluet
enallagma civile.desc: Familiar Bluet (Enallagma civile): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

encelia.name: Desert shrubs
encelia.desc: Low, sun-loving shrubs of the sandy plains. Browsers eat the foliage, and rodents eat seeds of desert plants like these.

encelia farinosa.name: Brittlebush
encelia farinosa.desc: A silvery shrub with yellow flowers that grows on rocky desert slopes.

enemion biternatum.name: Eastern false rue anemone
enemion biternatum.desc: Eastern false rue anemone (Enemion biternatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 34 times near the park in GBIF.

engraulis anchoita.name: Argentine anchoita
engraulis anchoita.desc: A small schooling fish of the Argentine coast that feeds on zooplankton and is prey for larger fish, squid, sea lions and penguins.

engraulis encrasicolus, sardinops sagax.name: Cape anchovy & sardine
engraulis encrasicolus, sardinops sagax.desc: Small schooling fish that eat plankton and feed the seals and seabirds of the Skeleton Coast.

engraulis mordax.name: Northern anchovy
engraulis mordax.desc: A schooling fish that eats plankton and is a main food for sea lions and seabirds.

enhydra lutris.name: Sea otter
enhydra lutris.desc: A marine weasel that eats shellfish and other seafloor animals. It is recorded in the park and is preyed on by orcas.

enhydra lutris nereis.name: Southern sea otter
enhydra lutris nereis.desc: Eats urchins, abalone, crabs and mussels, which keeps urchin numbers down and lets kelp grow. Great white sharks are its main predator in California.

enhydris enhydris.name: Rainbow water snake
enhydris enhydris.desc: A freshwater snake of Southeast Asian wetlands that hunts fish and frogs.

environment.name: River floods
environment.desc: Water from the Congaree and Wateree rivers regularly covers the forest floor.

eolophus roseicapilla.name: Galah
eolophus roseicapilla.desc: A pink and grey cockatoo that feeds on seeds and plant material, including pink mulla mulla in GloBI records.

epargyreus clarus.name: Silver-spotted Skipper
epargyreus clarus.desc: Silver-spotted Skipper (Epargyreus clarus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

eperua falcata.name: Wallaba
eperua falcata.desc: A legume tree of northern South America, also called bootlace tree, that can grow even in pure white sand. Its timber resists decay.

ephedra intermedia.name: Ephedra
ephedra intermedia.desc: A low, leafless shrub of dry rocky ground whose berries are eaten by Himalayan snowcocks.

ephedra trifurca.name: Longleaf joint-fir
ephedra trifurca.desc: Longleaf joint-fir (Ephedra trifurca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

ephedra viridis.name: Green ephedra
ephedra viridis.desc: Green ephedra (Ephedra viridis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 85 times near the park in GBIF.

ephemeroptera.name: Mayflies
ephemeroptera.desc: Mayfly and other insect larvae live in the cold, fast Tara and mountain streams. They feed fish and other stream animals.

epicauta puncticollis.name: Punctate blister beetle
epicauta puncticollis.desc: Punctate blister beetle (Epicauta puncticollis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

epicrates inornatus.name: Puerto Rican boa
epicrates inornatus.desc: The island's largest snake. Adults eat mostly mammals (rats and bats), plus birds, anoles and a few frogs.

epinephelus.name: Groupers
epinephelus.desc: Ambush predators of reef fish and crustaceans, hiding among coral heads and ledges. General reef ecology.

epinephelus coioides.name: Orange-spotted grouper
epinephelus coioides.desc: A large reef predator of the region. It eats fish, crustaceans and cephalopods, and is a target of fishing in the bay.

epinephelus striatus.name: Nassau grouper
epinephelus striatus.desc: Reef predator of fish and crustaceans. It gathers in huge spawning groups each winter, as at Glover's Reef, and is Critically Endangered.

epischura baikalensis.name: Epischura copepod
epischura baikalensis.desc: An endemic copepod that makes up most of the zooplankton biomass and filters the open water. Golomyanka and seals eat it.

epomophorus gambianus.name: Gambian epauletted fruit bat
epomophorus gambianus.desc: A fruit bat recorded feeding on silk cotton tree. It likely helps spread seeds and pollen.

eptesicus fuscus.name: Big brown bat
eptesicus fuscus.desc: Big brown bat (Eptesicus fuscus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 83 times near the park in GBIF.

equatorial glaciers.name: Equatorial glaciers
equatorial glaciers.desc: Five small glaciers on the highest peaks feed rivers down to the lowland swamps. UNESCO notes they are retreating quickly.

equatorial rainfall.name: Equatorial rainfall
equatorial rainfall.desc: Heavy, year-round rain keeps the Congo Basin forest wet and feeds the rivers and swamps around the reserve.

equatorial sunlight.name: Equatorial sunlight
equatorial sunlight.desc: Strong sun near the equator drives fast plant growth in the forest canopy.

equisetum arvense.name: Field horsetail
equisetum arvense.desc: A spore-bearing plant that colonizes bare, disturbed ground and is eaten by bears and moose.

equisetum laevigatum.name: Smooth scouring-rush
equisetum laevigatum.desc: Smooth scouring-rush (Equisetum laevigatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

equus africanus somalicus.name: Somali wild ass
equus africanus somalicus.desc: Critically endangered wild ass of the Horn of Africa that grazes in the Afar region; foals begin grazing within two weeks.

equus caballus.name: Wild horse
equus caballus.desc: Free-roaming horses live in the South Unit. Park staff manage the herd size, and a fence keeps horses and bison inside the park.

equus ferus.name: Przewalski's horse
equus ferus.desc: A small herd of about 25 of these wild horses lives in the park, grazing the steppe much as wild horses did in the Ice Age.

equus ferus caballus.name: Camargue horse
equus ferus caballus.desc: A hardy white horse that lives semi-wild in the Rhone delta marshes. Its wide hooves suit the soggy ground, and gardians ride it to herd cattle.

equus hemionus.name: Asiatic wild ass
equus hemionus.desc: A fast grazing equid of the open Gobi plains that roams long distances to find forage and water.

equus quagga.name: Plains zebra
equus quagga.desc: Grazes the taller grass first, clearing the way for wildebeest and gazelles.

equus zebra.name: Cape mountain zebra
equus zebra.desc: A grazer that prefers green grasses and also eats young restio shoots and bulbs. Now restricted to a few mountain reserves, including Cape Point.

eragrostis.name: Lovegrasses
eragrostis.desc: Eragrostis grasses dominate sandy grasslands around the pan, depending on soil and pan effects.

eragrostis hypnoides.name: Teal Love Grass
eragrostis hypnoides.desc: Teal Love Grass (Eragrostis hypnoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

eremias velox.name: Central Asian racerunner
eremias velox.desc: A quick small lizard of sandy and stony ground, commonly recorded here. Racerunners generally eat insects.

eremitalpa granti namibensis.name: Namib golden mole
eremitalpa granti namibensis.desc: A blind, sand-swimming mole that hunts insects under the dunes.

eremophila alpestris.name: Horned Lark
eremophila alpestris.desc: The most recorded bird near the plateau, a ground-nesting songbird of open country that eats seeds and small insects.

erethizon dorsatum.name: North American porcupine
erethizon dorsatum.desc: A slow bark and bud eater of the forest; the fisher is one of the few animals that regularly kills it.

erethizon dorsatus.name: North American porcupine
erethizon dorsatus.desc: A slow, bark-and-foliage eater of beech, hemlock and pine. Fishers are among the few predators that regularly kill it.

eretmochelys imbricata.name: Hawksbill sea turtle
eretmochelys imbricata.desc: A reef turtle whose diet is mostly sponges, with some algae, mangrove fruit and sea urchins. Mongooses raid its nests in the US Virgin Islands.

eriastrum pluriflorum.name: Tehachapi woollystar
eriastrum pluriflorum.desc: Tehachapi woollystar (Eriastrum pluriflorum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 27 times near the park in GBIF.

erica.name: Heaths
erica.desc: Hundreds of heath species grow in the Cape region, and their flowers supply nectar to sunbirds.

erica arborea.name: Tree heath
erica arborea.desc: Heather-family shrub forming the Erica belt of the moorland zone, above the forest.

erica dominans.name: Top heath
erica dominans.desc: A heath shrub of the high Drakensberg, whose tubular flowers offer nectar to birds. Genus-level link.

ericameria nauseosa.name: Rubber rabbitbrush
ericameria nauseosa.desc: A hardy shrub of the sandy shrublands around the dunes that deer can browse.
