ericameria nauseosa and others.name: Rabbitbrush & wildflowers
ericameria nauseosa and others.desc: Rabbitbrush, penstemons and other shrubs and flowers of the open ground. They feed insects, rabbits and bumblebees.

erigeron eatonii.name: Eaton's fleabane
erigeron eatonii.desc: Eaton's fleabane (Erigeron eatonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

erigeron linearis.name: Desert yellow fleabane
erigeron linearis.desc: Desert yellow fleabane (Erigeron linearis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.

erinaceus concolor.name: Southern white-breasted hedgehog
erinaceus concolor.desc: Ground-foraging insectivore recorded near the park; GloBI lists frogs, snakes, lizards and small rodents among its prey.

erinaceus europaeus.name: European hedgehog
erinaceus europaeus.desc: An insect-eating mammal that also takes frogs.

eriocoma hymenoides.name: Indian ricegrass
eriocoma hymenoides.desc: A bunchgrass of sandy desert soil, among the best-recorded grasses in the park area. Its seeds and foliage feed rodents and grazers.

eriodictyon californicum.name: YERBA SANTA
eriodictyon californicum.desc: YERBA SANTA (Eriodictyon californicum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 81 times near the park in GBIF.

eriogonum brevicaule.name: Shortstem buckwheat
eriogonum brevicaule.desc: Shortstem buckwheat (Eriogonum brevicaule): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

eriogonum collinum.name: Hill buckwheat
eriogonum collinum.desc: Hill buckwheat (Eriogonum collinum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

eriogonum deserticola.name: Colorado Desert buckwheat
eriogonum deserticola.desc: Colorado Desert buckwheat (Eriogonum deserticola): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

eriogonum fasciculatum.name: California buckwheat
eriogonum fasciculatum.desc: A common flowering shrub of the park with nectar-rich blooms and seeds, visited by bees and butterflies.

eriogonum havardii.name: Havard's buckwheat
eriogonum havardii.desc: Havard's buckwheat (Eriogonum havardii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

eriogonum jamesii.name: Antelope-sage
eriogonum jamesii.desc: Antelope-sage (Eriogonum jamesii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

eriogonum lachnogynum.name: Woolly-cup wild buckwheat
eriogonum lachnogynum.desc: Woolly-cup wild buckwheat (Eriogonum lachnogynum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

eriogonum ovalifolium.name: Cushion buckwheat
eriogonum ovalifolium.desc: Cushion buckwheat (Eriogonum ovalifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 285 times near the park in GBIF.

eriogonum racemosum.name: Redroot wild buckwheat
eriogonum racemosum.desc: Redroot wild buckwheat (Eriogonum racemosum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

eriogonum thymoides.name: Thyme-leaf wild buckwheat
eriogonum thymoides.desc: Thyme-leaf wild buckwheat (Eriogonum thymoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

eriogonum umbellatum.name: Sulfur-buckwheat
eriogonum umbellatum.desc: Sulfur-buckwheat (Eriogonum umbellatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

eryngium leavenworthii.name: Purple eryngo
eryngium leavenworthii.desc: Purple eryngo (Eryngium leavenworthii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.

eryngium yuccifolium.name: Button Eryngo
eryngium yuccifolium.desc: Button Eryngo (Eryngium yuccifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 30 times near the park in GBIF.

erynnis icelus.name: Dreamy Duskywing
erynnis icelus.desc: Dreamy Duskywing (Erynnis icelus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

erythemis simplicicollis.name: Eastern pondhawk
erythemis simplicicollis.desc: Predatory dragonfly of ponds and marshes that catches other insects, including butterflies like the Gulf fritillary.

erythrina herbacea.name: Eastern coralbean
erythrina herbacea.desc: Eastern coralbean (Erythrina herbacea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 41 times near the park in GBIF.

erythronium grandiflorum.name: Glacier lily
erythronium grandiflorum.desc: Yellow lily that blooms right after snowmelt. Its corms are dug up by grizzlies and ground squirrels.

erythronium montanum.name: Avalanche lily
erythronium montanum.desc: A meadow wildflower that blooms right after the snow melts, one of the most recorded plants near the park.

eryx elegans.name: Central Asian sand boa
eryx elegans.desc: A small boa that ambushes small rodents and lizards, recorded in the area.

eschrichtius robustus.name: Gray whale
eschrichtius robustus.desc: Migrates to the reserve lagoons to calve in winter. It scoops up seafloor sediment and strains out crustaceans.

eschscholzia californica.name: Californian Poppy
eschscholzia californica.desc: California Poppy (Eschscholzia californica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 750 times near the park in GBIF.

eschscholzia lemmonii.name: Lemmon's poppy
eschscholzia lemmonii.desc: Lemmon's poppy (Eschscholzia lemmonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.

esox lucius.name: Northern pike
esox lucius.desc: Ambush predator of weedy shallows. Adults eat mainly fish and frogs.

eubalaena australis.name: Southern right whale
eubalaena australis.desc: Breeds in the gulfs from May to December and feeds on zooplankton, mainly krill. Calves are pecked by kelp gulls, and orcas are its only known predator.

eucalyptus tetrodonta.name: Darwin stringybark
eucalyptus tetrodonta.desc: A dominant tree of the lowland eucalypt woodlands that cover most of the park. Its leaf litter and fallen wood feed the decomposers.

euchloe olympia.name: Olympia Marble
euchloe olympia.desc: Olympia Marble (Euchloe olympia): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

eudocimus ruber.name: Scarlet ibis
eudocimus ruber.desc: The swamp is the largest roost for this bird, which feeds on crustaceans, small fish, molluscs and insects; its red colour comes from the shellfish it eats.

eudorcas thomsonii.name: Thomson's gazelle
eudorcas thomsonii.desc: A small, fast grazer of the short-grass plains and the main food of cheetahs.

eudyptes chrysocome.name: Southern rockhopper penguin
eudyptes chrysocome.desc: Breeds in colonies on the Falklands and eats mainly krill and other crustaceans, plus squid and some fish.

eudyptes pachyrhynchus.name: Fiordland crested penguin
eudyptes pachyrhynchus.desc: Nests in coastal rainforest and feeds at sea, mostly on squid, krill and some fish.

eumetopias jubatus.name: Steller sea lion
eumetopias jubatus.desc: An opportunistic predator of schooling fish, including pollock, herring, sand lance and salmon. Orcas are the main predator.

eunectes murinus.name: Green anaconda
eunectes murinus.desc: A heavy water snake that ambushes capybaras, fish and other snakes.

eunectes notaeus.name: Yellow anaconda
eunectes notaeus.desc: A generalist that hunts in shallow wetland water for wading birds, apple snails, reptiles and mammals, mostly as floods recede.

euonymus atropurpureus.name: Bitter-ash
euonymus atropurpureus.desc: Bitter-ash (Euonymus atropurpureus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

eupatorium rotundifolium.name: Roundleaf thoroughwort
eupatorium rotundifolium.desc: Roundleaf thoroughwort (Eupatorium rotundifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

eupatorium serotinum.name: Fall boneset
eupatorium serotinum.desc: Fall boneset (Eupatorium serotinum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

eupeodes volucris.name: Bird Hover Fly
eupeodes volucris.desc: Bird Hover Fly (Eupeodes volucris): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 30 times near the park in GBIF.

euphausia.name: Krill and zooplankton
euphausia.desc: Small shrimp-like crustaceans that graze phytoplankton and feed fish, penguins and seabirds.

euphausia superba.name: Antarctic krill
euphausia superba.desc: Swarming crustacean that filters phytoplankton and scrapes ice algae. Whales, seals, penguins, squid and fish all eat it.

euphausiacea.name: Krill
euphausiacea.desc: Small shrimp-like crustaceans that graze plankton and swarm in coastal water. A main food for humpbacks and schooling fish.

euphorbia missurica.name: Missouri spurge
euphorbia missurica.desc: Missouri spurge (Euphorbia missurica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

euphorbia ouachitana.name: Ouachita spurge
euphorbia ouachitana.desc: Ouachita spurge (Euphorbia ouachitana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

euphydryas phaeton.name: Baltimore Checkerspot
euphydryas phaeton.desc: Baltimore Checkerspot (Euphydryas phaeton): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

euplagia quadripunctaria.name: Jersey tiger moth
euplagia quadripunctaria.desc: A day-flying moth whose caterpillars feed on plants such as dwarf elder.

euplexia benesimilis.name: American Angle Shade
euplexia benesimilis.desc: American Angle Shade (Euplexia benesimilis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

euploea.name: Crow butterflies
euploea.desc: Forest butterflies whose caterpillars feed on plants such as figs. Adults and young are food for lizards.

euploea core.name: Common crow butterfly
euploea core.desc: A common butterfly whose caterpillars feed on fig and other milky-sapped plants, in turn eaten by frogs and birds.

euploea darchia.name: Small brown crow
euploea darchia.desc: A butterfly of the crow group, whose caterpillars feed on forest plants such as figs, and adults take nectar.

euptoieta claudia.name: Variegated Fritillary
euptoieta claudia.desc: Variegated Fritillary (Euptoieta claudia): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

eurillas latirostris.name: Yellow-whiskered greenbul
eurillas latirostris.desc: The most-recorded bird near the park. It eats fruit and insects and so helps spread seeds.

eustoma russellianum.name: Eustoma russellianum
eustoma russellianum.desc: Eustoma russellianum (Eustoma russellianum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.

euterpe edulis.name: Juçara palm
euterpe edulis.desc: An Atlantic Forest palm harvested for heart of palm until it became uncommon. Its fruits are a food for forest birds and mammals.

euterpe oleracea.name: Açaí palm
euterpe oleracea.desc: Clusters of dark fruit feed toucans, tapirs and fish in flooded forest.

eutropis multifasciata.name: Brown mabuya skink
eutropis multifasciata.desc: A common forest-floor lizard that eats small invertebrates. GloBI records it eaten by the brown shrike, the common mock viper and the little egret.

euxoa ochrogaster.name: Redbacked Cutworm
euxoa ochrogaster.desc: Redbacked Cutworm (Euxoa ochrogaster): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

excoecaria agallocha.name: Gewa
excoecaria agallocha.desc: A salt-tolerant mangrove tree that grows alongside sundri, goran and keora in the tidal forest.

exocoetidae.name: Flying fish
exocoetidae.desc: Plankton-feeding fish of the open sea. They are the most common prey of great frigatebirds.

fagus grandifolia.name: American beech
fagus grandifolia.desc: A hardwood of the moister forest whose nuts and leaves feed deer, beavers and caterpillars.

fagus orientalis.name: Oriental beech
fagus orientalis.desc: A dominant broadleaf tree of the Caucasus mid-mountain forests; its nuts feed boar and rodents.

fagus sylvatica.name: European beech
fagus sylvatica.desc: The dominant tree of the site. UNESCO says beech has spread across Europe since the last Ice Age, and these stands show that natural process.

faidherbia albida.name: Winter thorn
faidherbia albida.desc: A tree that sheds its leaves in the rainy season. Elephants, antelope, buffalo and baboons eat its pods, and it fixes nitrogen.

faidherbia albida, salvadora and others.name: Ana tree & riverbed shrubs
faidherbia albida, salvadora and others.desc: Trees and shrubs along dry rivers. Desert elephants feed on the leaves and seedpods of ana trees in the dry season.

falco berigora.name: Brown falcon
falco berigora.desc: A widespread raptor that hunts lizards, small birds and other prey in open country; GloBI records show it taking several lizard species.

falco biarmicus.name: Lanner falcon
falco biarmicus.desc: A fast falcon that hunts birds over open country.

falco cherrug.name: Saker falcon
falco cherrug.desc: A falcon of open steppe whose main prey in Europe is ground squirrels and pigeons; it often nests in old stick nests in trees.

falco mexicanus.name: Prairie falcon
falco mexicanus.desc: Nests on cliff ledges, and Pinnacles has some of the highest breeding densities in North America. Hunts ground squirrels and birds.

falco novaeseelandiae.name: Kārearea (NZ falcon)
falco novaeseelandiae.desc: Bush falcons hunt forest edges in North Island forests. They catch mostly birds in flight, plus some hares and rabbits.

falco peregrinus.name: Peregrine falcon
falco peregrinus.desc: A migrant visitor that hunts birds over the keys. GloBI records it eating sooty terns and ruddy turnstones.

falco rupicolus.name: Rock kestrel
falco rupicolus.desc: A small falcon that hunts lizards and insects from cliffs and open ground.

falco sparverius.name: American Kestrel
falco sparverius.desc: American Kestrel (Falco sparverius): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 425 times near the park in GBIF.

falco tinnunculus.name: Eurasian kestrel
falco tinnunculus.desc: A small falcon, recorded here nearly 200 times. GloBI lists jirds and blackbirds among its prey.

fallugia paradoxa.name: Apache plume
fallugia paradoxa.desc: A shrub of rocky desert slopes and canyons, recorded in GloBI as browse for mule deer.

farfantepenaeus aztecus.name: Brown shrimp
farfantepenaeus aztecus.desc: Young shrimp grow in coastal marshes and then move offshore, where trawlers first reported the dead zone in 1950.

farfantepenaeus duorarum.name: Pink shrimp
farfantepenaeus duorarum.desc: Young shrimp use seagrass and mangrove shallows as nurseries and feed on small bottom matter.

fargesia.name: Arrow bamboo
fargesia.desc: Evergreen mountain bamboo that forms the understory. Wild pandas eat about 25 bamboo species, including Fargesia ones, so it underpins much of this web.

fejervarya limnocharis.name: Asian grass frog
fejervarya limnocharis.desc: A common frog of paddies and wet ground that eats insects and is itself prey for snakes and birds.

felis catus.name: Feral cat
felis catus.desc: Cat (Felis catus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

felis chaus.name: Jungle cat
felis chaus.desc: A small wild cat of wet grassland and scrub that hunts deer fawns, rodents and birds.

felis margarita.name: Sand cat
felis margarita.desc: A small desert cat that hunts at night for rodents and birds, and also kills lizards and venomous snakes. It gets most of its water from prey.

felis silvestris.name: European wildcat
felis silvestris.desc: A shy forest cat. In the Carpathians it feeds mainly on yellow-necked mice and voles.

fendlera rupicola.name: Fendlerbush
fendlera rupicola.desc: Fendlerbush (Fendlera rupicola): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 70 times near the park in GBIF.

ferocactus cylindraceus.name: Le Conte barrel cactus
ferocactus cylindraceus.desc: Le Conte barrel cactus (Ferocactus cylindraceus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 183 times near the park in GBIF.

festuca.name: Bunchgrasses
festuca.desc: Fescue-type grasses cover open slopes and meadows and are staple grazing for elk, sheep and goats.

festuca and other grasses.name: Afroalpine grasses
festuca and other grasses.desc: Tussock grasses and herbs of the high moorland and montane grassland. They feed the root-rats, hares and grazing antelope.

festuca campestris.name: Rough fescue & montane grasses
festuca campestris.desc: Bunchgrass of montane and foothill grassland that feeds elk, bighorn sheep and ground squirrels.

festuca caprina.name: Goat-beard grass
festuca caprina.desc: The most frequently recorded plant near the reserve, a tussock grass of the Afromontane grassland.

festuca gracillima.name: Coirón fescue
festuca gracillima.desc: The main grass of the Patagonian steppe, tolerant of wind and harsh weather; grazed by guanaco, hares and geese.

festuca kashmiriana.name: Kashmir fescue
festuca kashmiriana.desc: A tussock grass of the alpine steppe that forms part of the pasture grazed by plateau herbivores.

festuca rubra.name: Meadow grasses and herbs
festuca rubra.desc: Grasses and flowers of glades and mountain meadows, grazed by deer and bison.

ficus.name: Fig trees
ficus.desc: Fig trees bear fruit that fruit-eating bats, birds and primates eat. Ficus luschnathiana is among the well-recorded plants here.

ficus abutilifolia.name: Rock fig
ficus abutilifolia.desc: A fig that grows on rocky outcrops near the shore. Its fruit is recorded in the diet of birds such as the bulbul.

ficus benghalensis.name: Banyan
ficus benghalensis.desc: A large fig tree whose fruit is eaten by many birds and mammals, including golden jackals in GloBI records.

ficus carica.name: Common fig
ficus carica.desc: A fruit tree that grows wild on rocky slopes and near water; its fruit is eaten by many birds and mammals.

ficus spp..name: Strangler fig
ficus spp..desc: Fruits through much of the year, so it feeds monkeys, birds and fish when little else is ripe.

ficus variegata.name: Variegated fig
ficus variegata.desc: A fig tree of tropical forest whose fruit is eaten by monkeys, bats and fruit-eating birds, and was recorded in the park area.

fifth season.name: Spring flood
fifth season.desc: Snowmelt from the uplands spreads over meadows and forests each spring, flooding up to 175 square kilometres.

fiord seawater.name: Fiord seawater
fiord seawater.desc: Glaciers carved deep fiords along the coast, and their cool, steep-sided waters feed the marine plankton.

fire.name: Fire
fire.desc: Lightning fires, mostly in the wet season, and deep peat fires in dry spells renew sawgrass marshes.

flood pulse & river flow.name: Flood pulse & river flow
flood pulse & river flow.desc: Spring floods spread water, silt and fish across the floodplain. When the water drops, bare mud flats grow moist-soil plants.

floodplain silt.name: Floodplain silt
floodplain silt.desc: Soil laid down by the river on the terraces. It supports the riverine woodland and grasses.

floodplain silt and nutrients.name: Floodplain silt and nutrients
floodplain silt and nutrients.desc: Silt and dissolved nutrients left by the river and by decaying plants feed the wetland vegetation.

floodplain soil.name: Floodplain soil
floodplain soil.desc: Soil that stores the nutrients plants draw on.

floodplain soil & nutrients.name: Floodplain soil & nutrients
floodplain soil & nutrients.desc: Sediment and rotting plant matter left by the floods feed new growth.

floodwater.name: Floodwater
floodwater.desc: Rain fills the wetland, which is rainfall-fed. Shallow water supports the aquatic plants that deer and capybara eat.

foeniculum vulgare.name: Fennel
foeniculum vulgare.desc: Fennel (Foeniculum vulgare): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 61 times near the park in GBIF.

fomes fomentarius.name: Deadwood fungi
fomes fomentarius.desc: Bracket fungi such as tinder fungus rot dead beech wood, returning nutrients and making wood softer for beetles.

forelius pruinosus.name: High Noon Ant
forelius pruinosus.desc: High Noon Ant (Forelius pruinosus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 35 times near the park in GBIF.

forest soil.name: Forest soil
forest soil.desc: Nutrient-rich soil built from leaf litter and dead matter supports the forest plants.

forest soil & leaf litter.name: Forest soil & leaf litter
forest soil & leaf litter.desc: Thin mountain soils and fallen leaves hold the nutrients that trees, shrubs and the small animals of the forest floor depend on.

forest soil & litter.name: Forest soil & litter
forest soil & litter.desc: Leaf litter and soil hold nutrients that plants take up again.

forest soil & nutrients.name: Forest soil & nutrients
forest soil & nutrients.desc: Leaf litter and decaying wood build the soil that the trees and shrubs draw on.

forest soil & peat.name: Forest soil & peat
forest soil & peat.desc: Soils and peat swamps store nutrients and carbon. Wikipedia notes the park peat swamp forests hold carbon at high density.

forest soil and deadwood.name: Forest soil and deadwood
forest soil and deadwood.desc: Forest soil and rotting wood store nutrients that trees and shrubs draw on once decomposers release them.

forest soil and fallen logs.name: Forest soil and fallen logs
forest soil and fallen logs.desc: Fallen redwoods hold moisture and slowly return nutrients to the soil, and act as nursery sites for seedlings and homes for salamanders.

forest soil and leaf litter.name: Forest soil and leaf litter
forest soil and leaf litter.desc: Nutrients released from dead leaves, fruit and animals are taken up again by roots in the litter layer.

forest soil and litter.name: Forest soil and litter
forest soil and litter.desc: Leaf litter and soil hold the nutrients that the rainforest trees draw back up.

forest soil and nutrients.name: Forest soil and nutrients
forest soil and nutrients.desc: Leaf litter and dead wood break down into the nutrients that feed the beech and fir forest.

forest soil nutrients.name: Forest soil nutrients
forest soil nutrients.desc: Fallen logs, needles and carcasses break down into nutrients that the trees take up again.

formicidae.name: Desert ants
formicidae.desc: Ants eat saguaro fruit, so few saguaro seeds survive to sprout, and they also gather seeds from annual plants.

foulehaio procerior.name: Kikau (wattled honeyeater)
foulehaio procerior.desc: A lively nectar-feeding honeyeater of Fijian forest and gardens, likely a pollinator of flowers.

fouquieria splendens.name: Ocotillo
fouquieria splendens.desc: Ocotillo (Fouquieria splendens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 461 times near the park in GBIF.

fragaria virginiana.name: Thickleaved Wild Strawberry
fragaria virginiana.desc: Thickleaved Wild Strawberry (Fragaria virginiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.

frangula caroliniana.name: Indian-cherry
frangula caroliniana.desc: Indian-cherry (Frangula caroliniana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

frasera albicaulis.name: Whitestem elkweed
frasera albicaulis.desc: Whitestem elkweed (Frasera albicaulis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

frasera speciosa.name: Showy green gentian
frasera speciosa.desc: A tall flowering plant of mountain meadows. GloBI records Hunt's bumble bee feeding on it.

fratercula cirrhata.name: Tufted puffin
fratercula cirrhata.desc: A diving seabird that nests in burrows on cliffs and islands. Adults eat squid and krill, and chicks are fed mostly fish such as sand lance.

fregata magnificens.name: Magnificent frigatebird
fregata magnificens.desc: Takes fish, often flying fish, from the surface, and also harasses other seabirds until they drop their catch.

fregata minor.name: Great frigatebird
fregata minor.desc: Breeds here in large numbers (subspecies aldabrensis). Snatches flying fish from the sea surface and sometimes steals food from other seabirds.

freshwater algae.name: River algae and plants
freshwater algae.desc: Algae and water plants growing in the rivers and wetlands that cross the dry forest.

freshwater flooding.name: Freshwater flooding
freshwater flooding.desc: Water covering the low, flat peninsula for much of the year keeps the swamp a wetland and shapes its marsh vegetation.

freshwater inflow.name: Freshwater inflow
freshwater inflow.desc: The Caroni River meets the Gulf of Paria here, mixing fresh and salt water and carrying silt and nutrients into the swamp.

fringilla coelebs.name: Common chaffinch
fringilla coelebs.desc: The most often recorded bird near the park. It eats seeds and fruit, and also insects.

fritillaria purdyi.name: Purdy's fritillary
fritillaria purdyi.desc: Purdy's fritillary (Fritillaria purdyi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

fulica americana.name: American Coot
fulica americana.desc: American coot (Fulica americana): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 303 times near the park in GBIF.

fulica ardesiaca.name: Slate-colored coot
fulica ardesiaca.desc: A waterbird that eats mostly aquatic plants, with Chara a main part of its diet. It nests among reeds or on floating vegetation.

fulica atra.name: Eurasian coot
fulica atra.desc: A common waterbird of lagoons and reedbeds; GloBI records it eating common reed and other plants.

fungi.name: Decomposers
fungi.desc: Fungi, bacteria and invertebrates that recycle fallen leaves, wood and carcasses.

fungi and bacteria.name: Decomposers
fungi and bacteria.desc: Break down dead leaves, wood and animals and return nutrients to the volcanic soil.

fungi and decomposers.name: Fungi and decomposers
fungi and decomposers.desc: Fungi, bacteria and soil animals recycle fallen leaves, wood and carcasses back into the soil.

fungi and invertebrates.name: Decomposers
fungi and invertebrates.desc: Fungi, bacteria and litter animals that break down leaves, wood and dead seaweed and return nutrients to the soil.

fungi and soil microbes.name: Fungi and soil microbes
fungi and soil microbes.desc: Break down dead plants, carcasses and spawned-out salmon and return nutrients to the soil.

fungi, bacteria & detritivores.name: Fungi, bacteria & detritivores
fungi, bacteria & detritivores.desc: Break down dead plants, animals and seaweed, and return nutrients to the soil and sea.

fungi, bacteria and invertebrates.name: Soil decomposers
fungi, bacteria and invertebrates.desc: Fungi, bacteria and soil invertebrates break down dead leaves, wood and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

fungi, bacteria and termites.name: Leaf-litter decomposers
fungi, bacteria and termites.desc: Break down fallen leaves, fruit and carcasses, returning nutrients to thin forest soil.

fungi, bacteria, termites.name: Soil decomposers
fungi, bacteria, termites.desc: Break down fallen leaves, wood and dead animals and return nutrients to the thin soil.

fungi, termites & bacteria.name: Fungi, termites & bacteria
fungi, termites & bacteria.desc: Break down fallen leaves, wood and dead animals and return nutrients to the thin soil.

gadus chalcogrammus.name: Walleye pollock
gadus chalcogrammus.desc: A schooling cod relative of cold northern seas. It feeds on zooplankton and is key winter food for eagles and sea lions.

gaillardia aristata.name: Blanketflower
gaillardia aristata.desc: Blanketflower (Gaillardia aristata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

gaillardia pulchella.name: Firewheel
gaillardia pulchella.desc: Firewheel (Gaillardia pulchella): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 53 times near the park in GBIF.

galax urceolata.name: Beetleweed
galax urceolata.desc: Beetleweed (Galax urceolata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 129 times near the park in GBIF.

galemys pyrenaicus.name: Pyrenean desman
galemys pyrenaicus.desc: A small, rare aquatic mole that eats mostly stream insect larvae, especially caddisflies. Its main predator is the otter.

galeocerdo cuvier.name: Tiger shark
galeocerdo cuvier.desc: A large shark that eats sea turtles, fish and smaller sharks, and also scavenges dead animals.

galerella pulverulenta.name: Cape grey mongoose
galerella pulverulenta.desc: A small carnivore of scrub and fynbos that hunts rodents, reptiles and insects.

galerida cristata.name: Crested lark
galerida cristata.desc: A common ground-feeding bird of open steppe that eats seeds and insects. It is among the most recorded birds here.

galiniera saxifraga.name: Galiniera
galiniera saxifraga.desc: A montane shrub or small tree whose fruit is eaten by blue monkeys and several forest birds in recorded observations.

galium.name: Herbs and vines
galium.desc: Understory vines and herbs. Leaves, shoots and stems of such plants make up most of a gorilla's diet.

galium palustre.name: Marsh bedstraw and meadow plants
galium palustre.desc: Plants of damp meadows and forest edges, grazed by bison, red deer and wild boar in GloBI records.

gallinula chloropus.name: Common moorhen
gallinula chloropus.desc: A secretive omnivorous waterbird of reed edges that eats plants and small animals.

gallirallus sylvestris.name: Lord Howe woodhen
gallirallus sylvestris.desc: A flightless rail that eats worms, crustaceans and fruit, and sometimes shearwater eggs. Near 20 birds in the 1970s, it has recovered strongly after feral animals were removed.

gallus gallus.name: Red junglefowl
gallus gallus.desc: A ground-feeding forest bird, the wild ancestor of the chicken, and prey for cats and snakes.

gambelia wislizenii.name: Long-nosed leopard lizard
gambelia wislizenii.desc: A sit-and-chase predator that eats insects and other lizards.

gambia river.name: Gambia River
gambia river.desc: The slow, wide river that holds the islands of the park and supports water plants, fish and wet forest.

gambusia holbrooki.name: Eastern mosquitofish
gambusia holbrooki.desc: A tiny generalist that eats zooplankton, insects, and detritus. Bass, catfish and bluegill eat it, and so do wading birds.

gammarus.name: Freshwater shrimps
gammarus.desc: Small amphipod crustaceans that shred leaves and graze algae in streams and lake shallows. A favourite food of the dipper.

garrulus glandarius.name: Eurasian jay
garrulus glandarius.desc: A woodland crow that eats nuts, seeds and berries as well as small animals.

gastropoda.name: Endemic lake snails
gastropoda.desc: About 73 percent of freshwater snails in the basin are endemic. General ecology: many graze algae on the lake bed.

gauja river and springs.name: Gauja River and springs
gauja river and springs.desc: The park follows the old valley of the Gauja River, with springs and sandstone cliffs. Water and wet floodplain soils feed riverside trees.

gaultheria hispidula.name: Creeping Snowberry
gaultheria hispidula.desc: Creeping Snowberry (Gaultheria hispidula): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

gaultheria mucronata.name: Prickly heath
gaultheria mucronata.desc: A low evergreen shrub with berries that GloBI records as food for birds such as the austral thrush.

gaultheria procumbens.name: Checkerberry
gaultheria procumbens.desc: Wintergreen (Gaultheria procumbens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.

gaultheria shallon.name: Salal
gaultheria shallon.desc: An evergreen understory shrub with berries. Deer, elk, band-tailed pigeons and bears feed on it.

gavia immer.name: Common loon
gavia immer.desc: Dives for fish, mostly small ones including perch and walleye; eggs and chicks are taken by eagles, and fluctuating water can flood nests.

gavialis gangeticus.name: Gharial
gavialis gangeticus.desc: A fish-eating crocodilian with a narrow snout. Wild numbers crashed and a breeding centre in the park has released young into the rivers since 1981.

gayophytum diffusum.name: Spreading groundsmoke
gayophytum diffusum.desc: Spreading groundsmoke (Gayophytum diffusum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

gazella arabica.name: Arabian gazelle
gazella arabica.desc: A selective browser of acacia and other woody plants. About a thousand live on the Farasan Islands.

gazella dorcas.name: Dorcas gazelle
gazella dorcas.desc: A small, fast gazelle that grazes grasses and browses acacia and other shrubs, and is a staple prey of the Saharan cheetah.

gazella gazella.name: Mountain gazelle
gazella gazella.desc: A small grazing antelope of the hills and open ground around the valley, and the most recorded mammal in this area.

gazella marica.name: Arabian sand gazelle
gazella marica.desc: The rheem, the native gazelle of Qatar. Gazelles of the Arabian peninsula browse mainly acacia and other woody plants.

gazella subgutturosa.name: Goitered gazelle
gazella subgutturosa.desc: A slender gazelle of open gravel plains and desert, and one of the most-recorded large herbivores near the park.

genetta cristata.name: Crested servaline genet
genetta cristata.desc: A small forest carnivore. A GloBI record shows it eating Tullberg's soft-furred mouse.

genetta genetta.name: Common genet
genetta genetta.desc: A slender night hunter of small mammals, lizards, birds and insects, and sometimes fruit.

genetta pardina.name: Pardine genet
genetta pardina.desc: A small spotted nocturnal carnivore of West African forests that hunts rodents and other small animals.

gentiana.name: Gentians and meadow herbs
gentiana.desc: Alpine and karst grasslands hold some 700 vascular plants in the park, including many gentians, with rare and endemic species. They are summer forage for chamois.

gentiana septemfida.name: Alpine wildflowers
gentiana septemfida.desc: Gentians and other flowering herbs, among the best-recorded plants near the park, that colour the summer meadows.

gentiana verna.name: Spring gentian
gentiana verna.desc: A small blue wildflower of mountain meadows, recorded in the Sharr area, one of many alpine herbs there.

gentiana, primula, ranunculus.name: Alpine wildflowers
gentiana, primula, ranunculus.desc: Gentians, primroses and buttercups that marmots eat, along with other flowering plants of the high meadows.

geocapromys brownii.name: Jamaican hutia
geocapromys brownii.desc: A night-foraging rodent found only in Jamaica. It eats fruit, roots, bark and leaves from many plants.

geocapromys ingrahami.name: Bahamian hutia
geocapromys ingrahami.desc: A mostly plant-eating rodent that was introduced to the park in 1973 as a conservation measure. It eats leaves, shoots, fruit and bark.

geococcyx californianus.name: Greater roadrunner
geococcyx californianus.desc: A fast ground cuckoo that eats insects, spiders, mice, lizards and young rattlesnakes.

geomys arenarius.name: Desert pocket gopher
geomys arenarius.desc: A burrowing rodent of sandy soil that feeds on roots and other plant parts underground.

geospiza and relatives.name: Darwin's finches
geospiza and relatives.desc: A group of closely related finches whose beaks fit different foods. Some eat cactus fruit, flowers and buds, others seeds and insects.

geranium caespitosum.name: Pineywoods geranium
geranium caespitosum.desc: Pineywoods geranium (Geranium caespitosum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 27 times near the park in GBIF.

geranium maculatum.name: Spotted Crane's-bill
geranium maculatum.desc: Spotted Crane's-bill (Geranium maculatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.

geranium richardsonii.name: Richardson's crane's-bill
geranium richardsonii.desc: Richardson's crane's-bill (Geranium richardsonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.

geranium sanguineum.name: Bloody crane's-bill
geranium sanguineum.desc: A magenta-flowered perennial of the limestone grassland and pavement, among the most recorded plants in the area.

geranoaetus melanoleucus.name: Black-chested buzzard-eagle
geranoaetus melanoleucus.desc: Raptor that mostly hunts mid-sized mammals, with introduced rabbits a key prey, and will take carrion when needed.

geronticus eremita.name: Northern bald ibis
geronticus eremita.desc: Rediscovered near Palmyra in 2002. It probes the steppe for lizards and darkling beetles. The colony has since died out.

geukensia demissa.name: Atlantic ribbed mussel
geukensia demissa.desc: A filter feeder living in cordgrass beds. Its waste adds nitrogen and its mounds help cordgrass take hold.

geum idahoense.name: Geum idahoense
geum idahoense.desc: Geum idahoense (Geum idahoense): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

geum triflorum.name: Old-man's-whiskers
geum triflorum.desc: Old-man's-whiskers (Geum triflorum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

gilbertiodendron splendidum.name: Gilbertiodendron
gilbertiodendron splendidum.desc: Legume canopy trees that Wikipedia names among the characteristic trees of Sapo National Park.

gilia ochroleuca.name: Volcanic gilia
gilia ochroleuca.desc: Volcanic gilia (Gilia ochroleuca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

ginglymostoma cirratum.name: Nurse shark
ginglymostoma cirratum.desc: Bottom-feeding shark that eats conch, lobsters and other invertebrates, often resting under reef ledges by day.

giraffa camelopardalis.name: Giraffe
giraffa camelopardalis.desc: Browses the tops of acacias that no other herbivore can reach.

giraffa giraffa.name: Angolan giraffe
giraffa giraffa.desc: Etosha giraffes belong to the Angolan form of the southern giraffe and browse leaves, shoots and fruits of acacias and other trees.

giraffa thornicrofti.name: Thornicroft's giraffe
giraffa thornicrofti.desc: The Luangwa Valley giraffe browses leaves, including mopane, above where other herbivores can reach.

glacial lake.name: Glacial lakes
glacial lake.desc: The park has 118 glacial lakes, and Snezhnika, Europe's southernmost glacier, still survives.

glacial meltwater.name: Glacial meltwater
glacial meltwater.desc: Cold, silty meltwater flows into the fjords and mixes with sea water, affecting where plankton grows.

glacial rivers.name: Glacial rivers
glacial rivers.desc: Glaciers cover a large part of the park and feed the silty rivers that salmon run up from the coast.

glacier meltwater.name: Glacier meltwater
glacier meltwater.desc: The Aletsch Glacier is the longest in the Alps. Its ice and meltwater feed streams and wet ground below, while its retreat leaves fresh moraine for plants to colonise.

glaciers and snowmelt.name: Glaciers and snowmelt
glaciers and snowmelt.desc: About a dozen small glaciers and alpine tarns feed streams but are shrinking fast and may vanish within decades.

glaucomys sabrinus.name: Northern flying squirrel
glaucomys sabrinus.desc: A nocturnal glider of old forest that eats fungi, lichens and seeds, and is the main prey of the spotted owl.

glaucomys volans.name: Southern flying squirrel
glaucomys volans.desc: Southern flying squirrel (Glaucomys volans): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

glaucopsyche lygdamus.name: Silvery Blue
glaucopsyche lygdamus.desc: Silvery Blue (Glaucopsyche lygdamus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

glechoma hederacea.name: Ground-ivy
glechoma hederacea.desc: Ground-ivy (Glechoma hederacea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

gleditsia triacanthos.name: Honey locust
gleditsia triacanthos.desc: Honey locust (Gleditsia triacanthos): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 196 times near the park in GBIF.

glis glis.name: Edible dormouse
glis glis.desc: A tree-dwelling rodent that eats beech seeds and fruit and hibernates in winter.

glyceria striata.name: Fowl manna grass
glyceria striata.desc: Fowl manna grass (Glyceria striata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

goodyera oblongifolia.name: Rattlesnake plantain
goodyera oblongifolia.desc: Rattlesnake plantain (Goodyera oblongifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 36 times near the park in GBIF.

goodyera pubescens.name: Downy Rattlesnake-plantain
goodyera pubescens.desc: Downy Rattlesnake-plantain (Goodyera pubescens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 101 times near the park in GBIF.

gopherus agassizii.name: Desert tortoise
gopherus agassizii.desc: Threatened grazer that eats grasses, wildflowers and cactus and spends most of its life in burrows. Ravens take juveniles.

gopherus morafkai.name: Sonoran desert tortoise
gopherus morafkai.desc: A herbivore that eats mostly grasses and wildflowers, plus cactus fruit and growth. Eggs and young are taken by ravens, badgers and coyotes.

gorilla beringei.name: Mountain gorilla
gorilla beringei.desc: Mostly eats leaves, shoots, stems and pith, with some fruit. Bwindi holds almost half of all mountain gorillas.

gorilla beringei beringei.name: Mountain gorilla
gorilla beringei beringei.desc: Eats mostly leaves, shoots and stems, with some bark and roots, and also giant senecio centres. The park protects about a third of the world population.

gorilla gorilla.name: Western lowland gorilla
gorilla gorilla.desc: Mainly eats fruit, shoots, leaves and herbaceous stems, switching toward leaves and herbs when fruit is scarce. Listed among the primates of Monte Alen.

gorilla gorilla diehli.name: Cross River gorilla
gorilla gorilla diehli.desc: A rare gorilla of the Nigeria-Cameroon border hills. It eats fruit, herbs, bark and leaves, switching to herbs when fruit is scarce.

gorilla gorilla gorilla.name: Western lowland gorilla
gorilla gorilla gorilla.desc: Prefers ripe fruit but switches to leaves, herbs and bark when fruit is scarce. Spreads seeds in its dung.

granite-derived soil.name: Granite-derived soil
granite-derived soil.desc: Thin soils over granite hold nutrients that plants and meadows draw on.

grapsus grapsus.name: Sally Lightfoot crab
grapsus grapsus.desc: Bright red crab on the lava shore. It mainly grazes algae but is an opportunist that also eats animal matter and scavenges dead seals and birds.

grassland fire.name: Grassland fire
grassland fire.desc: Periodic burning has kept tall grassland open, though Wikipedia notes it can also threaten pygmy hogs sheltering in it.

grassland fires.name: Grassland fires
grassland fires.desc: Seasonal bushfires burn off old grass in the park, and fresh growth follows for grazers such as gaur.

grewia.name: Grewia shrubs
grewia.desc: Shrubs of the dry coastal forest and thicket, recorded in GBIF data near the reserve. Browsers can eat their leaves.

grewia hexamita.name: Giant donkeyberry
grewia hexamita.desc: A woody shrub of dry bushveld whose leaves and berries are eaten by elephant and by duikers and bushbuck.

grindelia hirsutula.name: Hairy gumweed
grindelia hirsutula.desc: Hairy gumweed (Grindelia hirsutula): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

grindelia squarrosa.name: Curly-cup Gumweed
grindelia squarrosa.desc: Curly-cup Gumweed (Grindelia squarrosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 105 times near the park in GBIF.

griselinia littoralis.name: Broadleaf
griselinia littoralis.desc: A common native forest tree whose leaves and fruit are eaten by browsing mammals and forest birds.

groundwater.name: Ephemeral river water
groundwater.desc: Dry rivers carry flood pulses and keep groundwater close to the surface, supporting trees, Welwitschia and elephants.

grus americana.name: Whooping crane
grus americana.desc: The park is the main breeding area of this endangered crane, which nests on marshes and eats animals, tubers and berries.

grus canadensis.name: Sandhill crane
grus canadensis.desc: Up to 450,000 lesser sandhill cranes stop in the central Platte valley each year. They feed on waste grain, seeds and invertebrates in fields and wet meadows.

grus grus.name: Common crane
grus grus.desc: An omnivore that eats mostly plant matter, waste grain, insects, frogs and small rodents. Big numbers pass through Hungary on migration.

grus japonensis.name: Red-crowned crane
grus japonensis.desc: An omnivorous wetland crane that eats fish, amphibians, insects, rodents and small reptiles, plus rice and reeds in winter. Wintering birds use the Korean peninsula.

grusonia clavata.name: Club cholla
grusonia clavata.desc: Club cholla (Grusonia clavata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 45 times near the park in GBIF.

gryllodes sigillatus.name: Indian house cricket
gryllodes sigillatus.desc: A widespread cricket that is recorded on the islands and is eaten by green anoles.

guarea glabra.name: Alligatorwood
guarea glabra.desc: A common tree of the forest understorey in the GBIF records here. Birds such as manakins and thrushes are recorded eating its fruit.

guarea macrophylla.name: Guarea tree
guarea macrophylla.desc: A rainforest tree whose fruit is recorded in GloBI as food for tapirs and toucans.

guatteria punctata.name: Guatteria
guatteria punctata.desc: A rainforest understorey tree whose fruits are eaten by birds and primates, which spread its seeds.

guazuma ulmifolia.name: Bastardcedar
guazuma ulmifolia.desc: A common tree of dry ground and forest islands whose fruit is eaten by peccaries and other forest animals.

gulo gulo.name: Wolverine
gulo gulo.desc: A strong scavenger and predator. GloBI records it eating caribou, ground squirrels, ptarmigan and voles.

gunnera magellanica.name: Gunnera
gunnera magellanica.desc: A small ground-hugging plant of damp, shaded ground, recorded as a main food of huemul in a Chilean fjord study.

gymnocladus dioicus.name: Kentucky coffeetree
gymnocladus dioicus.desc: Kentucky coffeetree (Gymnocladus dioicus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

gymnogyps californianus.name: California condor
gymnogyps californianus.desc: A large scavenger released near the canyon in 1996. It eats carrion of large mammals such as deer, and lead from ammunition in carcasses is a main threat.

gymnopleurus puncticollis.name: Dung beetles
gymnopleurus puncticollis.desc: Dung beetles are among the most recorded animals here. They bury dung, which returns nutrients to the soil.

gymnorhinus cyanocephalus.name: Pinyon jay
gymnorhinus cyanocephalus.desc: A social jay that feeds heavily on pinyon seeds and is well recorded in the park area.

gymnoschoenus sphaerocephalus.name: Buttongrass
gymnoschoenus sphaerocephalus.desc: The dominant plant of Tasmania's moorlands. Its rhizomes are eaten by burrowing crayfish, and the community is adapted to burning.

gymnothorax chilospilus.name: Lipspot moray
gymnothorax chilospilus.desc: A small moray eel living in reef crevices, and the main prey of the New Caledonian sea krait.

gymnothorax spp..name: Moray eel
gymnothorax spp..desc: Ambushes fish from crevices in the reef.

gypaetus barbatus.name: Bearded vulture
gypaetus barbatus.desc: Lives on bone, mostly 85 to 90 percent of an adult's diet, and drops big bones from the air to crack them.

gypohierax angolensis.name: Palm-nut vulture
gypohierax angolensis.desc: An unusual vulture that lives mainly on oil and raffia palm fruit, but also takes fish, crabs, frogs and carrion.

gyps africanus.name: White-backed vulture
gyps africanus.desc: Scavenges carcasses of elephant, buffalo, zebra and antelope.

gyps coprotheres.name: Cape vulture
gyps coprotheres.desc: A cliff-nesting scavenger that eats the soft tissue of carcasses and breeds in Lesotho. Endangered.

gyps fulvus.name: Griffon vulture
gyps fulvus.desc: A large scavenger of mountain carcasses, recorded often around the massif.

gyps himalayensis.name: Himalayan griffon
gyps himalayensis.desc: A big vulture that feeds on carrion of hoofed animals and is among the most often recorded birds here.

gyps rueppelli.name: Rüppell's vulture
gyps rueppelli.desc: Circles on thermals and arrives fast at carcasses, stripping them within hours.

gypsum sand.name: Gypsum sand
gypsum sand.desc: The dunes are made of gypsum left by dried lakes in a basin with no outlet. Only salt- and gypsum-tolerant plants thrive in it.

haaniella echinata.name: Prickly stick insect
haaniella echinata.desc: A large leaf-eating stick insect of Bornean forests, recorded repeatedly near the park.

hadenoecus subterraneus.name: Mammoth Cave cricket
hadenoecus subterraneus.desc: Eats whatever it can find. Wikipedia says its guano, eggs and carcasses feed many cave communities.

haematopus ostralegus.name: Eurasian oystercatcher
haematopus ostralegus.desc: Uses its strong bill to open cockles and mussels or to dig up worms. Despite its name, oysters are not a major food.

haemorhous mexicanus.name: House Finch
haemorhous mexicanus.desc: House Finch (Haemorhous mexicanus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 101 times near the park in GBIF.

hagenia abyssinica.name: Hagenia tree
hagenia abyssinica.desc: A highland tree of the montane woodland whose leaves are among the foods of the mountain nyala.

hagenius brevistylus.name: Dragonhunter
hagenius brevistylus.desc: Dragonhunter (Hagenius brevistylus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.

haliaeetus albicilla.name: White-tailed eagle
haliaeetus albicilla.desc: A large raptor that takes fish and, per the seal article, can prey on seal pups that leave their dens.

haliaeetus leucocephalus.name: Bald eagle
haliaeetus leucocephalus.desc: A large raptor that eats fish and carrion along the bay. Its numbers recovered after the DDT era.

haliaeetus leucogaster.name: White-bellied sea eagle
haliaeetus leucogaster.desc: A coastal raptor that takes fish about half of its diet, and also hunts waterbirds and reptiles. Nests in tall trees by water.

haliaeetus pelagicus.name: Steller's sea eagle
haliaeetus pelagicus.desc: Prefers salmon and trout in rivers and eats waterbirds on the coast. Dead spawned salmon feed those wintering inland.

haliaeetus sanfordi.name: Sanford's sea eagle
haliaeetus sanfordi.desc: Found only in the Solomon Islands. It eats mostly carrion along the tideline plus fish, and sometimes birds and fruit bats from the canopy.

haliaeetus vocifer.name: African fish eagle
haliaeetus vocifer.desc: Hunts fish from perches over open water, and also takes waterbirds and carrion.

haliaeetus vociferoides.name: Madagascar fish eagle
haliaeetus vociferoides.desc: Critically endangered eagle of western wetlands and lakes that hunts fish.

haliastur indus.name: Brahminy kite
haliastur indus.desc: Mainly a scavenger of dead animals. It occasionally hunts live prey such as bats.

haliastur sphenurus.name: Whistling kite
haliastur sphenurus.desc: Hunts small mammals, birds, fish and reptiles and eats carrion. It hovers at grass fires to catch fleeing prey.

halichoerus grypus.name: Gray seal
halichoerus grypus.desc: Hunts fish, especially sand eels, and hauls out in large numbers on outer Cape beaches.

halictus tripartitus.name: Tripartite Sweat Bee
halictus tripartitus.desc: Tripartite Sweat Bee (Halictus tripartitus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 206 times near the park in GBIF.

halimeda.name: Reef algae
halimeda.desc: Chalky green seaweed growing on reefs and sandy flats. Grazed by parrotfish and snails.

halimeda spp..name: Macroalgae
halimeda spp..desc: Seaweeds on reef flats that grazers keep from smothering the coral.

haliotis cracherodii.name: Black abalone
haliotis cracherodii.desc: A herbivorous snail that feeds mostly on drift algae and kelp. Critically endangered after overfishing and withering syndrome.

halocnemum strobilaceum.name: Saltmarsh glasswort
halocnemum strobilaceum.desc: A salt-tolerant shrub of saline coastal marshes around the Persian Gulf, which binds salty ground at the edge of the tidal flats.

halodule.name: Seagrass
halodule.desc: Underwater meadows in shallow lagoons and bays, grazed by green turtles and, in places, manatees.

halodule uninervis.name: Seagrass
halodule uninervis.desc: Underwater meadows that shelter young fish and feed turtles and dugongs.

halogeton glomeratus.name: Barilla
halogeton glomeratus.desc: Barilla (Halogeton glomeratus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 97 times near the park in GBIF.

halophila.name: Seagrass
halophila.desc: Fast-growing seagrass of shallow sandy bottoms; Halophila is a favoured food of dugongs.

halophila ovalis.name: Paddle weed
halophila ovalis.desc: A small, fast-growing seagrass that quickly colonises bare patches. Halophila is among the seagrasses dugongs eat most.

haloxylon ammodendron.name: Black saxaul
haloxylon ammodendron.desc: A tough desert shrub or small tree of loose sand. In the Gobi it is often the only tree, and its roots help hold dunes in place.

haloxylon persicum.name: White saxaul
haloxylon persicum.desc: A shrubby saxaul of shifting sands, one of the best-recorded plants in the area.

halyomorpha halys.name: Marmorated brown stink bug
halyomorpha halys.desc: Marmorated brown stink bug (Halyomorpha halys): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

halysidota tessellaris.name: Banded tussock moth
halysidota tessellaris.desc: Banded Tussock Moth (Halysidota tessellaris): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

hamanumida daedalus.name: Guinea-fowl butterfly
hamanumida daedalus.desc: A savanna butterfly whose caterpillars feed on legumes and whose adults are eaten by bee-eaters.

hamelia patens.name: Scarletbush
hamelia patens.desc: Shrub with nectar-rich flowers and small fruit; GloBI records bats, birds and butterflies feeding on it.

harmonia axyridis.name: Harlequin ladybird
harmonia axyridis.desc: Harlequin ladybird (Harmonia axyridis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

harpia harpyja.name: Harpy eagle
harpia harpyja.desc: Plucks sloths and monkeys from the canopy with enormous talons.

harpyopsis novaeguineae.name: Papuan eagle
harpyopsis novaeguineae.desc: A big forest eagle that hunts from the canopy. It takes possums, tree-kangaroos, forest wallabies and woolly rats, as well as birds and reptiles.

heaven lake and meltwater.name: Heaven Lake and meltwater
heaven lake and meltwater.desc: The crater lake on the summit feeds the Songhua, Tumen and Yalu rivers, and its shores support a few hundred plant species.

heavy pacific rain.name: Heavy Pacific rain
heavy pacific rain.desc: Wet maritime weather feeds the temperate rainforest and the many streams and lakes that run to the sea.

heavy rain.name: Heavy rain
heavy rain.desc: Wet tropical climate across the park, from the Arafura coast to the summits.

heavy rain and fog.name: Heavy rain and fog
heavy rain and fog.desc: Winter rain and summer fog drip keep the forest constantly wet; the Hoh and Quinault valleys are among the rainiest places in the continental US.

heavy rainfall.name: Heavy rainfall
heavy rainfall.desc: Over 7,000 mm of rain a year feeds more than 200 waterfalls and the cloud forest, the only humid tropical forest on an oceanic island in the region.

hediste diversicolor.name: Ragworm
hediste diversicolor.desc: A common mudflat worm that feeds on surface mud and organic particles. Fish, crabs and shorebirds hunt it.

hedone vibex.name: Hedone vibex
hedone vibex.desc: Hedone vibex (Hedone vibex): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

hedysarum alpinum.name: Alpine sweetvetch
hedysarum alpinum.desc: Alpine sweetvetch (Hedysarum alpinum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

helarctos malayanus.name: Sun bear
helarctos malayanus.desc: An omnivore that eats insects such as termites and ants, honey and fruit including figs. The tiger is its main predator.

helenium amarum.name: Bitter sneezeweed
helenium amarum.desc: Bitter sneezeweed (Helenium amarum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

heleobia.name: Heleobia snails
heleobia.desc: Tiny freshwater snails, many found only in the lake. They graze on the lake bottom and are eaten by frogs and fish.

heliamphora.name: Tepui pitcher plants
heliamphora.desc: Carnivorous plants of the tepuis that trap insects, mostly ants, in leaf pitchers to make up for scarce nutrients; many rely on bacteria to digest the prey.

helianthus annuus.name: Sunflower
helianthus annuus.desc: Sunflower (Helianthus annuus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

helianthus mollis.name: Ashy Sunflower
helianthus mollis.desc: Ashy Sunflower (Helianthus mollis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

helianthus petiolaris.name: Lesser sunflower
helianthus petiolaris.desc: An annual sunflower of sandy, disturbed soil whose seeds suit seed-eating rodents.

helichrysum.name: Everlasting shrubs
helichrysum.desc: Shrubby everlastings of the highlands; their spread into rodent habitat is listed as a pressure on the Ethiopian wolf.

helichrysum luteoalbum.name: Daisy
helichrysum luteoalbum.desc: Daisy (Helichrysum luteoalbum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

heliconia.name: Heliconia
heliconia.desc: Large-leaved herbs of forest openings and edges, common in the lowlands of Costa Rica.

heliotropium curassavicum.name: Seaside Heliotrope
heliotropium curassavicum.desc: Seaside Heliotrope (Heliotropium curassavicum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

heliotropium indicum.name: Indian Heliotrope
heliotropium indicum.desc: Indian Heliotrope (Heliotropium indicum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

heloderma suspectum.name: Gila monster
heloderma suspectum.desc: A slow venomous lizard that raids burrows and nests for eggs and small animals.

hemaris diffinis.name: Bumblebee Moth
hemaris diffinis.desc: Bumblebee Moth (Hemaris diffinis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

hemerocallis fulva.name: Orange Day-lily
hemerocallis fulva.desc: Orange Day-lily (Hemerocallis fulva): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

hemiargus hanno.name: Common Blue butterfly
hemiargus hanno.desc: A small butterfly whose caterpillars feed on legumes such as crab's eye. A source of insect food for lizards.

hemiechinus auritus.name: Long-eared hedgehog
hemiechinus auritus.desc: A small desert hedgehog that hunts at night for beetles and other invertebrates, and also takes small lizards.

hemiphaga novaeseelandiae.name: Kererū (NZ pigeon)
hemiphaga novaeseelandiae.desc: Mainly eats fruit, plus leaves, flowers and buds. Possums and rats compete for fruit and take eggs; stoats and cats kill adults and young.

hemitragus jemlahicus.name: Himalayan tahr
hemitragus jemlahicus.desc: Grazes grasses and browses shrubs on steep rocky slopes, moving downslope in winter. Snow leopards prey on it.

hepatica acutiloba.name: Sharp-lobed hepatica
hepatica acutiloba.desc: Sharp-lobed hepatica (Hepatica acutiloba): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 55 times near the park in GBIF.

hepatica americana.name: American hepatica
hepatica americana.desc: American hepatica (Hepatica americana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.

heptapleurum actinophyllum.name: Umbrella tree
heptapleurum actinophyllum.desc: Its fruit is eaten by birds, spectacled flying foxes, musky rat-kangaroos and red-legged pademelons. Its leaves feed tree-kangaroos.

heracleum maximum.name: Cow parsnip
heracleum maximum.desc: Cow parsnip (Heracleum maximum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 721 times near the park in GBIF.

heritiera fomes.name: Sundri
heritiera fomes.desc: The tree that gives the Sundarbans its name. UNESCO-listed forest descriptions and Wikipedia note it is very sensitive to rising salinity.

herpestes ichneumon.name: Egyptian mongoose
herpestes ichneumon.desc: A common Iberian carnivore that hunts rabbits, birds, reptiles and amphibians. The Iberian lynx often kills it.

herpestes javanicus.name: Small Indian mongoose
herpestes javanicus.desc: An introduced predator and the most recorded mammal near the park. It eats rodents, insects, birds and eggs and was named as a predator of nēnē.

hesperia comma.name: Common Branded Skipper
hesperia comma.desc: Common Branded Skipper (Hesperia comma): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

hesperis matronalis.name: Dame's-violet
hesperis matronalis.desc: Dame's-violet (Hesperis matronalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 88 times near the park in GBIF.

hesperostipa comata.name: Needle-and-thread grass
hesperostipa comata.desc: Needle-and-thread grass (Hesperostipa comata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

hesperoyucca whipplei.name: Our Lord's-candle
hesperoyucca whipplei.desc: Our Lord's-candle (Hesperoyucca whipplei): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 136 times near the park in GBIF.

hetaerina americana.name: American Rubyspot
hetaerina americana.desc: American Rubyspot (Hetaerina americana): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

heterodon platirhinos.name: Eastern Hognose Snake
heterodon platirhinos.desc: Eastern Hognose Snake (Heterodon platirhinos): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

heterohyrax brucei.name: Bruce's yellow-spotted hyrax
heterohyrax brucei.desc: A rock-dwelling mammal that lives in colonies in rocky terrain. Hyraxes eat a wide variety of plants and are hunted by raptors, snakes and carnivores.

heteromys desmarestianus.name: Desmarest's spiny pocket mouse
heteromys desmarestianus.desc: A small forest-floor rodent that eats seeds and fruit and is prey for snakes and small cats.

heteropogon contortus.name: Black speargrass
heteropogon contortus.desc: Another tall savanna grass listed for the park, growing alongside kangaroo grass on the dry hillsides.

heterotheca subaxillaris.name: Camphorweed
heterotheca subaxillaris.desc: Camphorweed (Heterotheca subaxillaris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

heterotheca villosa.name: Hairy false goldenaster
heterotheca villosa.desc: Hairy false goldenaster (Heterotheca villosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

hexaprotodon liberiensis.name: Pygmy hippopotamus
hexaprotodon liberiensis.desc: Forages at dusk on herbs, ferns, shoots and fallen fruit. Camera traps confirmed it in Sapo in 2008. Liberia holds most of the wild population.

hexastylis arifolia.name: Littlebrownjug
hexastylis arifolia.desc: Littlebrownjug (Hexastylis arifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 132 times near the park in GBIF.

hibiscus laevis.name: Scarlet rose-mallow
hibiscus laevis.desc: Scarlet rose-mallow (Hibiscus laevis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

hibiscus moscheutos.name: Common Rose-mallow
hibiscus moscheutos.desc: Common Rose-mallow (Hibiscus moscheutos): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

hieraaetus pennatus.name: Booted eagle
hieraaetus pennatus.desc: A small eagle that hunts birds, lizards and small mammals. GloBI records link it to chukar, ground squirrels and many small birds.

hierophis cypriensis.name: Cyprus whip snake
hierophis cypriensis.desc: Endemic to Cyprus and widespread in Troodos; eats lizards, amphibians, insects and other snakes.

hierophis gemonensis.name: Balkan racer
hierophis gemonensis.desc: A fast, slender snake of the Balkans that hunts lizards and small mammals.

highland mist.name: Highland mist
highland mist.desc: Cliffs and mountains catch cloud and mist, creating wetter refuges where many endemic plants grow.

highland soil.name: Highland soil
highland soil.desc: Nutrients recycled from dead plants and dung in the cool plateau soil feed the grasses, heath and lobelia.

hilaria rigida.name: Big galleta
hilaria rigida.desc: Tough bunchgrass of sandy and rocky desert ground, one of the main grasses available to grazers here.

himatione sanguinea.name: ʻApapane
himatione sanguinea.desc: A native honeycreeper that drinks ʻōhiʻa nectar and pollinates it. It also takes insects and spiders, mostly moths and butterflies in one study.

hippocamelus bisulcus.name: Huemul
hippocamelus bisulcus.desc: An endangered Andean deer of scrub and forest borders. Lenga is a common item in its diet, and the puma is its only natural predator.

hippodamia convergens.name: Convergent lady beetle
hippodamia convergens.desc: Convergent lady beetle (Hippodamia convergens): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 23 times near the park in GBIF.

hippophae rhamnoides.name: Sea buckthorn
hippophae rhamnoides.desc: Thorny shrub of riverbeds and valleys whose roots host nitrogen-fixing bacteria. Its berries are eaten by magpies and other birds.

hippopotamus amphibius.name: Hippopotamus
hippopotamus amphibius.desc: Grazes grass on land at night and rests in water by day. Its dung moves land nutrients into rivers, where it feeds fish and invertebrates.

hipposideros armiger.name: Great roundleaf bat
hipposideros armiger.desc: A large cave-roosting bat recorded often in the area. Ten threatened bat species have been recorded in the park, and bats eat flying insects at night.

hipposideros cervinus.name: Fawn leaf-nosed bat
hipposideros cervinus.desc: An insect-eating cave-roosting bat; it takes beetles and moths in flight close to vegetation, and is the most recorded mammal near Santo.

hippotragus equinus.name: Roan antelope
hippotragus equinus.desc: A large grass-eating antelope of Sudanian savanna, recorded often in the Arly area.

hodotermitidae.name: Harvester termites
hodotermitidae.desc: Termites that gather dry grass and carry it underground, turning scarce plant matter into food for other animals.

holbrookia maculata.name: Bleached earless lizard
holbrookia maculata.desc: A pale lizard of the White Sands dunes that eats insects and spiders. Its pale colour matches the sand.

holcosus undulatus.name: Rainbow ameiva
holcosus undulatus.desc: A fast ground lizard of forest floors that forages for insects and other small invertebrates.

honckenya peploides.name: Sea Sandwort
honckenya peploides.desc: Sea Sandwort (Honckenya peploides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

hopea.name: Hopea and other lowland trees
hopea.desc: Evergreen tropical wet forest on limestone below 800 m covers about three quarters of the park. Hopea is one of its listed trees, and the leaves and fruit of such trees feed primates and other forest animals.

hoplitis pilosifrons.name: Hairy-fronted Small-Mason
hoplitis pilosifrons.desc: Hairy-fronted Small-Mason (Hoplitis pilosifrons): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 78 times near the park in GBIF.

hordeum jubatum.name: Foxtail Barley
hordeum jubatum.desc: Foxtail Barley (Hordeum jubatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

hordeum spontaneum.name: Wild barley
hordeum spontaneum.desc: A wild grass that GBIF records often in the reserve. Seed-eating birds such as blackbirds are recorded eating barley in GloBI.

hot, salty shallow water.name: Hot, salty shallow water
hot, salty shallow water.desc: The Gulf is shallow and very saline. Its seagrasses tolerate a wide range of salinity, which helps them hold the shallows.

houbaropsis bengalensis.name: Bengal florican
houbaropsis bengalensis.desc: Endangered bird of tall grassland; Manas holds the largest population anywhere according to Wikipedia.

houstonia caerulea.name: Azure Bluet
houstonia caerulea.desc: Azure Bluet (Houstonia caerulea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 43 times near the park in GBIF.

houstonia procumbens.name: Roundleaf bluet
houstonia procumbens.desc: Roundleaf bluet (Houstonia procumbens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

houstonia pusilla.name: Tiny bluet
houstonia pusilla.desc: Tiny bluet (Houstonia pusilla): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

howea forsteriana.name: Kentia palm
howea forsteriana.desc: A palm found naturally only on Lord Howe Island, and a defining tree of its forests. Wild seeds are collected for a regulated export trade.

hudsonia tomentosa.name: Beach heath
hudsonia tomentosa.desc: Beach heath (Hudsonia tomentosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 73 times near the park in GBIF.

human food waste.name: Human food waste
human food waste.desc: Trash, compost, pet food and bird-feeder seed are an extra food supply for raccoons, coyotes, squirrels and urban birds.

humulus scandens.name: Japanese Hop
humulus scandens.desc: Japanese Hop (Humulus scandens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

hurricane winds.name: Hurricane winds
hurricane winds.desc: Hugo, Georges, Irma and Maria damaged the forest and cut parrot numbers. Open gaps let pioneer trees such as pumpwood take over.

huso huso.name: Beluga sturgeon
huso huso.desc: Giant migratory fish that runs up the Danube to spawn. Adults eat mainly large fish; it is critically endangered.

hyaena hyaena.name: Striped hyena
hyaena hyaena.desc: A shy scavenger of the dry forest that cleans up carcasses left by tigers and leopards.

hyalella.name: Hyalella amphipods
hyalella.desc: Small freshwater crustaceans, many endemic to the lake. They are a main food of the Titicaca water frog.

hydrangea quercifolia.name: Oak-leaf hydrangea
hydrangea quercifolia.desc: Oak-leaf hydrangea (Hydrangea quercifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 62 times near the park in GBIF.

hydrastis canadensis.name: Goldenseal
hydrastis canadensis.desc: Goldenseal (Hydrastis canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

hydrocharis morsus-ranae.name: Frogbit
hydrocharis morsus-ranae.desc: Frogbit (Hydrocharis morsus-ranae): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 37 times near the park in GBIF.

hydrochoerus hydrochaeris.name: Capybara
hydrochoerus hydrochaeris.desc: The world's largest rodent grazes riverbank plants and rests in water to avoid predators.

hydrocotyle bonariensis.name: Largeleaf pennywort
hydrocotyle bonariensis.desc: Largeleaf pennywort (Hydrocotyle bonariensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

hydrocynus forskahlii.name: Elongate tigerfish
hydrocynus forskahlii.desc: A fast predatory fish recorded in the Sudd system that hunts smaller fish.

hydrophyllum appendiculatum.name: Great waterleaf
hydrophyllum appendiculatum.desc: Great waterleaf (Hydrophyllum appendiculatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

hydropotes inermis.name: Chinese water deer
hydropotes inermis.desc: Lives among tall reeds, swamps and fields along rivers. Wikipedia says the DMZ has given it protected habitat, and that its Korean boom is linked to the loss of tigers and leopards.

hydroprogne caspia.name: Caspian tern
hydroprogne caspia.desc: Large tern that plunges for fish, hunting over bays and sometimes travelling far from its colony to feed.

hydrurga leptonyx.name: Leopard seal
hydrurga leptonyx.desc: Apex predator that eats penguins, other seals and krill, which it strains through its teeth.

hylaeus affinis.name: Eastern Masked Bee
hylaeus affinis.desc: Eastern Masked Bee (Hylaeus affinis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

hylaeus leptocephalus.name: Slender-faced Masked Bee
hylaeus leptocephalus.desc: Slender-faced Masked Bee (Hylaeus leptocephalus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

hyles lineata.name: White-lined sphinx moth
hyles lineata.desc: A hawk-moth whose caterpillars and adults feed on desert flowers and shrubs, and which is eaten by birds and lizards.

hylobates funereus.name: Eastern grey gibbon
hylobates funereus.desc: Wikipedia calls it the best-known arboreal mammal of the park, living mostly in the canopy. Gibbons mainly eat fruit.

hylobates lar.name: White-handed gibbon
hylobates lar.desc: Mostly eats fruit (about half its diet), plus leaves, insects and flowers; figs are a favourite. Long-term studies of its social life were done at Khao Yai.

hymenocallis occidentalis.name: Carolina spider-lily
hymenocallis occidentalis.desc: Carolina spider-lily (Hymenocallis occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

hymenolaimus malacorhynchos.name: Whio (blue duck)
hymenolaimus malacorhynchos.desc: Endangered duck of fast, clean mountain rivers that eats mainly midge and caddisfly larvae. Stoats destroy nests and kill nesting females.

hymenophyllum.name: Filmy ferns
hymenophyllum.desc: Thin-leaved ferns that thrive in constantly humid air; ferns are among the most recorded plants on the island.

hymenoxys hoopesii.name: Orange-sneezeweed
hymenoxys hoopesii.desc: Orange-sneezeweed (Hymenoxys hoopesii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

hymenoxys subintegra.name: Arizona rubberweed
hymenoxys subintegra.desc: Arizona rubberweed (Hymenoxys subintegra): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 28 times near the park in GBIF.

hyparrhenia.name: Thatching grasses
hyparrhenia.desc: Tall tropical grasses of the savanna, grazed when young and dry and flammable by the end of the dry season.

hyperacrius fertilis.name: True's vole
hyperacrius fertilis.desc: A small rodent recorded near the plateau. Voles of this kind are generally plant eaters and are prey for small carnivores and raptors.

hypericum perforatum.name: Perforate St John's-wort
hypericum perforatum.desc: Perforate St John's-wort (Hypericum perforatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.

hypericum revolutum.name: St. John's wort shrubs
hypericum revolutum.desc: An evergreen mountain shrub that the mountain nyala is recorded browsing.

hypersaline water.name: Hypersaline water
hypersaline water.desc: Hamelin Pool is about twice as salty as normal seawater, which suits stromatolite builders and keeps out animals that would graze them.

hyphaene coriacea.name: Doum palm
hyphaene coriacea.desc: A palm of the valley floor, recorded in the park, with fruit that elephants eat.

hyphaene petersiana.name: Real fan palm
hyphaene petersiana.desc: A palm of island and floodplain fringes whose fruit is eaten by elephants.

hyphantria cunea.name: Fall webworm
hyphantria cunea.desc: A moth caterpillar that feeds on the leaves of many trees, including cypress, maple and beech.

hypogeomys antimena.name: Giant jumping rat
hypogeomys antimena.desc: A rabbit-sized burrowing rodent of western dry forest that eats plant material from the forest floor.

hypolimnas bolina.name: Great eggfly (blue moon)
hypolimnas bolina.desc: A common butterfly whose caterpillars feed on forest-edge plants; adults visit flowers.

hypophthalmichthys molitrix.name: Silver carp (invasive)
hypophthalmichthys molitrix.desc: A filter feeder that eats mostly phytoplankton and also zooplankton. Competes with paddlefish, gizzard shad and young fish. The NPS works to keep invasive carp downstream.

hypopitys monotropa.name: Yellow Bird's-nest
hypopitys monotropa.desc: Yellow Bird's-nest (Hypopitys monotropa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

hypoxis curtissii.name: Curtis' star-grass
hypoxis curtissii.desc: Curtis' star-grass (Hypoxis curtissii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

hypoxis hirsuta.name: Common Goldstar
hypoxis hirsuta.desc: Common Goldstar (Hypoxis hirsuta): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.

hypsiprymnodon moschatus.name: Musky rat-kangaroo
hypsiprymnodon moschatus.desc: Eats fruit, fungi and invertebrates on the forest floor and scatter-hoards fruit, which can help seeds establish.

hystrix indica.name: Indian crested porcupine
hystrix indica.desc: A large rodent recorded near the park that eats roots, fruit and bark. Leopards hunt it.

icaricia icarioides.name: Boisduval's Blue
icaricia icarioides.desc: Boisduval's Blue (Icaricia icarioides): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

ichthyaetus hemprichii.name: Sooty gull
ichthyaetus hemprichii.desc: A very commonly recorded gull on this coast. Gulls are known to take turtle hatchlings as they crawl to the sea.

icthyophaga ichthyaetus.name: Grey-headed fish eagle
icthyophaga ichthyaetus.desc: A raptor of the park wetlands that Wikipedia lists among its fish-eating birds.

ictidomys tridecemlineatus.name: Thirteen-lined ground squirrel
ictidomys tridecemlineatus.desc: Eats seeds and insects, hibernates, and is a main prey of badgers and hawks.

idiocerus snowi.name: Idiocerus snowi
idiocerus snowi.desc: Idiocerus snowi (Idiocerus snowi): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

iguana iguana.name: Green iguana
iguana iguana.desc: A big leaf-eating lizard of the island forest, preyed on by birds and mammals when young.

iguazu river and falls.name: Iguazu River and falls
iguazu river and falls.desc: The river runs about 23 km through the park past the falls. Spray and river moisture keep the riverbank forest dense and green.

ilex glabra.name: Appalachian-tea
ilex glabra.desc: Appalachian-tea (Ilex glabra): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.

ilex mitis.name: African holly
ilex mitis.desc: A montane evergreen tree whose fruits are taken by turacos, bulbuls and other forest birds.

ilex opaca.name: American Holly
ilex opaca.desc: American Holly (Ilex opaca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 69 times near the park in GBIF.

ilex vomitoria.name: Yaupon
ilex vomitoria.desc: Yaupon (Ilex vomitoria): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

imantodes cenchoa.name: Blunthead treesnake
imantodes cenchoa.desc: A slender tree snake recorded in GloBI eating anoles.

impatiens capensis.name: Orange Balsam
impatiens capensis.desc: A moisture-loving wildflower of wet ground and stream edges. GloBI records cottontails and groundhogs eating it.

imperata cylindrica.name: Cogon grass
imperata cylindrica.desc: A tall grass of the open grasslands on the plateau, grazed by large herbivores such as elephants and sambar.

imperata cylindrica, saccharum.name: Tall grasses
imperata cylindrica, saccharum.desc: Tall wet grassland of cogon and Saccharum grasses that can reach several metres. It gives food, cover and nesting material to many grassland animals.

incilius alvarius.name: Sonoran Desert toad
incilius alvarius.desc: Big toad that emerges after summer rains to eat insects and other small prey.

infertile soils.name: Infertile soils
infertile soils.desc: The park's soils are poor and unsuited to farming, so nutrients returned by dung and decay matter to plant growth.

inga marginata.name: Inga
inga marginata.desc: A legume tree of the Atlantic Forest whose fruit is eaten by tapirs, capuchins and birds in GloBI records.

inga vera.name: Ice-cream bean
