inga vera.desc: A leguminous tree whose fruit pulp is eaten by many bats, birds and monkeys, per GloBI feeding records.

insecta.name: Forest insects
insecta.desc: Beetles, caterpillars and other insects feeding on forest foliage; food for birds.

intense sunlight.name: Intense sunlight
intense sunlight.desc: Thin air at 4,200 to 5,400 m means strong sun for the algae, grasses and cushion plants.

ipomoea imperati.name: Beach morningglory
ipomoea imperati.desc: Beach morningglory (Ipomoea imperati): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

ipomoea lacunosa.name: White Morning-glory
ipomoea lacunosa.desc: White Morning-glory (Ipomoea lacunosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

ipomoea pes-caprae.name: Bayhops
ipomoea pes-caprae.desc: Bayhops (Ipomoea pes-caprae): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

ipomoea quamoclit.name: Cypressvine
ipomoea quamoclit.desc: Cypressvine (Ipomoea quamoclit): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

ipomoea sagittata.name: Saltmarsh morningglory
ipomoea sagittata.desc: Saltmarsh morningglory (Ipomoea sagittata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

ipomopsis aggregata.name: Scarlet gilia
ipomopsis aggregata.desc: Scarlet gilia (Ipomopsis aggregata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

ips typographus.name: European spruce bark beetle
ips typographus.desc: A bark beetle that breeds under spruce bark and mainly attacks Norway spruce. Woodpeckers strip bark to reach its larvae.

iridomyrmex.name: Meat ants and other ants
iridomyrmex.desc: Ants are abundant in the red centre and are the staple food of the thorny devil. Many also hunt or scavenge other insects.

iris hartwegii.name: Sierra iris
iris hartwegii.desc: Sierra iris (Iris hartwegii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 160 times near the park in GBIF.

iris missouriensis.name: Rocky Mountain iris
iris missouriensis.desc: Blue Flag; Rocky Mountain Iris (Iris missouriensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 35 times near the park in GBIF.

iris pseudacorus.name: Paleyellow iris
iris pseudacorus.desc: Paleyellow iris (Iris pseudacorus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.

iris verna.name: Dwarf iris
iris verna.desc: Dwarf iris (Iris verna): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 45 times near the park in GBIF.

iris virginica.name: Blue flag
iris virginica.desc: Blue flag (Iris virginica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 56 times near the park in GBIF.

iron.name: Iron
iron.desc: Scarce in surface water, so it limits how much phytoplankton can grow.

irvingia gabonensis.name: Wild mango trees
irvingia gabonensis.desc: A large-seeded forest tree of the Congo Basin; its fruit is a food for forest animals, and elephants help carry its seeds.

irvingia gabonensis and relatives.name: Large-fruited forest trees
irvingia gabonensis and relatives.desc: Big-seeded trees such as wild mango depend on large animals to carry their seeds away. In the Cuvette Centrale many of them rely on forest elephants.

isa textula.name: Crowned Slug
isa textula.desc: Crowned Slug (Isa textula): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

ischaemum timorense.name: Timor murainagrass
ischaemum timorense.desc: A grass recorded in the park area. Grasses of this kind grow in open and floodplain ground and feed grazers such as deer.

island grasses.name: Grasses
island grasses.desc: Grasses and low plants of the arid lowlands and the wetter highlands. Tortoises, finches and introduced goats graze them.

island soil nutrients.name: Island soil nutrients
island soil nutrients.desc: Thin volcanic soils are enriched by decaying leaves and by nutrients the seabirds bring in from the sea.

island soils.name: Island soils
island soils.desc: Many islands began as termite mounds. Salts gather in island centres, and nutrients wash through the flooded margins.

isoberlinia doka.name: Isoberlinia doka
isoberlinia doka.desc: A dominant tree of Sudanian woodland on the deeper soils of the Atakora escarpment, according to Wikipedia. Baboons are recorded eating it.

isoptera.name: Termites
isoptera.desc: Termites and leafcutter ants are described as main herbivores and decomposers of the Cerrado. Their nests are a food source for anteaters.

jabiru mycteria.name: Jabiru
jabiru mycteria.desc: A huge stork that wades in shallows for fish, snails, frogs and snakes, and also eats carrion and dead fish in dry spells.

jaculus and relatives.name: Jerboas
jaculus and relatives.desc: Small, long-legged hopping rodents that shelter in burrows by day and forage at night on seeds and plant matter.

jarava ichu.name: Ichu bunchgrass
jarava ichu.desc: A tussock grass common on the altiplano slopes and rocky shores around the lake.

jikradia olitoria.name: Coppery Leafhopper
jikradia olitoria.desc: Coppery Leafhopper (Jikradia olitoria): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

juglans regia.name: Wild walnut
juglans regia.desc: Feral walnut trees grow in the river flood-land forests of the reserve. The nuts are a rich food for animals such as wild boar.

junco hyemalis.name: Dark-eyed Junco
junco hyemalis.desc: Dark-eyed Junco (Junco hyemalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1,078 times near the park in GBIF.

juncus dudleyi.name: Dudley Rush
juncus dudleyi.desc: Dudley Rush (Juncus dudleyi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

juncus effusus.name: Soft Rush
juncus effusus.desc: Soft Rush (Juncus effusus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

juncus ensifolius.name: Sword-leaved Rush
juncus ensifolius.desc: Sword-leaved Rush (Juncus ensifolius): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

juncus maritimus.name: Sea rush and salt meadow
juncus maritimus.desc: Rushes and salt-tolerant grasses of the brackish meadows where semi-wild horses and cattle graze.

juncus pelocarpus.name: Brownfruit Rush
juncus pelocarpus.desc: Brownfruit Rush (Juncus pelocarpus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

juncus xiphioides.name: Irisleaf rush
juncus xiphioides.desc: Irisleaf rush (Juncus xiphioides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

juniperus deppeana.name: Checker-bark juniper
juniperus deppeana.desc: Checker-bark juniper (Juniperus deppeana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

juniperus drupacea.name: Syrian juniper
juniperus drupacea.desc: A juniper of the mountain slopes that grows alongside cedar in Lebanon and Turkey.

juniperus occidentalis.name: Western juniper
juniperus occidentalis.desc: Western juniper (Juniperus occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 27 times near the park in GBIF.

juniperus osteosperma.name: Utah juniper
juniperus osteosperma.desc: A drought-tough tree of dry slopes. Its berry-like cones feed birds and small mammals, and jackrabbits and rodents help spread its seeds.

juniperus phoenicea.name: Phoenician juniper
juniperus phoenicea.desc: An evergreen tree of the reserve highlands. Its berry-like cones are mainly spread by birds that eat them.

juniperus polycarpos.name: Juniper
juniperus polycarpos.desc: The dominant tree of the reserve in sparse stands at mid altitude. Cinereous vultures nest on the old trees.

juniperus procera.name: African juniper
juniperus procera.desc: Evergreen conifer that dominates the Daallo escarpment forest alongside wild olive. Its blue-black berry-like cones feed birds such as bulbuls and pigeons.

juniperus sabina.name: Savin juniper
juniperus sabina.desc: Low evergreen shrub of dry slopes. Ibex browse juniper twigs in winter, and birds eat the cones.

juniperus scopulorum.name: Rocky Mountain juniper
juniperus scopulorum.desc: Rocky Mountain juniper (Juniperus scopulorum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

juniperus virginiana.name: Virginian Juniper
juniperus virginiana.desc: Virginian Juniper (Juniperus virginiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

junonia atlites.name: Grey pansy
junonia atlites.desc: A butterfly whose caterpillars feed on rice and other plants of open, wet ground.

junonia coenia.name: Common Buckeye
junonia coenia.desc: Common Buckeye (Junonia coenia): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

junonia grisea.name: Gray buckeye
junonia grisea.desc: Gray buckeye (Junonia grisea): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

kalahari sand and soil.name: Kalahari sand and soil
kalahari sand and soil.desc: Sandy soils recycle dung and dead plants into nutrients for grasses and trees.

kalmia latifolia.name: Calico-bush
kalmia latifolia.desc: Mountain laurel (Kalmia latifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

kaloula pulchra.name: Banded bullfrog
kaloula pulchra.desc: Burrowing frog that eats ants, termites and other small insects.

karst groundwater.name: Karst groundwater
karst groundwater.desc: Rain sinks straight through the porous limestone and surfaces as cenotes and springs, supplying the freshwater that wetlands and mangroves depend on.

karst limestone soil.name: Karst limestone soil
karst limestone soil.desc: The park sits on a forested karst landscape of limestone, with sinkholes, caves and thin soils.

karst springs and prespa seepage.name: Karst springs and Prespa seepage
karst springs and prespa seepage.desc: Springs on the eastern shore give about half of the lake's inflow, and over a fifth comes underground from Lake Prespa.

kentropyx calcarata.name: Striped forest whiptail
kentropyx calcarata.desc: A fast ground lizard of Amazonian and Guianan forests. It is recorded as prey of the fer-de-lance.

kerodon rupestris.name: Rock cavy
kerodon rupestris.desc: A rodent introduced by the military in the 1960s as game. Feral cats prey on it.

kinyongia tavetana.name: Kilimanjaro two-horned chameleon
kinyongia tavetana.desc: A chameleon found only on the mountain that hunts insects.

kniphofia foliosa.name: Red hot poker
kniphofia foliosa.desc: Tall flowering plant of the highlands. Mountain nyala eat it, and Ethiopian wolves have been seen drinking its nectar.

kobuk river.name: Kobuk River
kobuk river.desc: The river divides the park. Caribou cross it each year, and its valley is a wetland that supports willows and sedges.

kobus ellipsiprymnus.name: Waterbuck
kobus ellipsiprymnus.desc: The most recorded large mammal near the park. Mostly grazes grass and stays close to water.

kobus kob.name: Kob
kobus kob.desc: A grassland antelope, most numerous of the large herbivores recorded here. It feeds on grasses and stays near water.

kobus leche.name: Southern lechwe
kobus leche.desc: A floodplain antelope that grazes wet ground and is hunted by lions, leopards and wild dogs.

kobus megaceros.name: Nile lechwe
kobus megaceros.desc: An endangered, semi-aquatic antelope of the Sudd floodplains that grazes marsh vegetation in shallow water.

kobus vardonii.name: Puku
kobus vardonii.desc: A floodplain antelope of grassland near water and the best-recorded large grazer in the park area.

koeberlinia spinosa.name: Crown of thorns
koeberlinia spinosa.desc: Crown of thorns (Koeberlinia spinosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

koeleria.name: Tussock grass
koeleria.desc: Tufted grasses of the open moorland and tussock grassland above the tree line.

krascheninnikovia ceratoides.name: Pamirian winterfat
krascheninnikovia ceratoides.desc: A low, hardy shrub of dry mountain steppe and one of the most recorded plants near the park.

krascheninnikovia lanata.name: Winterfat
krascheninnikovia lanata.desc: Winterfat (Krascheninnikovia lanata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 59 times near the park in GBIF.

krigia biflora.name: Orange dwarf-dandelion
krigia biflora.desc: Orange dwarf-dandelion (Krigia biflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

krigia virginica.name: Virginia Dwarf-dandelion
krigia virginica.desc: Virginia Dwarf-dandelion (Krigia virginica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

kuroshio warm current.name: Kuroshio warm current
kuroshio warm current.desc: A warm ocean current flows past the Ryukyu islands and keeps the sea around the island warm, supporting its plankton and marine life.

labridae.name: Wrasses
labridae.desc: A varied family of reef fishes that eat small invertebrates; wrasses are common on coral reefs.

lactuca graminifolia.name: Grassleaf lettuce
lactuca graminifolia.desc: Grassleaf lettuce (Lactuca graminifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

ladeania lanceolata.name: Dune Scrufpea
ladeania lanceolata.desc: Dune Scrufpea (Ladeania lanceolata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

lagarosiphon.name: Aquatic plants
lagarosiphon.desc: Submerged water plants of the river channels and lagoons, a food base for plant-eating fish.

lagidium viscacia.name: Southern viscacha
lagidium viscacia.desc: A rock-dwelling rodent of the Andes that eats grasses, moss and lichens. The Andean mountain cat preys on it.

lagoon water.name: Warm, clear lagoon water
lagoon water.desc: Shallow, sheltered water inside the barrier reefs lets light reach seagrass beds and reef flats. Heat waves and silt are threats to such water.

lagopus lagopus.name: Willow ptarmigan
lagopus lagopus.desc: A ground bird of tundra and shrubland that eats berries, buds and willow, and is prey for foxes, wolves, lynx and eagles.

lagopus muta.name: Rock ptarmigan
lagopus muta.desc: The only bird that stays in Svalbard through winter, living on buds, twigs and seeds of low tundra plants.

lagostrophus fasciatus.name: Banded hare-wallaby
lagostrophus fasciatus.desc: A nocturnal vegetarian that shelters in dense thickets, favouring dune wattle scrub. Natural populations survive only on Bernier and Dorre islands; reintroduced to Dirk Hartog Island.

lagothrix lagothricha.name: Brown woolly monkey
lagothrix lagothricha.desc: Mostly eats fruit, switching to leaves and insects when fruit is scarce. It is an effective seed disperser that keeps seeds in its gut for a long time.

laguncularia racemosa.name: White mangrove
laguncularia racemosa.desc: White mangrove (Laguncularia racemosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 29 times near the park in GBIF.

lake edward and rivers.name: Lake Edward and rivers
lake edward and rivers.desc: The lake and the Rutshuru and other rivers hold the hippos, fish and crocodiles and feed the plankton.

lake ira lalaro wetland.name: Lake Ira Lalaro wetland
lake ira lalaro wetland.desc: The park's large freshwater lake and flood plain; its marshy margins grow grasses and are grazed by village livestock.

lake issyk-kul.name: Lake Issyk-Kul
lake issyk-kul.desc: A huge, deep lake with no outlet. It is slightly salty (about 0.6%), so it rarely freezes even at 1,607 m, and it holds many wintering waterbirds.

lake magadi.name: Lake Magadi
lake magadi.desc: A shallow, seasonal soda lake in the south-west of the crater, fed mainly by the Munge Stream. Its alkaline water grows the algae flamingos eat.

lake michigan & wetlands.name: Lake Michigan & wetlands
lake michigan & wetlands.desc: The park runs along the lake shore, and Wikipedia says extensive wetlands fill many depressions between the dune ridges.

lake superior.name: Lake Superior
lake superior.desc: The cold lake surrounds the island and strongly shapes its lowland temperatures. Sheltered bays and inland lakes hold aquatic plants.

lake urema floods.name: Lake Urema floods
lake urema floods.desc: Seasonal flooding spreads water over the floodplain, from about 10 km2 in dry spells to about 200 km2 in wet years.

lake water.name: Lake water
lake water.desc: Cool, clear freshwater at high altitude with oxygen that is limited by elevation. Reeds and underwater plants grow in its shallows.

lake water and nutrients.name: Lake water and nutrients
lake water and nutrients.desc: A huge, deep, clear freshwater lake. Its nutrients and plankton carry the open-water food chains.

lakes & waterholes.name: Lakes & waterholes
lakes & waterholes.desc: The park holds many lakes and streams, Padam Talao being the largest. In a dry landscape they draw grazers and the crocodiles that live in them.

lakes and clear water.name: Lakes and clear water
lakes and clear water.desc: Rainy, Kabetogama, Namakan and Sand Point lakes make up a large share of the park and hold its fish, algae and loon nesting waters.

lakes and rivers.name: Lakes and rivers
lakes and rivers.desc: Glacial lakes and rivers such as Lake Clark and the Kvichak watershed carry sockeye to spawning grounds and feed lake algae.

lakes, ponds & wetlands.name: Lakes, ponds & wetlands
lakes, ponds & wetlands.desc: Thousands of lakes and ponds and a huge network of streams make water central to life in the park.

lama glama.name: Llama
lama glama.desc: Herded by local communities for wool and meat. Grazing by llamas and alpacas is a conservation concern in the reserve.

lama guanicoe.name: Guanaco
lama guanicoe.desc: A wild camelid that grazes grasses, shrubs, herbs and lichens on the steppe. Its natural predators include the puma and the culpeo.

lamium amplexicaule.name: Henbit Dead-nettle
lamium amplexicaule.desc: Henbit Dead-nettle (Lamium amplexicaule): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

lamium purpureum.name: Red Dead-nettle
lamium purpureum.desc: Red Dead-nettle (Lamium purpureum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 66 times near the park in GBIF.

lampropeltis triangulum.name: Milk snake
lampropeltis triangulum.desc: Milk snake (Lampropeltis triangulum): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

land-clearing fires.name: Land-clearing fires
land-clearing fires.desc: UNESCO lists regular fires set for farming and grazing around the reserve as a threat. Fire also shapes the grassland.

lanius collaris.name: Southern fiscal
lanius collaris.desc: A shrike that perches in the open and hunts insects and small vertebrates. GloBI records it eating striped mice.

lanius collurio.name: Red-backed shrike
lanius collurio.desc: A small predatory songbird that hunts insects, lizards and small birds from perches.

lanius cristatus.name: Brown shrike
lanius cristatus.desc: A small predatory bird that eats insects and small lizards. GloBI records it eating the brown mabuya skink.

lanius excubitor.name: Great grey shrike
lanius excubitor.desc: A predatory songbird that takes small rodents, birds and large insects, and impales prey on thorns.

lanius ludovicianus.name: Loggerhead shrike
lanius ludovicianus.desc: A songbird that hunts like a hawk, taking lizards, mice, insects and small birds.

lanius nubicus.name: Masked shrike
lanius nubicus.desc: Eats mostly large insects, occasionally small vertebrates, and impales prey on thorns. Breeds on Cyprus.

lanius schach.name: Long-tailed shrike
lanius schach.desc: A predatory songbird that hunts large insects and small vertebrates from perches.

lantana camara.name: Lantana
lantana camara.desc: A shrub of forest edges and clearings. Monkeys eat its fruit and butterflies visit its flowers.

laportea canadensis.name: Canada Lettuce
laportea canadensis.desc: Canada Lettuce (Laportea canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

large japanese field mouse.name: Large Japanese field mouse
large japanese field mouse.desc: A forest mouse that feeds mainly on seeds and nuts such as acorns, and is prey for many predators.

larix decidua.name: European larch
larix decidua.desc: The most common tree of the valley floors in the park, mixed with spruce and Swiss stone pine. It marks the upper forest edge.

larix gmelinii.name: Dahurian larch
larix gmelinii.desc: A hardy larch of the northern forests, among the most recorded plants around these volcanoes.

larix laricina.name: Tamarack
larix laricina.desc: A deciduous conifer of wet bogs and fens that drops its needles each autumn.

larix occidentalis.name: Hackmatack
larix occidentalis.desc: Hackmatack (Larix occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

larix sibirica.name: Siberian larch
larix sibirica.desc: A deciduous conifer that is among the most recorded plants near the site and forms much of the forest belt on the slopes.

larrea tridentata.name: Creosote bush
larrea tridentata.desc: A common evergreen desert shrub of the Chihuahuan Desert flats. Its flowers feed bees, and GloBI records show honey bees and other insects using it.

larus argentatus.name: Herring gull
larus argentatus.desc: A scavenging shore bird that picks up dead fish, including alewife die-offs, from the beach.

larus canus.name: Mew gull
larus canus.desc: Coastal and lakeshore gull that eats voles and scavenges salmon remains.

larus delawarensis.name: Ring-billed Gull
larus delawarensis.desc: Ring-billed Gull (Larus delawarensis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 104 times near the park in GBIF.

larus dominicanus.name: Kelp gull
larus dominicanus.desc: An omnivorous gull that scavenges and hunts. Since at least 1996 it has pecked at living right whales off Valdés.

larus fuscus.name: Lesser black-backed gull
larus fuscus.desc: Abundant gull of the flats and shores; it takes crabs and other shore prey and also preys on other waterbirds.

larus glaucescens.name: Glaucous-winged gull
larus glaucescens.desc: The most often recorded bird here. Gulls scavenge the remains bears leave from salmon.

larus hyperboreus.name: Glaucous gull
larus hyperboreus.desc: Eats eggs, chicks and carrion, often following polar bears and foxes.

larus marinus.name: Great black-backed gull
larus marinus.desc: Great Black-backed Gull (Larus marinus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 25,148 times near the park in GBIF.

larus michahellis.name: Yellow-legged gull
larus michahellis.desc: Opportunistic gull that scavenges. Around the Mediterranean it accounts for about half of the predation on flamingo eggs and chicks.

larus occidentalis.name: Western gull
larus occidentalis.desc: A gull that breeds on the islands and feeds on fish and scavenged carcasses; GloBI records it eating sea lion and seal.

larus pacificus.name: Pacific gull
larus pacificus.desc: A big gull that eats fish, crabs, cephalopods and other seashore animals, and scavenges scraps. Drops shellfish onto rocks to break them.

larus smithsonianus.name: American herring gull
larus smithsonianus.desc: A generalist that eats shore invertebrates such as mussels, fish, eggs and carrion. It drops shellfish on rocks to crack them.

lasioglossum acuminatum.name: Pointed Sweat Bee
lasioglossum acuminatum.desc: Pointed Sweat Bee (Lasioglossum acuminatum): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

lasioglossum admirandum.name: Admirable Sweat Bee
lasioglossum admirandum.desc: Admirable Sweat Bee (Lasioglossum admirandum): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.

lasioglossum cressonii.name: Cresson's Dialictus
lasioglossum cressonii.desc: Cresson's Dialictus (Lasioglossum cressonii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 152 times near the park in GBIF.

lasioglossum marinum.name: Lasioglossum marinum
lasioglossum marinum.desc: Lasioglossum marinum (Lasioglossum marinum): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 248 times near the park in GBIF.

lasioglossum paraforbesii.name: Bald-spot Sweat Bee
lasioglossum paraforbesii.desc: Bald-spot Sweat Bee (Lasioglossum paraforbesii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 55 times near the park in GBIF.

lasioglossum pilosum.name: Hairy Sweat Bee
lasioglossum pilosum.desc: Hairy Sweat Bee (Lasioglossum pilosum): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 965 times near the park in GBIF.

lasioglossum sisymbrii.name: Tansy Mustard Sweat Bee
lasioglossum sisymbrii.desc: Tansy Mustard Sweat Bee (Lasioglossum sisymbrii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 752 times near the park in GBIF.

lasioglossum titusi.name: Titus' Lasioglossum
lasioglossum titusi.desc: Titus' Lasioglossum (Lasioglossum titusi): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 848 times near the park in GBIF.

lasioglossum versatum.name: Experienced Sweat Bee
lasioglossum versatum.desc: Experienced Sweat Bee (Lasioglossum versatum): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

lates calcarifer.name: Barramundi
lates calcarifer.desc: Predatory fish of estuaries and rivers that eats smaller fish, crustaceans and molluscs. Mangrove and tidal areas are used for breeding and feeding.

lathyrus eucosmus.name: Semmly vetchling
lathyrus eucosmus.desc: Semmly vetchling (Lathyrus eucosmus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

lathyrus japonicus.name: Sea Pea
lathyrus japonicus.desc: Sea Pea (Lathyrus japonicus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.

laticauda saintgironsi.name: Yellow-lipped sea krait
laticauda saintgironsi.desc: A sea snake endemic to New Caledonia that hunts mostly eel-like fishes, about half of them lipspot morays.

lava and volcanic soil.name: Lava and volcanic soil
lava and volcanic soil.desc: New flows start as bare rock, and pioneers such as ʻōhiʻa colonise them and slowly build soil.

leaf litter and alluvial soil.name: Leaf litter and alluvial soil
leaf litter and alluvial soil.desc: Forest floor and river deposits where nutrients are recycled for trees and grasses.

leersia lenticularis.name: Catchfly grass
leersia lenticularis.desc: Catchfly grass (Leersia lenticularis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

leersia oryzoides.name: Cut-grass
leersia oryzoides.desc: Cut-grass (Leersia oryzoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

leitneria floridana.name: Corkwood
leitneria floridana.desc: Corkwood (Leitneria floridana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

lemmiscus curtatus.name: Sagebrush vole
lemmiscus curtatus.desc: Sagebrush vole (Lemmiscus curtatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 88 times near the park in GBIF.

lemmus lemmus.name: Norway lemming
lemmus lemmus.desc: Eats mainly sedges, grasses and moss. Its population booms and crashes every three to four years, which in turn drives its predators.

lemmus trimucronatus.name: Brown lemming
lemmus trimucronatus.desc: A tundra rodent that eats sedges and other plants and is a common prey of foxes and stoats.

lemna gibba.name: Fat Duckweed
lemna gibba.desc: Fat Duckweed (Lemna gibba): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

lemna trisulca.name: Ivy-leaved Duckweed
lemna trisulca.desc: Ivy-leaved Duckweed (Lemna trisulca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

lemna valdiviana.name: Pale Duckweed
lemna valdiviana.desc: Pale Duckweed (Lemna valdiviana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

lemniscomys striatus.name: Typical striped grass mouse
lemniscomys striatus.desc: A small rodent of grassland, forest edge and secondary forest up to about 1,700 m. GloBI records the rhinoceros viper eating it.

lemur catta.name: Ring-tailed lemur
lemur catta.desc: Opportunistic omnivore eating mainly fruit and leaves. Tamarind can make up a big share of its diet in the dry season.

leonia glycycarpa.name: Leonia tree
leonia glycycarpa.desc: A rainforest tree whose fruit is recorded in GloBI as food for monkeys and many fruit-eating birds.

leonurus cardiaca.name: Motherwort
leonurus cardiaca.desc: Motherwort (Leonurus cardiaca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

leopardus geoffroyi.name: Geoffroy's cat
leopardus geoffroyi.desc: A small spotted cat. GloBI records it eating guinea pigs and young capybara among other prey.

leopardus pardalis.name: Ocelot
leopardus pardalis.desc: A nocturnal hunter of agoutis, birds and small mammals.

leopardus tigrinus.name: Oncilla
leopardus tigrinus.desc: A small forest cat that hunts rodents, lizards, birds, eggs and invertebrates, and climbs well. Listed for El Imposible.

lepidium davisii.name: Davis' peppercress
lepidium davisii.desc: Davis' peppercress (Lepidium davisii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

lepidium draba.name: Hoary cress
lepidium draba.desc: A crucifer of open ground and field edges; crucifers are among the plants great bustards eat.

lepidium latifolium.name: Dittander
lepidium latifolium.desc: Dittander (Lepidium latifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

lepidium montanum.name: Mountain pepperplant
lepidium montanum.desc: Mountain pepperplant (Lepidium montanum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

lepidium perfoliatum.name: Perfoliate Pepperwort
lepidium perfoliatum.desc: Perfoliate Pepperwort (Lepidium perfoliatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

lepidium virginicum.name: Least Pepperwort
lepidium virginicum.desc: Least Pepperwort (Lepidium virginicum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

lepidochelys kempii.name: Kemp's ridley turtle
lepidochelys kempii.desc: A small sea turtle that feeds mainly on crabs.

lepidoptera.name: Moths
lepidoptera.desc: Night-flying insects whose caterpillars eat desert plants. Wikipedia lists moths first among the prey of Mexican free-tailed bats.

lepomis macrochirus.name: Bluegill & lagoon fish
lepomis macrochirus.desc: Sunfish and other fish stocked in Forest Park's lakes, which the Missouri Department of Conservation helps manage. Bluegill feed largely on small aquatic insects.

leptailurus serval.name: Serval
leptailurus serval.desc: A slender cat that hunts rodents, and is recorded in the park among the root-rat predators.

leptecophylla tameiameiae.name: Pūkiawe
leptecophylla tameiameiae.desc: A native shrub of forests, bogs and alpine shrubland. Nēnē and other birds eat its berries and spread the seeds.

leptinotarsa decemlineata.name: Colorado Beetle
leptinotarsa decemlineata.desc: Colorado Beetle (Leptinotarsa decemlineata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

leptobrachium montanum.name: Montane large-eyed litter frog
leptobrachium montanum.desc: A frog of the forest floor that eats small invertebrates.

leptonychotes weddellii.name: Weddell seal
leptonychotes weddellii.desc: Dives deep for fish, notably toothfish, and squid. Leopard seals and orcas may take it.

leptonycteris yerbabuenae.name: Lesser long-nosed bat
leptonycteris yerbabuenae.desc: A migratory nectar-feeding bat and the main night pollinator of saguaro and agave flowers.

leptopelis kivuensis.name: Kivu tree frog
leptopelis kivuensis.desc: The most recorded amphibian near the park, a tree frog that feeds on small insects in the forest.

leptoptilos crumenifer.name: Marabou stork
leptoptilos crumenifer.desc: A big scavenging stork recorded feeding at carcasses of large mammals.

leptoptilos dubius.name: Greater adjutant
leptoptilos dubius.desc: A stork that mostly eats carrion and offal but also catches fish and frogs. Kaziranga once held the only known breeding site.

leptosiphon parviflorus.name: Leptosiphon parviflorus
leptosiphon parviflorus.desc: Leptosiphon parviflorus (Leptosiphon parviflorus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

leptosiphon rattanii.name: Rattan's linanthus
leptosiphon rattanii.desc: Rattan's linanthus (Leptosiphon rattanii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

leptotila verreauxi.name: White-tipped dove
leptotila verreauxi.desc: A ground-feeding dove of forest floor and edges. It is recorded eating the berries of West Indian milkberry.

lepus americanus.name: Snowshoe hare
lepus americanus.desc: Snowshoe hare (Lepus americanus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

lepus arcticus.name: Arctic hare
lepus arcticus.desc: A large hare of the tundra that browses low plants such as heather and willow.

lepus californicus.name: Black-tailed jackrabbit
lepus californicus.desc: Black-tailed jackrabbit (Lepus californicus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

lepus capensis.name: Cape hare
lepus capensis.desc: A grass and herb eater of open ground, and a regular prey of foxes, jackals and eagles.

lepus coreanus.name: Korean hare
lepus coreanus.desc: A hare of grassy and scrubby ground that feeds on plants.

lepus europaeus.name: European hare
lepus europaeus.desc: An introduced grazer. GloBI records it as prey of pumas, culpeos, caracaras and condors.

lepus nigricollis.name: Indian hare
lepus nigricollis.desc: A small grass-eating hare recorded near the park; GloBI lists it as prey of tigers, leopards and civets.

lepus starcki.name: Ethiopian highland hare
lepus starcki.desc: Eats moorland grasses and lives on open Afroalpine ground. The Ethiopian wolf and tawny eagle prey on it.

lepus timidus.name: Mountain hare
lepus timidus.desc: A hare of the high Alps that browses grasses, herbs and shrubs and is prey for foxes, stoats and eagles.

lepus tolai.name: Tolai hare
lepus tolai.desc: A hare of steppe and semi-desert that feeds on grasses and shrubs and is prey for foxes and wolves.

lepus townsendii.name: White-tailed jackrabbit
lepus townsendii.desc: White-tailed jackrabbit (Lepus townsendii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.

lepus victoriae.name: African savanna hare
lepus victoriae.desc: Grass-eating hare of the dry land around the wetlands.

lerema accius.name: Clouded Skipper
lerema accius.desc: Clouded Skipper (Lerema accius): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 29 times near the park in GBIF.

lespedeza capitata.name: Dusty-clover
lespedeza capitata.desc: Dusty-clover (Lespedeza capitata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 93 times near the park in GBIF.

lespedeza cuneata.name: Chinese Bush-clover
lespedeza cuneata.desc: Chinese Bush-clover (Lespedeza cuneata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

lespedeza violacea.name: Violet Lespedeza
lespedeza violacea.desc: Violet Lespedeza (Lespedeza violacea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

lethrinus nebulosus.name: Spangled emperor
lethrinus nebulosus.desc: Eats mainly molluscs, echinoderms and crustaceans over reef, seagrass and sand. Recorded in the Persian Gulf and heavily fished there.

leucanthemum vulgare.name: Oxeye Daisy
leucanthemum vulgare.desc: Oxeye Daisy (Leucanthemum vulgare): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

leucophaeus atricilla.name: Laughing gull
leucophaeus atricilla.desc: Abundant coastal gull that joins shorebirds in feeding on horseshoe crab eggs on the beaches.

lewisiopsis tweedyi.name: Tweedy's pussypaws
lewisiopsis tweedyi.desc: Tweedy's pussypaws (Lewisiopsis tweedyi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 54 times near the park in GBIF.

leymus.name: Pamir grasses
leymus.desc: Wheatgrasses and related grasses are among the commonly recorded plants of the high Pamir steppe and feed grazers.

leymus triticoides.name: Beardless wild rye
leymus triticoides.desc: Beardless wild rye (Leymus triticoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

liana.name: Lianas and understory shrubs
liana.desc: Woody climbers are common in the reserve forest; their leaves and shoots feed many browsers.

liatris punctata.name: Dotted gayfeather
liatris punctata.desc: Dotted gayfeather (Liatris punctata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

liatris pycnostachya.name: Prairie blazingstar
liatris pycnostachya.desc: Prairie blazingstar (Liatris pycnostachya): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

libytheana carinenta.name: American Snout
libytheana carinenta.desc: American Snout (Libytheana carinenta): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

lichens & mosses.name: Lichens & mosses
lichens & mosses.desc: Hardy growth that survives above 5,000 m, and food for musk deer in winter.

licuala ramsayi.name: Fan palm
licuala ramsayi.desc: A large rainforest palm of the Wet Tropics. Cassowaries eat fruit from the palm family.

lilium columbianum.name: Oregon lily
lilium columbianum.desc: Oregon lily (Lilium columbianum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

lilium philadelphicum.name: Flame Lily
lilium philadelphicum.desc: Flame Lily (Lilium philadelphicum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

lime-rich karst water.name: Lime-rich karst water
lime-rich karst water.desc: Water running through limestone and dolomite becomes loaded with calcium carbonate, the material of the tufa barriers.

limenitis archippus.name: Viceroy
limenitis archippus.desc: Viceroy (Limenitis archippus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

limenitis arthemis.name: Red-spotted Admiral
limenitis arthemis.desc: Red-spotted Admiral (Limenitis arthemis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

limenitis lorquini.name: Lorquin's Admiral
limenitis lorquini.desc: Lorquin's Admiral (Limenitis lorquini): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

limestone desert soil.name: Limestone desert soil
limestone desert soil.desc: Thin, rocky soil over limestone. Dead plants and animals break down slowly here and return nutrients to it.

limestone karst.name: Limestone karst
limestone karst.desc: The drowned limestone towers and islets that give the bay its shape. Thin soils and caves shelter plants and animals.

limestone karst and caves.name: Limestone karst and caves
limestone karst and caves.desc: The park sits in one of the two largest karst regions on Earth. Cliffs, caves and thin limestone soils shape which plants grow and give langurs and bats places to roost.

limestone karst soil.name: Limestone karst soil
limestone karst soil.desc: Thin soils sit over limestone hills 200 to 300 m high, separated by sinkholes and riddled with caves.

limestone pavement.name: Limestone pavement
limestone pavement.desc: Bare limestone covers much of the uplands; the cracks hold ferns and flowers and the thin soil suits low specialist plants.

limestone ridges & soil.name: Limestone ridges & soil
limestone ridges & soil.desc: The park sits on parallel limestone ridges above swampy lowlands, which shape where water and trees are.

limestone soil.name: Limestone soil
limestone soil.desc: A thin soil over raised coral limestone that holds the turf, scrub and mangrove roots.

limestone soil and nutrients.name: Limestone soil and nutrients
limestone soil and nutrients.desc: Thin soils over Dinaric limestone hold the nutrients that alpine meadows, bogs and forests draw on.

limestone soil nutrients.name: Limestone soil nutrients
limestone soil nutrients.desc: Nutrients in the reserve's limestone soils, returned by decomposers.

limosa lapponica.name: Bar-tailed godwit
limosa lapponica.desc: A long-billed shorebird that eats mostly worms, with some bivalves and crustaceans. It breeds in the Arctic and winters along coasts of Europe and Africa.

limulus polyphemus.name: American horseshoe crab
limulus polyphemus.desc: Spawns on Delaware Bay beaches in spring, females laying thousands of eggs. It eats molluscs and worms.

linaria johannis.name: Warsangli linnet
linaria johannis.desc: A finch found only in Somalia, in dry forest and high shrubland. It is Near Threatened because of habitat loss and is one of the species behind the Daallo bird area.

linaria vulgaris.name: Common Toadflax
linaria vulgaris.desc: Common Toadflax (Linaria vulgaris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

lindernia dubia.name: Moistbank Pimpernel
lindernia dubia.desc: Moistbank Pimpernel (Lindernia dubia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

linnaea borealis.name: Twinflower
linnaea borealis.desc: Twinflower (Linnaea borealis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 30 times near the park in GBIF.

linum lewisii.name: Lewis's flax
linum lewisii.desc: Lewis's flax (Linum lewisii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

liquidambar styraciflua.name: Sweetgum
liquidambar styraciflua.desc: Sweetgum (Liquidambar styraciflua): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

liriodendron tulipifera.name: Tulip-tree
liriodendron tulipifera.desc: A tall hardwood of moist Appalachian forests; its leaves feed the caterpillars of the eastern tiger swallowtail.

lithobates clamitans.name: Green frog
lithobates clamitans.desc: A pond and swamp-edge frog eaten by water snakes and herons.

lithobates grylio.name: Pig frog
lithobates grylio.desc: A big aquatic frog of lakes and wet prairies. Amphibians are called bio-indicators of environmental health by the refuge.

lithobates pipiens.name: Northern Leopard Frog
lithobates pipiens.desc: Northern Leopard Frog (Lithobates pipiens): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 51 times near the park in GBIF.

lithobates sphenocephalus.name: Southern leopard frog
lithobates sphenocephalus.desc: A wetland frog that eats insects and is itself prey for snakes, owls and otters.

lithocarpus.name: Montane oaks
lithocarpus.desc: Stone oaks are among the trees of the montane forest zone, which Wikipedia describes as oak, then rhododendron and conifer forest as you climb.

lithospermum canescens.name: Indian-paint
lithospermum canescens.desc: Indian-paint (Lithospermum canescens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

lithospermum caroliniense.name: Hairy puccoon
lithospermum caroliniense.desc: Hairy puccoon (Lithospermum caroliniense): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

lithospermum multiflorum.name: Manyflowered gromwell
lithospermum multiflorum.desc: Manyflowered gromwell (Lithospermum multiflorum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 47 times near the park in GBIF.

lithospermum ruderale.name: Western gromwell
lithospermum ruderale.desc: Western gromwell (Lithospermum ruderale): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

little bluestem and others.name: Glade grasses & wildflowers
little bluestem and others.desc: Plants of open, rocky, sun-baked glades where the soil is thin and trees are few. Fire management helps keep glades open.

little missouri river.name: Little Missouri River
little missouri river.desc: The river that carved the badlands and runs through all three units of the park.

littorina littorea.name: Common periwinkle
littorina littorea.desc: A snail that scrapes algae off intertidal rocks. Its grazing changes which seaweeds grow where.

lobatus gigas.name: Queen conch
lobatus gigas.desc: A snail that browses algae and seagrass in meadows. Overfishing is a concern in the Bahamas, and the park is a no-fishing zone.

lobelia cardinalis.name: Cardinalflower
lobelia cardinalis.desc: Cardinalflower (Lobelia cardinalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

lobelia deckenii.name: Giant lobelia
lobelia deckenii.desc: A tall rosette plant of the high moorland and alpine zones, recorded very often in GBIF here.

lobelia giberroa.name: Giant lobelia
lobelia giberroa.desc: A tall flowering Afromontane lobelia of the Albertine Rift highlands, whose nectar-rich flowers suit sunbirds.

lobelia rhynchopetalum.name: Giant lobelia
lobelia rhynchopetalum.desc: A tall rosette plant of the Afroalpine zone, found in the Bale Mountains and also in the Simien Mountains.

lobelia siphilitica.name: Great Blue Lobelia
lobelia siphilitica.desc: Great Blue Lobelia (Lobelia siphilitica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

lobelia telekii.name: Giant lobelia
lobelia telekii.desc: A tall, hairy-spired rosette plant of the afro-alpine zone, one of the giant lobelias adapted to freezing nights.

lobodon carcinophaga.name: Crabeater seal
lobodon carcinophaga.desc: Despite its name it lives almost entirely on krill, and it rests and breeds on pack ice.

loess soil.name: Loess soil
loess soil.desc: Deep wind-blown silt, over 90 feet thick in places, forms the steep ridges and holds the roots of prairie plants.

lomatium foeniculaceum.name: Desert-parsley
lomatium foeniculaceum.desc: Desert-parsley (Lomatium foeniculaceum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

lomatium multifidum.name: Carrot-leaved biscuit-root
lomatium multifidum.desc: Carrot-leaved biscuit-root (Lomatium multifidum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

lomatium nudicaule.name: Naked-stem lomatium
lomatium nudicaule.desc: Naked-stem lomatium (Lomatium nudicaule): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

lomatium planosum.name: Lomatium planosum
lomatium planosum.desc: Lomatium planosum (Lomatium planosum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

long snowy winters.name: Long snowy winters
long snowy winters.desc: The summit is cold and snowy for much of the year, and Heaven Lake is usually frozen from mid-October to mid-June.

long summer daylight.name: Long summer daylight
long summer daylight.desc: Near-constant summer light lets plants and lake algae grow fast in the short warm season.

lonicera.name: Honeysuckle & berry shrubs
lonicera.desc: Honeysuckle is one of several berry-bearing shrubs and vines that Ussuri brown bears eat in the region.

lonicera maackii.name: Amur Honeysuckle
lonicera maackii.desc: Amur Honeysuckle (Lonicera maackii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

lontra canadensis.name: North American river otter
lontra canadensis.desc: North American river otter (Lontra canadensis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

lophocebus albigena.name: Grey-cheeked mangabey
lophocebus albigena.desc: A fruit-eating canopy monkey on the reserve species list; the white-collared mangabey is also protected there.

lophocebus aterrimus.name: Black crested mangabey
lophocebus aterrimus.desc: A forest monkey recorded in the park area. Monkeys of this kind are prey of leopards and crowned eagles.

lophoceros fasciatus.name: African pied hornbill
lophoceros fasciatus.desc: A frequently recorded forest bird of the Nimba circle. Hornbills take fruit and insects.

lophophorus impejanus.name: Himalayan monal
lophophorus impejanus.desc: Digs through snow for tubers, shoots and some insects in forest and alpine meadows, moving down in winter.

lophura leucomelanos.name: Kalij pheasant
lophura leucomelanos.desc: An introduced game bird, heavily recorded in the park area, that forages on the ground for fruit, seeds and insects. The ʻio takes game birds.

lophuromys makundii.name: Brush-furred mice
lophuromys makundii.desc: Small rodents of the highland grass and scrub, a staple prey for servals and jackals.

lorinseria areolata.name: Dwarf chain fern
lorinseria areolata.desc: Dwarf chain fern (Lorinseria areolata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

loripes lucinalis.name: Lucine clam
loripes lucinalis.desc: Small clam of seagrass sediments that lives with sulfide-eating bacteria; a principal prey of wintering red knots.

lotus corniculatus.name: Bird's-foot-trefoil
lotus corniculatus.desc: A low yellow-flowered legume of short grassland. Butterflies and bumblebees take its nectar.

loudetia simplex.name: Mountain grassland grass
loudetia simplex.desc: A perennial bunch grass of African grasslands. Montane grassland like this caps the Nimba ridge above the forest and is home to the endemic Nimba toad.

low-intensity fire.name: Low-intensity fire
low-intensity fire.desc: Frequent, low fires are part of the natural cycle in ponderosa pine forest, clearing litter and keeping the forest open.

loxia curvirostra.name: Red crossbill
loxia curvirostra.desc: Finch with a crossed bill adapted to prise seeds out of conifer cones; recorded in large numbers in the pine forests.

loxodonta.name: African elephant
loxodonta.desc: Eats bark, leaves and fruit, and spreads seeds through its dung as it moves through the forest.

loxodonta africana.name: African elephant
loxodonta africana.desc: Elephants that follow dry riverbeds and may walk up to 70 km at night between water points. They eat browse such as ana tree leaves and pods.

loxodonta cyclotis.name: African forest elephant
loxodonta cyclotis.desc: Eats bark, leaves and many fruits and carries seeds kilometres from the parent tree. Often called the megagardener of the forest.

luangwa river floods.name: Luangwa River floods
luangwa river floods.desc: The meandering river floods the plains each wet season and leaves lagoons that keep fish, hippos and crocodiles through the dry season.

lubomirskiidae.name: Baikal sponges
lubomirskiidae.desc: Endemic filter feeders found from shallows to over 500 m deep. Most are green from symbiotic algae in their tissue.

lucanus cervus.name: Stag beetle
lucanus cervus.desc: Large beetle whose larvae develop in rotting wood, especially of oak, for several years.

luciobarbus subquincunciatus.name: Mesopotamian barbel
luciobarbus subquincunciatus.desc: A large barbel of the Tigris-Euphrates system and a staple of marsh fisheries.

ludwigia grandiflora.name: Water primrose
ludwigia grandiflora.desc: A sprawling aquatic plant of shallow water, recorded often here. Plants of its family (Onagraceae) are among those marsh deer eat.

lupinus.name: Lupines & wildflowers
lupinus.desc: Lupine and other mountain wildflowers bloom in meadows as the snow melts and feed deer, pikas and ground squirrels.

lupinus arbustus.name: Crest Lupine
lupinus arbustus.desc: Crest Lupine (Lupinus arbustus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

lupinus bicolor.name: Miniature lupine
lupinus bicolor.desc: Miniature lupine (Lupinus bicolor): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

lupinus dalesae.name: Lupinus dalesae
lupinus dalesae.desc: Lupinus dalesae (Lupinus dalesae): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 40 times near the park in GBIF.

lupinus dalesiae.name: Quincy lupine
lupinus dalesiae.desc: Quincy lupine (Lupinus dalesiae): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 48 times near the park in GBIF.

lupinus leucophyllus.name: Woolly-leaf lupine
lupinus leucophyllus.desc: Woolly-leaf lupine (Lupinus leucophyllus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

lupinus perennis.name: Sundial Lupine
lupinus perennis.desc: Sundial Lupine (Lupinus perennis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 212 times near the park in GBIF.

lupinus polyphyllus.name: Garden Lupin
lupinus polyphyllus.desc: Garden Lupin (Lupinus polyphyllus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

lupinus sellulus.name: Donner Lake lupine
lupinus sellulus.desc: Donner Lake lupine (Lupinus sellulus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

lupinus sericeus.name: Silky lupine
lupinus sericeus.desc: Silky lupine (Lupinus sericeus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.

lupinus sparsiflorus.name: Coulter's lupine
lupinus sparsiflorus.desc: Coulter's lupine (Lupinus sparsiflorus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

lupulella mesomelas.name: Black-backed jackal
lupulella mesomelas.desc: A scavenging hunter of the coast and desert. On the Skeleton Coast it takes seal pups and carrion and even licks moisture from stones.

lutjanus campechanus.name: Red snapper
lutjanus campechanus.desc: A reef fish and one of the Gulf's major catches. Eats shrimp, crabs and fish.

lutjanus griseus.name: Gray snapper
lutjanus griseus.desc: Hunts crabs, shrimp and small fish around mangroves, docks and grass flats.

lutra lutra.name: Eurasian otter
lutra lutra.desc: Eats mainly fish, adding amphibians and other prey; it needs clean water with plenty of prey.

lutrogale perspicillata.name: Smooth-coated otter
lutrogale perspicillata.desc: A fish-eating otter of the Brahmaputra channels and beels, itself recorded as tiger prey.

lycalopex culpaeus.name: Culpeo
lycalopex culpaeus.desc: A larger fox that takes hares, rodents, fruit and carrion, and sometimes young guanacos.

lycalopex griseus.name: Patagonian fox
lycalopex griseus.desc: A small fox of steppe and scrub. Where it shares ground with the culpeo it eats more rodents and is pushed out of prey-rich areas.

lycalopex gymnocercus.name: Pampas fox
lycalopex gymnocercus.desc: An omnivorous fox of open country. GloBI records it eating Brazilian guinea pigs.

lycaon pictus.name: African wild dog
lycaon pictus.desc: Hunts in packs and wears down gazelles, zebra and wildebeest calves.

lycium chilense.name: Lycium (matorral shrubs)
lycium chilense.desc: Thorny desert shrubs recorded on the peninsula. Maras are reported to eat Lycium among other shrubs and herbs.

lycopus uniflorus.name: Bugleweed
lycopus uniflorus.desc: Bugleweed (Lycopus uniflorus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

lycorma delicatula.name: Spotted lanternfly
lycorma delicatula.desc: Spotted lanternfly (Lycorma delicatula): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 140 times near the park in GBIF.

lymantria dispar.name: Spongy (gypsy) moth
lymantria dispar.desc: An introduced moth whose caterpillars strip oak and other leaves. Infestations from the early 1990s weakened the park's oak forests.

lynx canadensis.name: Canada lynx
lynx canadensis.desc: A specialist whose diet is mostly snowshoe hares, from about a third to nearly all depending on season and supply. It also takes squirrels, birds and young caribou.

lynx lynx.name: Eurasian lynx
lynx lynx.desc: Prefers roe deer where common, and also takes hares, squirrels and foxes. Wolves compete with it and can suppress its numbers.

lynx pardinus.name: Iberian lynx
lynx pardinus.desc: About three-quarters of its food is European rabbit. It also takes ducks, young deer and smaller carnivores such as mongooses and genets.

lynx rufus.name: Bobcat
lynx rufus.desc: Bobcat (Lynx rufus): a top predator in this web. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

lyrurus mlokosiewiczi.name: Caucasian grouse
lyrurus mlokosiewiczi.desc: A sedentary Near Threatened bird of open slopes with low rhododendron scrub beside broadleaf forest in the Pontic Mountains.

lyrurus tetrix.name: Black grouse
lyrurus tetrix.desc: The emblem of the nature park and endangered in the High Fens. Eats bilberry shoots and berries and, in winter, conifer needles; chicks eat insects.

lysichiton americanus.name: American Skunkcabbage
lysichiton americanus.desc: American Skunkcabbage (Lysichiton americanus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

lysimachia borealis.name: American starflower
lysimachia borealis.desc: American starflower (Lysimachia borealis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

lysimachia nummularia.name: Creeping-jenny
lysimachia nummularia.desc: Creeping-jenny (Lysimachia nummularia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 207 times near the park in GBIF.

lysimachia radicans.name: Trailing yellow loosestrife
lysimachia radicans.desc: Trailing yellow loosestrife (Lysimachia radicans): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

lytechinus variegatus.name: Variegated sea urchin
lytechinus variegatus.desc: A small urchin of seagrass meadows that grazes turtlegrass blades.

lythrum alatum.name: Angled purple loosestrife
lythrum alatum.desc: Angled purple loosestrife (Lythrum alatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

lythrum salicaria.name: Rainbow weed
lythrum salicaria.desc: Rainbow weed (Lythrum salicaria): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

lytta magister.name: Master blister beetle
lytta magister.desc: Large desert beetle that feeds on plants such as brittlebush, according to GloBI records.

macaca arctoides.name: Stump-tailed macaque
macaca arctoides.desc: One of several macaques in the park. An omnivore that eats fruit, seeds and other plant matter, and also takes some small animals.

macaca cyclopis.name: Formosan rock macaque
macaca cyclopis.desc: Taiwan's only monkey, living in troops. It eats fruit, young leaves, buds and grass stems, plus insects, snails and bird eggs.

macaca fascicularis.name: Long-tailed macaque
macaca fascicularis.desc: A fruit-eating monkey recorded often on the islands, an omnivore that forages for fruit.

macaca fuscata.name: Yakushima macaque
macaca fuscata.desc: A subspecies of the Japanese macaque that eats young leaves, seeds, flowers, fruit and insects, with its diet shifting with season and temperature.

macaca leonina.name: Northern pig-tailed macaque
macaca leonina.desc: One of the most recorded mammals around the park. GloBI records it eating fruit and shrubs such as jambolan and melastome.

macaca mulatta.name: Rhesus macaque
macaca mulatta.desc: The most-recorded monkey in GBIF near the bay. A flexible omnivore that eats fruit and leaves of island forests.

macaca nemestrina.name: Southern pig-tailed macaque
macaca nemestrina.desc: A ground and tree foraging monkey that eats fruit. Wikipedia lists it among tiger prey in Sumatra.

macaca silenus.name: Lion-tailed macaque
macaca silenus.desc: An endangered omnivore of the rainforest canopy that eats fruit, seeds, flowers and insects, and spreads seeds.

macaca sinica.name: Toque macaque
macaca sinica.desc: An omnivorous monkey of Sri Lanka that eats fruit, seeds and insects.

macaranga.name: Macaranga
macaranga.desc: A fast-growing pioneer tree genus of African montane forest; the species here is common in the Kibira area and used for chimpanzee nests.

macaranga dioica.name: Macaranga
macaranga dioica.desc: A fast-growing pioneer tree that colonises gaps in the forest and is often recorded around Santo.

macaranga tanarius.name: Macaranga
macaranga tanarius.desc: A fast-growing pioneer tree of forest gaps. GloBI records show langurs, hornbills and doves eating its fruit.

macaria brunneata.name: Rannoch Looper
macaria brunneata.desc: Rannoch Looper (Macaria brunneata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

machaeranthera tanacetifolia.name: Takhoka-daisy
machaeranthera tanacetifolia.desc: Takhoka-daisy (Machaeranthera tanacetifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.

maclura pomifera.name: Osage-Orange
maclura pomifera.desc: Osage-Orange (Maclura pomifera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

macoma balthica.name: Baltic tellin
macoma balthica.desc: A small clam that lies buried in the mud and feeds at the surface. Red knots like this bivalve on European mudflats.

macrocystis pyrifera.name: Giant kelp
macrocystis pyrifera.desc: Fast-growing brown alga anchored to rock that forms a floating canopy. Many animals depend on it for food or shelter.

macroglossus minimus.name: Northern blossom bat
macroglossus minimus.desc: A small fruit and nectar bat. GloBI records show it eating fig fruit, and it helps pollinate and spread forest plants.

macrohectopus branickii.name: Pelagic amphipod
macrohectopus branickii.desc: An open-water amphipod, often compared to krill. Golomyanka and Baikal seals eat it.

macronectes giganteus.name: Southern giant petrel
macronectes giganteus.desc: Large seabird that scavenges carcasses of seals and penguins.

macrophthalmus.name: Sentinel crabs
macrophthalmus.desc: A genus of soft-bottom crabs living on tidal flats of the Indo-Pacific, hunted by shorebirds that specialise on crabs.

macropus agilis.name: Agile wallaby
macropus agilis.desc: Grazes mainly at night on grasses and herbs, often near rivers and billabongs. It is the most recorded mammal near the park and a staple prey of crocodiles and dingoes.

macrotermes.name: Termites & fungi
macrotermes.desc: Termites and the fungi that work with them break down dead grass and wood, and their mounds seed new islands.

macrotermes carbonarius.name: Fungus-growing termites
macrotermes carbonarius.desc: Termites that gather dead plant matter and recycle it; a food source for frogs and other small animals.

macrotermes spp..name: Termites
macrotermes spp..desc: Chew dead grass and wood, and their mounds enrich the soil around them.

madoqua saltiana.name: Salt's dik-dik
madoqua saltiana.desc: A tiny antelope of bushland and thickets in the Horn of Africa. It feeds mainly on leaves and shoots of acacia and other shrubs.

maesa lanceolata.name: Maesa
maesa lanceolata.desc: A common African shrub or small tree of forest edges and clearings. Its berries are eaten by many forest birds.

magnolia macrophylla.name: Big-leaf magnolia
magnolia macrophylla.desc: Big-leaf magnolia (Magnolia macrophylla): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 119 times near the park in GBIF.

mahonia aquifolium.name: Hollyleaved barberry
mahonia aquifolium.desc: Hollyleaved barberry (Mahonia aquifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

mahonia harrisoniana.name: Mahonia harrisoniana
mahonia harrisoniana.desc: Mahonia harrisoniana (Mahonia harrisoniana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 29 times near the park in GBIF.

mahonia nervosa.name: Cascade barberry
mahonia nervosa.desc: Cascade barberry (Mahonia nervosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 75 times near the park in GBIF.

mahonia repens.name: Oregon grape
mahonia repens.desc: Oregon grape (Mahonia repens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 105 times near the park in GBIF.

maianthemum canadense.name: Canada mayflower
maianthemum canadense.desc: Canada mayflower (Maianthemum canadense): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 67 times near the park in GBIF.

maianthemum racemosum.name: False Solomon's-seal
maianthemum racemosum.desc: False Solomon's-seal (Maianthemum racemosum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 88 times near the park in GBIF.

maianthemum trifolium.name: Threeleaf False Lily of The Valley
maianthemum trifolium.desc: Threeleaf False Lily of The Valley (Maianthemum trifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.

malaclemys terrapin.name: Diamondback terrapin
malaclemys terrapin.desc: A salt-marsh turtle that eats crabs, snails, clams, worms and fish. Raccoons are its main nest predator.

malacosoma americana.name: Eastern Tent Caterpillar
malacosoma americana.desc: Eastern Tent Caterpillar (Malacosoma americana): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

malayopython reticulatus.name: Reticulated python
malayopython reticulatus.desc: A giant constrictor. Wikipedia lists pythons as potential orangutan predators, and one swallowed a sun bear in Borneo.

malayopython timoriensis.name: Timor python
malayopython timoriensis.desc: A python of the Lesser Sunda islands that preys on rodents and birds. It is a top land predator in this web.

mallomys rothschildi.name: Rothschild's woolly rat
mallomys rothschildi.desc: A giant rodent of New Guinea forests that eats karuka nuts. It is one of the larger rats recorded in the park.

malus fusca.name: Oregon crab apple
malus fusca.desc: Oregon crab apple (Malus fusca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

malvaviscus arboreus.name: Wax mallow
malvaviscus arboreus.desc: A leafy understory shrub with red flowers and berry-like fruit that birds feed on.

mammillaria lasiacantha.name: Lace-spine Nipple Cactus
mammillaria lasiacantha.desc: Lace-spine Nipple Cactus (Mammillaria lasiacantha): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

manas river floods.name: Manas River floods
manas river floods.desc: The Manas River and its tributaries spread silt across the plains and keep the early-growth riverside grassland renewed.

mandrillus leucophaeus.name: Drill
mandrillus leucophaeus.desc: An omnivorous monkey that prefers fruit, including figs, and also eats leaves, seeds, mushrooms and invertebrates such as ants.

mandrillus sphinx.name: Mandrill
mandrillus sphinx.desc: A large ground-living monkey of the forest that eats fruit, seeds and invertebrates. Recorded near the park and listed among its primates.

manilkara.name: Coastal forest trees
manilkara.desc: Trees of the Somali coastal forest. A sapote relative, Manilkara sulcata, is recorded in GBIF data near the reserve.

manilkara zapota.name: Sapodilla (chicozapote)
manilkara zapota.desc: A large native tree of southern Mexico and Central America. Its sweet fruit is eaten widely and its latex is the source of chicle.

maniola jurtina.name: Meadow brown
maniola jurtina.desc: A common grassland butterfly whose caterpillars eat grasses; adults and larvae feed birds and frogs.

many species.name: Desert annuals & grasses
many species.desc: Wildflowers and grasses that sprout after winter and monsoon rains and set seed quickly.

marantaceae.name: Marantaceae herbs
marantaceae.desc: Broad-leaved herbs that carpet openings in the forest understory and feed gorillas and elephants.

marcgravia rectiflora.name: Lira vine
marcgravia rectiflora.desc: A climbing vine whose fruit and nectar are recorded in the diet of several forest birds.

margarops fuscatus.name: Pearly-eyed thrasher
margarops fuscatus.desc: An opportunistic omnivore that eats insects, fruit, lizards and frogs, and the eggs and nestlings of other birds. It competes with parrots for nest cavities.

marine algae.name: Ocean phytoplankton
marine algae.desc: Microscopic algae at the base of the ocean food web that feeds young salmon.

marisma flooding.name: Marisma flooding
marisma flooding.desc: Seasonal flooding of the Guadalquivir delta marshes makes the shallow lagoons that waterbirds and wintering waterfowl depend on.

marmaronetta angustirostris.name: Marbled duck
marmaronetta angustirostris.desc: A threatened dabbling duck of shallow wetlands. The marshes are reported to hold a large share of the world population.

marmota baibacina.name: Gray marmot
marmota baibacina.desc: A burrowing rodent of mountain meadows and steppe that eats grasses and flowering plants. Many predators take it, including wolves, foxes and birds of prey.

marmota bobak.name: Bobak marmot
marmota bobak.desc: Burrowing steppe rodent that lives in colonies and feeds on grasses and herbs.

marmota caligata.name: Hoary marmot
marmota caligata.desc: A large ground squirrel of alpine meadows that eats plants and is prey for bears and other carnivores.

marmota camtschatica.name: Black-capped marmot
marmota camtschatica.desc: A burrowing alpine rodent of north-eastern Siberia and Kamchatka that grazes herbs and is prey for bears and foxes.

marmota caudata.name: Long-tailed marmot
marmota caudata.desc: A burrowing herbivore of alpine meadow and steppe that hibernates from about September to spring.

marmota flaviventris.name: Yellow-bellied marmot
marmota flaviventris.desc: A burrowing rodent of rocky meadows that eats green plants and hibernates through the long snow season.

marmota himalayana.name: Himalayan marmot
marmota himalayana.desc: Colonial burrowing grazer of alpine grassland. Snow leopards, wolves, red foxes and golden eagles hunt it.

marmota marmota.name: Alpine marmot
marmota marmota.desc: Colonial burrower that grazes meadows through summer, fattens up, then hibernates for months. Sentinels whistle when predators approach.

marmota monax.name: Groundhog
marmota monax.desc: Groundhog (Marmota monax): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

marsh mud & nutrients.name: Marsh mud & nutrients
marsh mud & nutrients.desc: Tidal sediment holds the nutrients that marsh plants draw on.

marshes and fishponds.name: Marshes and fishponds
marshes and fishponds.desc: Marshes and artificial fishponds, first dug in 1914-1918 and again in the 1950s, add reed beds and open water to the grassland.

martes americana.name: American marten
martes americana.desc: Slender forest carnivore. GloBI records show it eating red squirrels and snowshoe hares.

martes caurina.name: Pacific marten
martes caurina.desc: A forest predator that favours deep-snow country and hunts rodents and birds.

martes flavigula.name: Yellow-throated marten
martes flavigula.desc: An agile omnivorous marten that hunts small animals and may take panda cubs.

martes foina.name: Beech marten
martes foina.desc: An agile omnivorous hunter that takes small mammals, birds and fruit. The nearby pine marten is also on the park list.

martes martes.name: European pine marten
martes martes.desc: Agile forest hunter that eats rodents and birds and also fruit such as rowan berries and bilberries.

martes zibellina.name: Sable
martes zibellina.desc: A forest-dwelling marten of the taiga. It can take seal pups that leave their ice dens.

mauritia flexuosa.name: Buriti palm
mauritia flexuosa.desc: A palm of wet ground that Wikipedia says tapirs, peccaries, fish and monkeys depend on for its fruit. It marks the vereda wetlands.

mayflies, caddisflies and midges.name: Aquatic insect larvae
mayflies, caddisflies and midges.desc: Larvae living in mud and on wood. They feed on algae and detritus and are a main food for freshwater drum.

mayflies, stoneflies, caddisflies.name: Stream insects
mayflies, stoneflies, caddisflies.desc: Larvae in cold streams feed on leaf litter and algae, and in turn feed trout and stream salamanders.

maylandia.name: Mbuna
maylandia.desc: Colourful, mostly endemic rock-dwelling cichlids, often specialised feeders on algae growing on rocks.

mazama americana.name: Red brocket
mazama americana.desc: A forest deer recorded near the park that browses leaves and eats fruit and fungi; prey for jaguars.

mazama gouazoubira.name: Gray brocket
mazama gouazoubira.desc: A small forest deer that browses leaves and fruit; reported as a viable population in the park.

mazama temama.name: Central American red brocket
mazama temama.desc: A small forest deer that browses leaves and picks up fallen fruit. It is a prey animal of the big cats.

meandering rivers.name: Meandering rivers
meandering rivers.desc: Rivers and oxbow lakes carry fish and keep shifting the floodplain forest.

medeola virginiana.name: Indian Cucumber
medeola virginiana.desc: Indian Cucumber (Medeola virginiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

megachile inermis.name: Unarmed Leafcutter
megachile inermis.desc: Unarmed Leafcutter (Megachile inermis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 39 times near the park in GBIF.

megachile latimanus.name: Leafcutting bee
megachile latimanus.desc: Leafcutting bee (Megachile latimanus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 39 times near the park in GBIF.

megachile mendica.name: Flat-tailed Leaf-cutter Bee
megachile mendica.desc: Flat-tailed Leaf-cutter Bee (Megachile mendica): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

megachile relativa.name: Golden-tailed Leafcutter Bee
megachile relativa.desc: Golden-tailed Leafcutter Bee (Megachile relativa): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 41 times near the park in GBIF.

megacyllene robiniae.name: Locust Borer
megacyllene robiniae.desc: Locust Borer (Megacyllene robiniae): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 69 times near the park in GBIF.

megalopyge crispata.name: Black-waved Flannel Moth
megalopyge crispata.desc: Black-waved Flannel Moth (Megalopyge crispata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 28 times near the park in GBIF.

megapodius reinwardt.name: Orange-footed scrubfowl
megapodius reinwardt.desc: A megapode that eats seeds, fallen fruit and invertebrates, incubating eggs in mounds of rotting leaf litter.

megaptera novaeangliae.name: Humpback whale
megaptera novaeangliae.desc: The most recorded mammal near the park. It feeds on krill and small schooling fish in the bay in summer.

megascolecidae.name: Earthworms
megascolecidae.desc: Soil animals that eat leaf litter and mix it into the soil. They are the food of the long-beaked echidna.

megastigmus albifrons.name: Megastigmus albifrons
megastigmus albifrons.desc: Megastigmus albifrons (Megastigmus albifrons): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

mekong sediment and nutrients.name: Mekong sediment and nutrients
mekong sediment and nutrients.desc: Floodwater from the Mekong carries silt and nutrients into the lake; sediment-bound phosphorus helps feed its algae.

melaleuca viridiflora.name: Paperbark
melaleuca viridiflora.desc: A paperbark tree of wet lowlands and floodplain edges. Its flowers are visited by honeyeaters.

melampodium leucanthum.name: Plains blackfoot
melampodium leucanthum.desc: Plains blackfoot (Melampodium leucanthum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.

melanerpes carolinus.name: Red-bellied Woodpecker
melanerpes carolinus.desc: Red-bellied Woodpecker (Melanerpes carolinus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 23 times near the park in GBIF.

melanerpes erythrocephalus.name: Red-headed Woodpecker
melanerpes erythrocephalus.desc: Red-headed Woodpecker (Melanerpes erythrocephalus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 78 times near the park in GBIF.

melanerpes formicivorus.name: Acorn woodpecker
melanerpes formicivorus.desc: In California acorns make up half or more of its diet, which it stores in drilled granary trees, also eating sap and insects. One of the best-recorded birds near the park.

melanerpes portoricensis.name: Puerto Rican woodpecker
melanerpes portoricensis.desc: An endemic woodpecker. GloBI records it eating fruit and the lizard Anolis krugi.

melanerpes uropygialis.name: Gila woodpecker
melanerpes uropygialis.desc: Digs a new nest hole in saguaros each season; abandoned holes shelter elf owls, flycatchers and other birds.

melanoplus bivittatus.name: Two-striped grasshopper
melanoplus bivittatus.desc: A large grasshopper that chews grasses and forbs and feeds birds such as prairie-chickens.

melanoplus borealis.name: Northern grasshopper
melanoplus borealis.desc: Chews grasses and wildflowers in summer and feeds birds, mice and other small predators.

melanoplus differentialis.name: Differential Grasshopper
melanoplus differentialis.desc: Differential Grasshopper (Melanoplus differentialis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

melanoplus femurrubrum.name: Red-legged Grasshopper
melanoplus femurrubrum.desc: Red-legged Grasshopper (Melanoplus femurrubrum): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

melanoplus sanguinipes.name: Migratory Grasshopper
melanoplus sanguinipes.desc: Migratory Grasshopper (Melanoplus sanguinipes): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

melanosuchus niger.name: Black caiman
melanosuchus niger.desc: The largest predator in the flooded forest, eating fish, capybaras and anything else it can ambush.

melanotaenia.name: Rainbowfish
melanotaenia.desc: Small schooling fish of creeks and billabongs, part of the park's rich freshwater fish fauna. They graze algae and small insects and feed larger fish.

melanthera nivea.name: Snow Squarestem
melanthera nivea.desc: Snow Squarestem (Melanthera nivea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

melastoma malabathricum.name: Malabar melastome
melastoma malabathricum.desc: A shrub of open and disturbed ground. GloBI records elephants and macaques eating it.

meleagris gallopavo.name: Wild turkey
meleagris gallopavo.desc: Leans on hard mast such as acorns in fall and winter and on insects in summer. Poults depend almost entirely on insects for their first month.

meleagris ocellata.name: Ocellated turkey
meleagris ocellata.desc: Found only on the Yucatan Peninsula. It eats insects, seeds, nuts and leaves, and roosts in trees to avoid jaguars.

meles meles.name: European badger
meles meles.desc: An omnivore that eats earthworms, small mammals, amphibians and fruit. Recorded in the area.

melicope elleryana.name: Pink-flowered doughwood
melicope elleryana.desc: The favoured food plant of the Ulysses butterfly caterpillar.

melilotus officinalis.name: Yellow sweetclover
melilotus officinalis.desc: Yellow sweetclover (Melilotus officinalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 46 times near the park in GBIF.

melissodes agilis.name: Agile Long-horned Bee
melissodes agilis.desc: Agile Long-horned Bee (Melissodes agilis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

melissodes bimaculatus.name: Two-spotted Longhorn
melissodes bimaculatus.desc: Two-spotted Longhorn (Melissodes bimaculatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 145 times near the park in GBIF.

melithreptus albogularis.name: White-throated honeyeater
melithreptus albogularis.desc: Small bird of savanna woodland and paperbarks that feeds on nectar and insects.

melosira arctica.name: Ice algae
melosira arctica.desc: Algae growing on the underside of sea ice that start the spring bloom.

melospiza melodia.name: Song Sparrow
melospiza melodia.desc: Song Sparrow (Melospiza melodia): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3,344 times near the park in GBIF.

melozone aberti.name: Abert's Towhee
melozone aberti.desc: Abert's Towhee (Melozone aberti): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1,018 times near the park in GBIF.

melozone crissalis.name: California Towhee
melozone crissalis.desc: California Towhee (Melozone crissalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 77 times near the park in GBIF.

meltwater and rivers.name: Meltwater and rivers
