meltwater and rivers.desc: Snow and glacier melt feeds the lakes, mires and the river delta that wets the valleys and lowlands of the site.

melursus ursinus.name: Sloth bear
melursus ursinus.desc: Eats termites and ants, plus fruit and honey. Chitwan is said to hold a high density of them. Tigers are its main predator.

mentzelia laevicaulis.name: Blazingstar mentzelia
mentzelia laevicaulis.desc: Blazingstar mentzelia (Mentzelia laevicaulis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 136 times near the park in GBIF.

mentzelia nuda.name: Bractless blazingstar
mentzelia nuda.desc: Bractless blazingstar (Mentzelia nuda): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

mephitis mephitis.name: Striped skunk
mephitis mephitis.desc: Striped skunk (Mephitis mephitis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

mercenaria mercenaria.name: Northern quahog
mercenaria mercenaria.desc: A hard clam buried in bay sediments that filters plankton from the water. Long harvested in Rhode Island.

meriones tristrami.name: Tristram's jird
meriones tristrami.desc: A burrowing rodent that eats seeds and leaves. One of the most-recorded mammals in the area, and small prey for many predators.

merops bulocki.name: Red-throated bee-eater
merops bulocki.desc: A very commonly recorded insect-hunting bird that catches prey in flight near riverbanks.

merops ornatus.name: Rainbow bee-eater
merops ornatus.desc: A bird that catches flying insects in the air, including dragonflies, and was recorded often around the park.

merops pusillus.name: Little bee-eater
merops pusillus.desc: A small bird that catches flying insects on the wing; recorded in GBIF data near the reserve.

merops viridis.name: Blue-throated bee-eater
merops viridis.desc: A bird that catches flying insects in the air. GloBI records it eating the giant honey bee near the park.

mertensia franciscana.name: Franciscan bluebells
mertensia franciscana.desc: Franciscan bluebells (Mertensia franciscana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

mertensia macdougalii.name: Macdougal's bluebells
mertensia macdougalii.desc: Macdougal's bluebells (Mertensia macdougalii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 29 times near the park in GBIF.

mertensia virginica.name: Virginia bluebells
mertensia virginica.desc: Virginia bluebells (Mertensia virginica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 47 times near the park in GBIF.

mesa soils.name: Mesa soils
mesa soils.desc: Thin, well-drained soils on the mesa tops hold the roots of the woodland and recycle nutrients from dead matter.

mesalina brevirostris.name: Blanford's short-nosed desert lizard
mesalina brevirostris.desc: A small desert lizard recorded in the area. It feeds on small invertebrates and is prey for wheatears, shrikes and monitors.

mesocentrotus franciscanus.name: Red sea urchin
mesocentrotus franciscanus.desc: Grazes kelp. Without sea otters, which were hunted out in the fur trade, urchins can multiply and threaten kelp forests.

metopium brownei.name: Black poisonwood
metopium brownei.desc: A common Yucatan tree with oily fruits that birds such as toucans and parrots are recorded eating.

metrosideros polymorpha.name: ʻŌhiʻa lehua
metrosideros polymorpha.desc: A native tree whose flowers give nectar to honeycreepers. It grows in many Hawaiian forests and is a foundation of the native forest.

metrosideros umbellata.name: Southern rata
metrosideros umbellata.desc: A flowering tree of the southern forests. Possums are recorded eating its foliage.

metroxylon sagu.name: Sago palm
metroxylon sagu.desc: A palm of lowland swamp forests in New Guinea. Its trunk starch is a staple food for people along rivers such as the Sepik, and each stem flowers once and then dies while suckers carry on.

miconia.name: Miconia shrubs
miconia.desc: Small-fruited melastome plants that are common in the forest understory. GloBI records show many bats, birds and mammals feeding on their fruit.

miconia ciliata.name: Miconia
miconia ciliata.desc: A small tree or shrub of the melastome family with berries that many forest birds eat.

microbes and fungi.name: Decomposers
microbes and fungi.desc: Microbes and fungi break down dead plants, droppings and carcasses slowly in the cold and return nutrients to the soil.

microcarbo pygmaeus.name: Pygmy cormorant
microcarbo pygmaeus.desc: A fish-eating bird nesting in reeds and willows. The delta holds the largest colony of the species.

microcoleus.name: Biological soil crust
microcoleus.desc: A living skin of cyanobacteria, lichens, mosses, algae and microfungi. It binds sand grains against erosion, soaks up scarce rain and fixes nitrogen, but is easily broken by footsteps.

microphytobenthos.name: Mud-surface diatoms
microphytobenthos.desc: Microscopic algae living in the top millimetres of tidal mud. They feed many deposit-feeding animals when the flats are exposed.

micropogonias undulatus.name: Atlantic croaker
micropogonias undulatus.desc: Hunts worms, small crustaceans and other bottom prey.

micropotamogale lamottei.name: Nimba otter shrew
micropotamogale lamottei.desc: A small nocturnal semi-aquatic insectivore living along creeks in the Nimba area. Mining runoff threatens its streams.

micropterus dolomieu.name: Smallmouth bass
micropterus dolomieu.desc: Cool, clear Ozark streams with rock or gravel bottoms. Eats minnows, crayfish and large aquatic insects, and its eggs and fry are eaten by sunfish.

micropterus salmoides.name: Largemouth bass
micropterus salmoides.desc: A fish predator of sloughs and canals that eats small fish and crayfish.

microscopic algae.name: Phytoplankton
microscopic algae.desc: Drifting microscopic algae that feed filter feeders such as mussels. General ecological knowledge.

microscopic animals.name: Zooplankton
microscopic animals.desc: Tiny drifting animals that graze algae and are eaten by fish larvae and small fish.

microtus agrestis.name: Field vole
microtus agrestis.desc: Small grass-eating rodent of damp meadows and a staple prey for foxes, buzzards and cranes.

microtus arvalis.name: Common vole
microtus arvalis.desc: A small grass-eating rodent of open ground, the staple prey of many small predators.

microtus chrotorrhinus.name: Rock vole
microtus chrotorrhinus.desc: Rock vole (Microtus chrotorrhinus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

microtus gregalis.name: Narrow-headed vole
microtus gregalis.desc: A small grass-eating vole of steppe and meadow; foxes, stoats, eagles and bears are recorded eating it in GloBI.

microtus ilaeus.name: Kazakhstan vole
microtus ilaeus.desc: Small grass-eating rodent of Tian Shan meadows, and a food source for many predators.

microtus longicaudus.name: Long-tailed vole
microtus longicaudus.desc: A small plant-eating rodent of meadows and shrubby ground, recorded often in the area. Food for bears and other predators.

microtus montanus.name: Montane vole
microtus montanus.desc: A small grass-eating rodent and a staple for foxes, coyotes, hawks and eagles.

microtus ochrogaster.name: Prairie vole
microtus ochrogaster.desc: Prairie vole (Microtus ochrogaster): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

microtus oeconomus.name: Tundra vole
microtus oeconomus.desc: A small rodent of wet tundra and a well-recorded species here. It eats sedges and other plants, and is prey for foxes, stoats and wolves.

microtus pennsylvanicus.name: Meadow vole
microtus pennsylvanicus.desc: Meadow vole (Microtus pennsylvanicus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

microtus pinetorum.name: Woodland vole
microtus pinetorum.desc: Woodland vole (Microtus pinetorum): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

microtus socialis.name: Social vole
microtus socialis.desc: A small rodent of open grassy ground that feeds on plants and is prey for many predators.

midnight sun.name: Midnight sun
midnight sun.desc: Long summer daylight gives a short, intense growing season on the tundra; winter is dark.

midnight sun & polar night.name: Midnight sun & polar night
midnight sun & polar night.desc: Plants and algae can only grow in the bright summer months, when the sun stays above the horizon for weeks; in winter the long polar night shuts growth down.

midnight sun and short summer.name: Midnight sun and short summer
midnight sun and short summer.desc: Above the Arctic Circle the summer sun barely sets, so plants race through a short growing season before long dark winters.

midsummer daylight.name: Midsummer daylight
midsummer daylight.desc: Near-continuous summer light drives a short, intense growing season, while the winters are dark and cold.

mild winters.name: Mild winters
mild winters.desc: The Atlantic coast climate is mild, one reason arctic-alpine and southern plants can grow side by side.

milvus migrans.name: Black kite
milvus migrans.desc: The most-recorded bird near the bay, a raptor that takes live prey and scavenges dead fish and scraps near boats and harbours.

milvus milvus.name: Red kite
milvus milvus.desc: Raptor and frequent scavenger. It takes small mammals and frogs, and feeds on carcasses.

mimetes cucullatus.name: Common pagoda
mimetes cucullatus.desc: A fynbos shrub whose seeds are carried underground by native ants, which helps them survive fires.

mimosa quadrivalvis.name: Fourvalve Mimosa
mimosa quadrivalvis.desc: Fourvalve Mimosa (Mimosa quadrivalvis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

mimus polyglottos.name: Northern Mockingbird
mimus polyglottos.desc: NORTHERN MOCKINGBIRD (Mimus polyglottos): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 586 times near the park in GBIF.

mineral licks.name: Mineral licks
mineral licks.desc: Natural mineral-rich spots that forest ungulates, elephants and tapirs visit to supplement their diet.

mineral salt lick.name: Mineral salt lick
mineral salt lick.desc: The Poung Nyied salt lick draws sambar and other animals from a wide area, giving them minerals.

mineral soils and salts.name: Mineral soils and salts
mineral soils and salts.desc: Volcanic, mineral-rich ground and salt flats around the lake. Little organic matter builds up in the heat.

mirounga leonina.name: Southern elephant seal
mirounga leonina.desc: Dives deep for squid and fish and also eats krill. Valdés is the only continental breeding colony, and orcas take weaned pups and juveniles.

mist & seasonal rain.name: Mist & seasonal rain
mist & seasonal rain.desc: The scarp catches moisture rising from the Gulf of Aden coast, and the two main rains (April to June and October to November) support the forest.

mitchella repens.name: Partridgeberry
mitchella repens.desc: Partridge-berry (Mitchella repens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 97 times near the park in GBIF.

mitragyna.name: Riverside forest trees
mitragyna.desc: Trees of the wet riverbank forest whose leaves and overhanging branches feed monkeys and manatees.

mixed ornamental and food plants.name: Gardens & fruiting plants
mixed ornamental and food plants.desc: Flower beds, vegetable plots and berry-bearing shrubs that give seeds, fruit and foliage to birds, rabbits and insects.

mobula alfredi.name: Reef manta ray
mobula alfredi.desc: Filters zooplankton from the water with its wide mouth.

moist dune sand.name: Moist dune sand
moist dune sand.desc: Wikipedia says moist sand just under the surface lets dune plants, the tiger beetle and Ord's kangaroo rat survive here.

mole-rat soil.name: Mole-rat soil
mole-rat soil.desc: Burrowing giant root-rats loosen the ground, and the refilled tunnels hold looser, more nutrient-rich soil than the surrounding turf.

molinia caerulea.name: Purple moor-grass
molinia caerulea.desc: Tussock grass that spreads over drained or degraded bog. It is named as one of the problems restoration projects try to reverse.

moloch horridus.name: Thorny devil
moloch horridus.desc: A spiny lizard that eats mostly ants and drinks by channelling dew and damp sand to its mouth. Birds and goannas prey on it.

momotus lessonii.name: Lesson's motmot
momotus lessonii.desc: A large forest bird that eats insects, small lizards and fruit.

monachus monachus.name: Mediterranean monk seal
monachus monachus.desc: Rare seal of Cap Blanc, home to the largest surviving colony; it eats octopus, squid, mullet and sardines.

monarda bradburiana.name: Eastern beebalm
monarda bradburiana.desc: Eastern beebalm (Monarda bradburiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.

monarda citriodora.name: Lemon beebalm
monarda citriodora.desc: Lemon beebalm (Monarda citriodora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

monarda fistulosa.name: Mintleaf Beebalm
monarda fistulosa.desc: Mintleaf Beebalm (Monarda fistulosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

moneses uniflora.name: One-flowered Wintergreen
moneses uniflora.desc: One-flowered Wintergreen (Moneses uniflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

monochamus scutellatus.name: Whitespotted sawyer
monochamus scutellatus.desc: Whitespotted sawyer (Monochamus scutellatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 35 times near the park in GBIF.

monotropa uniflora.name: Indianpipe
monotropa uniflora.desc: Indian-pipe (Monotropa uniflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 84 times near the park in GBIF.

monsoon and typhoon rain.name: Monsoon and typhoon rain
monsoon and typhoon rain.desc: Heavy seasonal rain keeps the mountain forests wet and feeds the streams that carve the steep valleys.

monsoon floods.name: Monsoon floods
monsoon floods.desc: Wet-season rain floods the plains for months, spreading nutrients and filling billabongs that support plants, fish and waterbirds.

monsoon rain.name: Monsoon rain
monsoon rain.desc: Summer monsoon rain waters the lower slopes and forests.

monsoon rain and mist.name: Monsoon rain and mist
monsoon rain and mist.desc: Moist air from the Sichuan basin rises against the mountains, giving the wet climate that keeps the forest and bamboo lush.

monsoon rainfall.name: Monsoon rainfall
monsoon rainfall.desc: Heavy seasonal rain keeps the lowland forest wet year round and feeds the rivers that cross the reserve.

monsoon rains.name: Monsoon rains
monsoon rains.desc: Heavy monsoon rain feeds the rivers and keeps the forest evergreen.

monsoon upwelling.name: Monsoon upwelling
monsoon upwelling.desc: Summer monsoon winds draw nutrient-rich water to the surface of the Arabian Sea, making it one of the most productive seas on Earth.

montane rainfall and mist.name: Montane rainfall and mist
montane rainfall and mist.desc: Frequent rain and cloud on the Congo-Nile divide keep this high-altitude forest moist and growing.

morelia viridis.name: Green tree python
morelia viridis.desc: Eats mainly small mammals, with some lizards. Wikipedia names green tree pythons as predators of birds in New Guinea.

morone saxatilis.name: Striped bass
morone saxatilis.desc: The bay is one of the biggest breeding areas for this large predator, which eats menhaden, herring, shad and other fish.

moschus berezovskii.name: Forest musk deer
moschus berezovskii.desc: A small, shy deer of the forest and thickets that browses leaves, shoots and lichens.

moschus chrysogaster.name: Alpine musk deer
moschus chrysogaster.desc: A shy browser of herbs, shrub leaves, mosses and lichens in high conifer and shrub forest.

moschus fuscus.name: Black musk deer
moschus fuscus.desc: Small, secretive deer of high forest that feeds on plants and lichen. Preyed on by dholes and other carnivores.

moschus moschiferus.name: Siberian musk deer
moschus moschiferus.desc: A small, nocturnal, fanged but herbivorous deer that lives on rocky forested slopes; lichens make up about 99% of its winter diet.

motacilla cinerea.name: Gray wagtail
motacilla cinerea.desc: A slim bird of mountain streams that catches insects, including butterflies.

mountain rain and cloud.name: Mountain rain and cloud
mountain rain and cloud.desc: Rainfall on the slopes, heaviest on the south-east, sets the forest and bamboo belts and fills the rivers that supply the region.

mountain soil.name: Mountain soil
mountain soil.desc: Thin, nutrient-poor mountain soils. Pitcher plants make up for scarce nitrogen by catching insects and animal droppings.

mountain soil and leaf litter.name: Mountain soil and leaf litter
mountain soil and leaf litter.desc: Forest litter and mountain soils hold the nutrients that trees and meadow plants draw on.

mountain soil and litter.name: Mountain soil and litter
mountain soil and litter.desc: Forest litter and meadow soil hold the nutrients that rhododendron, bamboo and conifers draw on.

mountain soils.name: Mountain soils
mountain soils.desc: Thin soils on rock and glacial debris supply nutrients to plants, topped up as dead matter is broken down.

mountain springs.name: Mountain springs
mountain springs.desc: About fifty springs make Nimba a water tower for the Cavally, Cestos and Sassandra rivers.

mountain streams.name: Mountain streams
mountain streams.desc: Cold, clean, fast-flowing rivers are the habitat blue ducks need.

mountain streams and pools.name: Mountain streams and pools
mountain streams and pools.desc: Headwater streams, pools and waterfalls of the plateau, part of a wider area that supplies fresh water to Lesotho, South Africa and Namibia.

mountain streams and rivers.name: Mountain streams and rivers
mountain streams and rivers.desc: Rivers such as the Tes carry mountain water down to the basin, which has no outflow to the sea.

moving sand dunes.name: Moving sand dunes
moving sand dunes.desc: Wind-shifted dunes up to about 30 m high hold salt-tolerant, sand-adapted plants that anchor the sand.

mud and nutrients.name: Mud and nutrients
mud and nutrients.desc: Intertidal mud holds the nutrients that mangroves, seagrass and algae use, and is where much dead matter ends up.

muddy tidal flats.name: Muddy tidal flats
muddy tidal flats.desc: Sheltered, muddy intertidal shores and salt flats where mangroves root, and where dead plant matter is broken down.

mugil.name: Mullet
mugil.desc: Schooling coastal fish of lagoons and mangrove channels. Crocodiles and pelicans eat them.

mugil cephalus.name: Flathead grey mullet
mugil cephalus.desc: A schooling fish of shallow bays that feeds on algae and detritus; common prey of birds, dolphins and crocodiles.

muhlenbergia pungens.name: Sandhill muhly
muhlenbergia pungens.desc: Sandhill muhly (Muhlenbergia pungens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.

mullidae.name: Goatfishes
mullidae.desc: Fish that probe the sand for small animals. Goatfish make up about two-thirds of the diet of wedge-tailed shearwaters.

munida gregaria.name: Lobster krill
munida gregaria.desc: A small red squat lobster that swarms in the waters around the Falklands and southern South America and feeds many seabirds and fish.

muntiacus muntjak.name: Indian muntjac
muntiacus muntjak.desc: A small forest deer that browses and eats fallen fruit. Prey of dholes and tigers.

muntiacus reevesi.name: Formosan Reeves's muntjac
muntiacus reevesi.desc: A small forest deer that eats herbs, shoots, fruits, fungi and nuts. It is the most recorded mammal in the surrounding area.

muntiacus vuquangensis.name: Giant muntjac
muntiacus vuquangensis.desc: A large forest deer listed in the park, a browser on leaves and fruit, and one of the hoofed animals bears are reported to kill.

muntingia calabura.name: Strawberry tree
muntingia calabura.desc: A fast-growing fruit tree of village edges and dry land around the lake, eaten by fruit bats.

mus musculoides.name: Temminck's mouse
mus musculoides.desc: A small African rodent of grassy and bushy habitats; prey for the Great Lakes bush viper.

mus musculus.name: House mouse
mus musculus.desc: House mouse (Mus musculus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

muscardinus avellanarius.name: Hazel dormouse
muscardinus avellanarius.desc: A small arboreal rodent of hazel-rich woods that eats nuts, buds, flowers and some insects.

mustela erminea.name: Stoat
mustela erminea.desc: A small weasel that hunts voles, lemmings and birds. GloBI records both foxes and wolves eating it.

mustela nigripes.name: Black-footed ferret
mustela nigripes.desc: Lives in prairie dog burrows and eats mostly prairie dogs. Reintroduced near the park; about 100 live in the park.

mustela sibirica.name: Siberian weasel
mustela sibirica.desc: A small hunter of voles, hares and birds in forests and meadows.

mya truncata.name: Clams & seafloor worms
mya truncata.desc: Filter sinking algae from the seafloor and feed walruses.

myadestes obscurus.name: ʻŌmaʻo
myadestes obscurus.desc: A native thrush that mainly eats fruit, and also takes insects and small invertebrates.

mycteria americana.name: Wood stork
mycteria americana.desc: An endangered wader that feeds on fish concentrated in drying pools. Pythons have been found to eat storks.

mycteria leucocephala.name: Painted stork
mycteria leucocephala.desc: Wading bird that sweeps its bill through shallows for small fish and frogs; nests in colonies in trees near water.

myctophidae.name: Lanternfish
myctophidae.desc: Small deep-water fish that rise toward the surface at night to feed on plankton. Spinner dolphins hunt small fish of this kind.

myiagra vanikorensis.name: Vanikoro flycatcher
myiagra vanikorensis.desc: Mainly catches insects from a perch, and also takes lizards and small fruits.

myiarchus barbirostris.name: Sad flycatcher
myiarchus barbirostris.desc: A Jamaican flycatcher that hunts insects. The Jamaican boa is known to eat flycatcher nests.

myocastor coypus.name: Coypu
myocastor coypus.desc: Coypu (Myocastor coypus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

myodes gapperi.name: Gapper's Red-backed Mouse
myodes gapperi.desc: A small forest-floor rodent that eats plants, seeds and fungi and is a staple for owls.

myodes glareolus.name: Bank vole
myodes glareolus.desc: The most recorded mammal near the forest. It eats seeds, berries and herbs, and feeds foxes and owls.

myodes rufocanus.name: Grey red-backed vole
myodes rufocanus.desc: A common small rodent of forest and shrubland that eats bilberry and is food for many predators.

myodes rutilus.name: Northern red-backed vole
myodes rutilus.desc: The most recorded mammal near the park. A small woodland vole eating seeds, berries, fungi and lichen, and preyed on by foxes and wolverines.

myophonus borneensis.name: Bornean whistling thrush
myophonus borneensis.desc: A bird of mountain streams and forest floor that feeds on insects and other small animals.

myopus schisticolor.name: Wood lemming
myopus schisticolor.desc: A small rodent of mossy spruce forest that eats mosses and the shoots of dwarf shrubs such as cowberry.

myosurus minimus.name: Mousetail
myosurus minimus.desc: Mousetail (Myosurus minimus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

myotis grisescens.name: Gray bat
myotis grisescens.desc: Roosts in limestone caves and hunts insects over rivers and riverside forest.

myotis lucifugus.name: Little Brown Bat
myotis lucifugus.desc: Little Brown Bat (Myotis lucifugus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

myotis sodalis.name: Indiana bat
myotis sodalis.desc: The most recorded mammal near the park. Eats only flying insects such as moths and beetles and hibernates in cold caves.

myrcia.name: Myrcia trees
myrcia.desc: Myrtle-family trees and shrubs with small berries. Many birds are recorded eating Myrcia fruit.

myrianthus preussii.name: Myrianthus trees
myrianthus preussii.desc: A recorded understory tree of the Cross River forests with edible fruit; fleshy forest fruits like this feed primates and rodents.

myriophyllum aquaticum.name: Parrot's Feather
myriophyllum aquaticum.desc: Parrot's Feather (Myriophyllum aquaticum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 45 times near the park in GBIF.

myriophyllum sibiricum.name: Siberian water-milfoil
myriophyllum sibiricum.desc: Siberian water-milfoil (Myriophyllum sibiricum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

myriophyllum spicatum.name: Spiked Water-milfoil
myriophyllum spicatum.desc: Spiked Water-milfoil (Myriophyllum spicatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 56 times near the park in GBIF.

myrmecophaga tridactyla.name: Giant anteater
myrmecophaga tridactyla.desc: Rips open ant and termite nests and licks up thousands of insects.

mysis diluviana.name: Mysis
mysis diluviana.desc: A native shrimp-like crustacean of cold deep water. It eats mainly zooplankton, or algae and detritus when zooplankton is scarce.

mytilus.name: Blue mussels
mytilus.desc: Shellfish of rocky shores that filter plankton from the water. Sea otters crack them open.

mytilus californianus.name: California mussel
mytilus californianus.desc: Filters plankton from the water on wave-washed rock. Sea otters feed on mussels and so open up space on the rock for other species.

mytilus edulis.name: Blue mussel
mytilus edulis.desc: A filter feeder that clamps onto rocks in the tidal zone. Sea stars, whelks, gulls and eiders eat it.

mytilus trossulus.name: Bay mussel
mytilus trossulus.desc: Filter-feeding shellfish on rocky shores that eat plankton. Sea otters eat mussels.

n/a.name: Sunlight
n/a.desc: Light that reaches the forest floor in clearings and leaf-fall seasons drives plant growth.

naemorhedus caudatus.name: Long-tailed goral
naemorhedus caudatus.desc: A cliff-dwelling goat-antelope that eats grasses in summer and twigs, leaves and acorns in winter. A small endangered population lives in the DMZ.

naja arabica.name: Arabian cobra
naja arabica.desc: A venomous snake that hunts lizards and other small animals among the rocks of the highlands.

naja oxiana.name: Caspian cobra
naja oxiana.desc: A venomous snake of dry scrub that mainly eats small mammals, and also takes birds and other snakes.

najas minor.name: Brittle Waternymph
najas minor.desc: Brittle Waternymph (Najas minor): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 29 times near the park in GBIF.

nandinia binotata.name: African palm civet
nandinia binotata.desc: A tree-living nocturnal omnivore that eats fruit as well as small animals.

nanger soemmerringii.name: Soemmerring's gazelle
nanger soemmerringii.desc: One of the most commonly recorded antelopes of Djibouti's dry country, helped by the hunting ban of the early 1970s.

nannopterum auritum.name: Double-crested cormorant
nannopterum auritum.desc: A diving fish-eating bird. Alewife is believed to have created good feeding conditions for Great Lakes colonies.

narcissus poeticus.name: Pheasant's-eye Daffodil
narcissus poeticus.desc: Pheasant's-eye Daffodil (Narcissus poeticus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

nardus stricta.name: Mat-grass pasture
nardus stricta.desc: A tough tussock grass that makes up much of the upland summer pasture grazed by flocks and wild herbivores.

nasua narica.name: White-nosed coati
nasua narica.desc: An omnivore that forages on the ground for insects, small vertebrates, eggs, carrion and fruit.

nasua nasua.name: South American coati
nasua nasua.desc: An omnivore that climbs to eat fruit, hunts invertebrates and eggs, and is itself preyed on by jaguars.

natrix natrix.name: Grass snake
natrix natrix.desc: A semi-aquatic snake that hunts frogs and other amphibians around ponds and wet meadows.

natrix tessellata.name: Dice snake
natrix tessellata.desc: A semi-aquatic snake that hunts fish and amphibians in water.

necrosyrtes monachus.name: Hooded vulture
necrosyrtes monachus.desc: A small scavenging vulture recorded feeding on carcasses of hippo, waterbuck and elephant.

nectarinia famosa.name: Malachite sunbird
nectarinia famosa.desc: A long-tailed nectar-feeding bird that visits heaths and other flowering plants and also takes insects.

negaprion acutidens.name: Sicklefin lemon shark
negaprion acutidens.desc: An Indian Ocean shark that uses shallow sheltered waters such as mangrove creeks as a nursery.

nelumbo lutea.name: American lotus
nelumbo lutea.desc: American lotus (Nelumbo lutea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

nemastylis geminiflora.name: Prairie celestial
nemastylis geminiflora.desc: Prairie celestial (Nemastylis geminiflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

neocalanus.name: Copepods and zooplankton
neocalanus.desc: Tiny crustaceans that graze the spring bloom and pass its energy on to young salmon and schooling fish.

neofelis diardi.name: Sunda clouded leopard
neofelis diardi.desc: A tree-climbing cat. Wikipedia lists it as a potential predator of orangutans at Sikundur.

neofelis nebulosa.name: Clouded leopard
neofelis nebulosa.desc: A tree-climbing cat of dense forest, recorded in the reserve's evergreen forest. It hunts deer and other mammals.

neophocaena phocaenoides.name: Finless porpoise
neophocaena phocaenoides.desc: A small coastal porpoise recorded near the bay. It eats whatever is available, such as fish, crustaceans and cephalopods; gill nets are a main threat.

neophron percnopterus.name: Egyptian vulture
neophron percnopterus.desc: A small, opportunistic vulture and the most recorded bird in the area. It feeds mainly on carrion and also takes insects and eggs.

neotoma albigula.name: White-throated woodrat
neotoma albigula.desc: White-throated woodrat (Neotoma albigula): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

neotoma lepida.name: Desert woodrat
neotoma lepida.desc: A pack-rat of rocky desert slopes that feeds on cacti, juniper and other plants.

neotoma leucodon.name: White-toothed woodrat
neotoma leucodon.desc: A packrat for which cacti, especially cholla and prickly pear, are a major part of the diet.

neotoma mexicana.name: Mexican woodrat
neotoma mexicana.desc: A generalist that eats berries, nuts, acorns and foliage. It shelters in rock crevices and caves.

neotoma stephensi.name: Stephen's Woodrat
neotoma stephensi.desc: Stephen's Woodrat (Neotoma stephensi): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 72 times near the park in GBIF.

neotomodon alstoni.name: Mexican volcano mouse
neotomodon alstoni.desc: A burrowing rodent of high-elevation forest on the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt, and a recorded prey of the dusky rattlesnake.

neotragus pygmaeus.name: Royal antelope
neotragus pygmaeus.desc: One of the smallest antelopes in the world, a shy browser of leaves, shoots and fallen fruit in dense forest.

nepenthes rajah.name: Giant pitcher plant
nepenthes rajah.desc: A carnivorous plant and the most notable pitcher plant of the park. Tree shrews and summit rats lick nectar from its lid and defecate into the pitcher.

nereocystis luetkeana.name: Bull kelp
nereocystis luetkeana.desc: A canopy kelp of central and northern California coasts, eaten by black abalone there along with drift algae.

nerisyrenia linearifolia.name: White Sands fan mustard
nerisyrenia linearifolia.desc: White Sands fan mustard (Nerisyrenia linearifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

nerodia erythrogaster.name: Plain-bellied water snake
nerodia erythrogaster.desc: A swamp snake recorded eating frogs, and a regular visitor of floodplain pools.

nerodia fasciata.name: Banded water snake
nerodia fasciata.desc: A common water snake that eats frogs and toads.

nesotriccus ridgwayi.name: Cocos flycatcher
nesotriccus ridgwayi.desc: One of three endemic land birds; a small insect-catching bird of the island forest.

nestor notabilis.name: Kea
nestor notabilis.desc: Alpine parrot that eats roots, leaves, berries and insects, and also scavenges carrion.

new river & streams.name: New River & streams
new river & streams.desc: Water carved the gorge, and the riparian zone is the park's most biologically diverse area.

nicotiana glauca.name: Tree Tobacco
nicotiana glauca.desc: Tree Tobacco (Nicotiana glauca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

nicrophorus americanus.name: American burying beetle
nicrophorus americanus.desc: An endangered beetle present here in summer. Adults need small carcasses to breed and bury them to feed their young.

nilgiritragus hylocrius.name: Nilgiri tahr
nilgiritragus hylocrius.desc: An endangered mountain goat of the shola-grassland mosaic that grazes grass and small shrubs on rocky slopes.

nimbaphrynoides occidentalis.name: Nimba viviparous toad
nimbaphrynoides occidentalis.desc: A critically endangered toad found only in the high grasslands of Nimba at about 1,200 to 1,680 m. It gives birth to live young and does not tolerate disturbed ground.

nimbochromis.name: Predatory haps
nimbochromis.desc: Large cichlids that prey on other fish. Livingstoni plays dead to lure prey close.

nisaetus nipalensis.name: Mountain hawk-eagle
nisaetus nipalensis.desc: A forest raptor that nests in the park. In a Taiwan nest study giant flying squirrels and Pallas's squirrels were its main prey.

nitraria sibirica.name: Siberian nitraria
nitraria sibirica.desc: A salt-tolerant spiny shrub of sandy hollows and dune edges, recorded often in the park area.

nitrogen and phosphorus.name: Nutrient runoff
nitrogen and phosphorus.desc: Nitrogen and phosphorus from farms, towns, sewage and air pollution wash into the bay and fuel algal blooms.

nitrogen from land and sewage.name: Nitrogen from land and sewage
nitrogen from land and sewage.desc: Nitrogen is a key nutrient for the bay's algae. Cuts in wastewater nitrogen since 2006 have been followed by smaller annual phytoplankton blooms.

nitrophila occidentalis.name: Boraxweed
nitrophila occidentalis.desc: Boraxweed (Nitrophila occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

nitrosalsola vermiculata.name: Shrubby saltbush
nitrosalsola vermiculata.desc: A salt-tolerant shrub, named as a climax plant of the Syrian steppe, and a mainstay of grazing land.

niviventer culturatus.name: Taiwan white-bellied rat
niviventer culturatus.desc: A rodent of primary hemlock forest, recorded in Yushan National Park. Rodents like this are food for snakes and weasels.

nomascus leucogenys.name: Northern white-cheeked gibbon
nomascus leucogenys.desc: A tree-dwelling ape that eats mainly fruit with some leaves and buds. About 57 groups were estimated in this reserve in 2019.

notamacropus rufogriseus.name: Red-necked wallaby
notamacropus rufogriseus.desc: A grazing wallaby of open forest and heath, preyed on by devils, quolls and eagles.

nothofagus.name: Southern beech
nothofagus.desc: New Guinea beeches characterise lower and upper montane rain forest. UNESCO notes the park's beech forests are well represented and are hit by Phytophthora dieback.

nothofagus antarctica.name: Ñire
nothofagus antarctica.desc: A hardy southern beech of the forest edge, where the Magellanic forest meets the dry Patagonian steppe.

nothofagus cliffortioides.name: Mountain beech
nothofagus cliffortioides.desc: A beech tree of the park's cooler forests; Wikipedia names beech forest as one of the main forest types around Tongariro and Ruapehu.

nothofagus cunninghamii.name: Myrtle beech
nothofagus cunninghamii.desc: The main canopy tree of Tasmania's cool temperate rainforest, sharing the canopy with sassafras, leatherwood and conifers.

nothofagus menziesii.name: Silver beech
nothofagus menziesii.desc: A dominant tree of Fiordland forests. Its heavy seed years feed rodent booms that in turn feed stoats.

nothofagus pumilio.name: Lenga beech
nothofagus pumilio.desc: A deciduous southern beech that forms the dense high-latitude forests of the southern Andes. It tolerates hard frost and heavy snow and regrows easily after fire.

notomys alexis.name: Spinifex hopping mouse
notomys alexis.desc: A small hopping rodent of central Australia that lives in burrows on spinifex and mulga flats. It takes plant food and is prey for many predators.

nucifraga caryocatactes.name: Eurasian nutcracker
nucifraga caryocatactes.desc: A crow-family bird that feeds on conifer seeds, especially pine seeds, and stores them in caches.

nucifraga columbiana.name: Clark's nutcracker
nucifraga columbiana.desc: Feeds mainly on pine seeds, caches more than it needs, and also eats insects and carrion. It helps spread limber and whitebark pines.

numenius arquata.name: Eurasian curlew
numenius arquata.desc: Large wader whose long curved bill reaches worms and crabs buried in soft mud.

numida meleagris.name: Helmeted guineafowl
numida meleagris.desc: Ground-feeding flocks that eat seeds and insects, and nest on the ground.

nuphar.name: Pond lilies
nuphar.desc: Floating-leaved aquatic plants of ponds and slow water, a food for moose and beavers.

nuphar polysepala.name: Rocky Mountain pond-lily
nuphar polysepala.desc: Rocky Mountain pond-lily (Nuphar polysepala): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

nuphar variegata.name: Varigated Yellow Pond-Lily
nuphar variegata.desc: Varigated Yellow Pond-Lily (Nuphar variegata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

nura river and snowmelt.name: Nura River and snowmelt
nura river and snowmelt.desc: Spring snowmelt and the Nura River fill the lake basins; water levels vary from season to season.

nutrient-poor sandstone soil.name: Nutrient-poor sandstone soil
nutrient-poor sandstone soil.desc: Acidic soils from sandstone are low in nutrients, which shapes the stunted shrubs and the carnivorous plants.

nutrient-poor sandy soil.name: Nutrient-poor sandy soil
nutrient-poor sandy soil.desc: Fynbos grows on poor, acid sands from Table Mountain sandstone and similar rocks.

nutrient-poor soil.name: Nutrient-poor soil
nutrient-poor soil.desc: Heavy rain washes minerals out, so most nutrients are held in living plants and leaf litter.

nutrient-rich deep water.name: Nutrient-rich deep water
nutrient-rich deep water.desc: Currents lift nutrient-rich deep ocean water along the peninsula. Together with melting ice, it fuels spring plankton blooms.

nutrient-rich mud.name: Nutrient-rich mud
nutrient-rich mud.desc: Oxygen-poor mangrove mud holds the nutrients released by decomposing leaves and wood.

nutrients.name: Nutrients
nutrients.desc: Upwelling and river runoff supply nitrogen and phosphorus. Too much feeds algae at the coral's expense.

nutrients and runoff.name: Nutrients and runoff
nutrients and runoff.desc: Nutrients from land and recycled from dead matter feed plankton and algae. Excess runoff favours algae over coral.

nyctereutes procyonoides.name: Raccoon dog
nyctereutes procyonoides.desc: Common on the island though not native. It digs into sea turtle nests and takes baby turtles.

nymphaea alba.name: White water-lily
nymphaea alba.desc: Floating-leaved plant of the still channels and lakes. Muskrats and mute swans are recorded eating it.

nymphaea and utricularia.name: Waterlilies and bladderwort
nymphaea and utricularia.desc: Submerged and floating plants of the open sloughs that give food and cover to aquatic animals.

nymphaea lotus.name: Water lotus
nymphaea lotus.desc: A floating water plant of slow river channels and backwaters.

nymphaea odorata.name: American Waterlily
nymphaea odorata.desc: A floating-leaved plant of the open lakes and wet prairies, which cover about 60,000 acres of the refuge.

nymphalidae.name: Butterflies
nymphalidae.desc: Many butterflies live here, and the park is known for them. Caterpillars chew leaves, adults feed on fruit, sap or nectar.

nymphalis antiopa.name: Mourningcloak
nymphalis antiopa.desc: Mourningcloak (Nymphalis antiopa): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

nymphalis californica.name: California Tortoiseshell
nymphalis californica.desc: California Tortoiseshell (Nymphalis californica): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

oasis groundwater.name: Oasis groundwater
oasis groundwater.desc: Water close to the surface at oases and in wadis lets trees and palms grow where the surrounding desert is bare.

oasis springs.name: Oasis springs
oasis springs.desc: Scattered springs and seeps are the water that desert plants, wild asses, camels and bears gather around.

oasis springs and wadi.name: Oasis springs and wadi
oasis springs and wadi.desc: Springs such as Efqa and the small al-Qubur wadi water the Palmyra oasis, which supports palms and gardens amid dry desert.

occidryas chalcedona.name: Occidryas chalcedona
occidryas chalcedona.desc: Occidryas chalcedona (Occidryas chalcedona): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.

ocean currents.name: Ocean currents
ocean currents.desc: The island is the first landmark met by the North Equatorial Countercurrent, where currents meet and carry larvae and plankton across the Pacific.

ocean currents & nutrients.name: Ocean currents & nutrients
ocean currents & nutrients.desc: Open-ocean water around the islands carries nutrients and plankton that the reefs and fish depend on.

ocean passages.name: Ocean passages
ocean passages.desc: Natural gaps in the barrier reef, such as the Boulari passage, let ocean water flow into and out of the lagoon.

ochlodes sylvanoides.name: Woodland Skipper
ochlodes sylvanoides.desc: Woodland Skipper (Ochlodes sylvanoides): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

ochotona alpina.name: Alpine pika
ochotona alpina.desc: A small lagomorph living among scree and rocks that eats meadow plants. Snow leopards also hunt small mammals such as pikas.

ochotona coreana.name: Korean pika
ochotona coreana.desc: A small rock-dwelling relative of rabbits found in the mountains of northern North Korea and the Changbai range.

ochotona macrotis.name: Large-eared pika
ochotona macrotis.desc: A small lagomorph of rocky high slopes that eats grasses and herbs. Predators here are inferred from general knowledge.

ochotona pallasi.name: Pallas's pika
ochotona pallasi.desc: A small herbivore of rocky ground, among the most-recorded mammals near the park and food for small carnivores.

ochotona princeps.name: American pika
ochotona princeps.desc: A small herbivore of rock slopes that eats grasses and wildflowers and stores hay for winter. Hawks and eagles prey on it.

ochotona thibetana.name: Moupin pika
ochotona thibetana.desc: Colonial burrower of rocky ground under rhododendron and bamboo that stores haypiles of plants.

ocotea.name: Laurel family trees
ocotea.desc: Montane forest trees of the laurel family. Wikipedia notes laurels are among the fruit families Andean cock-of-the-rock eats.

ocotea leucoxylon.name: Ocotea
ocotea leucoxylon.desc: A tree of the laurel family. Its fruits are a food for forest birds and mammals.

ocotea usambarensis.name: Camphor wood
ocotea usambarensis.desc: A canopy tree of the wet southern montane forest, with ferns and epiphytes growing beneath and on it.

octopus vulgaris.name: Common octopus
octopus vulgaris.desc: Seabed hunter of crabs and shellfish; octopus and squid are the chief food of Mediterranean monk seals.

ocypode.name: Ghost crab
ocypode.desc: A burrowing beach crab that scavenges carrion and takes turtle hatchlings.

odobenus rosmarus.name: Walrus
odobenus rosmarus.desc: Digs clams out of the seabed with its whiskers.

odocoileus hemionus.name: Mule deer
odocoileus hemionus.desc: Mule deer (Odocoileus hemionus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

odocoileus virginianus.name: White-tailed deer
odocoileus virginianus.desc: White-tailed deer (Odocoileus virginianus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

odontomachus bauri.name: Trap-jaw ant
odontomachus bauri.desc: A leaf-litter ant that feeds on sugary fruit and nectar and on small invertebrates.

odontotermes.name: Termites
odontotermes.desc: Build mounds and recycle dry grass and wood. They are the main food of sloth bears.

oecophylla smaragdina.name: Asian weaver ant
oecophylla smaragdina.desc: Builds leaf nests in the canopy and hunts other insects in large colonies.

oenanthe cypriaca.name: Cyprus wheatear
oenanthe cypriaca.desc: Breeds only on Cyprus, often in woodland. Hunts insects and, in GloBI records, small lizards.

oenanthe deserti.name: Desert wheatear
oenanthe deserti.desc: An insectivore that picks ants, beetles and other insects from the ground. GloBI records show it eating small lizards too.

oenanthe isabellina.name: Isabelline wheatear
oenanthe isabellina.desc: A migratory insect-eating bird that winters in open country and is a prey item of wildcats in GloBI records.

oenothera fruticosa.name: Narrow-leaf Evening-primrose
oenothera fruticosa.desc: Narrow-leaf Evening-primrose (Oenothera fruticosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

oenothera hartwegii.name: Hartweg's Evening Primrose
oenothera hartwegii.desc: Hartweg's Evening Primrose (Oenothera hartwegii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 29 times near the park in GBIF.

oenothera macrocarpa.name: Ozark sundrop
oenothera macrocarpa.desc: Ozark sundrop (Oenothera macrocarpa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.

okapia johnstoni.name: Okapi
okapia johnstoni.desc: A shy forest giraffe relative that browses leaves, buds, ferns and fruit in the understory. Its main natural predator is the leopard.

olea.name: Wild olive
olea.desc: An evergreen tree that grows with juniper on the rocky scarp and helps form the dry montane forest canopy.

olneya tesota.name: Desert ironwood
olneya tesota.desc: Desert ironwood (Olneya tesota): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 157 times near the park in GBIF.

omocestus.name: Steppe grasshoppers
omocestus.desc: Grasshoppers eat steppe grasses and are prey for frogs and other small predators.

omocestus viridulus.name: Common green grasshopper
omocestus viridulus.desc: A grass-feeding grasshopper of meadows, recorded in the area.

omura congrua.name: Gaudy grasshopper
omura congrua.desc: A leaf-eating grasshopper of the forest understorey, food for lizards and other insect-eaters.

oncopeltus fasciatus.name: Large Milkweed Bug
oncopeltus fasciatus.desc: Large Milkweed Bug (Oncopeltus fasciatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 30 times near the park in GBIF.

oncorhynchus.name: Pacific salmon
oncorhynchus.desc: Salmon feed at sea, then return to streams to spawn and die. Their bodies carry ocean energy to bears, eagles, wolves and scavengers.

oncorhynchus clarkii bouvieri.name: Cutthroat trout
oncorhynchus clarkii bouvieri.desc: Yellowstone's native trout. Eats mayflies and fallen grasshoppers, and feeds otters, ospreys, eagles and bears.

oncorhynchus gorbuscha.name: Pink salmon
oncorhynchus gorbuscha.desc: Feeds on plankton, invertebrates and small fish at sea, then returns to streams to spawn. Spawned-out carcasses feed bears and stream life.

oncorhynchus mykiss.name: Rainbow trout
oncorhynchus mykiss.desc: An introduced predator. Wikipedia attributes the likely extinction of one Orestias species to competition and predation by introduced trout and silverside.

oncorhynchus nerka.name: Sockeye salmon
oncorhynchus nerka.desc: A landlocked sockeye that eats plankton. Fish were introduced to the lake, which likely had no native fish.

oncorhynchus spp..name: Pacific salmon
oncorhynchus spp..desc: Grow at sea, then swim up rivers to spawn and die, bringing ocean nutrients into the forest.

oncorhynchus tshawytscha.name: Chinook salmon
oncorhynchus tshawytscha.desc: Stocked since 1967 to control alewife. Adults eat mostly fish, and the population depends on yearly stocking.

oncosiphon pilulifer.name: Common Stinkweed
oncosiphon pilulifer.desc: Common Stinkweed (Oncosiphon pilulifer): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 28 times near the park in GBIF.

ondatra zibethicus.name: Muskrat
ondatra zibethicus.desc: Muskrat (Ondatra zibethicus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

onoclea sensibilis.name: Sensitive fern
onoclea sensibilis.desc: Sensitive fern (Onoclea sensibilis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 37 times near the park in GBIF.

onychognathus frater.name: Socotra starling
onychognathus frater.desc: An island endemic that eats grasshoppers and figs, and the berries of the dragon's blood tree, spreading its seeds.

onychognathus tristramii.name: Tristram's starling
onychognathus tristramii.desc: The most-recorded bird here. It eats fruit and insects, nests on cliffs, and likely spreads desert plant seeds over long distances.

onychomys arenicola.name: Grasshopper mouse
onychomys arenicola.desc: A carnivorous mouse that eats mostly insects and other invertebrates, plus small rodents like pocket mice.

onychomys leucogaster.name: Northern grasshopper mouse
onychomys leucogaster.desc: A small carnivorous mouse that hunts insects such as beetles and sometimes other small rodents.

onychoprion fuscatus.name: Sooty tern
onychoprion fuscatus.desc: Nests on Bush Key, the only US colony. Picks small fish from the sea surface, often far out over open water.

opheodrys aestivus.name: Rough Green Snake
opheodrys aestivus.desc: Rough Green Snake (Opheodrys aestivus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.

ophiophagus hannah.name: King cobra
ophiophagus hannah.desc: Mainly eats other snakes and lizards, and lives in the Himalayan foothills including the Terai.

opuntia.name: Prickly pear
opuntia.desc: Cacti like prickly pear store water in dry ground. GloBI records bighorn sheep eating cacti.

opuntia basilaris.name: Beavertail cactus
opuntia basilaris.desc: A flat-padded prickly pear whose fleshy pads store water; bighorn sheep use their horns to break open cactus to eat.

opuntia engelmannii.name: Engelmann prickly pear
opuntia engelmannii.desc: A pad-forming cactus whose pads and fruit are food for javelinas, rabbits and other desert animals.

opuntia humifusa.name: Prickly-pear cactus
opuntia humifusa.desc: Prickly-pear cactus (Opuntia humifusa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 114 times near the park in GBIF.

opuntia macrorhiza.name: Twistspine Pricklypear
opuntia macrorhiza.desc: Twistspine Pricklypear (Opuntia macrorhiza): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

opuntia phaeacantha.name: Prickly pear
opuntia phaeacantha.desc: One of the many cacti of Big Bend. Peccaries rely on prickly pear, and honey bees visit its flowers.

opuntia polyacantha.name: Cliff prickly-pear
opuntia polyacantha.desc: Cliff prickly-pear (Opuntia polyacantha): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

opuntia species.name: Prickly pear cactus
opuntia species.desc: Cactus whose pads, flowers and fruit feed tortoises and finches. On some islands it grows tree-like, which keeps its pads out of reach of grazers.

orcaella brevirostris.name: Irrawaddy dolphin
orcaella brevirostris.desc: A small dolphin of the Sundarbans waterways that hunts fish and shrimp in brackish water.

orcinus orca.name: Orca
orcinus orca.desc: Hunts seals, belugas and walruses as ice retreats and open water spreads.

orconectes pellucidus.name: Mammoth Cave crayfish
orconectes pellucidus.desc: An eyeless crayfish of cave streams, named for the park. Cave crayfish generally scavenge leaf litter and detritus washed in from above.

oreamnos americanus.name: Mountain goat
oreamnos americanus.desc: The park symbol. Eats grasses, herbs, sedges, mosses and lichens high on cliffs and alpine slopes.

oreochromis.name: Tilapia and bream
oreochromis.desc: Cichlid fish that feed on plants and algae. They are a main food of the African fish eagle.

oreochromis niloticus.name: Nile tilapia
oreochromis niloticus.desc: The main fish of Lake Edward fishery. It eats algae and is fed by hippo dung; fish eagles and crocodiles eat it.

oreochromis spp..name: Tilapia
oreochromis spp..desc: River fish that graze algae and feed crocodiles.

oreoleuciscus potanini.name: Altai osman and lake fish
oreoleuciscus potanini.desc: A cyprinid fish of Mongolia and Tuva; the Uvs Lake area has about 29 fish species in all, and the osman is the one eaten by people.

oreotragus oreotragus.name: Klipspringer
oreotragus oreotragus.desc: A small antelope of rocky ground, recorded in the park.

orestias.name: Orestias killifish
orestias.desc: A genus of pupfish, most of it endemic to Titicaca. Species eat crustaceans, snails, algae, plankton and other fish. Introduced trout and pollution threaten it.

ornithogalum umbellatum.name: Garden Star-of-Bethlehem
ornithogalum umbellatum.desc: Garden Star-of-Bethlehem (Ornithogalum umbellatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

orographic rain.name: Orographic rain
orographic rain.desc: Moist air rising up the southern slope drops its heaviest rain in the forest belt, while the northern slopes and alpine zone are much drier.

orthetrum sabina.name: Green marsh hawk
orthetrum sabina.desc: A common dragonfly of wetlands that hunts other flying insects, including smaller dragonflies, per GloBI.

oryctolagus cuniculus.name: European rabbit
oryctolagus cuniculus.desc: Grazes grasses and shoots and is the staple food of the Iberian lynx and Spanish imperial eagle. Disease has cut its numbers badly.

oryx gazella.name: Gemsbok
oryx gazella.desc: A desert antelope that can meet its water needs from wild melons and cucumbers. Lions and hyenas are its natural predators in Africa.

oryx leucoryx.name: Arabian oryx
oryx leucoryx.desc: Mostly a grass eater that follows rains to fresh growth and can go weeks without water. Semi-managed herds live in Qatar.

oryza.name: Wild and cultivated rice
oryza.desc: Wild rice and rice paddies cover parts of the floodplain and feed insects, rodents and wading birds.

oryza barthii.name: Wild rice & riverbank grasses
oryza barthii.desc: Wild rice and other grasses growing on wet, flooded ground. Hippos graze on grasses.

oryza sativa.name: Rice paddies
oryza sativa.desc: Farmland and paddies along the zone edges. Rice gleanings are an important winter food for red-crowned cranes in East Asia.

osmia lignaria.name: Blue Orchard Bee
osmia lignaria.desc: Blue Orchard Bee (Osmia lignaria): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 45 times near the park in GBIF.

osmunda spectabilis.name: American Royal Fern
osmunda spectabilis.desc: American Royal Fern (Osmunda spectabilis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 44 times near the park in GBIF.

osphranter rufus.name: Red kangaroo
osphranter rufus.desc: The largest marsupial of the desert, grazing mostly green grasses and forbs and browsing shrubs when food is scarce. It can go long periods without drinking.

osteolaemus.name: Congo dwarf crocodile
osteolaemus.desc: A small nocturnal crocodile of forest streams and swamps. In the Congo it eats mostly fish, with more crustaceans in the dry season.

osteopilus septentrionalis.name: Cuban tree frog
osteopilus septentrionalis.desc: Big, voracious frog that eats nearly anything it can swallow; knight anoles and various snakes prey on it.

ostrya carpinifolia.name: European hop-hornbeam
ostrya carpinifolia.desc: A deciduous tree recorded in the area that grows with oaks in the lower broadleaf woodland.

otaria byronia.name: South American sea lion
otaria byronia.desc: Eats fish such as anchovies and hake, squid and sometimes penguins. At Valdés orcas beach themselves to grab it near shore.

otaria flavescens.name: South American sea lion
otaria flavescens.desc: The Islas de Torres hold the region's largest colony. Eats fish and squid and sometimes fur seals.

otis tarda.name: Great bustard
otis tarda.desc: Hungary's national bird eats green plants, seeds and insects. Foxes and crows are serious predators of its eggs and chicks.

otocolobus manul.name: Pallas's cat
otocolobus manul.desc: A small, stocky wild cat of rocky steppe and desert that hunts pikas and small rodents.

otospermophilus beecheyi.name: California ground squirrel
otospermophilus beecheyi.desc: Mostly eats seeds, nuts and fruit, plus some insects. Rattlesnakes are its most frequent predators.

otospermophilus variegatus.name: Rock squirrel
otospermophilus variegatus.desc: Eats seeds, acorns, pine nuts and fruit, storing food in its burrow. Snakes, hawks and coyotes prey on it.

oulanka river & its floods.name: Oulanka River & its floods
oulanka river & its floods.desc: The river with its rapids and sandy valleys shapes the park, and its banks and alluvial meadows add habitat variety.

outwash sands and volcanic soil.name: Outwash sands and volcanic soil
outwash sands and volcanic soil.desc: Young, nutrient-poor soils of glacial sand and volcanic ash that plants colonise slowly and that dead matter helps enrich.

ovibos moschatus.name: Muskox
ovibos moschatus.desc: Stays on the tundra all year, circling its calves when wolves approach.

ovis ammon.name: Argali
ovis ammon.desc: The largest wild sheep, grazing grasses, sedges and herbs on open slopes. Wolves and snow leopards prey on it, and golden eagles take lambs.

ovis aries.name: Domestic sheep
ovis aries.desc: The main livestock of the summer pastures. Dead animals left on the mountain feed vultures and other scavengers.

ovis canadensis.name: Bighorn sheep
ovis canadensis.desc: A sure-footed grazer of rocky canyon country, listed among Arches' wildlife. Cougars prey on bighorn sheep.

ovis canadensis nelsoni.name: Desert bighorn sheep
ovis canadensis nelsoni.desc: Eats mainly grasses and shifts to other plants and cactus when grass is scarce. It can go long periods without drinking and escapes predators on steep rocky ground.

ovis canadensis sierrae.name: Sierra Nevada bighorn sheep
ovis canadensis sierrae.desc: An endangered high-country grazer of grasses and forbs that uses steep rocky ground to escape predators. Mountain lions are a major threat.

ovis dalli.name: Dall sheep
ovis dalli.desc: Grazes grasses, sedges and willow on steep alpine slopes, using lichens and mosses in winter. Denali was founded in part to protect the sheep.

ovis gmelini.name: Cyprus mouflon
ovis gmelini.desc: Endangered wild sheep, the national animal of Cyprus, living in the mountains of Paphos District. Eats leaves and grasses.

ovis nivicola.name: Snow sheep
ovis nivicola.desc: A wild sheep of Siberian mountains that grazes alpine slopes. Records near the volcanoes are few.

ovis vignei.name: Urial
ovis vignei.desc: A wild sheep native to the Hindu Kush and nearby ranges, found on grassland, open woodland and gentle slopes.

ovophis makazayazaya.name: Taiwan mountain pitviper
ovophis makazayazaya.desc: A montane pitviper of southeast Asia and Taiwan. A GloBI record shows it feeding on a Taiwan forest rodent.

oxalis articulata.name: Pink-sorrel
oxalis articulata.desc: Pink-sorrel (Oxalis articulata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

oxalis montana.name: Mountain Woodsorrel
oxalis montana.desc: Mountain Woodsorrel (Oxalis montana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

oxalis violacea.name: Violet wood-sorrel
oxalis violacea.desc: Violet wood-sorrel (Oxalis violacea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 27 times near the park in GBIF.

oxytropis.name: Oxytropis
oxytropis.desc: Cushion-forming legumes of stony alpine ground, well recorded near the park, that give grazers protein-rich forage.

oxytropis glabra.name: Oxytropis glabra
oxytropis glabra.desc: Oxytropis glabra (Oxytropis glabra): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

oxytropis splendens.name: Showy crazyweed
oxytropis splendens.desc: Showy crazyweed (Oxytropis splendens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 52 times near the park in GBIF.

oxytropis, astragalus.name: Milkvetches
oxytropis, astragalus.desc: Many Oxytropis and Astragalus species are recorded in the Nuratau slopes, some of them local endemics. Their leaves and seeds feed herbivores.

oxyura jamaicensis.name: Ruddy Duck
oxyura jamaicensis.desc: Ruddy Duck (Oxyura jamaicensis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 78 times near the park in GBIF.

ozotoceros bezoarticus.name: Pampas deer
ozotoceros bezoarticus.desc: A Near Threatened grassland deer that eats new growth, herbs and shrubs and follows flowering plants. Pumas and jaguars hunt it.

pachnoda marginata.name: Marginated Congo chafer
pachnoda marginata.desc: A colourful beetle recorded near Nimba. Adults feed on fruit and flowers and are prey for birds and small mammals.

pachychilon pictum.name: Albanian roach
pachychilon pictum.desc: A small fish of large, nutrient-poor lakes in the Ohrid and Skadar drainages. One of eight endemic cyprinids in Ohrid.

pachydactylus rangei.name: Web-footed gecko
pachydactylus rangei.desc: A night-active dune gecko with webbed feet. It eats small arthropods and gets most of its water from dew on plants.

palafoxia sphacelata.name: Othake
palafoxia sphacelata.desc: Othake (Palafoxia sphacelata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

palisota bracteosa.name: Forest floor herbs
palisota bracteosa.desc: Understorey herbs of the shaded forest floor, recorded in the park area. Herbs and ferns are food for ground browsers such as the pygmy hippo.

pan paniscus.name: Bonobo
pan paniscus.desc: Mainly a fruit eater and the second-largest fruit eater in the Congo rainforest after elephants. It disperses seeds of many tree species and sometimes hunts duikers.

pan troglodytes.name: Chimpanzee
pan troglodytes.desc: Eats mostly fruit, but also fishes for termites with sticks and hunts monkeys and small antelope in groups.

pan troglodytes verus.name: Western chimpanzee
pan troglodytes verus.desc: Taï chimpanzees crack hard nuts with tools and hunt other primates, including red colobus. The subspecies is Critically Endangered.

panda oleosa.name: Panda nut tree
panda oleosa.desc: A tall forest tree whose oily nuts are among the hardest foods in the forest.

pandanus boninensis.name: Bonin screw pine
pandanus boninensis.desc: An endemic screw pine of the island forests and scrub. Its fruit is eaten by the Bonin flying fox.

pandanus julianettii.name: Karuka pandanus
pandanus julianettii.desc: A screwpine of montane forest between about 1,300 and 3,300 m. Its nuts are eaten by possums and several rodents, including Rothschild's woolly rat, as well as by people.

pandanus tectorius.name: Screw pine
pandanus tectorius.desc: A coastal tree with fruit that flying foxes feed on.

pandion haliaetus.name: Osprey
pandion haliaetus.desc: Spends the northern winter fishing Amazon rivers and lakes, then flies north to breed. Ospreys nesting at Yellowstone belong to the same migratory population.

panesthia lata.name: Wood-feeding cockroach
panesthia lata.desc: A native cockroach that chews rotting wood and so helps break down dead timber on the forest floor.

pangasianodon gigas.name: Mekong giant catfish
pangasianodon gigas.desc: One of the largest freshwater fish; after its first year it mostly feeds on algae. Found in the Tonlé Sap, but now rare.

panicum amarum.name: Bitter panicgrass
panicum amarum.desc: Bitter panicgrass (Panicum amarum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

panicum coloratum.name: Klein grass
panicum coloratum.desc: A tufted grass recorded around the park. GloBI records list it as food of buffalo, waterbuck and zebra.

panicum repens.name: Torpedo grass
panicum repens.desc: A tough grass of wet margins and floodplains, among the most often recorded plants here and grazed by hippos and lechwe.

panicum turgidum.name: Desert panic grass
panicum turgidum.desc: Tough perennial desert grass listed among the plants of Djibouti's wadis and lowlands.

panicum virgatum.name: Switchgrass
panicum virgatum.desc: A tall native bunchgrass that grows with big bluestem and helps make up the dense tallgrass cover.

panthera leo.name: Lion
panthera leo.desc: Lions on the Skeleton Coast prey on seals and shorebirds. Inland they also hunt oryx and springbok.

panthera onca.name: Jaguar
panthera onca.desc: Hunts capybaras, tapirs, sloths and caimans, with a bite strong enough to crush skulls and shells.

panthera pardus.name: Leopard
panthera pardus.desc: The main natural predator of okapi and a hunter of duikers and monkeys in the forest.

panthera pardus pardus.name: African leopard
panthera pardus pardus.desc: The main large predator of the forest, taking monkeys, hyraxes and small antelope.

panthera pardus tulliana.name: Persian leopard
panthera pardus tulliana.desc: A big cat of the Caucasus mountains and a predator of wild goats and boar.

panthera tigris.name: Tiger
panthera tigris.desc: The top predator of the park. Hunts deer and wild boar, and also takes sloth bears and leopards.

panthera tigris altaica.name: Amur tiger
panthera tigris altaica.desc: Preys mainly on wapiti, wild boar, sika and roe deer. Tigers also suppress wolves, which are scarce in tiger forests.

panthera tigris tigris.name: Bengal tiger
panthera tigris tigris.desc: The only tigers living in mangroves. They swim between islands and eat deer, boar, fish, crabs and monitors.

panthera uncia.name: Snow leopard
panthera uncia.desc: Himalayan apex predator that lives above about 3,500 m. Blue sheep are its core prey, with tahr, musk deer and marmots also taken.

pantherophis alleghaniensis.name: Eastern Rat Snake
pantherophis alleghaniensis.desc: Eastern Rat Snake (Pantherophis alleghaniensis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

pantherophis obsoletus.name: Black Rat Snake
pantherophis obsoletus.desc: Black Rat Snake (Pantherophis obsoletus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

panulirus.name: Spiny lobsters
panulirus.desc: Crustaceans listed in the bay, which eat molluscs and other bottom animals and hide in rocky crevices.

panulirus argus.name: Caribbean spiny lobster
panulirus argus.desc: Young settle in seagrass and mangrove roots, adults shelter in reef holes. Eats snails, clams, urchins and carrion.

papilio.name: Swallowtail butterflies
papilio.desc: Forest butterflies such as the flying handkerchief swallowtail. They feed on flowers like lantana.

papilio canadensis.name: Canadian tiger swallowtail
papilio canadensis.desc: A northern butterfly whose caterpillars feed on aspen and other broadleaf trees.

papilio eurymedon.name: Pale Swallowtail
papilio eurymedon.desc: Pale Swallowtail (Papilio eurymedon): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

papilio glaucus.name: Eastern Tiger Swallowtail
papilio glaucus.desc: Eastern Tiger Swallowtail (Papilio glaucus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

papilio homerus.name: Homerus swallowtail
papilio homerus.desc: The largest butterfly in the Western Hemisphere. Adults sip nectar and females lay eggs on Ocotea. Blue and John Crow Mountains hold one of its two last populations.

papilio machaon.name: Old World swallowtail
papilio machaon.desc: Old World Swallowtail (Papilio machaon): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 23 times near the park in GBIF.

papilio palamedes.name: Palamedes Swallowtail
papilio palamedes.desc: A large butterfly of southeastern swamps whose caterpillars feed on bay trees such as swamp bay.

papilio polyxenes.name: American Swallowtail
papilio polyxenes.desc: American Swallowtail (Papilio polyxenes): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

papilio troilus.name: Spicebush Swallowtail
papilio troilus.desc: Spicebush Swallowtail (Papilio troilus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 33 times near the park in GBIF.

papilio ulysses.name: Ulysses butterfly
papilio ulysses.desc: Caterpillars eat leaves of doughwood and similar trees, and adults feed on its blossoms.

papilio zelicaon.name: Anise Swallowtail
papilio zelicaon.desc: Anise Swallowtail (Papilio zelicaon): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 86 times near the park in GBIF.

papio anubis.name: Olive baboon
papio anubis.desc: An omnivorous monkey that eats fruit, leaves and grass. It forages on the ground and sleeps in trees.

papio cynocephalus.name: Yellow baboon
papio cynocephalus.desc: An opportunistic omnivore of the park that eats fruit and seeds, including baobab.

papio hamadryas.name: Hamadryas baboon
papio hamadryas.desc: Omnivore eating grasses, seeds, fruit, acacia leaves, insects and small animals. Depends on a few permanent waterholes in the dry season.

papio papio.name: Guinea baboon
papio papio.desc: An opportunistic omnivore that eats fruit, roots, seeds, leaves and some small animals. Chimpanzees have been seen preying on it in Senegal.

papio ursinus.name: Chacma baboon
papio ursinus.desc: An opportunistic omnivore eating fruit, seeds, bulbs, insects and more. At Cape Point it also takes shellfish.

parabuteo unicinctus.name: Harris's hawk
parabuteo unicinctus.desc: Hunts in family groups, which lets it take jackrabbits, plus ground squirrels, kangaroo rats and quail.

paradisaea raggiana.name: Raggiana bird-of-paradise
paradisaea raggiana.desc: The national bird of Papua New Guinea. It eats mainly fruit and arthropods and is an important seed disperser for some New Guinea trees.

paradoxurus hermaphroditus.name: Asian palm civet
paradoxurus hermaphroditus.desc: An omnivorous nocturnal civet that eats fruit as well as small animals such as rats.

parahyaena brunnea.name: Brown hyena
parahyaena brunnea.desc: Mostly a scavenger that lives near seal colonies on the Namib coast. It eats seal pups and often steals kills from jackals.

paralaudakia himalayana.name: Himalayan agama
paralaudakia himalayana.desc: A rock-dwelling lizard recorded near the park that feeds mostly on insects.

paranapiacaba tricincta.name: Checkered Melon Beetle
paranapiacaba tricincta.desc: Checkered Melon Beetle (Paranapiacaba tricincta): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

parastacoides tasmanicus.name: Burrowing crayfish
parastacoides tasmanicus.desc: Lives in burrows on moorland and eats buttongrass rhizomes; its burrows aerate the peat.

parinari excelsa.name: Guinea plum
parinari excelsa.desc: A large evergreen tree that gives its name to the mossy Parinari forests on Nimba. Its fruit is eaten by chimpanzees and other animals.

park & garden soil.name: Park & garden soil
park & garden soil.desc: The soil beneath parks, yards and gardens holds the nutrients plants use.

parkinsonia microphylla.name: Foothill palo verde
parkinsonia microphylla.desc: A green-barked desert tree that acts as a nurse plant, shading young saguaros and softening temperature extremes around them.

parnassia grandifolia.name: Largeleaf grass of Parnassus
parnassia grandifolia.desc: Largeleaf grass of Parnassus (Parnassia grandifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.

parnassius apollo.name: Apollo butterfly
parnassius apollo.desc: A large, white alpine butterfly. Its caterpillars feed on stonecrops of rocky meadows.

parnassius smintheus.name: Mountain Parnassian
parnassius smintheus.desc: Mountain Parnassian (Parnassius smintheus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 439 times near the park in GBIF.

paronychia sessiliflora.name: Low nailwort
paronychia sessiliflora.desc: Low nailwort (Paronychia sessiliflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

parthenium integrifolium.name: American feverfew
parthenium integrifolium.desc: American feverfew (Parthenium integrifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

parthenocissus quinquefolia.name: Virginia-creeper
parthenocissus quinquefolia.desc: Virginia-creeper (Parthenocissus quinquefolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

parus major.name: Great tit
parus major.desc: A small woodland bird that eats seeds, fruit and insects, and is prey for hawks and woodpeckers.

pascopyrum smithii.name: Western wheatgrass
pascopyrum smithii.desc: A sod-forming perennial grass and South Dakota's state grass. Bison and prairie dogs eat it.

paspalum.name: Paspalum grasses
paspalum.desc: Warm-season grasses recorded often around the wetland. Grasses make up the largest share of the marsh deer diet, and grassland here evolved with fire.

passer ammodendri.name: Saxaul sparrow
passer ammodendri.desc: A small sparrow tied to saxaul and desert shrubs that eats seeds and some insects. Prey for shrikes, owls and snakes.

passer domesticus.name: House Sparrow
passer domesticus.desc: House Sparrow (Passer domesticus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 63 times near the park in GBIF.

passer montanus.name: Eurasian tree sparrow
passer montanus.desc: Small seed- and fruit-eating bird of villages and shrub thickets around the lake.

passerina ciris.name: Painted Bunting
passerina ciris.desc: Painted Bunting (Passerina ciris): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 578 times near the park in GBIF.

passerina cyanea.name: Indigo Bunting
passerina cyanea.desc: Indigo Bunting (Passerina cyanea): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 257 times near the park in GBIF.

passiflora aurantia.name: Orange passion flower
passiflora aurantia.desc: A passion-flower vine. GloBI records the eastern red lacewing butterfly feeding on it.

passiflora incarnata.name: Purple Passionflower
passiflora incarnata.desc: Purple passionflower (Passiflora incarnata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 52 times near the park in GBIF.

pastinaca sativa.name: Wild Parsnip
pastinaca sativa.desc: Wild Parsnip (Pastinaca sativa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 47 times near the park in GBIF.

patagioenas caribaea.name: Ring-tailed pigeon
patagioenas caribaea.desc: An endemic forest pigeon of Jamaica that feeds mostly on fruit and was among the most recorded birds near the park.

patagioenas leucocephala.name: White-crowned pigeon
patagioenas leucocephala.desc: A fruit-eating pigeon, one of the best-recorded birds near the park. GloBI records link it to pigeon berry fruit.

patagioenas squamosa.name: Scaly-naped pigeon
patagioenas squamosa.desc: A fruit-eating pigeon, with GloBI records of it eating pumpwood, lira vine and sierra palm fruit.

patch-burn fire.name: Patch-burn fire
patch-burn fire.desc: The preserve burns roughly a third of the prairie each year. Fire keeps brush out and draws bison to fresh regrowth.

paulownia tomentosa.name: Foxglove-tree
paulownia tomentosa.desc: Foxglove-tree (Paulownia tomentosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 44 times near the park in GBIF.

peace-athabasca delta floods.name: Peace-Athabasca Delta floods
peace-athabasca delta floods.desc: The inland delta of the Peace, Athabasca and Birch rivers; its water feeds the park's wetlands and meadows.

peat.name: Peat
peat.desc: Waterlogged, acid ground made of slowly decaying moss. Wikipedia says the High Fens bogs are over 10,000 years old.

peat and poor soils.name: Peat and poor soils
peat and poor soils.desc: Bogs on the coast are rich in peat, and the ultramafic Tablelands have stony, nutrient-poor soil. Plant growth is limited by what the ground supplies.

peat bogs and streams.name: Peat bogs and streams
peat bogs and streams.desc: The Bohemian Forest holds peat bogs and sources of rivers such as the Vltava, Otava and Uhlava, which keep soils wet.

peat soil.name: Peat soil
peat soil.desc: Slowly built organic soil in which marsh plants root.

peatland soil.name: Peatland soil
peatland soil.desc: Waterlogged swamp soils in the central basin store about 30 petagrams of carbon, roughly as much as all basin forests.

peaty acid soil.name: Peaty acid soil
peaty acid soil.desc: Cool, wet ground builds acidic peat soils under much of the moorland and bog, favouring heather and cottongrass.

pecari tajacu.name: Collared peccary
pecari tajacu.desc: Also called javelina. Its main foods are agaves and prickly pears, and its predators include cougars and coyotes.

pedicularis canadensis.name: Common lousewort
pedicularis canadensis.desc: Common lousewort (Pedicularis canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

pediocactus simpsonii.name: Ball Cactus
pediocactus simpsonii.desc: Ball Cactus (Pediocactus simpsonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 42 times near the park in GBIF.

pediomelum argophyllum.name: Silverleaf Indian breadroot
pediomelum argophyllum.desc: Silverleaf Indian breadroot (Pediomelum argophyllum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

pekania pennanti.name: Fisher
pekania pennanti.desc: A generalist hunter whose main prey are snowshoe hares and porcupines. It also eats small mammals and carrion.

pelea capreolus.name: Grey rhebok
pelea capreolus.desc: A woolly-coated antelope of grassy highlands, a browser that gets much of its water from its food.

pelecanus crispus.name: Dalmatian pelican
pelecanus crispus.desc: Nests on islands or in dense reeds in the delta. It swallows fish whole, including carp and pike.

pelecanus erythrorhynchos.name: American white pelican
pelecanus erythrorhynchos.desc: A winter visitor to Gulf bays and estuaries. Nests on lakes in the interior and also follows the Mississippi River in winter.

pelecanus occidentalis.name: Brown pelican
pelecanus occidentalis.desc: A diving seabird that hunts schooling fish over the bay.

pelecanus onocrotalus.name: Great white pelican
pelecanus onocrotalus.desc: Large fish-eating bird that breeds on the site's islands and fishes in the shallows.

pelecanus rufescens.name: Pink-backed pelican
pelecanus rufescens.desc: The most recorded bird near the islands. It scoops fish from shallow waters.

pelecyphora tuberculosa.name: Pelecyphora tuberculosa
pelecyphora tuberculosa.desc: Pelecyphora tuberculosa (Pelecyphora tuberculosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

pelecyphora vivipara.name: Pincushion cactus
pelecyphora vivipara.desc: Pincushion cactus (Pelecyphora vivipara): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

pellaea atropurpurea.name: Purple cliffbrake
pellaea atropurpurea.desc: Purple cliffbrake (Pellaea atropurpurea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

pellaea glabella.name: Dwarf cliffbrake
pellaea glabella.desc: Dwarf cliffbrake (Pellaea glabella): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

pelophylax ridibundus.name: Marsh frog
pelophylax ridibundus.desc: A large water frog of ponds and channels that eats insects; it is prey for herons, ibises, harriers and foxes in GloBI records.

pemphis acidula.name: Pemphis scrub
