pemphis acidula.desc: Dense shrub that covers much of the higher, rocky ground of the atoll.

penaeus and relatives.name: Shrimp
penaeus and relatives.desc: Young shrimp shelter among mangrove roots, and the forest supports commercial shrimp and crab catches.

penaeus latisulcatus.name: Western king prawn
penaeus latisulcatus.desc: Bottom-dwelling prawn of sandy seabeds that makes up much of the catch of the Shark Bay prawn fishery. A food item for many fish.

penaeus semisulcatus.name: Green tiger prawn
penaeus semisulcatus.desc: A prawn of sandy and muddy coastal waters whose juveniles favour estuaries; a commercially important species in the region.

penstemon angustifolius.name: Broadbeard beardtongue
penstemon angustifolius.desc: Broadbeard beardtongue (Penstemon angustifolius): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

penstemon cobaea.name: Cobaea beardtongue
penstemon cobaea.desc: Cobaea beardtongue (Penstemon cobaea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

penstemon confertus.name: Lesser yellow beardtongue
penstemon confertus.desc: Lesser yellow beardtongue (Penstemon confertus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

penstemon cyananthus.name: Wasatch penstemon
penstemon cyananthus.desc: Wasatch penstemon (Penstemon cyananthus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

penstemon cyanocaulis.name: Bluestem penstemon
penstemon cyanocaulis.desc: Bluestem penstemon (Penstemon cyanocaulis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 93 times near the park in GBIF.

penstemon deaveri.name: Mt. Graham beardtongue
penstemon deaveri.desc: Mt. Graham beardtongue (Penstemon deaveri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

penstemon deustus.name: Scabland penstemon
penstemon deustus.desc: Scabland penstemon (Penstemon deustus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 123 times near the park in GBIF.

penstemon eatonii.name: Eaton's penstemon
penstemon eatonii.desc: Eaton's penstemon (Penstemon eatonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

penstemon eriantherus.name: Fuzzytongue penstemon
penstemon eriantherus.desc: Fuzzytongue penstemon (Penstemon eriantherus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

penstemon fruticosus.name: Bush penstemon
penstemon fruticosus.desc: Bush penstemon (Penstemon fruticosus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

penstemon pseudospectabilis.name: Desert penstemon
penstemon pseudospectabilis.desc: Desert penstemon (Penstemon pseudospectabilis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 60 times near the park in GBIF.

penstemon purpusii.name: Snow Mountain beardtongue
penstemon purpusii.desc: Snow Mountain beardtongue (Penstemon purpusii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

penstemon richardsonii.name: Richardson's beardtongue
penstemon richardsonii.desc: Richardson's beardtongue (Penstemon richardsonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

penstemon strictus.name: Rocky Mountain penstemon
penstemon strictus.desc: Rocky Mountain penstemon (Penstemon strictus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

penstemon virgatus.name: Upright blue beardtongue
penstemon virgatus.desc: Upright blue beardtongue (Penstemon virgatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.

pentaclethra macroloba.name: Cashew-nut tree
pentaclethra macroloba.desc: A leguminous tree recorded in the reserve area, common in wet and swampy lowland forest.

pentadesma butyracea.name: Kanya
pentadesma butyracea.desc: A tree of damp forest and stream edges in West Africa, recorded near the reserve; it bears large fruits and is valued for its seed fat.

pepsis menechma.name: Elegant Tarantula-hawk Wasp
pepsis menechma.desc: Elegant Tarantula-hawk Wasp (Pepsis menechma): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

perca flavescens.name: Yellow perch
perca flavescens.desc: A small lake fish that feeds on zooplankton and insects, and is prey for walleye and loons.

perca fluviatilis.name: European perch
perca fluviatilis.desc: A predatory fish of the lagoon that eats smaller fish and invertebrates.

perennial springs.name: Perennial springs
perennial springs.desc: Springs such as Ein Prat, Ein Mabuah and Ein Qelt keep Wadi Qelt flowing in places and draw wildlife.

perideridia gairdneri.name: Common Yampah
perideridia gairdneri.desc: Common Yampah (Perideridia gairdneri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

perilla frutescens.name: Perilla (beefsteak mint)
perilla frutescens.desc: Perilla (beefsteak mint) (Perilla frutescens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 59 times near the park in GBIF.

peringia ulvae (hydrobia).name: Mudsnail
peringia ulvae (hydrobia).desc: A tiny snail that grazes the muddy surface in huge numbers. It is eaten by shrimp and by wading birds.

periophthalmus.name: Mudskipper
periophthalmus.desc: Amphibious fish of mudflats and mangroves that hunt small invertebrates; prey for coastal herons.

periophthalmus and relatives.name: Mudskippers
periophthalmus and relatives.desc: Amphibious fish that hop across exposed mudflats at low tide and eat small invertebrates.

periphyton.name: River algae
periphyton.desc: Green films on rocks in the Mara and Grumeti rivers that feed fish.

periphyton and watercress.name: Stream algae & aquatic plants
periphyton and watercress.desc: Algae on rocks and plants in clear, cool spring-fed streams grow the food that aquatic insects and crayfish graze.

perisoreus infaustus.name: Siberian jay
perisoreus infaustus.desc: A boreal forest bird named by Wikipedia as a park speciality. Recorded eating small birds and voles.

permafrost.name: Permafrost
permafrost.desc: Wikipedia describes the park's permafrost as discontinuous and the shallow permafrost as thawing. Frozen ground limits tree growth and holds water near the surface.

permafrost & peatlands.name: Permafrost & peatlands
permafrost & peatlands.desc: Cold, waterlogged bogs and fens that hold large stores of carbon. Black spruce, tamarack and mosses are among the plants that live there.

permafrost soil.name: Permafrost soil
permafrost soil.desc: Frozen ground limits roots to a thin summer layer and locks away carbon.

peromyscus boylii.name: Brush mouse
peromyscus boylii.desc: Brush mouse (Peromyscus boylii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

peromyscus eremicus.name: Cactus mouse
peromyscus eremicus.desc: Cactus mouse (Peromyscus eremicus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

peromyscus leucopus.name: White-footed mouse
peromyscus leucopus.desc: White-footed mouse (Peromyscus leucopus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

peromyscus maniculatus.name: Deer mouse
peromyscus maniculatus.desc: Deer mouse (Peromyscus maniculatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

peromyscus melanotis.name: Black-eared mouse
peromyscus melanotis.desc: An omnivore of seeds and insects that tolerates milkweed toxins and eats monarchs in numbers at the overwintering colonies.

peromyscus mexicanus.name: Mexican deer mouse
peromyscus mexicanus.desc: A small rodent of montane forests. It eats seeds, fruit and insects and is prey for snakes and small cats.

persea palustris.name: Swamp bay
persea palustris.desc: A wetland evergreen tree. Its leaves feed the caterpillars of the Palamedes swallowtail.

persicaria amphibia.name: Amphibious Bistort
persicaria amphibia.desc: Amphibious Bistort (Persicaria amphibia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

persicaria arifolia.name: Halberdleaf Tearthumb
persicaria arifolia.desc: Halberdleaf Tearthumb (Persicaria arifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

persicaria lapathifolia.name: Curlytop knotweed
persicaria lapathifolia.desc: Curlytop knotweed (Persicaria lapathifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

persicaria longiseta.name: Bristly Lady's Thumb
persicaria longiseta.desc: Bristly Lady's Thumb (Persicaria longiseta): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

persicaria pensylvanica.name: Pennsylvania Smartweed
persicaria pensylvanica.desc: Pennsylvania Smartweed (Persicaria pensylvanica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 31 times near the park in GBIF.

petaurista lena.name: Giant flying squirrel
petaurista lena.wiki: Red and white giant flying squirrel
petaurista lena.desc: A large nocturnal glider that eats mostly nuts and fruit with some leaves and insects. It was the most common prey in a Taiwan hawk-eagle nest study.

petrochelidon fulva.name: Cave swallow
petrochelidon fulva.desc: Eats flying insects caught on the wing and nests at the cave entrance, which Audubon lists as an Important Bird Area.

petrochelidon pyrrhonota.name: Cliff swallow
petrochelidon pyrrhonota.desc: Cliff swallow (Petrochelidon pyrrhonota): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 139 times near the park in GBIF.

petroica macrocephala.name: Tomtit (miromiro)
petroica macrocephala.desc: A small insect-eating forest bird that hunts beetles, caterpillars, spiders and other invertebrates.

petromyzon marinus.name: Sea lamprey
petromyzon marinus.desc: An invasive parasite that feeds on the blood of large fish such as lake trout and whitefish. It is held in check by control programs.

phacelia dubia.name: Appalachian phacelia
phacelia dubia.desc: Appalachian phacelia (Phacelia dubia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.

phacelia hirsuta.name: Fuzzy phacelia
phacelia hirsuta.desc: Fuzzy phacelia (Phacelia hirsuta): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

phacelia integrifolia.name: Gypsum phacelia
phacelia integrifolia.desc: Gypsum phacelia (Phacelia integrifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.

phacelia linearis.name: Narrow-leafed phacelia
phacelia linearis.desc: Narrow-leafed phacelia (Phacelia linearis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 74 times near the park in GBIF.

phacelia lutea.name: Yellow phacelia
phacelia lutea.desc: Yellow phacelia (Phacelia lutea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

phacelia tanacetifolia.name: Phacelia
phacelia tanacetifolia.desc: Phacelia (Phacelia tanacetifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 28 times near the park in GBIF.

phacochoerus africanus.name: Common warthog
phacochoerus africanus.desc: A grass-eating wild pig, one of the best recorded large mammals near the park.

phaenops intrusa.name: A metallic wood-boring beetle
phaenops intrusa.desc: A metallic wood-boring beetle (Phaenops intrusa): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 50 times near the park in GBIF.

phainopepla nitens.name: Phainopepla
phainopepla nitens.desc: Phainopepla (Phainopepla nitens): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 8,239 times near the park in GBIF.

phalacrocorax auritus.name: Double-crested Cormorant
phalacrocorax auritus.desc: Double-crested Cormorant (Phalacrocorax auritus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 512 times near the park in GBIF.

phalacrocorax carbo.name: Great cormorant
phalacrocorax carbo.desc: A diving fish-eater of lakes, one of the most recorded birds around Uvs Lake.

phalacrocorax harrisi.name: Flightless cormorant
phalacrocorax harrisi.desc: A flightless bird that hunts fish and small octopuses in shallow water near shore. A 1983 El Niño cut its numbers by about half.

phalacrocorax varius.name: Pied cormorant
phalacrocorax varius.desc: A diving seabird that eats mostly small bottom-dwelling fish, with some prawns and other crustaceans.

phalanger orientalis.name: Northern common cuscus
phalanger orientalis.desc: A tree-living marsupial that eats leaves and fruit. It was brought to Timor about 9,000 years ago and is hunted by local people.

phalaris arundinacea.name: Reed Canary-grass
phalaris arundinacea.desc: Reed Canary-grass (Phalaris arundinacea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 28 times near the park in GBIF.

phalcoboenus australis.name: Striated caracara
phalcoboenus australis.desc: A rare raptor of offshore islands. It scavenges and also takes seabird eggs and chicks, penguins and seal pups.

phaneroptera nana.name: Mediterranean katydid
phaneroptera nana.desc: A leaf-eating insect recorded near Erigavo that feeds on plant foliage and is prey for insect-eating birds and lizards.

pheidole.name: Native seed-dispersing ants
pheidole.desc: Native ants carry seeds of plants such as the common pagoda underground, where fire does not reach them. Invading Argentine ants have displaced them in places.

pheucticus melanocephalus.name: Black-headed grosbeak
pheucticus melanocephalus.desc: A winter bird at the colonies that tolerates monarch toxins well enough to eat them, though it must ease off periodically.

phigys solitarius.name: Collared lory
phigys solitarius.desc: Eats fruit, seeds, nectar and blossoms, and favors African tulip flowers.

philantomba maxwellii.name: Maxwell's duiker
philantomba maxwellii.desc: A small forest antelope that is locally abundant in Sapo and well recorded here. It feeds on leaves and fruit.

philantomba monticola.name: Blue duiker
philantomba monticola.desc: A tiny forest antelope that eats mostly fallen fruit, plus leaves, flowers and some ants.

philodryas baroni.name: Baron's green racer
philodryas baroni.desc: A slender, rear-fanged snake of Chaco woodland that preys on lizards, birds and small mammals.

phlox adsurgens.name: Northern phlox
phlox adsurgens.desc: Northern phlox (Phlox adsurgens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 41 times near the park in GBIF.

phlox bifida.name: Sand phlox
phlox bifida.desc: Sand phlox (Phlox bifida): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

phlox divaricata.name: Wild blue phlox
phlox divaricata.desc: Wild blue phlox (Phlox divaricata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 40 times near the park in GBIF.

phlox hoodii.name: Hood's phlox
phlox hoodii.desc: Hood's phlox (Phlox hoodii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

phlox longifolia.name: Longleaf phlox
phlox longifolia.desc: Longleaf phlox (Phlox longifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

phlox multiflora.name: Many-flowered phlox
phlox multiflora.desc: Many-flowered phlox (Phlox multiflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

phlox pilosa.name: Prairie phlox
phlox pilosa.desc: Prairie phlox (Phlox pilosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

phlox woodhousei.name: Star phlox
phlox woodhousei.desc: Star phlox (Phlox woodhousei): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 30 times near the park in GBIF.

phoca vitulina.name: Harbor seal
phoca vitulina.desc: Feeds on fish near the forest edges. Harbor seals are among the main prey of great white sharks in California.

phoebis sennae.name: Cloudless Giant Sulphur
phoebis sennae.desc: Cloudless Giant Sulphur (Phoebis sennae): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

phoenicaulis cheiranthoides.name: Wallflower phoenicaulis
phoenicaulis cheiranthoides.desc: Wallflower phoenicaulis (Phoenicaulis cheiranthoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

phoenicolacerta troodica.name: Cypriote wall lizard
phoenicolacerta troodica.desc: Lizard endemic to Cyprus found from sea level to about 1,600 m; needs shade. A prey of many birds and snakes.

phoeniconaias minor.name: Lesser flamingo
phoeniconaias minor.desc: Filters spirulina from alkaline water with its specialised bill. Thousands gather at shallow Lake Magadi on the crater floor, where hyenas prey on them.

phoenicoparrus andinus.name: Andean flamingo
phoenicoparrus andinus.desc: Filter feeder with a very broad diet, mostly diatoms from the lake bottom in shallow salty water. Breeds in colonies in the high Andes.

phoenicoparrus jamesi.name: James's flamingo
phoenicoparrus jamesi.desc: Feeds mainly on diatoms and other microscopic algae filtered from the water. Especially abundant at Laguna Colorada.

phoenicopterus chilensis.name: Chilean flamingo
phoenicopterus chilensis.desc: Filter-feeds in shallow water on algae, plankton and small invertebrates, stirring up sediment with its feet.

phoenicopterus roseus.name: Greater flamingo
phoenicopterus roseus.desc: Filters brine shrimp, algae, insect larvae and molluscs from shallow saline water. Yellow-legged gulls take many of its eggs and chicks around the Mediterranean.

phoenicurus ochruros.name: Black redstart
phoenicurus ochruros.desc: An insect-eating songbird of rocky ground, recorded often near the park.

phoenix dactylifera.name: Date palm
phoenix dactylifera.desc: The classic oasis tree. Its sugary fruit is eaten by people and wildlife, including foxes.

phoradendron californicum.name: Mesquite mistletoe
phoradendron californicum.desc: Mesquite mistletoe (Phoradendron californicum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 84 times near the park in GBIF.

phosphorus.name: Phosphorus
phosphorus.desc: The nutrient that limits algae growth in the open lake. Mussels hold much of it near the shore and bottom.

phosphorus inputs.name: Phosphorus inputs
phosphorus inputs.desc: Household wastewater has raised phosphorus in the sediments about 3.5-fold in a century, a main threat to the lake.

photinus carolinus.name: Synchronous firefly
photinus carolinus.desc: Famous for synchronized flashing in early summer near Elkmont. Its larvae live in soil and eat snails, worms and other soft-bodied animals.

phragmites australis.name: Common reed
phragmites australis.desc: Common Reed (Phragmites australis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

phrynosoma platyrhinos.name: Desert horned lizard
phrynosoma platyrhinos.desc: A flat-bodied lizard of sandy desert that eats mainly ants and is prey for hawks and roadrunners.

phyciodes tharos.name: Pearl Crescent
phyciodes tharos.desc: Pearl Crescent (Phyciodes tharos): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

phyla lanceolata.name: Lance-leaf fogfruit
phyla lanceolata.desc: Lance-leaf fogfruit (Phyla lanceolata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

phyllanthus polygonoides.name: Smartweed leaf-flower
phyllanthus polygonoides.desc: Smartweed leaf-flower (Phyllanthus polygonoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

phyllastrephus flavostriatus.name: Yellow-streaked greenbul
phyllastrephus flavostriatus.desc: A forest-understorey songbird recorded eating Maesa and Tarenna fruits.

phyllodoce empetriformis, luetkea pectin.name: Alpine heath & meadow plants
phyllodoce empetriformis, luetkea pectin.desc: Mountain heath, partridgefoot and other low plants of the subalpine meadows, which cover the slopes roughly between 4,000 and 7,000 feet.

phymatodes nitidus.name: Sequoia cone longhorn beetle
phymatodes nitidus.desc: Its larvae bore into giant sequoia cones, cutting off water to the scales so cones dry and open and release seed.

physalis walteri.name: Walter's groundcherry
physalis walteri.desc: Walter's groundcherry (Physalis walteri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

physaria filiformis.name: Limestone glade baldderpod
physaria filiformis.desc: Limestone glade baldderpod (Physaria filiformis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

physaria scrotiformis.name: West silver bladderpod
physaria scrotiformis.desc: West silver bladderpod (Physaria scrotiformis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 28 times near the park in GBIF.

physematium obtusum.name: Blunt-lobed woodsia
physematium obtusum.desc: Blunt-lobed woodsia (Physematium obtusum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

phytolacca americana.name: American Pokeweed
phytolacca americana.desc: Pokeweed (Phytolacca americana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 386 times near the park in GBIF.

phytoplankton.name: Phytoplankton
phytoplankton.desc: Drifting algae in the ocean water that feed zooplankton at the base of the open-water food chain.

piaya cayana.name: Squirrel cuckoo
piaya cayana.desc: A long-tailed forest cuckoo that hunts large insects in the canopy and also eats fruit, such as milkberry.

pica hudsonia.name: Black-billed Magpie
pica hudsonia.desc: A clever, omnivorous bird that feeds at carcasses among other foods.

pica pica.name: Eurasian magpie
pica pica.desc: Omnivorous crow relative, the most recorded bird near the lake. Eats berries such as sea buckthorn along with insects and scraps.

picea abies.name: Norway spruce
picea abies.desc: A widespread conifer of the forest. Its seeds feed squirrels and its bark is where spruce bark beetles breed.

picea glauca.name: White spruce
picea glauca.desc: A conifer whose seeds feed red squirrels and which forms the forest along park lakes and rivers.

picea mariana.name: Black spruce
picea mariana.desc: The most widespread tree of the northern forest. Wikipedia notes it tolerates shallow soil, permafrost and waterlogged ground, though it grows slowly.

picea orientalis.name: Oriental spruce
picea orientalis.desc: A conifer of the Caucasus forests. Winter-feeding chamois use conifer needles and bark, and squirrels take conifer seed.

picea schrenkiana.name: Schrenk's spruce
picea schrenkiana.desc: The main conifer of the Tian Shan forests, forming important stands above about 2,000 m.

picea sitchensis.name: Sitka spruce
picea sitchensis.desc: A large conifer that forms the forest of the lower bay, on ground exposed by ice long ago.

pieris brassicae.name: Large White butterfly
pieris brassicae.desc: Butterfly whose caterpillars eat the leaves of herbs; adults and larvae feed insect-eating birds and lizards.

pieris rapae.name: Small White
pieris rapae.desc: Small White (Pieris rapae): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

piliocolobus badius.name: Western red colobus
piliocolobus badius.desc: A leaf- and fruit-eating monkey of the high canopy. Wikipedia calls it a frequent prey of chimpanzees.

piliocolobus preussi.name: Preuss's red colobus
piliocolobus preussi.desc: A rare leaf-eating monkey of the Cameroon-Nigeria forests, living high in the canopy.

piliocolobus spp..name: Red colobus monkeys
piliocolobus spp..desc: Leaf-eating monkeys of the forest canopy. Chimpanzees and crowned eagles hunt them.

pilosella aurantiaca.name: Orange Hawkweed
pilosella aurantiaca.desc: Orange Hawkweed (Pilosella aurantiaca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

pimenta racemosa.name: Bayrum tree
pimenta racemosa.desc: A forest tree recorded in the park; GloBI records fruit bats feeding on it.

pinanga.name: Understorey palms
pinanga.desc: Small palms of the shady forest floor; the park also has abundant rattan, gingers and ferns beneath the canopy.

pinaroloxias inornata.name: Cocos finch
pinaroloxias inornata.desc: Found only on Cocos Island, it eats berries and insects and uses varied foraging methods learned from other finches.

pinus.name: Pines
pinus.desc: Pines share the mountain slopes with oaks between roughly 1,500 and 3,000 m, below the oyamel belt.

pinus albicaulis.name: Whitebark pine
pinus albicaulis.desc: A high-elevation pine whose large seeds feed nutcrackers, squirrels and bears. Blister rust and pine beetles threaten it.

pinus banksiana.name: Jack pine
pinus banksiana.desc: A pine of dry, sandy ground whose resin-sealed cones open after fire to release seed.

pinus brutia.name: Turkish pine
pinus brutia.desc: Covers about 175,000 hectares of Cyprus, roughly 90% of its woodland, and is the most important forestry tree.

pinus cembra.name: Swiss stone pine
pinus cembra.desc: A conifer of the uppermost forest belt in the Alps. On the Aletsch side it forms forest on moraine laid down after the glacier maximum around 1850.

pinus contorta.name: Lodgepole pine
pinus contorta.desc: A conifer that recolonizes old burn areas in the subalpine zone. It is a host of the mountain pine beetle.

pinus echinata.name: Shortleaf pine
pinus echinata.desc: Pine dominates the south-facing slopes of the park. It tolerates fire and grows well on dry, nutrient-poor upland soils.

pinus edulis.name: Pinyon pine
pinus edulis.desc: A slow-growing pine of the pinyon-juniper woodland that covers much of the rim. Its large seeds feed wildlife.

pinus flexilis.name: Limber pine
pinus flexilis.desc: A high-elevation white pine with large seeds that Clark's nutcracker eats and caches.

pinus halepensis.name: Aleppo pine
pinus halepensis.desc: A Mediterranean pine of the sandy coastal forests, which are increasingly dominated by pines.

pinus heldreichii.name: Bosnian pine
pinus heldreichii.desc: A tough high-mountain pine that reaches the alpine tree line. Baikushev's pine in Pirin is estimated to be over 1,300 years old, Bulgaria's oldest tree.

pinus jeffreyi.name: Jeffrey pine
pinus jeffreyi.desc: Jeffrey pine (Pinus jeffreyi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 125 times near the park in GBIF.

pinus koraiensis.name: Korean pine
pinus koraiensis.desc: Its seeds stay in the cones until birds such as the nutcracker carry them off. The mixed Korean pine and broadleaf forest is described as the tiger's home forest.

pinus longaeva.name: Great Basin bristlecone pine
pinus longaeva.desc: Grows in open stands near treeline on rocky, often dolomite soils where few other plants thrive. It is the oldest known living non-clonal organism.

pinus nigra.name: European black pine
pinus nigra.desc: Dense forests cover much of the park, including old stands with trees about 400 years old and over 50 m tall. Chamois eat conifers in winter.

pinus occidentalis.name: Hispaniolan pine
pinus occidentalis.desc: The dominant pine of the open upper forest, whose seedlings do well after fire.

pinus palustris.name: Longleaf Pine
pinus palustris.desc: Longleaf pine (Pinus palustris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

pinus peuce.name: Macedonian pine
pinus peuce.desc: One of the park's largest forest types, covering roughly 54 square kilometres of the mountain slopes.

pinus ponderosa.name: Bull Pine
pinus ponderosa.desc: The main tree of the park's middle elevations. Clark's nutcrackers and jays eat its seeds, and GloBI records nutcrackers doing so.

pinus pumila.name: Siberian dwarf pine
pinus pumila.desc: A sprawling shrubby pine forming dense thickets above the treeline. Its seeds are harvested and spread by nutcrackers.

pinus rigida.name: Pitch pine
pinus rigida.desc: A hardy pine of sandy, poor soils that dominates much of the Cape's pine barrens woodland.

pinus sibirica.name: Siberian pine
pinus sibirica.desc: A five-needled pine of the mountain taiga whose large seeds are a food for birds such as the nutcracker.

pinus strobiformis.name: Border Limber Pine
pinus strobiformis.desc: Border Limber Pine (Pinus strobiformis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 103 times near the park in GBIF.

pinus strobus.name: Eastern white pine
pinus strobus.desc: Once the dominant tree here, white and red pine were reduced by logging and few large mature stands remain.

pinus sylvestris.name: Scots pine
pinus sylvestris.desc: Conifer of the drier forest and bog edges, whose twigs and bark browsers use in winter.

pinus taeda.name: Loblolly pine
pinus taeda.desc: Loblolly pine (Pinus taeda): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 55 times near the park in GBIF.

piper aequale.name: Piper
piper aequale.desc: A shrub of the pepper family. Fruit-eating bats such as Carollia are key dispersers of Piper seeds.

piper hostmannianum.name: Pepper plant
piper hostmannianum.desc: A forest understory shrub of the pepper genus. Its fruit is a favourite of Carollia fruit bats.

pipilo erythrophthalmus.name: Eastern Towhee
pipilo erythrophthalmus.desc: Eastern Towhee (Pipilo erythrophthalmus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1,175 times near the park in GBIF.

pipilo maculatus.name: Spotted Towhee
pipilo maculatus.desc: Spotted Towhee (Pipilo maculatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4,814 times near the park in GBIF.

pipra pipra.name: White-crowned manakin
pipra pipra.desc: A small fruit-eating forest bird, recorded very often here, that takes berries such as Miconia.

piranga rubra.name: Summer Tanager
piranga rubra.desc: Summer Tanager (Piranga rubra): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 146 times near the park in GBIF.

pistacia atlantica.name: Mount Atlas mastic tree
pistacia atlantica.desc: A tough tree of dry hill country that is recorded in the reserve. GloBI records blackbirds eating from it.

pistacia lentiscus.name: Mastic tree
pistacia lentiscus.desc: An evergreen Mediterranean shrub of coastal scrub, whose berries are eaten by some mammals.

pistia stratiotes.name: Water lettuce
pistia stratiotes.desc: Floating plant listed by UNESCO among the invasive aquatic plants that spread after the dam; warthogs are recorded eating it.

pitangus sulphuratus.name: Great kiskadee
pitangus sulphuratus.desc: One of the best-recorded birds here. GloBI records it eating Myrcia fruit, and it also takes insects and small prey.

pitohui dichrous.name: Hooded pitohui
pitohui dichrous.desc: Eats mostly fruit, especially figs, plus insects and other invertebrates. Its skin and feathers carry batrachotoxin, which may deter predators.

pittosporum viridiflorum.name: Cape pittosporum
pittosporum viridiflorum.desc: An evergreen forest tree whose fruit and foliage feed monkeys and many birds.

pituophis catenifer.name: Bullsnake
pituophis catenifer.desc: Bullsnake (Pituophis catenifer): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

pituophis catenifer sayi.name: Bullsnake
pituophis catenifer sayi.desc: A large constrictor that eats rodents and birds. GloBI records include kangaroo rats, mice and doves.

pituophis melanoleucus.name: Northern pine snake
pituophis melanoleucus.desc: A big constrictor that hunts mice and other small mammals, often in their burrows. It favours sandy habitat that burns often, and foxes dig up its nests.

pityopsis falcata.name: Sickleleaf Silkgrass
pityopsis falcata.desc: Sickleleaf Silkgrass (Pityopsis falcata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

plagiodontia aedium.name: Hispaniolan hutia
plagiodontia aedium.desc: A threatened, nocturnal island rodent that mainly eats roots and fruits.

plagiosiphon emarginatus.name: Plagiosiphon
plagiosiphon emarginatus.desc: A rainforest tree or shrub of West Africa often found near rivers. Colobus monkeys are recorded eating it in GloBI.

planera aquatica.name: Water-elm
planera aquatica.desc: Water-elm (Planera aquatica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.

plantago coronopus.name: Buck's-horn Plantain
plantago coronopus.desc: Buck's-horn Plantain (Plantago coronopus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

plantago lanceolata.name: Ribwort Plantain
plantago lanceolata.desc: Ribwort Plantain (Plantago lanceolata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

plantago patagonica.name: Woolly Indianwheat
plantago patagonica.desc: Woolly Indianwheat (Plantago patagonica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

platalea leucorodia.name: Eurasian spoonbill
platalea leucorodia.desc: Wading bird that sweeps its bill through shallows for small fish and crustaceans; the site is a major wintering ground.

platanista gangetica.name: Ganges river dolphin
platanista gangetica.desc: A freshwater dolphin that lives in the less salty channels and hunts fish and shrimp.

platanthera ciliaris.name: Yellow fringed orchid
platanthera ciliaris.desc: Yellow fringed orchid (Platanthera ciliaris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.

platanthera dilatata.name: White Bog Orchid
platanthera dilatata.desc: White Bog Orchid (Platanthera dilatata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

platanus occidentalis.name: Sycamore
platanus occidentalis.desc: Sycamore (Platanus occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

platanus wrightii.name: Arizona sycamore
platanus wrightii.desc: Arizona sycamore (Platanus wrightii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 190 times near the park in GBIF.

platte river flow.name: Platte River flow
platte river flow.desc: Spring and summer flows keep channels open and wet meadows green, but Wikipedia says river water is overappropriated and has shrunk since the mid-20th century.

platystemon californicus.name: Cream-cups
platystemon californicus.desc: Cream-cups (Platystemon californicus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

plectrophenax nivalis.name: Snow bunting
plectrophenax nivalis.desc: A small songbird of rocky highlands and shores that eats seeds and berries of heath plants.

plectropomus leopardus.name: Coral trout
plectropomus leopardus.desc: A reef predator that hunts damselfish and parrotfish.

plegadis falcinellus.name: Glossy ibis
plegadis falcinellus.desc: Wades in very shallow water for insect larvae, worms, snails and crustaceans, plus the occasional frog.

plegadis ridgwayi.name: Puna ibis
plegadis ridgwayi.desc: Probes shallow water and mud for invertebrates, and takes amphibians and small fish when it can. It nests in tall wetland vegetation.

plethodon cinereus.name: Eastern red-backed salamander
plethodon cinereus.desc: Lungless salamander of the leaf litter that eats small invertebrates. It is among the most recorded animals near the park.

plethodontidae.name: Lungless salamanders
plethodontidae.desc: The Smokies hold up to 31 salamander species, earning the title Salamander Capital of the World. These small amphibians eat tiny invertebrates.

pleuronectes platessa.name: European plaice
pleuronectes platessa.desc: Young plaice settle on shallow flats and stay for a few months before moving to deeper water. They eat shrimp, then worms and bivalves.

ploceus capensis.name: Cape weaver
ploceus capensis.desc: A seed and insect eating bird of southern African grassland and scrub, a regular prey of shrikes.

pluvialis squatarola.name: Black-bellied Plover
pluvialis squatarola.desc: Black-bellied Plover (Pluvialis squatarola): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 254 times near the park in GBIF.

poa.name: Native grasses
poa.desc: Grasses of the meadows are a main food of Utah prairie dogs, which favour a few native grass species.

poa alpina.name: Alpine meadow-grass
poa alpina.desc: A common grass of high mountain meadows, grazed by insects and small mammals.

poa annua.name: Annual Meadow-grass
poa annua.desc: Annual Meadow-grass (Poa annua): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

poa cookii.name: Cook's tussock grass
poa cookii.desc: Tussock grass of subantarctic coasts and slopes. Introduced rabbits graze it.

poa fendleriana.name: Muttongrass
poa fendleriana.desc: Muttongrass (Poa fendleriana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

poa flabellata.name: Tussac grass
poa flabellata.desc: A tall coastal grass that grows in dense clumps about 2 m high and dominates the shoreline where it grows. Penguins, albatrosses and seals use it for cover and nesting.

poa glauca.name: Arctic grasses
poa glauca.desc: Hardy grasses of dry slopes and gravel. GloBI records common redpolls eating Poa glauca.

poa secunda.name: Sandberg's bluegrass
poa secunda.desc: Sandberg's bluegrass (Poa secunda): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

poaceae.name: Floodplain grasses
poaceae.desc: Grasses along rivers and swamp edges are grazed by hippos at night.

poaceae and carex.name: Alpine grasses & sedges
poaceae and carex.desc: Short-turf meadow plants above the treeline, grazed by wild and domestic hoofed animals and by marmots.

poaceae and wildflowers.name: Mountain meadow grasses & wildflowers
poaceae and wildflowers.desc: Grasses and flowering plants of the wetter high meadows, eaten by elk, deer and small rodents.

podocarpus.name: Montane forest trees
podocarpus.desc: Podocarpus and other evergreen trees of the cloud forest on the middle slopes, home to monkeys, hyraxes and elephants.

podocarpus urbanii.name: Blue Mountain yacca
podocarpus urbanii.desc: A native conifer of the high Blue Mountain forest, one of the plant species recorded most often in the park area.

podoces panderi.name: Turkestan ground jay
podoces panderi.desc: A ground-living crow of sandy desert with low shrubs, and the best-recorded bird near the reserve. Forages on the ground.

podophyllum peltatum.name: Mayapple
podophyllum peltatum.desc: Mayapple (Podophyllum peltatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.

poecile atricapillus.name: Black-capped Chickadee
poecile atricapillus.desc: Black-capped Chickadee (Poecile atricapillus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.

poecile carolinensis.name: Carolina Chickadee
poecile carolinensis.desc: Carolina Chickadee (Poecile carolinensis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 180 times near the park in GBIF.

poecile rufescens.name: Chestnut-backed Chickadee
poecile rufescens.desc: Chestnut-backed Chickadee (Poecile rufescens): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 38 times near the park in GBIF.

poecilia latipinna.name: Sailfin molly
poecilia latipinna.desc: A small fish that grazes algae and plant matter. It is a staple prey for wading birds and larger fish.

pogoniulus bilineatus.name: Yellow-rumped tinkerbird
pogoniulus bilineatus.desc: A small forest barbet recorded eating Maesa and Tarenna fruits.

pogonocichla stellata.name: White-starred robin
pogonocichla stellata.desc: A forest-floor songbird that feeds on insects and also takes fruit such as Ilex and Maesa berries.

pogonomyrmex californicus.name: California harvester ant
pogonomyrmex californicus.desc: Gathers seeds of desert plants for its nest and is prey for horned lizards.

pogonomyrmex rugosus.name: Rough harvester ant
pogonomyrmex rugosus.desc: A seed-collecting ant that stores seeds in underground nests. It is a common insect of the park's dry grassland.

polioptila caerulea.name: Blue-gray Gnatcatcher
polioptila caerulea.desc: Blue-gray Gnatcatcher (Polioptila caerulea): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 585 times near the park in GBIF.

polistes dominula.name: Paper Wasp
polistes dominula.desc: Paper Wasp (Polistes dominula): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.

polistes exclamans.name: Paper wasp
polistes exclamans.desc: Paper wasp (Polistes exclamans): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

polyboroides radiatus.name: Madagascar harrier-hawk
polyboroides radiatus.desc: Raptor that kills some sifaka infants and also takes lemurs and reptiles.

polyboroides typus.name: African harrier-hawk
polyboroides typus.desc: A raptor with flexible legs that probes cavities and nests for prey. It is often recorded near the park.

polychaeta.name: Marine worms
polychaeta.desc: Bristle worms living in the mud, a major prey of shorebirds that probe the flats.

polychaetes and bivalves.name: Seafloor worms & clams
polychaetes and bivalves.desc: Bottom dwellers that feed on sinking algae and detritus. They suffocate when oxygen drops very low.

polygaloides paucifolia.name: Polygaloides paucifolia
polygaloides paucifolia.desc: Polygaloides paucifolia (Polygaloides paucifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

polygonia comma.name: Eastern Comma
polygonia comma.desc: Eastern Comma (Polygonia comma): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

polygonia faunus.name: Green Comma
polygonia faunus.desc: Green Comma (Polygonia faunus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 40 times near the park in GBIF.

polygonia interrogationis.name: Question Mark
polygonia interrogationis.desc: Question Mark (Polygonia interrogationis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

polygonum kelloggii.name: Polygonum kelloggii
polygonum kelloggii.desc: Polygonum kelloggii (Polygonum kelloggii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 38 times near the park in GBIF.

polygonum polygaloides.name: Milkwort Knotweed
polygonum polygaloides.desc: Milkwort Knotweed (Polygonum polygaloides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

polymnia canadensis.name: Whiteflower leafcup
polymnia canadensis.desc: Whiteflower leafcup (Polymnia canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 27 times near the park in GBIF.

polyodon spathula.name: Paddlefish
polyodon spathula.desc: A giant filter feeder that eats mainly zooplankton, with a few insect larvae and small fish.

polypedates cruciger.name: Hour-glass tree frog
polypedates cruciger.desc: A common tree frog of Sri Lanka that eats insects at night.

polypedates leucomystax.name: Common tree frog
polypedates leucomystax.desc: A tree frog that catches insects at night; GloBI records it as prey of the striped bronzeback.

polystepha pilulae.name: Oak Leaf Gall Midge
polystepha pilulae.desc: Oak Leaf Gall Midge (Polystepha pilulae): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

polystichum acrostichoides.name: Christmas Fern
polystichum acrostichoides.desc: Christmas Fern (Polystichum acrostichoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.

polystichum munitum.name: Western Swordfern
polystichum munitum.desc: Sword fern (Polystichum munitum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.

pomacea.name: Apple snails
pomacea.desc: Wikipedia calls them a keystone group of the Pantanal. They eat dead plant matter in oxygen-poor floodwater and are food for many animals.

pomacea paludosa.name: Florida apple snail
pomacea paludosa.desc: A large freshwater snail that grazes on algae and plants. It is nearly the only food of the snail kite.

pomacentridae.name: Damselfish
pomacentridae.desc: Guards patches of algae and picks plankton from the water above the reef.

pomatomus saltatrix.name: Bluefish
pomatomus saltatrix.desc: A fast schooling predator that hunts forage fish such as menhaden.

pongo abelii.name: Sumatran orangutan
pongo abelii.desc: Mainly a fruit eater that favours figs and gathers at fruiting fig trees. Insects, leaves and bark add to the diet. Wikipedia says the park is one of two remaining habitats.

pontederia azurea.name: Anchored waterhyacinth
pontederia azurea.desc: A rooted emergent water plant of marshes and lagoon edges. Pontederiaceae are a major part of what marsh deer eat.

pontederia cordata.name: Pickerelweed
pontederia cordata.desc: Pickerelweed (Pontederia cordata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 48 times near the park in GBIF.

pontederia crassipes.name: Aquatic plants
pontederia crassipes.desc: Floating and submerged plants of the beels, or flood lakes. Rhinos eat them, but invasive water hyacinth can choke the water bodies.

pontia beckerii.name: Becker's White
pontia beckerii.desc: Becker's White (Pontia beckerii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

pontia protodice.name: Checkered White
pontia protodice.desc: Checkered White (Pontia protodice): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

pontoporia blainvillei.name: Franciscana
pontoporia blainvillei.desc: A small coastal dolphin, the best-recorded mammal here, that feeds on fish and squid in shallow water.

pooecetes gramineus.name: Vesper Sparrow
pooecetes gramineus.desc: Vesper Sparrow (Pooecetes gramineus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 594 times near the park in GBIF.

poor acidic soils.name: Poor acidic soils
poor acidic soils.desc: Cerrado soils are well drained and mostly acidic and low in nutrients, which helps set what can grow.

poor, dry soils.name: Poor, dry soils
poor, dry soils.desc: Thin soils over limestone and sand in the west and south, with low and erratic winter rain, favour drought-adapted plants.

poor, wet soils.name: Poor, wet soils
poor, wet soils.desc: Nutrient-poor ultisols that drain badly, so nutrients cycle quickly through living plants and leaf litter.

popillia japonica.name: Japanese Beetle
popillia japonica.desc: Japanese Beetle (Popillia japonica): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

populus deltoides.name: Necklace Poplar
populus deltoides.desc: Necklace Poplar (Populus deltoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

populus deltoides, acer saccharinum.name: Cottonwood & silver maple
populus deltoides, acer saccharinum.desc: Bottomland forest trees that flood each spring. Beavers and deer use them.

populus fremontii.name: Fremont cottonwood
populus fremontii.desc: A riverside tree of the canyon floor that grows along the Virgin River and shades the streamside community.

populus heterophylla.name: Swamp poplar
populus heterophylla.desc: Swamp poplar (Populus heterophylla): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

populus tremula.name: Aspen
populus tremula.desc: A fast-growing riverside and forest tree. Beavers fell it and moose and hares browse its bark and twigs.

populus tremuloides.name: Quaking aspen
populus tremuloides.desc: A broadleaf tree that sprouts quickly after disturbance. Moose, hares and beavers eat its bark, twigs and shoots.

porcella salvania.name: Pygmy hog
porcella salvania.desc: An omnivore of tall dense grassland that digs roots and tubers and shelters in grass-lined nests. The only known wild population is at Manas.

porifera.name: Marine sponges
porifera.desc: Filter feeders on the reef that strain tiny particles from the water. They are the main food of hawksbill turtles.

porphyrio hochstetteri.name: Takahe
porphyrio hochstetteri.desc: Large flightless rail rediscovered in the Murchison Mountains in 1948. It eats mainly the leaves of snow tussock.

posidonia australis.name: Ribbonweed
posidonia australis.desc: A seagrass whose meadows in Shark Bay include one giant clone covering about 200 square km. Rhizomes anchor the sand and the leaves slow silt.

posoqueria latifolia.name: Needle flower
posoqueria latifolia.desc: A tropical understory tree with fragrant flowers and fruit that bats and birds in the area are recorded eating.

potamochoerus porcus.name: Red river hog
potamochoerus porcus.desc: A forest pig that forages for fruit, roots and plants. GloBI has a record of it feeding on forest elephant.

potamogeton.name: Pondweed & water lilies
potamogeton.desc: Aquatic plants of ponds and sheltered bays. Moose wade in to eat them, mainly for sodium.

potamogeton crispus.name: Curled Pondweed
potamogeton crispus.desc: Curled Pondweed (Potamogeton crispus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 33 times near the park in GBIF.

potamogeton lucens.name: Shining pondweed
potamogeton lucens.desc: A submerged aquatic plant recorded in the marsh area, providing food and cover in open water.

potentilla supina.name: Bushy Cinquefoil
potentilla supina.desc: Bushy Cinquefoil (Potentilla supina): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

prairie fire.name: Prairie fire
prairie fire.desc: Fire is one of the environmental factors the park manages, including prescribed burns that clear old growth.

prairie soil.name: Prairie soil
prairie soil.desc: Nutrients released by decay return to the soil and feed the next season of plant growth.

prairie soil & badland clays.name: Prairie soil & badland clays
prairie soil & badland clays.desc: Soils on the benches hold the grass roots; the eroding badland slopes stay mostly bare.

praomys jacksoni.name: Jackson's soft-furred mouse
praomys jacksoni.desc: The most-recorded mammal near the park; an abundant forest floor rodent that eats seeds, fruit and insects.

praomys tullbergi.name: Tullberg's soft-furred mouse
praomys tullbergi.desc: A small forest rodent that forages on the forest floor and is prey for genets and snakes.

prenolepis imparis.name: American Winter Ant
prenolepis imparis.desc: American Winter Ant (Prenolepis imparis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

presbytis thomasi.name: Thomas's langur
presbytis thomasi.desc: A leaf-monkey of northern Sumatra. GloBI records show it eating fig and Macaranga fruit near the park.

prestoea acuminata.name: Sierra palm
prestoea acuminata.desc: Dominates the palm forest zone on shallow soils at about 600 m. Its fruit is eaten by birds in the forest.

primula.name: Alpine meadow flowers
primula.desc: Alpine meadows above the treeline are rich in primulas, gentians and grasses that grazers and small mammals eat.

pringlea antiscorbutica.name: Kerguelen cabbage
pringlea antiscorbutica.desc: Edible cabbage-like plant of subantarctic islands. Introduced rabbits eat it, so it now survives mainly where rabbits cannot reach.

pringleophaga kerguelensis.name: Kerguelen flightless moth
pringleophaga kerguelensis.desc: Flightless moth whose larvae feed on Kerguelen cabbage, a major part of the native litter-feeding fauna.

priodontes maximus.name: Giant armadillo
priodontes maximus.desc: Eats mainly termites and ants, and its burrows are used by many other animals, making it a habitat engineer.

prionailurus bengalensis.name: Leopard cat
prionailurus bengalensis.desc: Small wild cat that hunts small mammals; GloBI records include dusky leaf monkey and plantain squirrel.

prionailurus viverrinus.name: Fishing cat
prionailurus viverrinus.desc: A wetland cat that ambushes prey at the water's edge. Fish are its main food, with crabs and rodents also taken.

pristurus sokotranus.name: Socotra rock gecko
pristurus sokotranus.desc: A small rock-dwelling gecko of the island, and one of its many endemic reptiles.

problema bulenta.name: Rare Skipper
problema bulenta.desc: Rare Skipper (Problema bulenta): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

procambarus alleni.name: Slough crayfish
procambarus alleni.desc: A crayfish that grazes on plants and microbes, and survives the dry season in burrows and wet refuges. Many wading birds, fish and mammals eat it.

procambarus clarkii.name: Red swamp crayfish
procambarus clarkii.desc: A North American crayfish introduced to Spain for cultivation. It spreads easily in disturbed wetlands and now feeds many wading birds and otters.

procavia capensis.name: Rock hyrax
procavia capensis.desc: A rock-dwelling herbivore of the mountain slopes, frequently recorded near the site.

prochilodus lineatus.name: Curimbata & other detritus fish
prochilodus lineatus.desc: A migratory fish that feeds on fine organic matter. Most Pantanal fish are detritus eaters, which makes them a major food source for predators.

procolobus verus.name: Olive colobus
procolobus verus.desc: A small, secretive leaf-eating monkey of the lower forest levels, also recorded eating Plagiosiphon.

procyon cancrivorus.name: Crab-eating raccoon
procyon cancrivorus.desc: Omnivore of marshy places in Trinidad that eats crabs, shellfish, fish, amphibians and fruit.

procyon lotor.name: Raccoon
procyon lotor.desc: Raccoon (Procyon lotor): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

proechimys semispinosus.name: Tome's spiny rat
proechimys semispinosus.desc: A common forest rodent that eats seeds and fruit on the ground and is food for snakes, hawks and small cats.

promerops cafer.name: Cape sugarbird
promerops cafer.desc: A nectar specialist that feeds on proteas and also takes insects and spiders. It is common in mature fynbos and almost absent from recently burned areas.

propithecus verreauxi.name: Verreaux's sifaka
propithecus verreauxi.desc: Mostly a leaf eater, also taking fruit, flowers and bark. Infants are hunted by fossas and harrier-hawks.

prosopeia personata.name: Masked shining parrot
prosopeia personata.desc: A big parrot found only on Viti Levu, living in lowland and hill forest and gardens.

prosopis alba.name: White carob (algarrobo)
prosopis alba.desc: A thorny, drought-tolerant Chaco tree that bears sugary pods; mammals and birds eat the pods and fruit.

prosopis glandulosa.name: Honey mesquite
prosopis glandulosa.desc: A deep-rooted desert shrub that can reach groundwater and stabilise sand around its base.

prosopis pubescens.name: Screw-bean
prosopis pubescens.desc: Screw-bean (Prosopis pubescens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 79 times near the park in GBIF.

prosopis velutina.name: Velvet mesquite
prosopis velutina.desc: A desert tree whose seed pods and foliage feed many animals.

prosthemadera novaeseelandiae.name: Tūī
prosthemadera novaeseelandiae.desc: A common native honeyeater of the park's forests, feeding on nectar and fruit.

protea repens.name: Sugarbush protea
protea repens.desc: A common protea of the fynbos, recorded very often near the site. Its nectar-rich flower heads feed the Cape sugarbird.

proteles cristata.name: Aardwolf
proteles cristata.desc: A small hyena relative that specializes in eating termites.

protopterus aethiopicus.name: Marbled lungfish
protopterus aethiopicus.desc: An air-breathing fish of swamps that eats fish and molluscs; it is a key prey of the shoebill.

protoxerus stangeri.name: Forest giant squirrel
protoxerus stangeri.desc: Forages for fruits and seeds of trees and lianas, cracking tough nuts, plus a few insects.

prunella vulgaris.name: Selfheal
prunella vulgaris.desc: Selfheal (Prunella vulgaris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

prunus africana.name: African cherry
prunus africana.desc: A big montane forest tree whose fruit is eaten by monkeys, birds and other forest animals.

prunus arborea.name: Prunus arborea
prunus arborea.desc: A forest tree that GloBI records as eaten by Asian elephants near the park.

prunus bucharica.name: Bukhara almond
prunus bucharica.desc: A wild almond of the Central Asian foothills that grows at roughly 1,000 to 1,800 m. The cinereous vulture nests in Bukhara almond trees in this range, per the Key Biodiversity Areas factsheet.

prunus padus.name: Bird cherry
prunus padus.desc: A small tree of moist floodplain woods, well recorded in the park. Its fruit and twigs feed many animals.

prunus serotina.name: Rum Cherry
prunus serotina.desc: Rum Cherry (Prunus serotina): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

prunus virginiana.name: Chokecherry
prunus virginiana.desc: A thicket-forming shrub of draws and slopes whose leaves and fruit are eaten by deer and other animals.

psaltoda insularis.name: Lord Howe cicada
psaltoda insularis.desc: An insect of the island forest. Cicadas feed on plant sap, and many are prey for birds.

psammodynastes pulverulentus.name: Common mock viper
psammodynastes pulverulentus.desc: A small snake that hunts lizards, and GloBI records it eating the brown mabuya skink.

psammophis lineolatus.name: Steppe ribbon racer
psammophis lineolatus.desc: A slender, fast snake of sandy deserts that eats lizards such as the steppe agama.

psammophis mossambicus.name: Olive grass snake
psammophis mossambicus.desc: A slender snake; GloBI records show it eating the African striped skink.

psammophylax rhombeatus.name: Rhombic skaapsteker
psammophylax rhombeatus.desc: A grassland snake that eats frogs, lizards and small mammals.

psarocolius montezuma.name: Montezuma oropendola
psarocolius montezuma.desc: A well-recorded colonial bird; GloBI shows it eating cocoplum, Davilla and coral-bean fruit.

pseudanthias.name: Reef planktivores
pseudanthias.desc: Small schooling reef fish that pick zooplankton from the water above the coral. Their role here is general reef ecology.

pseudaspis cana.name: Mole snake
pseudaspis cana.desc: A constrictor that eats mainly rodents and other small vertebrates, a common snake of the Cape.

pseudois nayaur.name: Blue sheep (bharal)
pseudois nayaur.desc: A grazer of alpine meadows and rocky slopes. It is the favoured prey of snow leopards, and wolves also hunt it.

pseudonympha varii.name: Vari's brown
pseudonympha varii.desc: A grassland butterfly of the Drakensberg; browns of this group have grass-feeding caterpillars. General ecology.

pseudopanurgus aestivalis.name: Aestival Bare-miner
pseudopanurgus aestivalis.desc: Aestival Bare-miner (Pseudopanurgus aestivalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.

pseudopus apodus.name: European glass lizard
pseudopus apodus.desc: A big legless lizard that eats insects, snails and small vertebrates, including other lizards in GloBI records.

pseudorca crassidens.name: False killer whale
pseudorca crassidens.desc: A toothed whale that preys on large fish such as adult yellowfin tuna.

pseudoroegneria.name: Bunchgrasses and sedges
pseudoroegneria.desc: Native grasses and sedges that grow among the sagebrush and in wet meadows, grazed by elk and bison.

pseudoroegneria spicata.name: Bluebunch wheatgrass
pseudoroegneria spicata.desc: A bunchgrass of the northern range and the base of the grazing chain for elk, bison and pronghorn.

pseudoryx nghetinhensis.name: Saola
pseudoryx nghetinhensis.desc: A rare ox-like animal confined to the Annamite Range, listed in the park as possibly present. It feeds on leaves, including spleenwort, pulled into the mouth with a long tongue.

pseudotsuga menziesii.name: Douglas Fir
pseudotsuga menziesii.desc: A dominant tall conifer of the lower forests. Its seeds are eaten by Douglas squirrels, chickadees and other small animals.

psidium cattleianum.name: Strawberry guava
psidium cattleianum.desc: An introduced fruiting tree that invades native forest. Several birds and feral pigs eat its fruit and spread the seeds.

psilocorsis reflexella.name: Dotted Leaftier
psilocorsis reflexella.desc: Dotted Leaftier (Psilocorsis reflexella): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

psilopogon pulcherrimus.name: Golden-naped barbet
psilopogon pulcherrimus.desc: A montane Bornean bird recorded thousands of times near the park; barbets in general take fruit such as figs.

pteralopex taki.name: New Georgia monkey-faced bat
pteralopex taki.desc: A large fruit bat found in the Solomon Islands. Fruit bats eat fruit and are food for the Sanford's sea eagle.

pteridium aquilinum.name: Bracken
pteridium aquilinum.desc: A fern of forest clearings and edges that spreads across open ground.

pterocles coronatus.name: Crowned sandgrouse
pterocles coronatus.desc: A ground-dwelling desert bird that feeds mainly on seeds.

pterodroma hypoleuca.name: Bonin petrel
pterodroma hypoleuca.desc: A seabird that nests in burrows on the islands and feeds at sea. Rats and cats are predators of burrow nests.

pterois volitans.name: Red lionfish
pterois volitans.desc: Invasive fish that eats small fish and crustaceans on Caribbean reefs and can cut the numbers of native reef fish.

pteronura brasiliensis.name: Giant otter
pteronura brasiliensis.desc: Hunts fish in family groups along river banks.

pteropus anetianus.name: Vanuatu flying fox
pteropus anetianus.desc: A fruit bat found only in Vanuatu and listed as Vulnerable. Flying foxes are fruit and nectar eaters and are hunted for food on Santo.

pteropus conspicillatus.name: Spectacled flying fox
pteropus conspicillatus.desc: Feeds mainly on rainforest fruit and on flowers of Syzygium and eucalypts. Endangered, partly after a 2018-19 heatwave.

pteropus lylei.name: Lyle's flying fox
pteropus lylei.desc: A large fruit bat of Cambodia and nearby countries that roosts in trees and feeds on fruit such as strawberry tree.

pteropus pselaphon.name: Bonin flying fox
pteropus pselaphon.desc: Endemic fruit bat of the Ogasawara and Volcano Islands, listed as endangered. It eats fruit such as Pandanus and flowers.

pteropus rufus.name: Madagascan flying fox
pteropus rufus.desc: A large fruit bat that roosts in groups and feeds at night on fruit and flowers.

pteropus samoensis.name: Samoa flying fox
pteropus samoensis.desc: A fruit bat that feeds on fruit, leaves and flowers in forest. Hunting and forest clearance threaten it.

pteropus tonganus.name: Pacific flying fox
pteropus tonganus.desc: A fruit bat that eats fruit, pollen and nectar, and pollinates some trees as it feeds.

ptilinopus cinctus.name: Black-backed fruit dove
ptilinopus cinctus.desc: A very commonly recorded forest bird of the area that feeds mainly on fruit, including figs, and spreads seeds.

ptilinopus greyi.name: Red-bellied fruit dove
ptilinopus greyi.desc: A fruit dove of lowland forest in Vanuatu, New Caledonia and the Santa Cruz Islands, and one of the most recorded birds near Santo.

ptilotus exaltatus.name: Pink mulla mulla
ptilotus exaltatus.desc: A showy desert wildflower that blooms after rain. Galahs have been recorded eating it.

ptyas mucosa.name: Oriental rat snake
ptyas mucosa.desc: A fast ground snake of forest and fields that eats small vertebrates and is itself prey of the king cobra.

ptyodactylus ragazzii.name: Ragazzi's fan-footed gecko
ptyodactylus ragazzii.desc: Rock-dwelling gecko recorded near the lake that hunts small insects such as locusts and other arthropods.

pugettia producta.name: Kelp crab
pugettia producta.desc: A crab of kelp holdfasts and canopy that grazes on kelp; kelp crabs are among the animals that eat kelp.

puma concolor.name: Puma
puma concolor.desc: Puma (Puma concolor): a top predator in this web. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

puma concolor coryi.name: Florida panther
puma concolor coryi.desc: A rare big cat that hunts deer, hogs, raccoons and other mammals. Pythons eat the same prey.

purshia stansburiana.name: Stansbury cliffrose
purshia stansburiana.desc: A woody desert shrub. Wikipedia lists cliffrose among the plants mule deer commonly browse.

purshia tridentata.name: Antelope bitterbrush
purshia tridentata.desc: Antelope bitterbrush (Purshia tridentata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 161 times near the park in GBIF.

pusa hispida.name: Ringed seal
pusa hispida.desc: Lives under the ice, keeping breathing holes open and hunting cod.

pusa sibirica.name: Baikal seal (nerpa)
pusa sibirica.desc: The only seal living entirely in fresh water. Golomyanka make up most of its diet, and it digs breathing holes and dens in the ice.

pycnonotus barbatus.name: Common bulbul
pycnonotus barbatus.desc: A common fruit-eating songbird; records show it eating the fruits of Ilex, Macaranga, Maesa and Tarenna.

pycnonotus cafer.name: Red-vented bulbul
pycnonotus cafer.desc: A well-recorded songbird that eats fruit and insects. GloBI records include it eating Melastoma and being eaten by the green vine snake.

pycnonotus jocosus.name: Red-whiskered bulbul
pycnonotus jocosus.desc: The best-recorded bird in the surrounding area. It eats fruit and insects, and spreads seeds.

pycnopodia helianthoides.name: Sunflower sea star
pycnopodia helianthoides.desc: A big predatory sea star that eats many urchins. Sea star wasting disease wiped it out from California waters from 2013, and urchins have been rising since.

pygathrix nemaeus.name: Red-shanked douc
pygathrix nemaeus.desc: A colourful leaf-eating monkey. Wikipedia says the park runs a semi-wild zone that protects primates such as the douc.

pygocentrus nattereri.name: Red-bellied piranha
pygocentrus nattereri.desc: Hunts fish in groups and scavenges dead animals in the river.

pygoctenucha terminalis.name: Pygoctenucha terminalis
pygoctenucha terminalis.desc: Pygoctenucha terminalis (Pygoctenucha terminalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

pygoscelis adeliae.name: Adelie penguin
pygoscelis adeliae.desc: Ice-dependent penguin that feeds on krill. Leopard seals hunt it.

pygoscelis papua.name: Gentoo penguin
pygoscelis papua.desc: Penguin of the Peninsula that eats krill and fish. Leopard seals prey on it.

pylodictis olivaris.name: Flathead catfish
pylodictis olivaris.desc: Mostly eats fish once larger than about 25 cm. Prey includes gizzard shad, drum, carp and crayfish.

pyrrhocorax graculus.name: Alpine chough
pyrrhocorax graculus.desc: Cliff-nesting crow that eats insects in summer and berries in colder months. Golden eagles and ravens take choughs or their young.

pyrus.name: Wild pears
pyrus.desc: The reserve is home to several wild pear species, including ones named after the area, whose fruit feeds many animals.

python bivittatus.name: Burmese python
python bivittatus.desc: An invasive constrictor released from the pet trade. It eats mammals and birds, and has caused steep declines in medium-sized mammals.

python molurus.name: Indian rock python
python molurus.desc: A large constrictor that GloBI records eating hog deer.

python natalensis.name: African rock python
python natalensis.desc: An ambush predator that takes birds and medium-sized mammals such as impala.

python regius.name: Ball python
python regius.desc: A constrictor that eats rodents and other small vertebrates; recorded prey includes forest rodents and the forest giant squirrel.

python sebae.name: African rock python
python sebae.desc: A large forest snake. Wikipedia names a rock python among predators of young pygmy hippos.

qualea.name: Fire-adapted cerrado trees
qualea.desc: Qualea trees dominate much of the Cerrado. Many Cerrado trees have thick corky bark that protects them from fire.

quercus.name: Oaks
quercus.desc: Black oak dominates savanna on sandy soils per Wikipedia, which lists Indiana Dunes as a remnant oak savanna. Acorns feed many animals.

quercus alba.name: White oak
quercus alba.desc: White oak (Quercus alba): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus alnifolia.name: Golden oak
quercus alnifolia.desc: Endemic to Cyprus; the main broadleaved tree of the conifer forests. Its stands hold soil on stony slopes and build humus.

quercus aquifolioides.name: Hengduan Mountain oak
quercus aquifolioides.desc: An evergreen mountain oak recorded often around the area. Its acorns and leaves feed forest animals.

quercus castaneifolia.name: Chestnut-leaved oak
quercus castaneifolia.desc: A Hyrcanian forest oak, recorded often near the park. Its acorns are food for forest mammals.

quercus chrysolepis.name: Canyon live oak
quercus chrysolepis.desc: CANYON LIVE OAK (Quercus chrysolepis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 77 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus douglasii.name: Blue oak
quercus douglasii.desc: Dominant tree of the dry blue oak woodland in the Sierra foothills, alongside gray pine and other oaks. Its acorns are eaten by wildlife.

quercus gambelii.name: Gambel oak
quercus gambelii.desc: Oak scrub of the canyon rim. Deer browse it and squirrels and bears eat the acorns; it regrows from root sprouts after fire.

quercus hypoleucoides.name: Silverleaf oak
quercus hypoleucoides.desc: Silverleaf oak (Quercus hypoleucoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 127 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus infectoria, quercus coccifera.name: Oaks
quercus infectoria, quercus coccifera.desc: Oak woodland, including kermes oak, is among the most recorded vegetation near the reserve. Acorns feed wild boar.

quercus john-tuckeri.name: Tucker's oak
quercus john-tuckeri.desc: Tucker's oak (Quercus john-tuckeri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus kelloggii.name: California black oak
quercus kelloggii.desc: A mid-elevation oak whose acorns and leaves feed deer, bears and rodents.

quercus laevis.name: Catesby's oak
quercus laevis.desc: Catesby's oak (Quercus laevis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 35 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus macranthera.name: Caucasian oak
quercus macranthera.desc: Forms the oak woodland at higher elevations, producing acorns and shade for the forest community.

quercus macrocarpa.name: Bur oak
quercus macrocarpa.desc: Bur oak (Quercus macrocarpa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 88 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus marilandica.name: Blackjack oak
quercus marilandica.desc: Blackjack oak (Quercus marilandica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 31 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus michauxii.name: Basket oak
quercus michauxii.desc: A bottomland oak of the floodplain whose acorns are mast for deer, squirrels and hogs. Congaree holds many champion trees.

quercus mongolica.name: Mongolian oak
quercus mongolica.desc: One of the main trees of the peninsula lowland forests. Its acorns are a food for bears and rodents.

quercus muehlenbergii.name: Chinkapin oak
quercus muehlenbergii.desc: Chinkapin oak (Quercus muehlenbergii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus nigra.name: Water oak
quercus nigra.desc: A common bottomland oak whose acorns feed deer, squirrels and jays.

quercus petraea.name: Sessile oak
quercus petraea.desc: A widespread forest oak in the area and the best recorded tree in the GBIF records. Its acorns feed deer, boar, jays and rodents.

quercus robur.name: Pedunculate oak
quercus robur.desc: Giant old oaks, some individually named, grow in the forest. Their acorns and shoots feed boar, deer and voles.

quercus rubra.name: Red Oak
quercus rubra.desc: Red Oak (Quercus rubra): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus rugosa.name: Netleaf oak
quercus rugosa.desc: Netleaf oak (Quercus rugosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 104 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus spp..name: Oaks (white oak and relatives)
quercus spp..desc: The dominant upland trees. The MDC lists white oak acorns as food for turkeys, deer, squirrels, jays, raccoons and mice, with acorns ripening in autumn.

quercus suber.name: Cork oak
quercus suber.desc: An evergreen oak of the park's Mediterranean woodland. Red deer and wild boar feed on its acorns and foliage.

quercus virginiana.name: Live oak
quercus virginiana.desc: Live oak (Quercus virginiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus, carya.name: Oaks & hickories
quercus, carya.desc: Dominant trees of the drier forest. Their acorns and nuts are the fall mast that bears, turkeys, deer and squirrels fatten on.

quincula lobata.name: Purple-ground-cherry
quincula lobata.desc: Purple-ground-cherry (Quincula lobata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.

quiscalus major.name: BOAT-TAILED GRACKLE
quiscalus major.desc: BOAT-TAILED GRACKLE (Quiscalus major): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 339 times near the park in GBIF.

quiscalus quiscula.name: Common Grackle
quiscalus quiscula.desc: Common Grackle (Quiscalus quiscula): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

rafetus euphraticus.name: Euphrates softshell turtle
rafetus euphraticus.desc: An opportunistic omnivore of rivers and marshes, eating crabs, plants, insects and fish and readily taking carcasses.

rafflesia keithii.name: Rafflesia
rafflesia keithii.desc: A parasitic flowering plant that lives inside a host vine and shows itself only as a huge flower; endemic to Sabah.

rain.name: Rain
rain.desc: Wet Pacific air dumps heavy precipitation on the mountain, feeding the old-growth forest on its lower slopes.

rain & cloud moisture.name: Rain & cloud moisture
rain & cloud moisture.desc: Cool, humid summers and dry winters, with cloud-forest moisture, support the oyamel forest.

rain & humidity.name: Rain & humidity
rain & humidity.desc: Wet, humid air keeps ravines moist for hemlock and rhododendron.

rain & meltwater.name: Rain & meltwater
rain & meltwater.desc: Water from rain and melting snow feeds streams and waterfalls such as the Krimml Waterfalls and keeps the alpine meadows watered.

rain & mountain fog.name: Rain & mountain fog
rain & mountain fog.desc: Heavy rainfall and cool, moist air keep the high forests and streams wet.

rain & mountain moisture.name: Rain & mountain moisture
rain & mountain moisture.desc: The park gets roughly 50 inches of rain a year with no dry season, plus winter snow, which keeps the ridge forests and streams moist.

rain & river floods.name: Rain & river floods
rain & river floods.desc: Daily rain and yearly river floods carry nutrients and open the forest to fish.

rain & rock creek.name: Rain & Rock Creek
rain & rock creek.desc: Rain feeds Rock Creek, the stream running through the park. Stormwater runoff from the surrounding city pollutes the waterways.

rain & snow.name: Rain & snow
rain & snow.desc: Precipitation is scarce in this semi-arid country, and it controls how green the grass gets.

rain & snowfall.name: Rain & snowfall
rain & snowfall.desc: The west side gets far more precipitation than the east, with deep snowpacks of 10 to 25 feet at their early March peak in the mountains.

rain & snowmelt.name: Rain & snowmelt
rain & snowmelt.desc: Under 10 inches of rain fall a year, and unpredictably. The soil crust absorbs and holds what does arrive.

rain & spring recharge.name: Rain & spring recharge
rain & spring recharge.desc: Rain soaking into the mountains feeds the hot springs and the forest, which is why the park is managed to protect the water system.

rain & tepui mist.name: Rain & tepui mist
rain & tepui mist.desc: The Gran Sabana gets roughly 1,600 to 2,200 mm of rain a year, with a rainy season of about ten months.

rain and cloud.name: Rain and cloud
rain and cloud.desc: Wet windward slopes feed the rainforest, while the dry Kaʻū side stays arid.

rain and cloud mist.name: Rain and cloud mist
rain and cloud mist.desc: Heavy rainfall and cloud on the Andean slope feed the park's forests and bromeliads.

rain and mist.name: Rain and mist
rain and mist.desc: Frequent cloud and rain on the volcano slopes keep the montane forest, bamboo and vine zones growing.

rain and river mist.name: Rain and river mist
rain and river mist.desc: Wikipedia gives the Alto Parana forest roughly 1,200 to 1,600 mm of rain a year, with a drier season from April to September.

rain and rivers.name: Rain and rivers
rain and rivers.desc: The park drains to the Soča (Adriatic) and the Sava (Black Sea), with waterfalls, gorges and glacial lakes.

rain and rock run-off.name: Rain and rock run-off
rain and rock run-off.desc: Rainfall is low and irregular. Rain also pours off the rock domes and concentrates water and nutrients in drainage lines and at their bases.

rain and sea mist.name: Rain and sea mist
rain and sea mist.desc: Moist ocean air rising over the Serra do Mar slopes brings heavy rain to the escarpment forests, which keeps them lush.

rain and snow.name: Rain and snow
rain and snow.desc: Mount Washington receives very high precipitation, about 91 inches a year, feeding moist forests and alpine plants.

rain and snowmelt.name: Rain and snowmelt
rain and snowmelt.desc: Water sinks quickly into the limestone, and underground rivers drain some of the glacial lakes, so streams and lakes matter more than the dry slopes suggest.

rain and streams.name: Rain and streams
rain and streams.desc: Abundant precipitation feeds the mountain streams, beaver ponds and forest wetlands.

rain and typhoons.name: Rain and typhoons
rain and typhoons.desc: Rain waters the islands, which have no big rivers, and typhoon winds shape the wind-clipped scrub on ridges and cliffs.

rain, fog and snow.name: Rain, fog and snow
rain, fog and snow.desc: Moisture from the Gulf of St. Lawrence and a snowy winter shape the plants that grow here, from forest to coastal bog.

rainfall.name: Rainfall
rainfall.desc: Rain and river water set how much the plants can grow.

rainfall and cloud.name: Rainfall and cloud
rainfall and cloud.desc: Trade winds rise over the mountains and drop heavy rain, in places over six metres a year, with no distinct dry season.

rainforest soil.name: Rainforest soil
rainforest soil.desc: Nutrients held in thin, wet soils are recycled quickly from fallen leaves and dead wood.

rainwater depressions (rawdat).name: Rainwater depressions (rawdat)
rainwater depressions (rawdat).desc: Shallow depressions called rawdat collect rainwater and hold richer plant life than the surrounding rocky desert.

rainy season.name: Rainy season
rainy season.desc: Seasonal rain raises the river and floods low ground, and manatees move up rivers in the wet season.

ramganga and reservoir.name: Ramganga and reservoir
ramganga and reservoir.desc: The Ramganga runs through the reserve and the Kalagarh dam flooded about 80 km2 of riverine land, creating habitat for fish and gharial.

ramphastos dicolorus.name: Red-breasted toucan
ramphastos dicolorus.desc: A large-billed bird that swallows fruit whole, including palm fruit, and drops the seeds away from the parent plant.

ramphastos sulfuratus.name: Keel-billed toucan
ramphastos sulfuratus.desc: Eats mainly fruit, including black poisonwood and wax mallow, and also takes small animals such as birds.

ramphastos toco.name: Toco toucan
ramphastos toco.desc: Swallows whole fruit and drops the seeds far from the parent tree.

ramphastos tucanus.name: White-throated toucan
ramphastos tucanus.desc: The most recorded bird near Yasuni. Large-billed fruit eater that swallows fruit whole.

rana iberica.name: Iberian frog
rana iberica.desc: Frog of cool mountain streams, catching small invertebrates; widely eaten by snakes, birds and mammals.

rana temporaria.name: Common frog
rana temporaria.desc: Amphibian of wet heath and pools that eats insects and other small invertebrates. Snakes, foxes and raptors eat it.

rangifer tarandus.name: Caribou
rangifer tarandus.desc: Migrates in large herds, eating lichen in winter and sedges in summer.

rangifer tarandus caribou.name: Woodland caribou
rangifer tarandus caribou.desc: Feeds heavily on lichens. Wikipedia lists boreal woodland caribou as threatened.

ranunculus glaberrimus.name: Sagebrush buttercup
ranunculus glaberrimus.desc: Sagebrush buttercup (Ranunculus glaberrimus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
