ranunculus hispidus.name: Bristly buttercup
ranunculus hispidus.desc: Bristly buttercup (Ranunculus hispidus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

ranunculus sceleratus.name: Celery-leaved Buttercup
ranunculus sceleratus.desc: Celery-leaved Buttercup (Ranunculus sceleratus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

raphia.name: Raffia palms
raphia.desc: Palms of swamps and wet ground. Their fruit is a main food of the palm-nut vulture.

rare rainfall.name: Rare rainfall
rare rainfall.desc: Rain is scarce and unpredictable across the Sahara. A shower can briefly turn dry wadis and sand green with grasses.

rare winter rain.name: Rare winter rain
rare winter rain.desc: Rain is scarce and irregular. After a shower, desert plants leaf out quickly and herds can follow the new growth.

ratibida columnifera.name: Yellow coneflower
ratibida columnifera.desc: Yellow coneflower (Ratibida columnifera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 46 times near the park in GBIF.

ratibida pinnata.name: Drooping prairie-coneflower
ratibida pinnata.desc: Drooping prairie-coneflower (Ratibida pinnata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

rattus argentiventer.name: Ricefield rat
rattus argentiventer.desc: A rodent of rice fields and wet grassland that eats rice and is prey for snakes, birds and otters.

rattus baluensis.name: Summit rat
rattus baluensis.desc: A night-active rat that licks nectar from giant pitcher lids and defecates into them; one of the most recorded mammals near the park.

rattus colletti.name: Dusky rat
rattus colletti.desc: Rodent of the cracking-clay floodplains, found in large numbers when the grass is lush. It is food for dingoes, kites and small carnivores.

rattus exulans.name: Polynesian rat
rattus exulans.desc: An omnivore spread across the Pacific by settlers. It eats seeds, fruit, insects, lizards and bird eggs.

rattus rattus.name: Black rat
rattus rattus.desc: Introduced omnivore that eats eggs and hatchlings of tortoises and iguanas and has wiped out young tortoises on some islands.

ratufa indica.name: Malabar giant squirrel
ratufa indica.desc: A large canopy squirrel that feeds on fruit, flowers, nuts and bark. Leopards are recorded eating it.

ratufa macroura.name: Sri Lankan giant squirrel
ratufa macroura.desc: A large tree squirrel of the forest canopy that feeds on fruit, seeds and bark.

recurvirostra americana.name: American Avocet
recurvirostra americana.desc: American Avocet (Recurvirostra americana): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1,460 times near the park in GBIF.

recurvirostra andina.name: Andean avocet
recurvirostra andina.desc: A wader of high salt lakes that sweeps its upturned bill through shallow water for small invertebrates. Well recorded in the area.

red and green seaweeds.name: Intertidal algae
red and green seaweeds.desc: Red and green seaweeds grow on the rocky shore in the cold, nutrient-rich water. Marine iguanas and crabs graze them.

red sand and limestone country.name: Red sand and limestone country
red sand and limestone country.desc: Arid sandy land of the peninsulas and islands, home to the shrubs, grasses and ground-dwelling animals of the terrestrial side.

redunca redunca.name: Bohor reedbuck
redunca redunca.desc: A grazing antelope of wet grassland. Ethiopian wolves have taken reedbuck calves.

reef water.name: Cool, clear reef water
reef water.desc: Corals live close to their heat limit. During marine heatwaves they bleach and can die, while reef algae spread.

regulus calendula.name: Ruby-crowned Kinglet
regulus calendula.desc: Ruby-crowned Kinglet (Regulus calendula): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 4,618 times near the park in GBIF.

reithrodontomys megalotis.name: Western harvest mouse
reithrodontomys megalotis.desc: A small seed and plant eater of grassy cover. One of the most recorded rodents near the park.

restio.name: Restios
restio.desc: Reed-like plants that are a defining part of fynbos. The Cape mountain zebra eats young restio shoots.

retreating glaciers.name: Retreating glaciers
retreating glaciers.desc: Glaciers have been receding for decades, leaving bare ground where plants then colonise in stages.

rhabdomys dilectus.name: Four-striped grass mouse
rhabdomys dilectus.desc: Small rodent of the open montane grassland and the most recorded mammal in the GBIF data here.

rhabdomys pumilio.name: Striped mouse
rhabdomys pumilio.desc: A common small rodent of open shrubland that eats plant matter and insects, and is prey for many predators.

rhacophorus malabaricus.name: Malabar flying frog
rhacophorus malabaricus.desc: One of the many endemic tree frogs of the Ghats. It hunts insects at night in wet forest.

rhanterium epapposum.name: Arfaj
rhanterium epapposum.desc: A yellow-flowered shrub native to Qatar, regarded as a main desert forage plant for camels and sheep. It leafs out quickly after rain.

rhea americana.name: Greater rhea
rhea americana.desc: A large flightless bird that mainly eats broad-leaved plants, seeds and fruit, plus insects and small animals. Cougars are its main predator.

rhea pennata.name: Darwin's rhea
rhea pennata.desc: A flightless bird of Patagonian scrub that eats mostly plants, plus the odd lizard or insect, and outruns predators.

rhincodon typus.name: Whale shark
rhincodon typus.desc: The biggest fish, a filter feeder on plankton, seen in the island waters.

rhinella marina.name: Cane toad
rhinella marina.desc: An introduced toad that eats ants and many other small animals.

rhinoceros sondaicus.name: Javan rhinoceros
rhinoceros sondaicus.desc: Critically endangered browser of shoots, twigs and fallen fruit. Ujung Kulon holds its only known wild population, about 82 animals per Wikipedia.

rhinoceros unicornis.name: Indian rhinoceros
rhinoceros unicornis.desc: A grazer of tall alluvial grasslands that also eats leaves, fruits and water plants. Chitwan holds most of Nepal's rhinos.

rhinolophus pearsonii.name: Pearson's horseshoe bat
rhinolophus pearsonii.desc: One of many insect-eating bats recorded in the forest. It hunts flying insects at night.

rhinopithecus bieti.name: Black snub-nosed monkey
rhinopithecus bieti.desc: Endemic to northwest Yunnan and neighbouring Tibet. It lives higher than any other non-human primate and lives mostly on lichen.

rhinopithecus roxellana.name: Golden snub-nosed monkey
rhinopithecus roxellana.desc: A leaf-eating primate of the high mixed and conifer forests that moves lower in winter.

rhipidura albiscapa.name: Grey fantail
rhipidura albiscapa.desc: A small insect-catching forest bird, widely recorded around Santo.

rhizophora.name: Mangroves
rhizophora.desc: Aldabra has seven mangrove species lining the lagoon edge, forming a key part of the coastal ecosystem.

rhizophora apiculata.name: Mangroves
rhizophora apiculata.desc: Mangroves such as Rhizophora and Sonneratia line the coast of the park in salt-tolerant stands.

rhizophora mangle.name: Red mangrove
rhizophora mangle.desc: Lines the shore with prop roots that shelter young fish, mollusks and crustaceans; its leaf litter feeds the shallows.

rhizophora mucronata.name: Red mangrove
rhizophora mucronata.desc: A stilt-rooted mangrove of tidal creeks in the Indian Ocean region. Its tangled roots shelter small animals and trap sediment.

rhododendron.name: Rhododendron
rhododendron.desc: Flowering shrubs of the higher forest zones, which provide nectar and flowers for birds.

rhododendron calendulaceum.name: Flame Azalea
rhododendron calendulaceum.desc: Flame Azalea (Rhododendron calendulaceum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 88 times near the park in GBIF.

rhododendron caucasicum.name: Caucasian rhododendron
rhododendron caucasicum.desc: A low evergreen shrub of the high Caucasus, known as the Georgian snow rose. Its alpine scrub is the open-slope habitat the Caucasian grouse favours.

rhododendron ferrugineum.name: Alpine rose and dwarf shrubs
rhododendron ferrugineum.desc: Low evergreen shrubs on acidic alpine slopes. Dwarf shrubs are part of the autumn and winter diet of Alpine ibex.

rhododendron groenlandicum.name: Bog Labrador Tea
rhododendron groenlandicum.desc: An evergreen shrub of bogs and heath. Caribou, hares and voles nibble it.

rhododendron maximum.name: Great laurel
rhododendron maximum.desc: A dominant evergreen understory shrub of moist Appalachian slopes and streamsides that forms dense thickets and gives shelter to wildlife.

rhododendron menziesii.name: Pacific menziesia
rhododendron menziesii.desc: Pacific menziesia (Rhododendron menziesii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

rhododendron pseudochrysanthum.name: Yushan rhododendron
rhododendron pseudochrysanthum.desc: A Taiwanese rhododendron, a shrub of the high mountain zone, whose tough leaves form thickets near the treeline.

rhododendron roseum.name: Rhododendron roseum
rhododendron roseum.desc: Rhododendron roseum (Rhododendron roseum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 39 times near the park in GBIF.

rhododendron spp..name: Rhododendron
rhododendron spp..desc: Shrubs that dominate the slopes at roughly 4,000 to 5,000 m together with juniper, according to Wikipedia on the park.

rhodophyta and phaeophyceae.name: Reef algae
rhodophyta and phaeophyceae.desc: Seaweeds and turf algae growing on the rocky reefs. Green turtles are herbivores that graze plant growth like this.

rhombomys opimus.name: Great gerbil
rhombomys opimus.desc: A colonial burrowing rodent of Central Asian deserts that eats plant material. It is prey for reptiles, owls and foxes.

rhone water and silt.name: Rhone water and silt
rhone water and silt.desc: The Rhone splits into two arms that feed the delta with fresh water and mud. Some of the lagoons are remnants of old river channels.

rhus aromatica.name: Fragrant sumac
rhus aromatica.desc: Fragrant sumac (Rhus aromatica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

rhus copallina.name: Black Sumac
rhus copallina.desc: Black Sumac (Rhus copallina): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

rhus glabra.name: Smooth sumac
rhus glabra.desc: Smooth sumac (Rhus glabra): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

rhus integrifolia.name: Lemonade berry
rhus integrifolia.desc: An evergreen shrub of island scrub and canyons with flowers visited by insects.

rhus microphylla.name: Desert sumac
rhus microphylla.desc: Desert sumac (Rhus microphylla): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.

rhus typhina.name: Stag's-horn Sumach
rhus typhina.desc: Stag's-horn Sumach (Rhus typhina): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 54 times near the park in GBIF.

rhynchonycteris naso.name: Proboscis bat
rhynchonycteris naso.desc: Small insectivorous bat that roosts on waterside trunks and feeds on flying insects such as mosquitoes.

rhynchospora colorata.name: Starrush whitetop
rhynchospora colorata.desc: Starrush whitetop (Rhynchospora colorata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

rhynchospora fusca.name: Brown Beak-sedge
rhynchospora fusca.desc: Brown Beak-sedge (Rhynchospora fusca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

rhyticeros undulatus.name: Wreathed hornbill
rhyticeros undulatus.desc: A large hornbill recorded by GloBI eating fig and Macaranga fruit near the park.

ribes americanum.name: American black currant
ribes americanum.desc: American black currant (Ribes americanum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

ribes aureum.name: Golden Currant
ribes aureum.desc: Golden currant (Ribes aureum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

ribes cereum.name: Squaw currant
ribes cereum.desc: Squaw currant (Ribes cereum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

ribes malvaceum.name: Chaparral current
ribes malvaceum.desc: Chaparral current (Ribes malvaceum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 45 times near the park in GBIF.

ribes montigenum.name: Alpine prickly currant
ribes montigenum.desc: Alpine prickly currant (Ribes montigenum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 48 times near the park in GBIF.

ribes roezlii.name: Sierra gooseberry
ribes roezlii.desc: Sierra gooseberry (Ribes roezlii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

rio grande & springs.name: Rio Grande & springs
rio grande & springs.desc: The river and desert springs create a green riparian strip and isolated wet habitats across the dry landscape.

rissa tridactyla.name: Black-legged kittiwake
rissa tridactyla.desc: A surface-feeding gull that eats fish such as capelin, herring and sand lance in the Gulf of Alaska.

river flood pulse.name: River flood pulse
river flood pulse.desc: The Pascagoula floods its low forests in the wet season. This moves seeds and nutrients and keeps cypress swamp and bottomland forest wet.

river floods.name: River floods
river floods.desc: Monsoon floods and erosion along the Rapti and Narayani keep reshaping banks and sandbars, opening new ground for kans grass.

river nutrients.name: River nutrients
river nutrients.desc: Nitrogen and phosphorus carried by the Mississippi, mostly from farm runoff and sewage, fuel the summer blooms.

river sediment & nutrients.name: River sediment & nutrients
river sediment & nutrients.desc: The rivers drain much of Alabama and deliver silt and nutrients that build the delta soils.

river sediment and nutrients.name: River sediment and nutrients
river sediment and nutrients.desc: The lagoon was formed from sediment carried down by the Shkumbin and Seman rivers, which also feed it with nutrients.

river silt & nutrients.name: River silt & nutrients
river silt & nutrients.desc: The Danube carries sediment and nutrients into the delta. Upstream dams have cut the sediment supply.

river silt and nutrients.name: River silt and nutrients
river silt and nutrients.desc: Floodwater delivers silt and nutrients that feed reed beds.

river soil.name: River soil
river soil.desc: Damp, flooded riverbank soil that feeds palms, trees and grasses.

river-valley soil.name: River-valley soil
river-valley soil.desc: Sandy, nutrient-rich floodplain soil under the meadows, fields and cottonwood groves.

rivers.name: Rivers
rivers.desc: Eastward-flowing rivers such as the Olifants, Letaba and Sabie bring water and support thickets along their banks.

rivers and lake water.name: Rivers and lake water
rivers and lake water.desc: Slow rivers, Lake Paliastomi and flooded marshes make up more than half of the protected area and carry water and nutrients across the plain.

robinia pseudoacacia.name: False acacia
robinia pseudoacacia.desc: False-acacia (Robinia pseudoacacia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

rocky mountain soils.name: Rocky mountain soils
rocky mountain soils.desc: Thin, rocky and often limestone-based soils; bristlecone pines dominate dolomite ground where few other plants grow.

rocky shale & desert soil.name: Rocky shale & desert soil
rocky shale & desert soil.desc: The Nurata range is mostly shales, sandstone and limestone, with soils thin and dry in places.

rocky soil.name: Rocky soil
rocky soil.desc: The park is hilly with rocky ground and open meadows, between roughly 215 and 505 m above sea level.

rollandia microptera.name: Titicaca grebe
rollandia microptera.desc: A flightless, endangered grebe. Nearly 95% of its prey mass is Orestias. It breeds in the reed belt and drowns in gill nets.

romalea microptera.name: Eastern lubber grasshopper
romalea microptera.desc: A large, slow grasshopper that eats broadleaf plants such as beggarticks.

rosa arkansana.name: Prairie rose
rosa arkansana.desc: Prairie rose (Rosa arkansana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

rosa multiflora.name: Many-flowered Rose
rosa multiflora.desc: Many-flowered Rose (Rosa multiflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

rosa omeiensis.name: Rose and shrub thickets
rosa omeiensis.desc: A wild rose of the mountain scrub. Its flowers feed pollinators and its hips feed fruit eaters.

rosa rugosa.name: Rugosa Rose
rosa rugosa.desc: Rugosa Rose (Rosa rugosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 282 times near the park in GBIF.

rosalia alpina.name: Rosalia longicorn
rosalia alpina.desc: A blue-grey beetle whose larvae develop in dead and dying beech wood, so it depends on old forest.

rostrhamus sociabilis.name: Snail kite
rostrhamus sociabilis.desc: A raptor whose diet is almost all apple snails. The Everglades kite is endangered, and drought or loss of snails hurts it.

rousettus aegyptiacus.name: Egyptian rousette
rousettus aegyptiacus.desc: A fruit bat recorded near Nimba in GBIF data. Fruit bats feed on figs and other fruit and spread seeds at night.

rubus.name: Brambles & wild raspberries
rubus.desc: Thorny shrubs whose summer fruit is food for bears, birds and small mammals.

rubus fruticosus.name: Bramble
rubus fruticosus.desc: A thorny scrambling shrub of clearings and forest edges whose leaves and berries feed many animals.

rubus idaeus.name: Red raspberry
rubus idaeus.desc: A bramble of forest openings. Its fruit and leaves feed moose, bumble bees, foxes and birds.

rubus occidentalis.name: Black Raspberry
rubus occidentalis.desc: Black Raspberry (Rubus occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

rubus parviflorus.name: Thimbleberry
rubus parviflorus.desc: A shrub with soft berries and leaves that deer browse and bears and other animals eat.

rubus pubescens.name: Dwarf red blackberry
rubus pubescens.desc: A low forest-floor berry plant recorded near the park; its fruit is eaten by bears and foxes.

rubus spectabilis.name: Salmonberry
rubus spectabilis.desc: A berry shrub of the coastal forest and shrub thickets. Its fruit is food for bears and birds.

rubus spectabilis, oplopanax horridus.name: Salmonberry and devil's club
rubus spectabilis, oplopanax horridus.desc: Understory shrubs of wet forest; berries feed bears and birds, and the shrubs near salmon streams also take up salmon nitrogen.

rucervus duvaucelii.name: Swamp deer
rucervus duvaucelii.desc: A deer of the wet grassland, one of the species tigers hunt in the park.

rudbeckia hirta.name: Black-eyed-susan
rudbeckia hirta.desc: Black-eyed-susan (Rudbeckia hirta): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.

rudbeckia subtomentosa.name: Sweet coneflower
rudbeckia subtomentosa.desc: Sweet coneflower (Rudbeckia subtomentosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

ruellia humilis.name: Fringe-leaf ruellia
ruellia humilis.desc: Fringe-leaf ruellia (Ruellia humilis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

rupicapra pyrenaica.name: Pyrenean chamois (izard)
rupicapra pyrenaica.desc: A sure-footed mountain goat-antelope that browses grass, lichens and buds on steep slopes up to about 3,000 m. It is the best-recorded large animal here.

rupicapra rupicapra.name: Chamois
rupicapra rupicapra.desc: Eats alpine grasses and herbs in summer and conifers in winter, moving down to pine forest. A main prey of wolves and a regular carrion source.

rupicola peruvianus.name: Andean cock-of-the-rock
rupicola peruvianus.desc: A cloud-forest bird of ravines and streams. It eats mostly fruit plus insects, and its leks attract predators such as jaguars and ocelots.

rupornis magnirostris.name: Roadside hawk
rupornis magnirostris.desc: A common medium-sized raptor of forest edges that hunts lizards, small mammals and large insects.

rusa timorensis.name: Timor deer (Javan rusa)
rusa timorensis.desc: Grazes grass, leaves and fallen fruit. It is the main prey of the Komodo dragon on the park islands.

rusa unicolor.name: Sambar
rusa unicolor.desc: A large forest deer that browses and grazes. A favoured prey of tigers.

rutilus rutilus.name: Roach
rutilus rutilus.desc: A freshwater fish of reedy lakes, typical of the small and medium fish that Dalmatian pelicans swallow whole.

río plátano floods.name: Río Plátano floods
río plátano floods.desc: The river and its lagoons carry water and silt through the lowlands and shape the wetlands and gallery forest.

sabal minor.name: Dwarf Palmetto
sabal minor.desc: Dwarf Palmetto (Sabal minor): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

sabal palmetto.name: Cabbage palm
sabal palmetto.desc: Cabbage palm (Sabal palmetto): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

saccharum.name: Tall elephant grasses
saccharum.desc: Tall grasses cover the largest share of the park, and regrow quickly after the monsoon floods and winter burns that open new feeding ground.

saccharum spontaneum.name: Kans grass
saccharum spontaneum.desc: A tall grass that is among the first plants to colonise fresh sandbanks. Tall grasslands cover roughly a fifth of the park.

sagittaria lancifolia.name: Bulltongue
sagittaria lancifolia.desc: Bulltongue (Sagittaria lancifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 44 times near the park in GBIF.

sagittaria montevidensis.name: Giant arrowhead
sagittaria montevidensis.desc: Giant arrowhead (Sagittaria montevidensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

saiga tatarica.name: Saiga antelope
saiga tatarica.desc: Nomadic steppe grazer that eats many plants, including some poisonous to other animals. Wolves are the main threat to adults.

salicornia.name: Glasswort and saltbush
salicornia.desc: Salt-tolerant plants of the lake shores and saline flats; glasswort and saltbush were both recorded near the reserve.

salicornia europaea.name: Glasswort
salicornia europaea.desc: A salt-tolerant succulent of salt marshes and lagoon margins, among the well-recorded plants around the lagoon.

salicornia fruticosa.name: Glasswort
salicornia fruticosa.desc: A succulent salt-tolerant shrub of the saline flats, recorded commonly around the lagoons; one of the plants adapted to the salty conditions.

salicornia rubra.name: Rocky Mountain glasswort
salicornia rubra.desc: Rocky Mountain glasswort (Salicornia rubra): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

saline lake water.name: Saline lake water
saline lake water.desc: Uvs Lake is shallow and salty, at roughly half the salinity of the ocean, because salts build up in a basin with no outlet.

saline limestone soils.name: Saline limestone soils
saline limestone soils.desc: Alkaline, mineral-rich soils around the pan. Salty dust blown from the pan adds minerals to soils downwind.

salix.name: Willows
salix.desc: Shrubs of lowland and tundra that moose browse, according to the park service. Hares, ptarmigan, ground squirrels and Dall sheep eat them too.

salix alba.name: White willow
salix alba.desc: Tree of the wet river levees and floodplain, rooted in the seasonally flooded ground.

salix arctica.name: Arctic willow
salix arctica.desc: A dwarf willow hugging the ground on tundra. Willows are the most commonly eaten plant for muskoxen in winter.

salix atrocinerea.name: Rusty willow
salix atrocinerea.desc: Streamside willow whose leaves fall into the water and feed stream insects.

salix bebbiana.name: Beaked willow
salix bebbiana.desc: A willow of wet ground. Wood bison eat willow leaves in summer, and beavers and moose browse willows.

salix caprea.name: Goat willow
salix caprea.desc: A willow of forest edges and river banks whose shoots and bark are browsed by hares and moose.

salix caroliniana.name: Carolina willow
salix caroliniana.desc: Carolina willow (Salix caroliniana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

salix geyeriana.name: Geyer's willow
salix geyeriana.desc: Geyer's willow (Salix geyeriana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

salix glauca.name: Grayleaf willow
salix glauca.desc: Low shrubby willows of the tundra and river valleys. Willow ptarmigan are recorded eating grayleaf willow.

salix humilis.name: Prairie Willow
salix humilis.desc: Prairie Willow (Salix humilis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

salix interior.name: Sandbar willow
salix interior.desc: Sandbar willow (Salix interior): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

salix lanata.name: Woolly willow
salix lanata.desc: A low, silvery willow of Icelandic heaths and river plains; willow shoots and buds are a staple for grazers and ptarmigan.

salix lucida.name: Shining Willow
salix lucida.desc: Shining Willow (Salix lucida): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

salix nigra.name: Black willow
salix nigra.desc: Colonizes new sandbars and banks. Beavers, muskrats and deer all browse it.

salix polaris.name: Polar willow
salix polaris.desc: A tiny creeping arctic willow of tundra and rocky slopes, recorded as food for reindeer.

salix pycnostachya.name: Willow
salix pycnostachya.desc: Willows are shrubs and trees of damp ground and are recorded near the park. Local people collect shrubs for fuel and winter fodder.

salix spp..name: Willow
salix spp..desc: Streamside shrubs that feed moose and beaver and hold the banks that trout streams run between.

salmo letnica.name: Ohrid trout
salmo letnica.desc: An endemic, endangered trout that preys on smaller fish. Overfishing and illegal fishing have cut its numbers.

salmo trutta.name: Brown trout
salmo trutta.desc: A fish of cold, clear mountain rivers and lakes that eats aquatic insects and smaller fish. Prey for otters.

salmon-borne nitrogen.name: Salmon-borne nitrogen
salmon-borne nitrogen.desc: Nitrogen from the ocean arrives in spawning salmon and is spread along streams by floods and by animals that carry and eat the carcasses.

salmon-borne nutrients.name: Salmon-borne nutrients
salmon-borne nutrients.desc: Salmon bring ocean-grown nutrients inland, and their remains are broken down into nutrients that feed streamside soil and lakes.

salpa thompsoni.name: Salps
salpa thompsoni.desc: Free-floating filter feeders. In low-ice years they tend to replace krill and may compete with them for food.

salt and brine.name: Salt and brine
salt and brine.desc: Lagoons cut off from the sea by sandbars and long-used salt pans hold salty water. Brine shrimp tolerate salinity that keeps most fish out.

salt-lake water.name: Salt-lake water
salt-lake water.desc: Shallow, salty, mineral-rich lagoons with borates and sulfates set the home of the algae, diatoms and brine shrimp.

salvator merianae.name: Argentine tegu
salvator merianae.desc: A big omnivorous lizard eating insects, eggs, fruit and carrion. Cougars and jaguars are among its predators.

salvelinus alpinus.name: Arctic char
salvelinus alpinus.desc: A cold-water fish found in lakes. Landlocked populations eat insects, bottom invertebrates and zooplankton.

salvelinus fontinalis.name: Brook trout
salvelinus fontinalis.desc: The park's only native trout, now mostly in cold high streams after non-native rainbow and brown trout took over lower reaches. Eats insects and small animals.

salvelinus namaycush.name: Lake trout
salvelinus namaycush.desc: The native top predator, nearly wiped out by lampreys and overfishing. Hatchery stocking helps rebuild it.

salvia dorrii.name: Purple sage
salvia dorrii.desc: Grayball sage (Salvia dorrii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

salvia elegans.name: Pineapple sage
salvia elegans.desc: One of many sages and wildflowers recorded around the reserve. Its nectar feeds monarchs, bees and hummingbirds.

salvia lyrata.name: Lyreleaf sage
salvia lyrata.desc: Lyreleaf sage (Salvia lyrata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

salvia spathacea.name: Crimson pitcher sage
salvia spathacea.desc: Crimson pitcher sage (Salvia spathacea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 73 times near the park in GBIF.

sambucus canadensis.name: American elderberry
sambucus canadensis.desc: American elderberry (Sambucus canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

sambucus ebulus.name: Dwarf elder
sambucus ebulus.desc: A tall herb whose berries are eaten by birds, and whose foliage feeds the caterpillars of the Jersey tiger moth.

san juan and bartola rivers.name: San Juan and Bartola rivers
san juan and bartola rivers.desc: Rivers along and through the reserve that bring water and carry nutrients through the forest.

sand dunes & soil.name: Sand dunes & soil
sand dunes & soil.desc: Dunes rise to nearly 200 feet inland from the beach, and the NPS says all stages of plant succession can be seen on the youngest ones.

sand dunes & soils.name: Sand dunes & soils
sand dunes & soils.desc: Fixed and mobile dunes and sandy soils carry the pine, scrub and cork oak woodland beside the marsh.

sander vitreus.name: Walleye
sander vitreus.desc: A top sport fish of the big lakes; adults eat mostly fish, often yellow perch.

sandy acidic soil.name: Sandy acidic soil
sandy acidic soil.desc: Sandy, acid, nutrient-poor soil is why the region is called the Barrens.

sandy cays.name: Sandy cays
sandy cays.desc: The park has about 144 acres of land, mostly low sand keys. Bush Key is closed in Feb to Sep to protect nesting terns and noddies.

sandy desert soil.name: Sandy desert soil
sandy desert soil.desc: Thin, easily eroded soils of the Colorado Plateau. Nitrogen and nutrients are scarce and the crust helps hold the soil in place.

sandy soil.name: Sandy soil
sandy soil.desc: Loose sand and gravel soils are poor in nutrients; dead matter returning to them is what lets plants grow.

sandy soil and dunes.name: Sandy soil and dunes
sandy soil and dunes.desc: Loose sand holds little organic matter. Deep-rooted shrubs help anchor it, and returning nutrients feed the plants.

sandy, nutrient-poor soil.name: Sandy, nutrient-poor soil
sandy, nutrient-poor soil.desc: Sand and gravel hold little organic matter. Windblown dust is one source of nutrients.

sandy, nutrient-poor soils.name: Sandy, nutrient-poor soils
sandy, nutrient-poor soils.desc: Some forest here grows on pure white sand, where nutrients are scarce and recycled quickly from fallen leaves and wood.

sandy, salty steppe soil.name: Sandy, salty steppe soil
sandy, salty steppe soil.desc: Thin, dry ground broken by salt lakes supports mostly low shrubs.

sanguinaria canadensis.name: Red puccoon
sanguinaria canadensis.desc: Bloodroot (Sanguinaria canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 35 times near the park in GBIF.

sapajus apella.name: Tufted capuchin
sapajus apella.desc: An omnivorous monkey that eats fruit, including Guatteria, and also insects and small animals.

sapajus nigritus.name: Black capuchin
sapajus nigritus.desc: A monkey that eats fruit, seeds and other foods. GloBI records it feeding on Miconia and Psychotria fruit, and pumas prey on it.

sarcobatus vermiculatus.name: Greasewood
sarcobatus vermiculatus.desc: Greasewood (Sarcobatus vermiculatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

sarcophilus harrisii.name: Tasmanian devil
sarcophilus harrisii.desc: The world's largest surviving marsupial carnivore, mainly a scavenger that favours wombats. Devil facial tumour disease has cut its numbers sharply.

sarcoramphus papa.name: King vulture
sarcoramphus papa.desc: Finds carcasses by smell and opens them up for smaller vultures.

sardinella.name: Sardines
sardinella.desc: Schooling plankton-feeding fish that carry energy from plankton up to seabirds, dolphins and ospreys.

sardinella aurita.name: Round sardinella
sardinella aurita.desc: A schooling fish that filters plankton and is prey for seabirds and larger fish.

sardinella longiceps.name: Indian oil sardine
sardinella longiceps.desc: A schooling fish of the Arabian Sea that feeds on plankton and is a key prey fish for birds, dolphins and larger fish.

sardines and similar.name: Sardines and small schooling fish
sardines and similar.desc: Small schooling fish eating plankton. Sea lions, penguins and cormorants hunt them, and they die off or move away in El Niño years.

sarracenia alata.name: Pale pitcherplant
sarracenia alata.desc: Pale pitcherplant (Sarracenia alata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 67 times near the park in GBIF.

sarracenia flava.name: Yellow Pitcherplant
sarracenia flava.desc: Yellow Pitcherplant (Sarracenia flava): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 156 times near the park in GBIF.

sarracenia minor.name: Rainhat-trumpet
sarracenia minor.desc: Rainhat-trumpet (Sarracenia minor): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 107 times near the park in GBIF.

sarracenia purpurea.name: Pitcher Plant
sarracenia purpurea.desc: Frog's-britches (Sarracenia purpurea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

sasa kurilensis.name: Kuril bamboo grass
sasa kurilensis.desc: A dwarf bamboo that carpets the forest floor and clearings of Hokkaido, a staple browse for deer.

sassafras albidum.name: Sassafras
sassafras albidum.desc: A common understory tree of the park with aromatic twigs and leaves. Its fruit and twigs feed wildlife.

sauromalus ater.name: Common chuckwalla
sauromalus ater.desc: A large plant-eating lizard that feeds on desert shrubs such as creosote bush and wedges into rock crevices.

saururus cernuus.name: Lizard's tail
saururus cernuus.desc: Lizard's tail (Saururus cernuus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 55 times near the park in GBIF.

saussurea falconeri.name: Saussurea
saussurea falconeri.desc: A flowering herb of the summer wildflower meadows that bloom across the plateau after the snow retreats.

savanna soil.name: Savanna soil
savanna soil.desc: Shallow soils on the rocky cliffs and deeper soils on summits and escarpments support different woodland.

sayornis nigricans.name: Black Phoebe
sayornis nigricans.desc: Black Phoebe (Sayornis nigricans): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 9,658 times near the park in GBIF.

sayornis phoebe.name: Eastern Phoebe
sayornis phoebe.desc: Eastern Phoebe (Sayornis phoebe): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 361 times near the park in GBIF.

scarce rain.name: Scarce rain
scarce rain.desc: Rainfall in the park ranges from about 10 inches a year at Castolon to 18 in the Chisos Basin. Plant growth depends on it.

scarce rain and flash floods.name: Scarce rain and flash floods
scarce rain and flash floods.desc: The park averages only about 200 mm of precipitation a year. Late-summer storms bring most of it, often as sudden flash floods.

scarce rain and snow.name: Scarce rain and snow
scarce rain and snow.desc: The park is cold semi-arid, with about 413 mm of precipitation a year, so water is the main limit on plant growth.

scarce rain and snowmelt.name: Scarce rain and snowmelt
scarce rain and snowmelt.desc: The puna is dry. Meltwater and rare rain feed the grasslands, bogs and lagoons.

scarce rainfall.name: Scarce rainfall
scarce rainfall.desc: Rain is scarce and irregular; the park lost roughly 39% of its annual precipitation between 1895 and 2016, and plants and animals depend on it.

scarce seasonal rain.name: Scarce seasonal rain
scarce seasonal rain.desc: Only roughly 100 to 200 mm of rain falls a year in the Afar region, so brief wadi flows matter for plants and animals.

scarce, seasonal rain.name: Scarce, seasonal rain
scarce, seasonal rain.desc: The islands have one of the driest climates in Indonesia, with roughly 800 to 1,000 mm of rain a year, so growth is tied to the wet season.

scarus.name: Parrotfish
scarus.desc: Reef fish that scrape algae from rock and coral. Grazing keeps algae from smothering the reef.

scarus spp..name: Parrotfish
scarus spp..desc: Scrapes algae off the reef with a beak and excretes the ground limestone as sand.

sceliphron caementarium.name: Mud Dauber
sceliphron caementarium.desc: Mud Dauber (Sceliphron caementarium): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

sceloporus becki.name: Island fence lizard
sceloporus becki.desc: A lizard of the islands that eats insects and other small invertebrates. Island foxes eat lizards.

sceloporus graciosus.name: Sagebrush lizard
sceloporus graciosus.desc: A small lizard of open, sunny ground that eats insects and is itself eaten by snakes and hawks.

sceloporus grammicus.name: Mesquite lizard
sceloporus grammicus.desc: A common small lizard of the mountain forests that hunts insects.

sceloporus occidentalis.name: Western Fence Lizard
sceloporus occidentalis.desc: A common lizard of rocks and brush that eats insects and other small invertebrates.

sceloporus undulatus.name: Eastern fence lizard
sceloporus undulatus.desc: A sun-loving lizard of open sandy pine woods that hunts insects. Black racers hunt it.

schefflera.name: Schefflera
schefflera.desc: Montane forest trees and shrubs whose fruit is a main food of the splendid astrapia.

schismus arabicus.name: Spring annual grasses
schismus arabicus.desc: Short-lived grasses and herbs that sprout after rain and set seed quickly, a seasonal feast for seed and leaf eaters.

schistocerca gregaria.name: Desert locust
schistocerca gregaria.desc: Eats about its own weight in green plants daily. After good rains it can form huge swarms that strip vegetation.

schizachyrium scoparium.name: Little bluestem
schizachyrium scoparium.desc: A shorter bunchgrass of drier prairie ground.

schoenoplectus californicus.name: Totora reed
schoenoplectus californicus.desc: A tall sedge growing in shallow water, mainly less than 3 m deep. Its reed belt is breeding habitat for the Titicaca grebe, and the Uru people build their floating islands from it.

schoenoplectus tabernaemontani.name: Grey Club-rush
schoenoplectus tabernaemontani.desc: Grey Club-rush (Schoenoplectus tabernaemontani): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

sciaenops ocellatus.name: Red drum
sciaenops ocellatus.desc: Hunts crabs, shrimp and fish in marshes and bays.

scirpus cyperinus.name: Woolgrass
scirpus cyperinus.desc: Woolgrass (Scirpus cyperinus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

scirpus pedicellatus.name: Stalked bulrush
scirpus pedicellatus.desc: Stalked bulrush (Scirpus pedicellatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

sciurus aberti.name: Abert's Squirrel
sciurus aberti.desc: Lives in ponderosa pine forest and eats pine seeds. Its Kaibab race lives only on the Kaibab Plateau, including the North Rim.

sciurus anomalus.name: Caucasian squirrel
sciurus anomalus.desc: A tree squirrel of the northeastern forests that feeds on seeds and nuts.

sciurus carolinensis.name: Eastern gray squirrel
sciurus carolinensis.desc: Eastern gray squirrel (Sciurus carolinensis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

sciurus deppei.name: Deppe's squirrel
sciurus deppei.desc: A tree squirrel of tropical forests that eats fruit and seeds. Recorded within the circle around the site.

sciurus griseus.name: Western Gray Squirrel
sciurus griseus.desc: Western Gray Squirrel (Sciurus griseus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 121 times near the park in GBIF.

sciurus niger.name: Fox squirrel
sciurus niger.desc: Fox squirrel (Sciurus niger): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

sciurus vulgaris.name: Red squirrel
sciurus vulgaris.desc: Eats conifer seeds, nuts and buds in the canopy, and is taken by foxes and lynx.

scleractinia.name: Reef corals
scleractinia.desc: Hard corals on the outer reefs and in the lagoon. Bleaching in 2016 cut hard coral cover on seaward reefs by over half, and juveniles have since returned.

sclerocarya birrea.name: Marula
sclerocarya birrea.desc: A large fruiting tree common in the central woodlands. Elephants eat its bark, leaves and fruit.

scolia dubia.name: Blue-winged Scoliid Wasp
scolia dubia.desc: Blue-winged Scoliid Wasp (Scolia dubia): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

scopus umbretta.name: Hamerkop
scopus umbretta.desc: A wading bird of shallow water that mainly eats amphibians and fish, and a generalist hunter.

scutellaria bushii.name: Bush's skullcap
scutellaria bushii.desc: Bush's skullcap (Scutellaria bushii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.

scutellaria galericulata.name: Skullcap
scutellaria galericulata.desc: Skullcap (Scutellaria galericulata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

scylla serrata.name: Mud crab
scylla serrata.desc: A large crab of estuaries and mangroves. Juveniles stay in the mangroves and the species is highly cannibalistic.

scyphozoa.name: Jellyfish
scyphozoa.desc: Drifting predators of plankton and a main food of loggerhead turtles at sea.

sea ice.name: Sea ice
sea ice.desc: A platform for algae, seals and bears. It shrinks every year as the Arctic warms.

seabed sediment.name: Seabed sediment
seabed sediment.desc: Sandy and muddy bottom where seagrass roots, burrowing animals and buried organic matter are found.

seasonal fire.name: Seasonal fire
seasonal fire.desc: Fire shapes the Cerrado, and many of its plants have thick, corky bark or other traits that let them survive it.

seasonal flood.name: Seasonal flood
seasonal flood.desc: Rain on the Angolan highlands sends a pulse of water that reaches the delta in the dry season and spreads over the sands.

seasonal flood pulse.name: Seasonal flood pulse
seasonal flood pulse.desc: Monsoon rains reverse the flow of the Tonlé Sap River, and the lake swells from roughly 2,500 km2 to over 16,000 km2, drowning forest and fields.

seasonal flooding.name: Seasonal flooding
seasonal flooding.desc: Rivers flood the swamp forests and riverbank grasses, spreading water and nutrients.

seasonal floodwater.name: Seasonal floodwater
seasonal floodwater.desc: Chobe and Linyanti floodwater spreads across the floodplains in the wet season and shrinks in the dry season.

seasonal grazing (transhumance).name: Seasonal grazing (transhumance)
seasonal grazing (transhumance).desc: Flocks and herds are driven to high summer pastures each year, a long-running practice that helps keep the uplands open.

seasonal rain.name: Seasonal rain
seasonal rain.desc: Rain on the steep, rocky hillsides drives growth in the dry forest and runs off to the bays.

seasonal rain and mist.name: Seasonal rain and mist
seasonal rain and mist.desc: The cold current brings drizzle for much of the year, and rainfall swings wildly between years, with El Niño years much wetter.

seasonal rainfall.name: Seasonal rainfall
seasonal rainfall.desc: A wet season from about October to April brings most of the water. Baobab trunks swell and shrink with it, and the long dry season leaves the forest mostly leafless.

seasonal rains.name: Seasonal rains
seasonal rains.desc: Rain arrives in two seasons and sets the timing of the whole migration.

seasonal rains and river floods.name: Seasonal rains and river floods
seasonal rains and river floods.desc: The wet season fills the Comoé River and its tributaries and its seasonal ponds; many ponds dry out in the dry season.

seasonal river flooding.name: Seasonal river flooding
seasonal river flooding.desc: The Essequibo, Siparuni and Burro-Burro rivers bound and cross the reserve. Rising water spreads into low forest and swamp.

seawater & currents.name: Seawater & currents
seawater & currents.desc: Warm, clear water carries plankton and keeps temperature in the narrow range corals tolerate.

seawater and nutrients.name: Seawater and nutrients
seawater and nutrients.desc: Salty, nutrient-bearing water of the bay and its tidal flats, which feeds plankton and mangroves. Pollution and silt cloud it.

sebastes spp..name: Rockfish
sebastes spp..desc: Use the kelp understory for shelter and feeding, taking small invertebrates there.

sediment & nutrients.name: Sediment & nutrients
sediment & nutrients.desc: Silt carries nitrogen and phosphorus onto the floodplain. Much of it travels downriver to the Gulf of Mexico.

sedum nuttallii.name: Yellow stonecrop
sedum nuttallii.desc: Yellow stonecrop (Sedum nuttallii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 117 times near the park in GBIF.

sedum pulchellum.name: Widowscross
sedum pulchellum.desc: Widowscross (Sedum pulchellum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

sedum spathulifolium.name: Colorado stonecrop
sedum spathulifolium.desc: Colorado stonecrop (Sedum spathulifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.

sedum ternatum.name: Wild stonecrop
sedum ternatum.desc: Wild stonecrop (Sedum ternatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

seiurus aurocapilla.name: Ovenbird
seiurus aurocapilla.desc: Ovenbird (Seiurus aurocapilla): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 47 times near the park in GBIF.

selenia aurea.name: Golden selenia
selenia aurea.desc: Golden selenia (Selenia aurea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

semicossyphus pulcher.name: California sheephead
semicossyphus pulcher.desc: A reef fish that eats sea urchins, crabs and molluscs. Wikipedia calls it a keystone predator of urchins in southern California.

semnopithecus entellus.name: Northern plains gray langur
semnopithecus entellus.desc: A leaf-and-fruit-eating monkey that is regular prey for tigers and leopards and sometimes for crocodiles.

semnopithecus hector.name: Tarai gray langur
semnopithecus hector.desc: A leaf and fruit eating monkey of the forest and its edges, hunted by leopards and tigers.

semnopithecus johnii.name: Nilgiri langur
semnopithecus johnii.desc: A leaf- and fruit-eating monkey of the southern Western Ghats; GloBI records langurs eating figs and jamun.

semnopithecus vetulus.name: Purple-faced langur
semnopithecus vetulus.desc: A mostly leaf-eating monkey of closed-canopy wet-zone forest that also eats fruit, flowers and seeds. Its range is now small and fragmented.

sempervivum.name: Houseleeks
sempervivum.desc: Succulent rosettes on rock and thin soil. They are the caterpillar food plant of the Apollo butterfly, which also takes a bitter compound from them.

senecio spartioides.name: Broom groundsel
senecio spartioides.desc: Broom groundsel (Senecio spartioides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

senegal river floodwater.name: Senegal River floodwater
senegal river floodwater.desc: The sanctuary lies in the Senegal River delta, a chain of lakes, backwaters and channels that depend on river water.

senegalia nigrescens.name: Knobthorn
senegalia nigrescens.desc: A thorny savanna tree, browsed by giraffes and a main tree on the eastern grazing lands.

senna roemeriana.name: Twoleaf senna
senna roemeriana.desc: Twoleaf senna (Senna roemeriana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 79 times near the park in GBIF.

senna tora.name: Sickle senna
senna tora.desc: A common weedy shrub of the park area. GloBI records show chital and sambar eating it.

sepia.name: Cuttlefish
sepia.desc: Wikipedia lists cuttlefish among the bay species. They hunt small fish and crustaceans.

sequoia sempervirens.name: Coast redwood
sequoia sempervirens.desc: The tallest tree on Earth. It takes up fog water through its leaves and bark, and its canopy builds soil that holds life high above ground.

sequoiadendron giganteum.name: Giant sequoia
sequoiadendron giganteum.desc: Grows in scattered groves on the western slope. Thick bark protects mature trees from fire, and fire clears the ground for seedlings.

seriola lalandi.name: Yellowtail kingfish
seriola lalandi.desc: A fast open-water fish that eats other fish and squid. Visitors can hand-feed kingfish at Ned's Beach.

serrasalmus.name: Piranha
serrasalmus.desc: Omnivorous river fish whose diet varies widely: fish and other animals, but also fruit, seeds and leaves. They often scavenge.

sesarmidae.name: Mangrove crabs
sesarmidae.desc: Small crabs of mangrove mud that feed on fallen mangrove leaves and so move mangrove nutrients into the mud and other animals.

sesuvium revolutifolium.name: Sesuvium revolutifolium
sesuvium revolutifolium.desc: Sesuvium revolutifolium (Sesuvium revolutifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

setaria viridis.name: Grasses & meadow herbs
setaria viridis.desc: Bristle-grass, dandelion, clover and other open-ground plants that geese and small herbivores graze.

setophaga and leiothlypis spp..name: Boreal warblers
setophaga and leiothlypis spp..desc: Insect-eating songbirds. Some warblers are linked to spruce budworm outbreaks, which supply abundant caterpillar food.

setophaga coronata.name: Yellow-rumped Warbler
setophaga coronata.desc: Yellow-rumped Warbler (Setophaga coronata): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 370 times near the park in GBIF.

setophaga occidentalis.name: Hermit Warbler
setophaga occidentalis.desc: Hermit Warbler (Setophaga occidentalis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1,884 times near the park in GBIF.

setophaga petechia.name: Yellow Warbler
setophaga petechia.desc: Yellow Warbler (Setophaga petechia): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 580 times near the park in GBIF.

setophaga pinus.name: Pine Warbler
setophaga pinus.desc: Pine Warbler (Setophaga pinus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 232 times near the park in GBIF.

shallow lagoons.name: Shallow lagoons
shallow lagoons.desc: Warm, sheltered lagoons where eelgrass grows. They are the calving grounds for gray whales each winter.

shallow saline lakes.name: Shallow saline lakes
shallow saline lakes.desc: Tengiz is a shallow salt lake, about 2.5 m deep on average, and the neighbouring Korgalzhyn lake is the northernmost nesting site of greater flamingos.

shallow salty groundwater.name: Shallow salty groundwater
shallow salty groundwater.desc: Groundwater lies only a few feet under the dunes, deeper to the east and shallower to the west, and it is very salty.

shepherdia canadensis.name: Canadian buffaloberry
shepherdia canadensis.desc: A berry-bearing shrub of open forest. GloBI records show bears eating the berries and snowshoe hares eating the plant.

shepherdia rotundifolia.name: Roundleaf buffaloberry
shepherdia rotundifolia.desc: Roundleaf buffaloberry (Shepherdia rotundifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 52 times near the park in GBIF.

sherardia arvensis.name: Field Madder
sherardia arvensis.desc: Field Madder (Sherardia arvensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

shifting sand dunes.name: Shifting sand dunes
shifting sand dunes.desc: Wind and waves keep the sandy shore moving; only plants adapted to salt spray and drifting sand can hold it.

shorea robusta.name: Sal
shorea robusta.desc: The dominant tree of the park, making up about 70 percent of the cover and forming the purest stands in the central lowlands.

short mountain summer.name: Short mountain summer
short mountain summer.desc: At high elevation the growing season is brief, so plants grow fast in summer and animals feed, store fat or hibernate.

short summer sun.name: Short summer sun
short summer sun.desc: Meadow plants have only a brief snow-free season, so they flower and set seed quickly once the snow melts.

sialia currucoides.name: Mountain Bluebird
sialia currucoides.desc: Mountain Bluebird (Sialia currucoides): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 60 times near the park in GBIF.

sialia mexicana.name: Western Bluebird
sialia mexicana.desc: Western Bluebird (Sialia mexicana): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 5,858 times near the park in GBIF.

sialia sialis.name: Eastern Bluebird
sialia sialis.desc: Eastern Bluebird (Sialia sialis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 30 times near the park in GBIF.

sidalcea neomexicana.name: New Mexico checker
sidalcea neomexicana.desc: New Mexico checker (Sidalcea neomexicana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

sideritis.name: Mountain herbs
sideritis.desc: Aromatic herbs such as mountain tea (Sideritis raeseri) grow here and have long been gathered by local healers.

siganus.name: Rabbitfish
siganus.desc: Plant-eating reef fish that graze seagrass and algae. They are a typical link from seagrass beds to larger fish.

siganus canaliculatus.name: White-spotted spinefoot
siganus canaliculatus.desc: A herbivorous fish of the Gulf that eats mainly benthic algae and some seagrass; it is trapped by local fishers.

sigaus piliferus.name: North Island grasshopper
sigaus piliferus.desc: A short-horned grasshopper restricted to alpine and sub-alpine habitats of the North Island, including the central volcanic region.

sigmodon hispidus.name: Hispid cotton rat
sigmodon hispidus.desc: HISPID COTTON RAT (Sigmodon hispidus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

silene acaulis.name: Alpine tundra plants
silene acaulis.desc: Low cushion plants, such as moss campion, make up the tundra vegetation, which covers over a third of the park. Recovery from trampling takes centuries.

silene csereii.name: European catchfly
silene csereii.desc: European catchfly (Silene csereii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

silene laciniata.name: Cardinal catchfly
silene laciniata.desc: Cardinal catchfly (Silene laciniata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

silene stellata.name: Starry Campion
silene stellata.desc: Starry Campion (Silene stellata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

silene virginica.name: Fire-pink
silene virginica.desc: Fire-pink (Silene virginica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 33 times near the park in GBIF.

silene vulgaris.name: Bladder Campion
silene vulgaris.desc: Bladder Campion (Silene vulgaris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

sillaginidae.name: Whitings
sillaginidae.desc: Small bottom-feeding fish of shallow sandy bays that eat small crustaceans and worms. Prey for dolphins, cormorants and sharks.

silphium laciniatum.name: Prairie wildflowers
silphium laciniatum.desc: Compass plant, gayfeather, milkweed and many other wildflowers add most of the prairie plant diversity and feed insects and browsers.

simalia kinghorni.name: Scrub python
simalia kinghorni.desc: A large ambush predator of the rainforest that takes flying foxes, wallabies and tree-kangaroos.

simmondsia chinensis.name: Jojoba
simmondsia chinensis.desc: Jojoba (Simmondsia chinensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

sisyrinchium bellum.name: Western blue-eyed grass
sisyrinchium bellum.desc: Western blue-eyed grass (Sisyrinchium bellum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 60 times near the park in GBIF.

sitta canadensis.name: Red-breasted Nuthatch
sitta canadensis.desc: Red-breasted Nuthatch (Sitta canadensis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 986 times near the park in GBIF.

sitta carolinensis.name: White-breasted Nuthatch
sitta carolinensis.desc: White-breasted Nuthatch (Sitta carolinensis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

sitta pygmaea.name: Pygmy Nuthatch
sitta pygmaea.desc: Pygmy Nuthatch (Sitta pygmaea): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 511 times near the park in GBIF.

smallanthus uvedalia.name: Bear's-foot
smallanthus uvedalia.desc: Bear's-foot (Smallanthus uvedalia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.

smartweeds and millets.name: Moist-soil plants
smartweeds and millets.desc: Plants that sprout on exposed mud flats when floods recede. Their seeds feed ducks.

smilax bona-nox.name: Catbrier
smilax bona-nox.desc: A thorny, tangling vine of woods and thickets whose leaves and berries are eaten by wildlife.

snake river and wetlands.name: Snake River and wetlands
snake river and wetlands.desc: Rises on the Yellowstone Plateau and runs through the valley, with side channels and wetlands such as Willow Flats and Oxbow Bend that support willow, cottonwood and aspen.

snow.name: Winter snowpack
snow.desc: Lake Helen gets roughly 600 to 700 inches a year, and meltwater feeds meadows and forests into summer.

snow & glacier melt.name: Snow & glacier melt
snow & glacier melt.desc: The park holds glaciers such as the Pasterze; winter snow cover and summer meltwater shape which plants grow and where animals can feed.

snow & winter cold.name: Snow & winter cold
snow & winter cold.desc: Long cold winters bury forage, so winter food and shelter shape which animals thrive.

snow and cold winters.name: Snow and cold winters
snow and cold winters.desc: Deep snow and cold shape winter foraging, and heavy snowfall on the high peaks feeds streams in spring.

snow and glacier melt.name: Snow and glacier melt
snow and glacier melt.desc: Snow and ice cap the summit. Most of the ice cover has vanished since 1912, and the forest below acts as the main water reservoir.

snow and ice melt.name: Snow and ice melt
snow and ice melt.desc: Winter snow and the ice field of Yolyn Am feed meltwater into the mountain valleys and the dry plains below.

snow and snowfields.name: Snow and snowfields
snow and snowfields.desc: Snow insulates the ground in winter and its meltwater wets the tundra in spring. Perennial snowfields in the Brooks Range have shrunk a great deal since 1985.

snow and snowmelt.name: Snow and snowmelt
snow and snowmelt.desc: Winter snow supplies much of the moisture the rim plants use; the park averages about 120 inches of snowfall a year.

snow and winter cold.name: Snow and winter cold
snow and winter cold.desc: Deep winter snow and cold limit food for herbivores and cover carcasses, shaping when bears, wolves and ravens eat.

snow cover.name: Snow cover
snow cover.desc: Long winters bury willow and lichen under snow, forcing caribou to dig for food. Meltwater feeds tundra plants in spring.

snow cover & ice crusts.name: Snow cover & ice crusts
snow cover & ice crusts.desc: Snow shelters tundra plants through winter and melts into summer water. Rain falling on snow can freeze into an ice crust that locks reindeer out of their food.

snowmelt & streams.name: Snowmelt & streams
snowmelt & streams.desc: Winter snowpack melts into the rivers and soils that carry algae, willows and meadow grasses through the dry summer.

snowmelt and glacier meltwater.name: Snowmelt and glacier meltwater
snowmelt and glacier meltwater.desc: Meltwater from snowfields and glaciers feeds meadows and streams in spring and summer.

snowmelt and glacier water.name: Snowmelt and glacier water
snowmelt and glacier water.desc: Meltwater from winter snow and the glaciers around Belukha feeds the meadows and the rivers below.

snowmelt and marsh.name: Snowmelt and marsh
snowmelt and marsh.desc: Melting snow feeds streams and the deep marshy soil of the flat ground between mountains, watering the plateau through summer.

snowmelt and medano creek.name: Snowmelt and Medano Creek
snowmelt and medano creek.wiki: Great Sand Dunes National Park and Preserve
snowmelt and medano creek.desc: Mountain snowmelt feeds Medano Creek and the water table. Wikipedia says peak creek flow is usually late May to early June.

snowmelt and summer rain.name: Snowmelt and summer rain
snowmelt and summer rain.desc: The park receives roughly 15 to 18 inches of precipitation a year, more than nearby Zion, and it feeds the plateau's trees and meadows.

snowpack.name: Snowpack
snowpack.desc: Winter snow cover decides when meadows green up and pushes animals such as chamois down to lower, forested slopes.

snowpack & glacier meltwater.name: Snowpack & glacier meltwater
snowpack & glacier meltwater.desc: Winter snow and glaciers feed the headwaters of major rivers rising in the mountains and water the valleys through summer.

snowpack & glaciers.name: Snowpack & glaciers
snowpack & glaciers.desc: Deep winter snow buries the high meadows and sets how early plants can grow. Its melt feeds the streams.

snowpack & kaweah meltwater.name: Snowpack & Kaweah meltwater
snowpack & kaweah meltwater.desc: Most precipitation falls in winter, as heavy snow at Lodgepole elevation. Meltwater feeds the Kaweah River drainage and the forests and woodlands it crosses.

snowpack & meltwater.name: Snowpack & meltwater
snowpack & meltwater.desc: The mountains collect snow that feeds streams, springs and meadows in dry surroundings; the park even holds a small glacier.

snowpack & snowmelt.name: Snowpack & snowmelt
snowpack & snowmelt.desc: Winter snow feeds meadows and streams through the dry summer. The park page says warming brings earlier melt, drier summers and a longer fire season.

snowpack and glacier melt.name: Snowpack and glacier melt
snowpack and glacier melt.desc: Winter snow and melting glaciers feed the streams and lakes and set the length of the growing season on the high slopes. Glaciers in the park have shrunk sharply since the 1800s.

snowpack and meltwater.name: Snowpack and meltwater
snowpack and meltwater.desc: Winter snow insulates low shrubs and hares, and the spring melt waters the tundra.

snowpack and snowmelt.name: Snowpack and snowmelt
snowpack and snowmelt.desc: Winter snow on the high slopes melts into streams and glacial lakes, watering the pastures below.

soil.name: Volcanic soil
soil.desc: Soils on volcanic rock supply nutrients to the park's forests and meadows.

soil & leaf litter.name: Soil & leaf litter
soil & leaf litter.desc: Forest litter and thin karst soils hold the nutrients the trees draw on.

soil & nutrients.name: Soil & nutrients
soil & nutrients.desc: Thin, rocky soils on volcanic rock. Nutrients return to them as dead plants and animals are broken down.

soil & peat.name: Soil & peat
soil & peat.desc: Nutrients in wetland soils feed the plants.

soil and limestone minerals.name: Soil and limestone minerals
soil and limestone minerals.desc: Thin northern soils, built on limestone in much of the region, hold the nutrients that plants draw on.

soil and nutrients.name: Soil and nutrients
soil and nutrients.desc: Soil holds the nutrients plants take up.

soil and peat nutrients.name: Soil and peat nutrients
soil and peat nutrients.desc: Nutrients held in wetland soil are recycled from dead plants and animals and feed new plant growth.

soil and sediment nutrients.name: Nutrients
soil and sediment nutrients.desc: Nutrients from forest litter, mangrove mud and recycled dead matter support plant growth on land and in the shallows.

soil and soil crust.name: Soil and soil crust
soil and soil crust.desc: Crusts of lichens, algae, fungi and cyanobacteria slow erosion, add nitrogen and help soil hold moisture.

soil fungi and bacteria.name: Decomposers
soil fungi and bacteria.desc: Break down dead plants and animals, including fallen saguaros, and return nutrients to the soil.

soil nutrients.name: Soil nutrients
soil nutrients.desc: Weathered volcanic rock and rotting leaf litter feed the forest trees.

soils and geology.name: Soils and geology
soils and geology.desc: Granite in the west and basalt in the east shape the soils and so the plant communities.

solanum americanum.name: Small-flowered Nightshade
solanum americanum.desc: Small-flowered Nightshade (Solanum americanum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

solanum carolinense.name: Horse-nettle
solanum carolinense.desc: Horse-nettle (Solanum carolinense): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

solanum dulcamara.name: Bittersweet
solanum dulcamara.desc: Bitter nightshade (Solanum dulcamara): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

solanum elaeagnifolium.name: Silverleaf nightshade
solanum elaeagnifolium.desc: Silverleaf nightshade (Solanum elaeagnifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 58 times near the park in GBIF.

solanum lycocarpum.name: Wolf apple
solanum lycocarpum.desc: A tomato-like fruit that Wikipedia says can make up 40 to 90 percent of the maned wolf's diet and is available all year.

solanum sisymbriifolium.name: Sticky nightshade
solanum sisymbriifolium.desc: Sticky nightshade (Solanum sisymbriifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

solar energy.name: Sunlight
solar energy.desc: Light powers the algae, eelgrass and marsh grass that start the estuary food web.

solenodon paradoxus.name: Hispaniolan solenodon
solenodon paradoxus.desc: An endangered nocturnal insectivore that probes soil and rotten logs for arthropods and also takes snails and small reptiles.

solidago sempervirens.name: Seaside goldenrod
solidago sempervirens.desc: A coastal wildflower of dunes and marsh edges, common on Block Island and the Rhode Island shore.

solidago uliginosa.name: Bog Goldenrod
solidago uliginosa.desc: Bog Goldenrod (Solidago uliginosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

somateria mollissima.name: Common eider
somateria mollissima.desc: A sea duck that dives for mussels and crabs along the rocky coast. Wikipedia lists mussels as a favorite food.

sophora chrysophylla.name: Māmane
sophora chrysophylla.desc: A native subalpine tree whose flowers are nectar for ʻamakihi and ʻiʻiwi. It grows on the high slopes of Hawaiian volcanoes.

sorbus aucuparia.name: Rowan
sorbus aucuparia.desc: A small tree whose berries are eaten by foxes, martens and many birds.

sorex araneus.name: Common shrew
sorex araneus.desc: A tiny insectivore of the leaf litter that hunts beetles, worms and other invertebrates.

sorghastrum nutans.name: Indiangrass
sorghastrum nutans.desc: Indian Grass (Sorghastrum nutans): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

sorghastrum nutans, panicum virgatum.name: Indiangrass & switchgrass
sorghastrum nutans, panicum virgatum.desc: Tall warm-season grasses that grow alongside big bluestem.

sorghum.name: Savanna grasses
sorghum.desc: Tall grasses of the open woodland understorey. Fresh green shoots after a burn draw in wallabies and other grazers.

sorindeia grandifolia.name: Sorindeia trees
sorindeia grandifolia.desc: A forest tree whose fruit has been recorded as food for the Guinea turaco, piping hornbill and African green pigeon.

sousa plumbea.name: Indian Ocean humpback dolphin
sousa plumbea.desc: A shallow coastal dolphin that mostly eats sciaenid fish, cephalopods and crustaceans.

sousa teuszii.name: Atlantic humpback dolphin
sousa teuszii.desc: Rare coastal dolphin that herds mullet and other inshore fish, sometimes towards Imraguen fishers' nets.

south nahanni river and meltwater.name: South Nahanni River and meltwater
south nahanni river and meltwater.desc: The river and its tributaries run the length of the reserve and water the willow thickets, sedge meadows and river flats.

southern patagonian ice field.name: Southern Patagonian Ice Field
southern patagonian ice field.desc: The great ice cap feeds dozens of glaciers such as Perito Moreno, which end in Lake Argentino and shape the valleys and rivers.

spaelotis clandestina.name: Clandestine Dart Moth
spaelotis clandestina.desc: Clandestine Dart Moth (Spaelotis clandestina): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 121 times near the park in GBIF.

sparisoma viride.name: Stoplight parrotfish
sparisoma viride.desc: A reef grazer that scrapes algae off coral rock, helping keep corals from being smothered.

sparse stony soil.name: Sparse stony soil
sparse stony soil.desc: Sandy, well-drained, nutrient-poor ground that yareta prefers and the grasses must make do with.

spartina alterniflora.name: Smooth cordgrass
spartina alterniflora.desc: Fringe marshes that shelter young shrimp, crabs and fish.

spartium junceum.name: Spanish broom
spartium junceum.desc: Spanish broom (Spartium junceum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 59 times near the park in GBIF.

spathodea campanulata.name: African tulip tree
spathodea campanulata.desc: An introduced, invasive tree with nectar-rich flowers that attract birds and insects.

spatula clypeata.name: Northern Shoveler
spatula clypeata.desc: Northern Shoveler (Spatula clypeata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1,413 times near the park in GBIF.

spatula discors.name: Blue-winged Teal
spatula discors.desc: Blue-winged Teal (Spatula discors): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 7,235 times near the park in GBIF.

spawning rivers and streams.name: Spawning rivers and streams
spawning rivers and streams.desc: Small, short rivers where salmon and other salmonids return to spawn, carrying ocean nutrients inland.

spermophilus citellus.name: European ground squirrel
spermophilus citellus.desc: A burrowing grazer that needs short turf, which grazing maintains. It eats plants, seeds and insects and is a main prey of saker falcons.

spermophilus fulvus.name: Yellow ground squirrel
spermophilus fulvus.desc: A large burrowing ground squirrel of Central Asian deserts and steppe. It eats plants and is prey for raptors and foxes.

spermophilus relictus.name: Relict ground squirrel
spermophilus relictus.desc: Burrowing rodent of Central Asian mountains found in Kyrgyzstan, a plant eater and prey for raptors.

spermophilus xanthoprymnus.name: Asia Minor ground squirrel
spermophilus xanthoprymnus.desc: A burrowing ground squirrel of open steppe that eats plants and is taken by buzzards and kestrels.

speyeria atlantis.name: Atlantis Fritillary
speyeria atlantis.desc: Atlantis Fritillary (Speyeria atlantis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 71 times near the park in GBIF.

speyeria cybele.name: Great Spangled Fritillary
speyeria cybele.desc: Great Spangled Fritillary (Speyeria cybele): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

speyeria idalia.name: Regal fritillary
speyeria idalia.desc: A butterfly the MDC names among the species that cannot persist without prairie. Adults feed on nectar from flowers such as milkweed and coneflower.

sphaeralcea coccinea.name: Moss-rose
sphaeralcea coccinea.desc: A low orange-flowered wildflower of dry prairie that prairie dogs favour in late summer and fall.

sphaeralcea munroana.name: Munro's globemallow
sphaeralcea munroana.desc: Munro's globemallow (Sphaeralcea munroana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

sphaerophysa salsula.name: Austrian peaweed
sphaerophysa salsula.desc: Austrian peaweed (Sphaerophysa salsula): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

sphaeropteris lunulata.name: Tree fern
sphaeropteris lunulata.desc: A tree fern recorded often in the wetter forest, part of the layered understorey.

sphagnum.name: Peat moss
sphagnum.desc: Moss that builds the raised bogs. Wikipedia says its slowly decaying remains accumulate as peat and its wet carpets hold many times their dry weight in water.

sphecius speciosus.name: Cicada Killer
sphecius speciosus.desc: Cicada Killer (Sphecius speciosus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

spheniscus magellanicus.name: Magellanic penguin
spheniscus magellanicus.desc: Eats small fish such as anchoita, plus squid and krill. Wikipedia reports about 150,000 breeding pairs at the peninsula.

spheniscus mendiculus.name: Galápagos penguin
spheniscus mendiculus.desc: The only penguin living on the equator. It depends on cold Cromwell Current upwelling to supply the small fish it eats.

sphingidae.name: Hawk moths
sphingidae.desc: Night-flying moths that carry baobab pollen from tree to tree while feeding on nectar.

sphyraena barracuda.name: Great barracuda
sphyraena barracuda.desc: An ambush predator of reefs and shallows; young stay in mangroves and seagrass.

sphyrna.name: Hammerhead sharks
sphyrna.desc: Hammerheads are reported in the park, which records eleven shark species, and hunt fish and squid around the reef.

sphyrna lewini.name: Scalloped hammerhead
sphyrna lewini.desc: A schooling shark that eats mainly bony fish, along with squid and octopus. It is an opportunist that takes what is abundant.

spigelia marilandica.name: Indian-pink
spigelia marilandica.desc: Indian-pink (Spigelia marilandica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

spilornis cheela.name: Crested serpent eagle
spilornis cheela.desc: A forest raptor that hunts snakes and lizards from perches under the canopy and is one of the best-recorded birds nearby.

spinulum annotinum.name: Interrupted Clubmoss
spinulum annotinum.desc: Interrupted Clubmoss (Spinulum annotinum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

spinus pinus.name: Pine Siskin
spinus pinus.desc: Pine Siskin (Spinus pinus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 389 times near the park in GBIF.

spinus psaltria.name: Lesser Goldfinch
spinus psaltria.desc: Lesser Goldfinch (Spinus psaltria): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 64 times near the park in GBIF.

spinus spinus.name: Eurasian siskin
spinus spinus.desc: A small finch that eats seeds of alder and birch, and is prey for forest jays and stoats.

spinus tristis.name: American Goldfinch
spinus tristis.desc: American Goldfinch (Spinus tristis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2,894 times near the park in GBIF.

spiraea alba.name: Pale Bridewort
spiraea alba.desc: Pale Bridewort (Spiraea alba): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

spiranthes lacera.name: Northern Slender Ladies'-tresses
spiranthes lacera.desc: Northern Slender Ladies'-tresses (Spiranthes lacera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

spirogyra.name: River algae
spirogyra.desc: Green algae growing in the slow rivers, oxbow lakes and pools, the base of the aquatic food chain.

spiza americana.name: Dickcissel
spiza americana.desc: A grassland songbird that nests in prairie and eats insects and seeds.

spizella breweri.name: Brewer's Sparrow
spizella breweri.desc: Brewer's Sparrow (Spizella breweri): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 609 times near the park in GBIF.

spizella pallida.name: Clay-colored Sparrow
spizella pallida.desc: Clay-colored Sparrow (Spizella pallida): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 324 times near the park in GBIF.

spizella passerina.name: Chipping Sparrow
spizella passerina.desc: Chipping Sparrow (Spizella passerina): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4,028 times near the park in GBIF.

spizella pusilla.name: Field Sparrow
spizella pusilla.desc: Field Sparrow (Spizella pusilla): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1,400 times near the park in GBIF.

sporobolus.name: Pan-edge salt grass
sporobolus.desc: Salt-tolerant Sporobolus grass grows on the otherwise bare pan margins. It is protein-rich and eaten by wildebeest and springbok.

sporobolus airoides.name: Alkali sacaton
sporobolus airoides.desc: A bunchgrass that tolerates alkaline soil. The park notes that such grasses feed many small animals, and their seeds feed rodents.

sporobolus pyramidalis.name: West Indian dropseed
sporobolus pyramidalis.desc: A tall tussock grass recorded often in the area. GloBI has records of hippos, elephants, warthogs and hartebeest eating it.

sporobolus virginicus.name: Tortoise turf
sporobolus virginicus.desc: A short mix of grasses and herbs, dwarfed by constant grazing, that grows in the tortoises' pastures.

spring rain & snowmelt.name: Spring rain & snowmelt
spring rain & snowmelt.desc: Moisture comes mainly in the cooler months, so plant growth surges in spring and slows in the hot dry summer.

spring-fed water.name: Spring-fed water
spring-fed water.desc: Springs keep Ozark streams cool and clear year round, the habitat that hellbenders and smallmouth bass need.

springs & seeps.name: Springs & seeps
springs & seeps.desc: Rattlesnake Springs and Oak Spring are rare permanent water in the park, and Rattlesnake Springs is a wooded oasis with over 300 bird species recorded.

springs & waterholes.name: Springs & waterholes
springs & waterholes.desc: Dry-season waterholes fed by springs concentrate wildlife, so animals gather and are easier for predators to find.

springs and oases.name: Springs and oases
springs and oases.desc: Natural oases, springs and seeps are rare water sources vital to resident wildlife, and support the native fan palm.

springtails, snails, worms.name: Leaf-litter invertebrates
springtails, snails, worms.desc: Tiny animals that eat decaying leaves and fungi on the forest floor. They are food for salamanders and firefly larvae.

stachys tenuifolia.name: Smooth hedgenettle
stachys tenuifolia.desc: Smooth hedgenettle (Stachys tenuifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

standing and fallen deadwood.name: Standing and fallen deadwood
standing and fallen deadwood.desc: In unmanaged old forest, dead trees are left to stand and rot. They house beetles, fungi and the birds that feed on them.

stanleya pinnata.name: Desert prince's-plume
stanleya pinnata.desc: Desert prince's-plume (Stanleya pinnata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

staphida everetti.name: Chestnut-crested yuhina
staphida everetti.desc: A busy flocking bird that takes insects and fruit; one of the most recorded birds near the park.

staphylea trifolia.name: American bladdernut
staphylea trifolia.desc: American bladdernut (Staphylea trifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

stenaria nigricans.name: Prairie bluets
stenaria nigricans.desc: Prairie bluets (Stenaria nigricans): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

stenella longirostris.name: Spinner dolphin
stenella longirostris.desc: Resident in large numbers. It eats small mesopelagic fish, squid and shrimp, and is preyed on by sharks.

stenocara and other darkling beetles.name: Fog-basking beetles
stenocara and other darkling beetles.desc: Darkling beetles that harvest fog on their bumpy backs and drink the droplets that roll to their mouths. They scavenge wind-blown plant debris.

stenocereus gummosus.name: Dagger cactus
stenocereus gummosus.desc: A sprawling columnar cactus of the Baja desert. Pronghorn include cacti in their diet, and succulents are a water source for desert animals.

stenocereus thurberi.name: Organpipe cactus
stenocereus thurberi.desc: Organpipe cactus (Stenocereus thurberi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1,003 times near the park in GBIF.

stephanoaetus coronatus.name: Crowned eagle
