stephanoaetus coronatus.desc: A powerful forest eagle that mostly takes monkeys, with duikers, bats and other small animals also on the menu.

steppe and desert soil.name: Steppe and desert soil
steppe and desert soil.desc: Dry, often salty soils hold the nutrients that grasses, shrubs and trees draw on, and are replenished by decomposers.

stercorarius antarcticus.name: Brown skua
stercorarius antarcticus.desc: A bold seabird that takes eggs and chicks from penguin colonies and scavenges carcasses.

stercorarius longicaudus.name: Long-tailed jaeger
stercorarius longicaudus.desc: A tundra-nesting seabird that hunts lemmings and small birds in summer.

stercorarius maccormicki.name: South polar skua
stercorarius maccormicki.desc: Seabird that robs penguin colonies of eggs and chicks and scavenges carrion.

stercorarius parasiticus.name: Parasitic jaeger
stercorarius parasiticus.desc: A seabird of prey that nests on the tundra and takes lemmings and the eggs and chicks of other birds.

stercorarius skua.name: Great skua
stercorarius skua.desc: Nests on the sands by the lagoon; it kills seabirds, steals fish from other birds and eats carrion.

sterna paradisaea.name: Arctic tern
sterna paradisaea.desc: Nests near the lagoon in large numbers and dives for herring and other small fish.

stetsonia coryne.name: Toothpick cactus
stetsonia coryne.desc: A tall columnar cactus of the dry Chaco, one of the succulents that store water through the dry season.

stipa.name: Needlegrasses
stipa.desc: Low, drought-hardy bunch grasses are among the main plants of the Gobi, grazed by wild and domestic hoofed animals.

stipa barbata.name: Feather grass
stipa barbata.desc: A tussock grass named among the climax plants of the Syrian Desert. Overgrazing has replaced such plants with grasses of lower feed value.

stipagrostis.name: Desert bunch grasses
stipagrostis.desc: Grasses of sandy desert that green up after rain. Related Stipagrostis grasses are the main food of Arabian oryx in Oman.

stipagrostis and others.name: Desert grasses
stipagrostis and others.desc: Tough, drought-adapted grasses grow in sparse tufts and sprout quickly after rain. Their leaves and seeds feed many desert animals.

stipagrostis species.name: Dune grasses
stipagrostis species.desc: Tussock grasses that grow on Namib dunes and gravel plains and feed grazers, seed eaters and termites.

stolephorus.name: Anchovies
stolephorus.desc: Small schooling fish that feed on zooplankton in the open bay and are food for larger fish, seabirds and porpoises.

stony mountain soil.name: Stony mountain soil
stony mountain soil.desc: Thin, rocky soils on dry slopes hold the steppe, juniper and oak communities, which cover the reserve in altitude bands.

stony, salty soils.name: Stony, salty soils
stony, salty soils.desc: The plateau is limestone with chert gravel, and run-off ends in salt flats. Poor soil and little water limit plant cover.

streams & gallery forest.name: Streams & gallery forest
streams & gallery forest.desc: Strips of forest along watercourses hold moisture through the dry season and shelter plants and animals that need damp ground.

streams and swamps.name: Streams and swamps
streams and swamps.desc: Rivers and wet hollows give shy water-loving animals such as the pygmy hippo daytime cover and cool, moist ground.

strepera graculina.name: Pied currawong
strepera graculina.desc: An omnivorous bird eating insects, fruit and the eggs and young of other birds. The island has its own vulnerable subspecies.

streptopelia decaocto.name: Eurasian Collared Dove
streptopelia decaocto.desc: Eurasian Collared-Dove (Streptopelia decaocto): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 58 times near the park in GBIF.

strix aluco.name: Tawny owl
strix aluco.desc: A woodland owl hunting small mammals such as voles at night.

strix nebulosa.name: Great gray owl
strix nebulosa.desc: Hunts small rodents by sound, even under snow, and sometimes takes squirrels or hares. Nests in old raptor nests and broken-topped trees.

strix occidentalis caurina.name: Northern spotted owl
strix occidentalis caurina.desc: Lives in old-growth forest and eats mostly small mammals, especially flying squirrels; competes with invading barred owls.

strix varia.name: Barred owl
strix varia.desc: The park highlights it as a signature species. It hunts small mammals, frogs and some snakes in old-growth bottomland forest.

strombosia scheffleri.name: Strombosia trees
strombosia scheffleri.desc: Understory and mid-canopy rainforest trees whose fruit is eaten by chimpanzees and guenons, according to GloBI records.

strongylocentrotus purpuratus.name: Purple sea urchin
strongylocentrotus purpuratus.desc: Grazes kelp, often eating drifting pieces. Without enough predators it can multiply and strip an area bare, leaving an urchin barren.

strongylopus grayii.name: Clicking stream frog
strongylopus grayii.desc: A small frog of streams and wet grass that feeds on insects and is eaten by shrikes and snakes.

strophostyles helvola.name: BEACH PEA
strophostyles helvola.desc: BEACH PEA (Strophostyles helvola): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

struthio camelus.name: Common ostrich
struthio camelus.desc: A huge flightless bird that eats plants, seeds and some insects on open desert plains.

strymon melinus.name: Cotton Square Borer
strymon melinus.desc: Cotton Square Borer (Strymon melinus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

strymon sylvinus.name: Strymon sylvinus
strymon sylvinus.desc: Strymon sylvinus (Strymon sylvinus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

stuckenia pectinata.name: Fennel Pondweed
stuckenia pectinata.desc: Fennel Pondweed (Stuckenia pectinata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.

sturnella magna.name: Eastern meadowlark
sturnella magna.desc: A grassland songbird recorded often near the park that eats insects and seeds.

sturnella neglecta.name: Western Meadowlark
sturnella neglecta.desc: Western Meadowlark (Sturnella neglecta): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 179 times near the park in GBIF.

sturnus vulgaris.name: European Starling
sturnus vulgaris.desc: European Starling (Sturnus vulgaris): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 143 times near the park in GBIF.

stylophorum diphyllum.name: Celandine-poppy
stylophorum diphyllum.desc: Celandine-poppy (Stylophorum diphyllum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

styrax redivivus.name: Snowdrop bush
styrax redivivus.desc: Snowdrop bush (Styrax redivivus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 76 times near the park in GBIF.

suaeda nigra.name: Bush seepweed
suaeda nigra.desc: Bush seepweed (Suaeda nigra): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

sula dactylatra.name: Masked booby
sula dactylatra.desc: A seabird that plunge-dives for flying fish and squid. Its eggs are open to rats and other egg predators.

sula leucogaster.name: Brown booby
sula leucogaster.desc: Plunge-diving seabird that feeds on flying fish and other fish near the surface.

sula sula.name: Red-footed booby
sula sula.desc: Nests in the trees and shrubs and hunts flying fish and squid at sea.

sulu sea currents.name: Sulu Sea currents
sulu sea currents.desc: Ocean currents move water, larvae and plankton across the isolated atolls and carry them to the reef edges.

summer light.name: Summer light
summer light.desc: The park lies north of the Arctic Circle, so growth is crammed into a short summer of very long days.

summer monsoon rain.name: Summer monsoon rain
summer monsoon rain.desc: About 42 percent of the park's scarce rain falls from July to September, triggering the main burst of grass and wildflower growth.

summer rain.name: Summer rain
summer rain.desc: Rain wets the sand sheet and shrublands and helps seeds sprout.

summer rains.name: Summer rains
summer rains.desc: Rains fill pans and swell the rivers, and turn the grasslands green.

summer sun.name: Summer sun
summer sun.desc: Short alpine summers drive the growth of meadows and scrub above the tree line.

summer sun and long days.name: Summer sun and long days
summer sun and long days.desc: North of the Arctic Circle the summer sun barely sets, giving plants a short, intense growing season.

summer sunlight.name: Summer sunlight
summer sunlight.desc: Long summer days power a short, intense growing season on the tundra.

sun.name: Sun
sun.desc: Sunlight powers the marsh plants and grasses.

sun and altitude.name: Sun and altitude
sun and altitude.desc: Short alpine summers and cold winters set the growing season, from about 450 m in the canyons to over 2,500 m on the peaks.

suncus etruscus.name: Etruscan shrew
suncus etruscus.desc: One of the smallest mammals on Earth and one of Socotra's few native mammals. It hunts small invertebrates.

sundasciurus jentinki.name: Jentink's squirrel
sundasciurus jentinki.desc: A small squirrel of montane Borneo forest, recorded often near the park.

sunlight.name: Sunlight
sunlight.desc: Plants turn sunlight into food, which starts the whole web.

sunlight and altitude.name: Sunlight and altitude
sunlight and altitude.desc: Strong high-altitude light drives growth in meadows and forests between the gorges and the snowline.

sunlight and dry-season heat.name: Sunlight and dry-season heat
sunlight and dry-season heat.desc: Strong sun and heat, up to about 40 C in the May to October dry season, drive the savanna growth and its seasonal browning.

sunlight and heat.name: Sunlight and heat
sunlight and heat.desc: Intense light powers the sparse plant life, but extreme summer heat and dryness limit where plants and animals can live.

sus barbatus.name: Bornean bearded pig
sus barbatus.desc: A forest pig that roots through the leaf litter for fallen fruit, seeds and invertebrates.

sus scrofa.name: Wild boar
sus scrofa.desc: Feral pig (Sus scrofa): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

swamps & rivers.name: Swamps & rivers
swamps & rivers.desc: Swamp and seasonally flooded forest make up about a quarter of the park, with the Sinoe River on its west side. Home to the pygmy hippo.

swampy lowlands.name: Swampy lowlands
swampy lowlands.desc: Low wet ground between the limestone ridges where water collects and forest meets wetland.

swietenia macrophylla.name: Big-leaf mahogany
swietenia macrophylla.desc: Planted here in the mid 1900s, it now forms much of the tall canopy beside the older native trees.

syagrus romanzoffiana.name: Queen palm
syagrus romanzoffiana.desc: Its sticky orange-pulped fruit is eaten by toucans, coatis, tapirs, agoutis and many birds, which spread the seeds.

sylvia curruca.name: Lesser whitethroat
sylvia curruca.desc: A very commonly recorded warbler near the park. It hunts insects in shrubs and is eaten by red foxes in GloBI records.

sylvicapra grimmia.name: Common duiker
sylvicapra grimmia.desc: Small antelope browsing leaves and fruit, seen above the timberline.

sylvilagus aquaticus.name: SWAMP RABBIT
sylvilagus aquaticus.desc: SWAMP RABBIT (Sylvilagus aquaticus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

sylvilagus audubonii.name: Desert cottontail
sylvilagus audubonii.desc: A small rabbit that is active at dawn and dusk and eats plants. Rattlesnakes, bullsnakes and bobcats take it.

sylvilagus bachmani.name: Brush rabbit
sylvilagus bachmani.desc: Eats plants and, per Wikipedia, preys on young redwood seedlings. Prey for foxes and cougars.

sylvilagus floridanus.name: Eastern cottontail
sylvilagus floridanus.desc: Eastern cottontail (Sylvilagus floridanus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

sylvilagus nuttallii.name: Mountain cottontail
sylvilagus nuttallii.desc: Mountain cottontail (Sylvilagus nuttallii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

sylvilagus palustris.name: Marsh rabbit
sylvilagus palustris.desc: A grass-eating rabbit of wet prairies and hammock edges. Pythons have sharply cut its numbers where they are established.

sylvisorex vulcanorum.name: Volcano forest shrew
sylvisorex vulcanorum.desc: A small insect-eating mammal of Albertine Rift forest floors, among the more recorded mammals near the park.

symbiodiniaceae.name: Zooxanthellae
symbiodiniaceae.desc: Microscopic algae living inside coral that pass sugars to their host.

symphoricarpos orbiculatus.name: Buck Brush
symphoricarpos orbiculatus.desc: Buck Brush (Symphoricarpos orbiculatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

symphyotrichum campestre.name: Western meadow aster
symphyotrichum campestre.desc: Western meadow aster (Symphyotrichum campestre): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

symphyotrichum lateriflorum.name: Calico Aster
symphyotrichum lateriflorum.desc: Calico Aster (Symphyotrichum lateriflorum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

symphyotrichum racemosum.name: Small-head aster
symphyotrichum racemosum.desc: Small-head aster (Symphyotrichum racemosum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

symplocarpus foetidus.name: Polecatweed
symplocarpus foetidus.desc: Polecatweed (Symplocarpus foetidus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

synanthedon exitiosa.name: Peachtree Borer
synanthedon exitiosa.desc: Peachtree Borer (Synanthedon exitiosa): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

syncerus caffer.name: African buffalo
syncerus caffer.desc: Herds graze tall, coarse grass and are hard for most predators to take down.

syncerus caffer nanus.name: Forest buffalo
syncerus caffer nanus.desc: A smaller forest form of the African buffalo that feeds on herbs and grasses in forest clearings and along the swamps.

synthliboramphus antiquus.name: Ancient murrelet
synthliboramphus antiquus.desc: A burrow-nesting seabird; about half the world population breeds on Haida Gwaii. Eats small fish and crustaceans.

syzygium.name: Satinash and lilly pilly
syzygium.desc: Rainforest trees whose fruit and flowers feed cassowaries and spectacled flying foxes.

syzygium cumini.name: Jamun
syzygium cumini.desc: A fruiting forest tree. GloBI records elephants, macaques, squirrels and many birds eating its fruit.

tachyoryctes macrocephalus.name: Giant root-rat
tachyoryctes macrocephalus.desc: Burrowing rodent found only in the Bale highlands. It forages on grasses and herbs from burrow mouths and is the main prey of the Ethiopian wolf.

tadarida brasiliensis.name: Mexican free-tailed bat
tadarida brasiliensis.desc: The cave's famous summer bat colony flies out at dusk to feed on moths and other flying insects. Their guano carries insect energy into the cave.

tadorna ferruginea.name: Ruddy shelduck
tadorna ferruginea.desc: Omnivorous duck of lakes and rivers that eats grasses, shoots, water plants and invertebrates. Breeds in Central Asia from March and April.

taeniatherum caput-medusae.name: Steppe grasses
taeniatherum caput-medusae.desc: Grasses and sedges cover about 45% of the Nuratau site (grassland), growing fast in the damp spring. They are the main forage on the lower slopes and desert fringe.

tamarindus indica.name: Tamarind
tamarindus indica.desc: A leafy tree whose pods are a key dry-season food for ring-tailed lemurs.

tamarix ramosissima.name: Salt cedar
tamarix ramosissima.desc: Salt cedar (Tamarix ramosissima): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

tamias dorsalis.name: Cliff chipmunk
tamias dorsalis.desc: Cliff chipmunk (Tamias dorsalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 36 times near the park in GBIF.

tamias minimus.name: Least chipmunk
tamias minimus.desc: Least chipmunk (Tamias minimus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

tamias sibiricus.name: Siberian chipmunk
tamias sibiricus.desc: A small seed-eating ground rodent of the forest, and a prey item for foxes, sables and bears in GloBI records.

tamias striatus.name: Eastern chipmunk
tamias striatus.desc: Eastern chipmunk (Tamias striatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

tamias umbrinus.name: Uinta chipmunk
tamias umbrinus.desc: The most recorded mammal near the park. A small forest rodent that feeds mainly on seeds and is prey for hawks.

tamiasciurus douglasii.name: Douglas squirrel
tamiasciurus douglasii.desc: Stores conifer cones in middens; bears raid these for whitebark pine seeds.

tamiasciurus hudsonicus.name: American red squirrel
tamiasciurus hudsonicus.desc: American red squirrel (Tamiasciurus hudsonicus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

tanacetum vulgare.name: Tansy
tanacetum vulgare.desc: Tansy (Tanacetum vulgare): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

tapirella bairdii.name: Baird's tapir
tapirella bairdii.desc: Browses leaves and twigs of understory plants and eats fruit in season. Some hard seeds, such as sapodilla, pass through it intact.

tapirus bairdii.name: Baird's tapir
tapirus bairdii.desc: A large browser of leaves and twigs in wet forest and swamp. Adults have few natural predators besides jaguars and big crocodiles.

tapirus terrestris.name: Lowland tapir
tapirus terrestris.desc: Eats fruit and leaves, and spreads seeds across the forest in its dung.

taraxacum officinale.name: Dandelion
taraxacum officinale.desc: Dandelion (Taraxacum officinale): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 51 times near the park in GBIF.

taraxia tanacetifolia.name: Tansyleaf evening primrose
taraxia tanacetifolia.desc: Tansyleaf evening primrose (Taraxia tanacetifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.

tarenna.name: Tarenna
tarenna.desc: A shrubby understorey plant of Afromontane forest whose small fruits are eaten by birds.

tauraco schuettii.name: Black-billed turaco
tauraco schuettii.desc: A fruit-eating forest bird; GloBI records show it eating Ilex mitis and Maesa lanceolata fruits.

taurotragus oryx.name: Common eland
taurotragus oryx.desc: Africa's largest antelope, which feeds on grasses and shrubs. Rarely recorded near the reserve.

taxidea taxus.name: American badger
taxidea taxus.desc: American badger (Taxidea taxus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

taxodium distichum.name: Bald cypress
taxodium distichum.desc: Extremely flood-tolerant swamp conifer of the Southeast. Floodwaters carry its seeds along, and squirrels eat them.

tayassu pecari.name: White-lipped peccary
tayassu pecari.desc: A herd-living forest pig that eats fruits, seeds and roots and is prey for jaguars and pumas.

tegeticula synthetica.name: Yucca moth
tegeticula synthetica.desc: Pollinates Joshua trees while laying eggs in the flowers; its larvae eat some of the seeds.

telmatobius culeus.name: Titicaca water frog
telmatobius culeus.desc: A fully aquatic frog that eats mainly amphipods and snails, and adults also take Orestias fish. Overcollection, pollution and trout have cut its numbers.

tenaxia.name: Highland grasses
tenaxia.desc: Montane and afroalpine grasslands cover much of the plateau and are the main food of geladas.

tenebrionidae.name: Darkling beetles
tenebrionidae.desc: Hardy ground beetles of sandy deserts that feed on plant matter and debris, and feed many lizards and birds.

tenrecidae.name: Tenrecs
tenrecidae.desc: Small insect-eating mammals unique to Madagascar, hunted by the fossa.

tenualosa ilisha.name: Hilsa
tenualosa ilisha.desc: A plankton-feeding fish that lives in estuaries and swims up rivers to spawn. It is Bangladesh's national fish.

tephrosia virginiana.name: Goat's rue
tephrosia virginiana.desc: Goat's rue (Tephrosia virginiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

terathopius ecaudatus.name: Bateleur
terathopius ecaudatus.desc: A short-tailed eagle that eats both live prey, such as snakes and birds, and a good deal of carrion.

teratoscincus scincus.name: Common wonder gecko
teratoscincus scincus.desc: A nocturnal gecko of sand dunes that shelters in a deep burrow by day and eats insects and other lizards.

termites, scarab beetles, fungi, bacteri.name: Decomposers
termites, scarab beetles, fungi, bacteri.desc: Beetles, termites and microbes break down dung, dead plants and carcasses, returning nutrients to the sand.

termitidae.name: Termites
termitidae.desc: Feed on dead wood and plant litter, and are a main food of giant anteaters and giant armadillos.

termitoidae.name: Termites
termitoidae.desc: Break down dead wood and leaf litter and recycle nutrients. Chimpanzees fish them out of mounds with sticks.

terpsiphone viridis.name: African paradise flycatcher
terpsiphone viridis.desc: Insect-catching forest bird, also recorded taking Lantana fruit.

tetrao urogallus.name: Western capercaillie
tetrao urogallus.desc: Huge grouse of the old pinewoods, feeding on pine shoots and bilberry; its eggs, chicks and adults are taken by predators.

tetraogallus himalayensis.name: Himalayan snowcock
tetraogallus himalayensis.desc: A large alpine game bird that feeds on plants on open high slopes, and lives in the park per Wikipedia.

tettigonia caudata.name: Bush-cricket
tettigonia caudata.desc: A large bush-cricket of dry shrubby ground. It chews leaves and some other insects and feeds lizards and bats.

teucrium canadense.name: American Germander
teucrium canadense.desc: American Germander (Teucrium canadense): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

thalassarche melanophris.name: Black-browed albatross
thalassarche melanophris.desc: The Falklands hold the largest breeding population in the world. It eats fish, squid, crustaceans, carrion and fishery discards.

thalasseus bengalensis.name: Lesser crested tern
thalasseus bengalensis.desc: Plunge-dives for fish in salt water and breeds in island colonies; the archipelago is an Important Bird Area.

thalasseus bergii.name: Great crested tern
thalasseus bergii.desc: A fish-eating tern that plunge-dives for small schooling fish along the shore.

thalassia testudinum.name: Turtle grass
thalassia testudinum.desc: The main seagrass of the bay. Its meadows shelter young fish and invertebrates, and its dead leaves supply much of the detritus.

thalassiosira.name: Phytoplankton
thalassiosira.desc: Microscopic drifting algae in the surrounding sea, the base of the open-water food chain.

thalassodendron.name: Seagrass
thalassodendron.desc: Meadows in the shallow lagoon that green turtles graze.

thalassodendron ciliatum.name: Seagrass
thalassodendron ciliatum.desc: A seagrass of shallow East African and Indian Ocean waters, forming meadows that feed grazers and shelter small fish.

thalictrum thalictroides.name: Rue-anemone
thalictrum thalictroides.desc: Rue-anemone (Thalictrum thalictroides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 40 times near the park in GBIF.

thamnophis sirtalis.name: Common garter snake
thamnophis sirtalis.desc: A widespread snake of wet ground that eats small mammals and amphibians and is prey for herons and foxes.

thamnosma montana.name: Mohave desertrue
thamnosma montana.desc: Mohave desertrue (Thamnosma montana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 129 times near the park in GBIF.

thelesperma filifolium.name: Stiff greenthread
thelesperma filifolium.desc: Stiff greenthread (Thelesperma filifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 83 times near the park in GBIF.

thelypodium brachycarpum.name: Short-podded thelypody
thelypodium brachycarpum.desc: Short-podded thelypody (Thelypodium brachycarpum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

themeda triandra.name: Red grass
themeda triandra.desc: The tall grass of the plains. Fire and grazing keep it growing back each year.

themeda, cymbopogon, arundinella.name: Shola grasses
themeda, cymbopogon, arundinella.desc: Frost- and fire-resistant tussock grasses cover the high montane grasslands between the shola forest patches.

theobroma subincanum.name: Wild cacao relative
theobroma subincanum.desc: A forest tree whose fruit is eaten by peccaries, deer, agoutis and monkeys, according to GloBI feeding records.

theropithecus gelada.name: Gelada
theropithecus gelada.desc: A grazing primate of the Ethiopian Highlands, with grass blades making up most of its diet; it sleeps on cliff ledges.

thin alpine soil.name: Thin alpine soil
thin alpine soil.desc: Poor, shallow soils above the treeline; plants there are dwarfed and deep rooted.

thin boreal soil.name: Thin boreal soil
thin boreal soil.desc: Soils on the island are thin, so shallow-rooted trees dominate and nutrients cycle quickly through leaf litter.

thin cold soil.name: Thin cold soil
thin cold soil.desc: Plants face strong winds, thin soils and a short growing season, according to the park service.

thin desert soil.name: Thin desert soil
thin desert soil.desc: Hot, dry conditions limit soil formation, so slopes stay stony and plants depend on what nutrients decomposers release.

thin glacial soils.name: Thin glacial soils
thin glacial soils.desc: Granite bedrock and thin soils shaped by glaciers hold the forest's nutrients, which are recycled from dead matter.

thin limestone soil.name: Thin limestone soil
thin limestone soil.desc: Shallow soil over limestone; litter decay by microbes recycles nutrients to the forest.

thin mountain soil.name: Thin mountain soil
thin mountain soil.desc: Cold, thin soils slow plant growth and nutrient release.

thin rocky soil.name: Thin rocky soil
thin rocky soil.desc: Shallow soils on the canyon rim hold little water and nutrients, so decomposers recycling dead matter matter to the plants.

thin soil on ancient rock.name: Thin soil on ancient rock
thin soil on ancient rock.desc: The park sits on very old Canadian Shield bedrock, with glacial scours and deposits shaping where soil and water collect.

thin tundra soil.name: Thin tundra soil
thin tundra soil.desc: Cold, thin soils keep most trees and shrubs small, according to Wikipedia.

thin tundra soil & bird guano.name: Thin tundra soil & bird guano
thin tundra soil & bird guano.desc: Soils are thin and thaw only in summer. Seabird droppings below bird cliffs fertilise the slopes, where the lushest vegetation grows.

thomomys bottae.name: Botta's pocket gopher
thomomys bottae.desc: Botta's pocket gopher (Thomomys bottae): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

thraupis palmarum.name: Palm tanager
thraupis palmarum.desc: A common fruit-eating songbird; GloBI records show it eating Miconia fruit.

thrinax radiata.name: Florida thatch palm
thrinax radiata.desc: A coastal palm that is one of the most recorded plants near the reserve. Its fruit is eaten by animals such as spider monkeys.

thryothorus ludovicianus.name: Carolina Wren
thryothorus ludovicianus.desc: Carolina Wren (Thryothorus ludovicianus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 897 times near the park in GBIF.

thuja plicata.name: Western Red-cedar
thuja plicata.desc: Western Red-cedar (Thuja plicata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

thunnus albacares.name: Yellowfin tuna
thunnus albacares.desc: Fast open-water hunter of flying fish and other baitfish. Industrial fisheries are its main cause of death.

thylogale billardierii.name: Tasmanian pademelon
thylogale billardierii.desc: A small wallaby that rests in thick cover by day and feeds on grass and shoots in open ground near the forest edge after dark.

thylogale stigmatica.name: Red-legged pademelon
thylogale stigmatica.desc: A small rainforest wallaby that eats umbrella tree fruit.

thymus praecox.name: Mother of thyme
thymus praecox.desc: A creeping, aromatic herb of thin limestone soils that flowers in the short turf.

thyridopteryx ephemeraeformis.name: Common bagworm
thyridopteryx ephemeraeformis.desc: Common bagworm (Thyridopteryx ephemeraeformis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

tian shan meltwater.name: Tian Shan meltwater
tian shan meltwater.desc: Snowmelt and glacier streams from the surrounding mountains: about 118 rivers and streams feed the lake and water the valleys and shores.

tiarella trifoliata.name: Sugar-scoop
tiarella trifoliata.desc: Sugar-scoop (Tiarella trifoliata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

tidal flats and sabkha.name: Tidal flats and sabkha
tidal flats and sabkha.desc: Tidal mudflats and salt flats line the coast of the reserve islands and host wintering waders and mangroves.

tidal flooding.name: Tidal flooding
tidal flooding.desc: Seawater floods and drains the low mudflats and salt marshes, bringing food in and exposing invertebrates to wading birds at low tide.

tidal lagoon.name: Tidal lagoon
tidal lagoon.desc: A large, shallow lagoon of seagrass, mudflats and mangroves that empties and refills with the tides.

tidal lagoons (khaurs).name: Tidal lagoons (khaurs)
tidal lagoons (khaurs).desc: Lagoons such as Khaur Jarama have mudflats, scattered mangroves and fish nursery habitat, and feed wintering waders.

tidal mixing.name: Tides and salt water
tidal mixing.desc: Tides reach about 58 miles up the river, mixing fresh and salt water and flooding the marsh twice a day.

tidal mudflats.name: Tidal mudflats
tidal mudflats.desc: Vast intertidal flats and sand banks hold the seagrass beds and feed the wintering shorebirds.

tidal salinity.name: Tidal salinity
tidal salinity.desc: Tides and the balance of fresh and salt water set which trees survive. Rising sea level and less river flow push salt further inland.

tidal sea water.name: Tidal sea water
tidal sea water.desc: Twice-daily tides flood the coastal mangroves and bring in salt water and sediment.

tidal sediment.name: Marsh mud and nutrients
tidal sediment.desc: Muddy marsh soil holds the nutrients that cordgrass takes up.

tides.name: Tides
tides.desc: Rising and falling tides wet and expose the rocky shore twice a day and set where seaweeds and shellfish can live.

tides and brackish water.name: Tides and brackish water
tides and brackish water.desc: Tides flood the channels and lagoons twice a day, setting the salinity that mangroves tolerate and moving crabs, fish and larvae in and out.

tides and cool ocean water.name: Tides and cool ocean water
tides and cool ocean water.desc: Tides and ocean exchange flush the bay, bringing cooler, saltier water in from Rhode Island Sound.

tides and currents.name: Tides and currents
tides and currents.desc: Tides flush the mangroves and shallow banks, carrying nutrients and larvae.

tides and lagoons.name: Tides and lagoons
tides and lagoons.desc: Tides flood the mangrove and seagrass shallows with salt water and move nutrients and larvae in and out.

tides and river flooding.name: Tides and river flooding
tides and river flooding.desc: Coastal tides and flooding rivers soak the swamps and mangroves along the Pacific side of the site.

tides and salt water.name: Tides and salt water
tides and salt water.desc: Tides flood and drain the mangrove mud twice a day, bringing salt water that mangroves tolerate and most other plants do not.

tigris-euphrates floodwater.name: Tigris-Euphrates floodwater
tigris-euphrates floodwater.desc: The marshes depend on river flow. Drainage and upstream dams cut it, and reflooding after 2003 let wetlands partly recover.

tilapia and others.name: Freshwater fish
tilapia and others.desc: Fish of the seasonal rivers and lakes that graze on algae and small aquatic life.

tillandsia usneoides.name: Spanish moss
tillandsia usneoides.desc: Spanish moss (Tillandsia usneoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

timane river and waterholes.name: Timane River and waterholes
timane river and waterholes.desc: The Timane River runs through old channels toward Cerro Leon and feeds an inland basin; seasonal pools matter for wildlife in a dry land.

tipularia discolor.name: Crippled cranefly
tipularia discolor.desc: Crippled cranefly (Tipularia discolor): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 37 times near the park in GBIF.

tisza river floods.name: Tisza River floods
tisza river floods.desc: The Tisza shaped this plain; its changing course is thought to have started the alkalinisation of the soils about 10,000 years ago.

tockus deckeni.name: Von der Decken's hornbill
tockus deckeni.desc: A hornbill of dry bush and coastal woodland in East Africa. It eats insects and other small prey, and fruit.

todiramphus sacer.name: Pacific kingfisher
todiramphus sacer.desc: A perch-and-pounce hunter that takes insects, lizards, frogs and crabs, and is found across the South Pacific including Vanuatu.

todus mexicanus.name: Puerto Rican tody
todus mexicanus.desc: A tiny insect-eating bird endemic to the island. GloBI also records it taking fruit of pumpwood.

todus todus.name: Jamaican tody
todus todus.desc: A tiny endemic bird that catches insects and other small invertebrates in the forest understory.

tolypeutes matacus.name: Southern three-banded armadillo
tolypeutes matacus.desc: An armadillo that can roll into a ball; it feeds mainly on ants and termites and some plant matter.

tomostima cuneifolia.name: Wedge Leaf Whitlow-grass
tomostima cuneifolia.desc: Wedge Leaf Whitlow-grass (Tomostima cuneifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

tor putitora.name: Golden mahseer
tor putitora.desc: A large river fish of Himalayan rivers that grazes algae and other foods and feeds the gharial.

townsendia texensis.name: Texas Townsend daisy
townsendia texensis.desc: Texas Townsend daisy (Townsendia texensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.

toxicodendron diversilobum.name: Pacific poison-oak
toxicodendron diversilobum.desc: Pacific poison-oak (Toxicodendron diversilobum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 63 times near the park in GBIF.

toxicodendron radicans.name: Poison Ivy
toxicodendron radicans.desc: Poison Ivy (Toxicodendron radicans): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

toxostoma curvirostre.name: Curve-billed Thrasher
toxostoma curvirostre.desc: Curve-billed Thrasher (Toxostoma curvirostre): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 2,230 times near the park in GBIF.

trachylepis atlantica.name: Noronha skink
trachylepis atlantica.desc: An endemic island lizard, the most recorded reptile near the site. Small insects are its likely food.

trachylepis striata.name: African striped skink
trachylepis striata.desc: A lizard that hunts insects and is preyed on by snakes.

trachypithecus geei.name: Golden langur
trachypithecus geei.desc: A tree-dwelling leaf, fruit, seed and flower eater found only in a small area of Bhutan and Assam.

trachypithecus hatinhensis.name: Hatinh langur
trachypithecus hatinhensis.desc: A leaf-eating monkey of limestone forest that sleeps in cliff crevices and caves. Wikipedia says the park holds the largest known population in the world.

trachypithecus obscurus.name: Dusky leaf monkey
trachypithecus obscurus.desc: Tree-living monkey that eats mainly leaves, along with fruit and flowers.

trachypithecus poliocephalus.name: Cat Ba langur
trachypithecus poliocephalus.desc: A critically endangered primate found only on Cat Ba Island. Over 70% of its diet is leaves, and it can drink salt water.

trachypithecus shortridgei.name: Shortridge's langur
trachypithecus shortridgei.desc: An endangered leaf-eating monkey of northern Myanmar forests that lives in the canopy and feeds on leaves and fruit.

tradescantia occidentalis.name: Prairie spiderwort
tradescantia occidentalis.desc: Prairie spiderwort (Tradescantia occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

tradescantia virginiana.name: White spiderwort
tradescantia virginiana.desc: White spiderwort (Tradescantia virginiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 57 times near the park in GBIF.

tragelaphus buxtoni.name: Mountain nyala
tragelaphus buxtoni.desc: Large antelope found only in the Ethiopian Highlands east of the Rift. It mostly browses herbs and shrubs, and the leopard is its main predator.

tragelaphus scriptus.name: Bushbuck
tragelaphus scriptus.desc: A shy antelope of forest edges and thickets that browses leaves and shoots.

tragelaphus spekii.name: Sitatunga
tragelaphus spekii.desc: A swamp antelope that feeds on sedges, fresh grasses and herbs at wetland edges. It hides in deep water, partly submerged, when threatened.

tragelaphus strepsiceros.name: Greater kudu
tragelaphus strepsiceros.desc: A woodland browser of leaves and shoots. Kudu are a main prey of spotted hyenas in Etosha.

tragulus kanchil.name: Lesser mouse-deer
tragulus kanchil.desc: Tiny hoofed mammal of the forest floor that eats fallen fruit and leaves.

trapa natans.name: Water Nut
trapa natans.desc: Water Nut (Trapa natans): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 96 times near the park in GBIF.

trapelus sanguinolentus.name: Steppe agama
trapelus sanguinolentus.desc: A common desert lizard that hunts insects by day. It is recorded as prey of the steppe ribbon racer.

travertine lake water.name: Travertine lake water
travertine lake water.desc: Mineral-rich water deposited calcium carbonate that built the travertine dams holding the six lakes, which sustain the shoreline vegetation.

trema orientale.name: Trema
trema orientale.desc: A fast-growing pioneer tree recorded near the reserve, found in forest edges and clearings where it makes small fruits.

tremarctos ornatus.name: Spectacled bear
tremarctos ornatus.desc: South America's only bear, mostly vegetarian: bromeliads, palm nuts, fallen fruit and a little meat. Cloud forest is its best habitat.

triadenum fraseri.name: Fraser's Marsh St. Johnswort
triadenum fraseri.desc: Fraser's Marsh St. Johnswort (Triadenum fraseri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

triaenodon obesus.name: Whitetip reef shark
triaenodon obesus.desc: A reef shark that rests in caves by day and hunts reef fish, octopus and crustaceans at night; Tubbataha is noted for very high densities of it.

tribulus terrestris.name: Small Caltrops
tribulus terrestris.desc: Small Caltrops (Tribulus terrestris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

trichechus manatus.name: West Indian manatee
trichechus manatus.desc: A slow, gentle grazer of seagrass that visits the bay. Boat strikes are a main danger.

trichechus senegalensis.name: West African manatee
trichechus senegalensis.desc: Lives in the Gambia River. River manatees mostly eat vegetation overhanging the banks and have few natural enemies besides crocodiles and people.

trichodes ornatus.name: Common Checkered Beetle
trichodes ornatus.desc: Common Checkered Beetle (Trichodes ornatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.

trichoglossus haematodus.name: Rainbow lorikeet
trichoglossus haematodus.desc: A nectar and fruit feeder. Eucalypt nectar is an important food, and it also takes figs.

trichoptera.name: Caddisfly larvae
trichoptera.desc: Aquatic larvae that graze algae and plant matter on stones and are food for trout and dippers.

trichoscypha.name: Trichoscypha
trichoscypha.desc: Forest trees with fleshy fruit. GloBI records show several monkeys and a forest mouse feeding on them.

trichostema lanatum.name: Woolly blue-curls
trichostema lanatum.desc: Woolly blue-curls (Trichostema lanatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 48 times near the park in GBIF.

trichosurus vulpecula.name: Common brushtail possum
trichosurus vulpecula.desc: Introduced from Australia. It eats the leaves of native trees and continues to damage the forest.

trifolium alpinum.name: Alpine clover
trifolium alpinum.desc: Flowering legume of high pastures. Herbs like this are eaten by grazers in summer, and it is a larval food plant for the mountain clouded yellow butterfly.

trifolium depauperatum.name: Dwarf sack clover
trifolium depauperatum.desc: Dwarf sack clover (Trifolium depauperatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

trifolium pratense.name: Red Clover
trifolium pratense.desc: Meadow legume of valley grasslands and shores, eaten by birds and grazers.

trifolium repens.name: White Clover
trifolium repens.desc: White Clover (Trifolium repens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

trillium.name: Spring wildflowers
trillium.desc: Trilliums, mayapple, phlox and other woodland flowers that carpet the forest floor in spring and are recorded often in the park.

trillium catesbaei.name: Bashful wakerobin
trillium catesbaei.desc: Bashful wakerobin (Trillium catesbaei): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 96 times near the park in GBIF.

trillium cuneatum.name: Little sweet Betsy
trillium cuneatum.desc: Little sweet Betsy (Trillium cuneatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

trillium erectum.name: Red Trillium
trillium erectum.desc: Red Trillium (Trillium erectum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 41 times near the park in GBIF.

trillium grandiflorum.name: Large white trillium
trillium grandiflorum.desc: A spring woodland wildflower of the forest floor. GloBI records white-tailed deer browsing it.

trillium ovatum.name: Pacific trillium
trillium ovatum.desc: Pacific trillium (Trillium ovatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

trillium recurvatum.name: Prairie trillium
trillium recurvatum.desc: Prairie trillium (Trillium recurvatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

trillium sessile.name: Sessile trillium
trillium sessile.desc: Sessile trillium (Trillium sessile): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

trillium undulatum.name: Painted trillium
trillium undulatum.desc: Painted trillium (Trillium undulatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 30 times near the park in GBIF.

trillium viridescens.name: Tapertip wakerobin
trillium viridescens.desc: Tapertip wakerobin (Trillium viridescens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

trimeresurus albolabris.name: White-lipped pit viper
trimeresurus albolabris.desc: A tree-dwelling venomous snake that ambushes lizards and other small animals.

trimeresurus insularis.name: White-lipped island pitviper
trimeresurus insularis.desc: A venomous tree snake and the most recorded reptile near the park. GloBI records show it eating tree frogs.

trimeresurus sabahi.name: Sabah bamboo pitviper
trimeresurus sabahi.desc: A Bornean pitviper of mountain forest, usually seen on branches of shrubs; it takes small vertebrates such as frogs and rodents.

tringa semipalmata.name: Willet
tringa semipalmata.desc: Willet (Tringa semipalmata): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 78 times near the park in GBIF.

trioceros cristatus.name: Crested chameleon
trioceros cristatus.desc: A forest chameleon of Cameroon and neighbouring countries that is recorded near the reserve and feeds on small invertebrates.

trioceros johnstoni.name: Johnston's chameleon
trioceros johnstoni.desc: A highland forest chameleon of the Albertine Rift that catches insects in the shrub layer.

triodia.name: Spinifex
triodia.desc: Spiky hummock grasses that cover much of the red sandplain and dunes of central Australia.

triphosa haesitata.name: Tissue Moth
triphosa haesitata.desc: Tissue Moth (Triphosa haesitata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

tripsacum dactyloides.name: Eastern Gamagrass
tripsacum dactyloides.desc: Eastern Gamagrass (Tripsacum dactyloides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

trirhabda bacharidis.name: Groundselbush beetle
trirhabda bacharidis.desc: Groundselbush beetle (Trirhabda bacharidis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.

trochilus polytmus.name: Red-billed streamertail
trochilus polytmus.desc: Jamaica's national bird, the most recorded species here. It feeds mainly on nectar and also catches small insects.

trollius europaeus and others.name: Mountain meadow herbs
trollius europaeus and others.desc: Globeflower and many other flowering herbs of the pastures and meadows above the tree line, part of a flora of about 2,600 plant species.

troodos rock and thin soil.name: Troodos rock and thin soil
troodos rock and thin soil.desc: The massif is an uplifted slab of ancient oceanic crust; the golden oak is restricted to its igneous rocks.

tropical rain.name: Heavy rainfall
tropical rain.desc: The islands are wet. Rain feeds the rainforest and runs down steep slopes to the sea.

tropical rainfall.name: Tropical rainfall
tropical rainfall.desc: Heavy, year-round rain feeds the rivers and keeps the lowland forest and peat swamps wet.

tropical sun.name: Sunlight
tropical sun.desc: Strong year-round sun powers the rainforest canopy and the algae and plankton of the reef.

tropical sunlight.name: Tropical sunlight
tropical sunlight.desc: Year-round warmth and light drive the forest canopy.

tropidacris cristata.name: Giant red-winged grasshopper
tropidacris cristata.desc: A very large tropical grasshopper that chews leaves, and is prey for lizards and birds.

tsuga canadensis.name: Eastern hemlock
tsuga canadensis.desc: A shade-tolerant evergreen of the park's cool ravines. GloBI records both deer and beavers feeding on it.

tsuga chinensis.name: Chinese hemlock
tsuga chinensis.desc: A conifer that dominates a mid-elevation forest belt in the park, roughly between 2,500 and 3,500 m. It shelters many forest animals.

tsuga heterophylla.name: Western hemlock
tsuga heterophylla.desc: A shade-tolerant conifer of the lower, wetter forests where the old-growth stands are found.

tsuga mertensiana.name: Mountain hemlock
tsuga mertensiana.desc: A conifer of deep-snow subalpine forest and one of the most recorded trees around the rim.

tundra soil.name: Tundra soil
tundra soil.desc: Thin, cold soils over permafrost where nutrients are released slowly.

tundra soil and permafrost.name: Tundra soil and permafrost
tundra soil and permafrost.desc: Island ground that was never glaciated. Its thin, cold soil feeds sedges, willows and the meadows of the warmer valleys.

tupaia montana.name: Mountain treeshrew
tupaia montana.desc: Eats mostly arthropods plus wild fruit, and licks nectar from pitcher plants including N. rajah, leaving droppings in them. Endemic to Borneo.

turdus falcklandii.name: Austral thrush
turdus falcklandii.desc: A common thrush of forests and gardens that eats berries and invertebrates.

turdus grayi.name: Clay-colored thrush
turdus grayi.desc: A widespread thrush that eats fruit, recorded on milkberry, alligatorwood and wax mallow.

turdus merula.name: Eurasian blackbird
turdus merula.desc: A thrush that GloBI records eating barley and Pistacia atlantica. It is itself prey for foxes, jackals and kestrels.

turdus migratorius.name: American Robin
turdus migratorius.desc: American Robin (Turdus migratorius): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 33 times near the park in GBIF.

turdus plumbeus.name: Red-legged thrush
turdus plumbeus.desc: Thrush that eats fruit and invertebrates, GloBI records it taking scarletbush.

tursiops aduncus.name: Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphin
tursiops aduncus.desc: Eats a wide range of fish and squid. Some Shark Bay dolphins wear marine sponges on their snouts, seemingly as tools to probe the seabed for fish.

tursiops truncatus.name: Bottlenose dolphin
tursiops truncatus.desc: Visits the bay seasonally or year-round and eats fish including menhaden.

tympanuchus cupido.name: Greater prairie-chicken
tympanuchus cupido.desc: Eats seeds, fruit, green plants and insects such as grasshoppers. Wikipedia says Missouri once held hundreds of thousands but only about 500 remain, and that the MDC is bringing birds in from Kansas and Nebraska.

typha.name: Cattails
typha.desc: Tall emergent plants of the park's marshes and beaver ponds, eaten by muskrats and beavers.

typha angustifolia.name: Lesser Bulrush
typha angustifolia.desc: Lesser Bulrush (Typha angustifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 27 times near the park in GBIF.

typha domingensis.name: Southern cattail
typha domingensis.desc: A tall emergent marsh plant that grows with reeds in the shallow water of the marshes.

typha latifolia.name: Bulrush
typha latifolia.desc: Bulrush (Typha latifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

tyria jacobaeae.name: Cinnabar
tyria jacobaeae.desc: Cinnabar (Tyria jacobaeae): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

tyto glaucops.name: Ashy-faced owl
tyto glaucops.desc: A night hunter that preys on solenodons, which evolved with few land predators.

uca.name: Fiddler crabs
uca.desc: Burrowing crabs that sift mud for algae, microbes and detritus, and are a main food for wading birds and other predators here.

uca and related genera.name: Fiddler crabs
uca and related genera.desc: Burrowing crabs that sift mud for algae, microbes and detritus. Many predators hunt them, and they rework the sediment as they feed.

ulex minor.name: Dwarf gorse
ulex minor.desc: Spiny evergreen shrub that, with heather, dominates the shrublands covering most of the site.

ulva.name: Green seaweed
ulva.desc: Sea lettuce and other algae grow on the shallow reefs and are a food for green turtles.

ulva and others.name: Benthic algae
ulva and others.desc: Over 305 species of seaweed have been recorded in the marine park, about 15 percent of them found nowhere else. They are the grazing base of the reef.

uniola paniculata.name: Seaoats
uniola paniculata.desc: Seaoats (Uniola paniculata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

unionidae.name: Freshwater mussels
unionidae.desc: The upper river has dozens of mussel species. They filter algae from the water, and freshwater drum eat them. The NPS reports their numbers are recovering.

uria lomvia.name: Thick-billed murre
uria lomvia.desc: A seabird that dives deep for cod and nests on crowded cliffs.

urnisa guttulosa.name: Grasshoppers
urnisa guttulosa.desc: Plant-eating insects that boom after rain and feed lizards, birds and small marsupials.

urochloa.name: Signalgrass
urochloa.desc: Grasses of open patches among the thorn forest, one of the well-recorded plant groups near the park; seeds feed doves and others.

urocissa ornata.name: Sri Lanka blue magpie
urocissa ornata.desc: An endemic forest bird that eats mainly insects, frogs and small lizards, plus some fruit, and may take eggs or chicks of other birds.

urocitellus armatus.name: Uinta ground squirrel
urocitellus armatus.desc: Common on the valley floor, eats plants and seeds and is prey for coyotes, eagles and bears.

urocitellus columbianus.name: Columbian Ground Squirrel
urocitellus columbianus.desc: Burrowing squirrel of meadows and slopes that eats plants and bulbs. It is a prey of many predators and one of the best-recorded mammals near the park.

urocitellus parryii.name: Arctic ground squirrel
urocitellus parryii.desc: Eats willows, berries, seeds and some insects and stores food for winter. Predators include foxes, wolves, bears, lynx and eagles.

urocitellus undulatus.name: Long-tailed ground squirrel
urocitellus undulatus.desc: A burrowing ground squirrel of steppe and meadows and the most recorded mammal near the site. Steppe eagles and foxes take it.

urocyon cinereoargenteus.name: Gray fox
urocyon cinereoargenteus.desc: Gray fox (Urocyon cinereoargenteus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

urocyon littoralis.name: Island fox
urocyon littoralis.desc: A small fox found only on the islands. It eats fruit, insects, lizards, birds and deer mice.

uromastyx aegyptia.name: Egyptian mastigure
uromastyx aegyptia.desc: A large spiny-tailed lizard of open, gravelly desert. It shelters in burrows and feeds mainly on plants and seeds.

ursus americanus.name: Black bear
ursus americanus.desc: Black bear (Ursus americanus): a top predator in this web. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

ursus americanus carlottae.name: Haida Gwaii black bear
ursus americanus carlottae.desc: Largest native land mammal of the archipelago. Eats salmon, shellfish and plants, and carries salmon remains into the forest.

ursus arctos.name: Brown bear
ursus arctos.desc: Roams the taiga shore. It is the only known natural predator of adult Baikal seals, though attacks are thought to be rare.

ursus arctos beringianus.name: Kamchatka brown bear
ursus arctos beringianus.desc: Eats berries, pine nuts, salmon and small mammals. Males can exceed 600 kg before winter.

ursus arctos gobiensis.name: Gobi bear
ursus arctos gobiensis.desc: A rare brown bear living near desert oases. It eats mostly plants and roots, with a little animal food such as rodents.

ursus arctos horribilis.name: Grizzly bear
ursus arctos horribilis.desc: The reserve is thought to hold around 500 grizzlies. They eat ground squirrels, moose, caribou and sheep, as well as plants.

ursus arctos lasiopus.name: Ussuri brown bear
ursus arctos lasiopus.desc: Mostly vegetarian, eating acorns, Korean pine seeds and berries. Bears steal about 35% of tiger kills in Sikhote-Alin and can also kill tigers.

ursus maritimus.name: Polar bear
ursus maritimus.desc: Hunts seals from the sea ice, so it depends on that ice to feed.

ursus thibetanus.name: Asian black bear
ursus thibetanus.desc: An omnivore that eats bamboo shoots, nuts and fruit and also meat. It can prey on panda cubs.

urtica dioica.name: Common nettle
urtica dioica.desc: A nutrient-loving plant of clearings and stream edges. Its leaves are the food plant of Small tortoiseshell caterpillars.

usnea.name: Tree lichens
usnea.desc: Lichens growing on trunks and branches. They are the near-total winter food of musk deer.

uta stansburiana.name: Side-blotched lizard
uta stansburiana.desc: A small, very commonly recorded lizard that hunts insects and is prey for snakes, other lizards and hawks.

uvularia grandiflora.name: Bellwort
uvularia grandiflora.desc: Bellwort (Uvularia grandiflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.

vaccinium.name: Cowberry and bilberry
vaccinium.desc: Low heath shrubs of the subalpine and bog zones. Their berries are eaten by black bears.

vaccinium and others.name: Berries & understory plants
vaccinium and others.desc: Blueberries, huckleberries and other soft fruits and greens that feed bears, turkeys and deer in summer.

vaccinium angustifolium.name: Lowbush blueberry
vaccinium angustifolium.desc: A low shrub with berries eaten by black bears and browsed by deer.

vaccinium arboreum.name: Farkleberry
vaccinium arboreum.desc: Farkleberry (Vaccinium arboreum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

vaccinium corymbosum.name: Highbush blueberry
vaccinium corymbosum.desc: A fruiting shrub of the swamp margins and islands whose berries feed birds and mammals.

vaccinium macrocarpon.name: Cranberry
vaccinium macrocarpon.desc: A low trailing shrub of acidic bogs and wet sands. Its berries are eaten by wildlife and it is grown commercially in the region.

vaccinium membranaceum.name: Thinleaf huckleberry
vaccinium membranaceum.desc: A berry shrub of subalpine slopes. Its berries are eaten by bears and many other animals.

vaccinium myrtilloides.name: Canada blueberry
vaccinium myrtilloides.desc: Canada blueberry (Vaccinium myrtilloides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

vaccinium myrtillus.name: Bilberry
vaccinium myrtillus.desc: A low forest-floor shrub whose leaves and berries are eaten by deer and voles.

vaccinium ovatum.name: California Huckleberry
vaccinium ovatum.desc: California Huckleberry (Vaccinium ovatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 620 times near the park in GBIF.

vaccinium parvifolium.name: Red-huckleberry
vaccinium parvifolium.desc: Red-huckleberry (Vaccinium parvifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 61 times near the park in GBIF.

vaccinium reticulatum.name: ʻŌhelo
vaccinium reticulatum.desc: A native shrub of volcanic slopes with edible red or yellow berries that birds such as the nēnē eat.

vaccinium spp..name: Blueberries & berry shrubs
vaccinium spp..desc: Low shrubs that Canadian boreal fires encourage. Their berries feed bears and small mammals.

vaccinium uliginosum.name: Bog bilberry
vaccinium uliginosum.desc: A tundra berry shrub. Wild blueberries are a main part of the bears' diet in Denali, and caribou, ptarmigan and ground squirrels also eat the plant or fruit.

vaccinium vitis-idaea.name: Cowberry
vaccinium vitis-idaea.desc: Low evergreen shrub with tart berries. GloBI records it eaten by caribou, ptarmigan, longspurs, foxes and ravens.

vachellia.name: Acacia
vachellia.desc: Thorny acacia trees grow in the warm lower parts of the reserve. Nubian ibex browse their leaves, rearing up or climbing into the branches.

vachellia nilotica.name: Babul
vachellia nilotica.desc: A thorny acacia of dry country. Its pods and leaves are browsed by hoofed animals such as nilgai and blackbuck.

vachellia tortilis.name: Umbrella thorn acacia
vachellia tortilis.desc: Thorny acacias grow in wadis where moisture collects. Their leaves and pods are browsed by gazelles, addax and others.

vachellia xanthophloea.name: Fever tree
vachellia xanthophloea.desc: A yellow-barked acacia of wet ground, recorded in the park.

valerianella radiata.name: Beaked cornsalad
valerianella radiata.desc: Beaked cornsalad (Valerianella radiata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

valley soil.name: Valley soil
valley soil.desc: Soil of the valley floor holds the mopane woodland and grassland; dung and dead matter return nutrients to it.

valley soils.name: Valley soils
valley soils.desc: Alluvial valley soils and forest litter supply nutrients to the plants.

vallisneria and potamogeton spp..name: Wild celery & pondweeds
vallisneria and potamogeton spp..desc: Underwater plants rooted in the river bed. The FWS and Wikipedia describe submerged vegetation as important for fish and waterfowl. Canvasbacks eat the tubers.

vanessa atalanta.name: Red Admiral
vanessa atalanta.desc: Red Admiral (Vanessa atalanta): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

vanessa cardui.name: Painted Lady
vanessa cardui.desc: Painted Lady (Vanessa cardui): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

varanus bengalensis.name: Bengal monitor
varanus bengalensis.desc: A large lizard of dry forest and scrub that eats insects and small animals and scavenges carrion.

varanus giganteus.name: Perentie
varanus giganteus.desc: Australia's largest lizard, an apex predator of rocky arid country that eats reptiles, small mammals and carrion.

varanus gouldii.name: Sand goanna
varanus gouldii.desc: A relentless forager on mice, small mammals, birds, lizards and eggs. Adults also eat carrion.

varanus griseus.name: Desert monitor
varanus griseus.desc: A large lizard that hunts small mammals, reptiles and insects across sand and gravel plains.

varanus komodoensis.name: Komodo dragon
varanus komodoensis.desc: The largest lizard. Adults ambush deer, pigs and buffalo and also eat carrion; young eat insects, birds, eggs and small reptiles.

varanus nebulosus.name: Clouded monitor
varanus nebulosus.desc: Common large lizard of the forest that eats frogs and other small animals.

varanus niloticus.name: Nile monitor
varanus niloticus.desc: A water-loving lizard recorded near the park. Eats fish, crabs, frogs, eggs, small animals and invertebrates, as well as carrion.

varanus salvadorii.name: Crocodile monitor
varanus salvadorii.desc: A very long arboreal lizard of lowland rainforest and mangrove swamps. It eats birds, eggs, rats, bandicoots, frogs and carrion.

varanus salvator.name: Water monitor
varanus salvator.desc: A large lizard that forages along creeks and mudflats. Tiger remains in the Sundarbans have included water monitors.

varanus varius.name: Lace monitor
varanus varius.desc: Mainly eats carrion but also takes eggs, birds and small mammals, and often raids brushturkey nest mounds.

various cephalopods.name: Antarctic squid
various cephalopods.desc: Squid are among the animals that eat krill, and they in turn feed seals and other predators.

vatnajökull ice cap.name: Vatnajökull ice cap
vatnajökull ice cap.desc: Europe's largest ice cap by volume sits at the heart of the park and feeds the rivers, outwash plains and glacial lagoons around it.

venegasia carpesioides.name: Canyon sunflower
venegasia carpesioides.desc: Canyon sunflower (Venegasia carpesioides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 65 times near the park in GBIF.

verbascum blattaria.name: Moth Mullein
verbascum blattaria.desc: Moth Mullein (Verbascum blattaria): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

verbascum thapsus.name: Great Mullein
verbascum thapsus.desc: Great Mullein (Verbascum thapsus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

verbena canadensis.name: Rose mock vervain
verbena canadensis.desc: Rose mock vervain (Verbena canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

verbena stricta.name: Hoary vervain
verbena stricta.desc: Hoary verbena (Verbena stricta): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 34 times near the park in GBIF.

verbesina alternifolia.name: Wingstem
verbesina alternifolia.desc: Wingstem (Verbesina alternifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 54 times near the park in GBIF.

verbesina encelioides.name: Golden Crownbeard
verbesina encelioides.desc: Golden Crownbeard (Verbesina encelioides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

verbesina helianthoides.name: Gravelweed
verbesina helianthoides.desc: Gravelweed (Verbesina helianthoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

veredas & rio preto streams.name: Veredas & Rio Preto streams
veredas & rio preto streams.desc: Water-table swings, streams and gallery forests give the dry savanna wet refuges. The Rio Preto is the park's main river.

veronica anagallis-aquatica.name: Blue Water-speedwell
veronica anagallis-aquatica.desc: Blue Water-speedwell (Veronica anagallis-aquatica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

veronica persica.name: Common Field-speedwell
veronica persica.desc: Common Field-speedwell (Veronica persica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 51 times near the park in GBIF.

veronicastrum virginicum.name: Blackroot
veronicastrum virginicum.desc: Blackroot (Veronicastrum virginicum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

vespa crabro.name: European Hornet
vespa crabro.desc: European Hornet (Vespa crabro): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

vespula consobrina.name: Blackjacket
vespula consobrina.desc: Blackjacket (Vespula consobrina): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

vespula maculifrons.name: Eastern Yellowjacket
vespula maculifrons.desc: Eastern Yellowjacket (Vespula maculifrons): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

vestiaria coccinea.name: ʻIʻiwi
vestiaria coccinea.desc: A native honeycreeper that drinks nectar from lobelias and ʻōhiʻa and eats small arthropods. Avian malaria is the main driver of its decline.

viburnum acerifolium.name: Mapleleaf viburnum
viburnum acerifolium.desc: Mapleleaf viburnum (Viburnum acerifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

viburnum lantanoides.name: Hobblebush
viburnum lantanoides.desc: Hobblebush (Viburnum lantanoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.

viburnum rufidulum.name: Blue haw
viburnum rufidulum.desc: Blue haw (Viburnum rufidulum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

vicia americana.name: Peavine
vicia americana.desc: Peavine (Vicia americana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

vicugna vicugna.name: Vicuña
vicugna vicugna.desc: Wild camelid that grazes low clump grasses on open plains and rests on the slopes at night. Pumas and culpeos prey on it.

vigna unguiculata.name: Wild cowpeas
vigna unguiculata.desc: Climbing legumes of the savanna. Their leaves are food for caterpillars of the guinea-fowl butterfly.

viola pedata.name: Bird-foot Violet
viola pedata.desc: Bird-foot Violet (Viola pedata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

viola sororia.name: Bayou Violet
viola sororia.desc: Bayou Violet (Viola sororia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

vipera ammodytes.name: Nose-horned viper
vipera ammodytes.desc: A venomous snake of rocky Balkan slopes that eats lizards, small mammals and birds.

vipera aspis.name: Asp viper
vipera aspis.desc: Venomous snake of sunny rocky slopes. GloBI records it eating voles, lizards and small mammals.

vipera berus.name: Common adder
vipera berus.desc: A venomous snake of forest edges that eats small mammals, lizards and amphibians.

vireo bellii.name: Bell's Vireo
vireo bellii.desc: Bell's Vireo (Vireo bellii): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

vireo griseus.name: White-eyed Vireo
vireo griseus.desc: White-eyed Vireo (Vireo griseus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 504 times near the park in GBIF.

vireo olivaceus.name: Red-eyed Vireo
vireo olivaceus.desc: Red-eyed vireo (Vireo olivaceus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 4,375 times near the park in GBIF.

virgin river.name: Virgin River
virgin river.desc: Its North Fork carved Zion Canyon, and the river corridor supports cottonwood, willow and boxelder along its banks.

vitellaria paradoxa.name: Shea tree
vitellaria paradoxa.desc: A savanna tree whose fruit is eaten by fruit bats and baboons in GloBI records.

vitis vinifera.name: Grape vine
vitis vinifera.desc: Wild and grown vines on the sunny shores. GloBI records link its fruit to foxes, bears, martens and dormice.

volcanic ash soil.name: Volcanic ash soil
volcanic ash soil.desc: Ash and pumice from the eruption of Mount Mazama left sandy, fast-draining soils that hold little water.

volcanic island soils.name: Volcanic island soils
volcanic island soils.desc: Thin soils over rugged volcanic hills support the savanna grasses and dry deciduous woodland of the islands.

volcanic mountain soil.name: Volcanic mountain soil
volcanic mountain soil.desc: Thin, young soils built on volcanic rock and glacial debris support the forests and meadows.

volcanic soil.name: Volcanic soil
volcanic soil.desc: Young lava and ash soils hold the nutrients the plants draw on, and are returned by decomposers.

volcanic soils.name: Volcanic soils
volcanic soils.desc: Pumice and ash soils are nutrient-poor, but red tussock tolerates them across the volcanic plateau.

vombatus ursinus.name: Common wombat
vombatus ursinus.desc: A burrowing grazer of grass and other plants. Its tunnels are used by many other animals and its digging turns over the soil.

vossia cuspidata.name: Hippo grass
vossia cuspidata.desc: A robust floodplain grass of the Sudd that grows in deeper water and is a main swamp plant.

vulpes corsac.name: Corsac fox
vulpes corsac.desc: A small steppe fox that hunts jerboas, hares and waterbirds, with GloBI records of these meals.

vulpes lagopus.name: Arctic fox
vulpes lagopus.desc: Hunts lemmings, raids nests and follows polar bears and wolves to scavenge.

vulpes macrotis.name: Kit fox
vulpes macrotis.desc: A small nocturnal fox that mainly eats rodents, notably kangaroo rats, plus rabbits, reptiles, insects and carrion.

vulpes velox.name: Swift fox
vulpes velox.desc: A small desert fox. GloBI records it eating rodents such as brush mice and cotton rats.

vulpes vulpes.name: Red fox
vulpes vulpes.desc: Red fox (Vulpes vulpes): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

vulpes vulpes necator.name: Sierra Nevada red fox
vulpes vulpes necator.desc: A rare montane fox with a small Lassen population. Its diet is mostly rodents and mule deer, plus birds, insects and manzanita berries.

vulpes zerda.name: Fennec fox
vulpes zerda.desc: A small, omnivorous fox with big ears. In Algeria it eats insects, small vertebrates and date palm fruit.

vultur gryphus.name: Andean condor
vultur gryphus.desc: A huge scavenger that glides over the steppe and ice field, feeding on carcasses of guanacos, hares and livestock.

waisila creek.name: Waisila Creek
waisila creek.desc: Streams and pools run through the reserve and feed the creeks and rivers downstream.

warm clear ocean water.name: Warm clear ocean water
warm clear ocean water.desc: The northern Florida Reef sits in warm subtropical water; the park protects the reef section that makes up about half its area.

warm clear water.name: Warm clear water
warm clear water.desc: Warm, nutrient-poor water from the Gulf Stream system keeps the water clear. A 1977 cold snap killed about 96% of shallow branching coral here.

warm lagoon water.name: Warm lagoon water
warm lagoon water.desc: The enclosed lagoon is shallow, averaging about 25 m deep, and warm and clear enough for reef corals and seagrass to thrive.

warm sea temperature.name: Warm sea temperature
warm sea temperature.desc: Corals live in a narrow warm band. Marine heat waves cause bleaching, which hit the Belize reef in 1998.

warm shallow sea.name: Warm shallow sea
warm shallow sea.desc: The Red Sea around the islands is warm and salty, with shallow banks where seagrass beds and coral grow.

warm subtropical sea.name: Warm subtropical sea
warm subtropical sea.desc: Warm, clear open ocean around the islands supports reef algae, plankton and the fish that seabirds and whales feed on.

warm sunlight.name: Warm sunlight
warm sunlight.desc: Year-round warmth and light in the subtropical latitudes support tall, layered forest growth.

warm, salty red sea water.name: Warm, salty Red Sea water
warm, salty red sea water.desc: The enclosed Red Sea is warm and salty, and its clear water carries drifting plankton across the shallow shelf around the islands.

warm, shallow, sheltered bay.name: Warm, shallow, sheltered bay
warm, shallow, sheltered bay.desc: The bay is shallow, about 9 m deep on average, and its sheltered sandy floors carry some of the largest seagrass meadows known.

washingtonia filifera.name: California fan palm
washingtonia filifera.desc: The only palm native to California; grows in the park only at oases with year-round water.

wasmannia auropunctata.name: Forest ants
wasmannia auropunctata.desc: Ants are abundant in the leaf litter and on plants. They take nectar and sugary foods and are a main prey for small lizards, frogs and birds.

water.name: River pools
water.desc: The Arly, Pendjari and Mekrou rivers and their pools hold water for animals in the dry season and feed the riverside forest.

waterholes & pans.name: Waterholes & pans
waterholes & pans.desc: Shallow pans and waterholes. In the dry winter, wildebeest, zebra and impala gather at them.

waterlogged peat.name: Waterlogged peat
waterlogged peat.desc: Peat layers built up over thousands of years underlie the bogs and marshes; they hold water and nutrients that the plants draw on.

weinmannia.name: Weinmannia
weinmannia.desc: A cloud-forest tree genus, with Weinmannia pinnata among the broadleaf trees reported in the park.

welwitschia mirabilis.name: Welwitschia
welwitschia mirabilis.desc: A long-lived plant with two strap-like leaves. It takes up moisture from fog as well as from groundwater.

westerly rain.name: Westerly rain
westerly rain.desc: Moist westerly winds off the Tasman Sea drop more than seven metres of rain a year on much of the park, feeding the temperate rainforest.

westerly rain and snow.name: Westerly rain and snow
westerly rain and snow.desc: The Andes catch Pacific moisture on the west side, leaving the steppe to the east dry. This sets the line between forest and grassland.

wet coastal ground.name: Wet coastal ground
wet coastal ground.desc: Tussac forms dense stands on wet ground close to the shore, and dead plant matter and seabird waste are recycled there.

wet river valleys and meadows.name: Wet river valleys and meadows
wet river valleys and meadows.desc: The forest sits on the Baltic-Black Sea watershed and holds river valleys and wetlands. UNESCO notes that wet meadows need continued water flow and management.

wet, windswept soil.name: Wet, windswept soil
wet, windswept soil.desc: Kerguelen cabbage grows where soil water stays high, in a climate with constant wind.

wet-season rain.name: Wet-season rain
wet-season rain.desc: Rain falls mainly from May to November and feeds the grasslands, lakes and the Harenna Forest.

wet-season rain and floods.name: Wet-season rain and floods
wet-season rain and floods.desc: About 1,100 mm of rain falls a year, mostly June to November, and the Pendjari River floods seasonally.

wet-season rains.name: Wet-season rains
wet-season rains.desc: Rain falls mostly in the wet season, and the Cerrado has a strong dry season from about April to September.

white nile flood pulse.name: White Nile flood pulse
white nile flood pulse.desc: Water from upstream spreads across the flat clay plain each wet season, flooding the swamp and shrinking back in the dry season. It sets which plants grow where.

wildfire.name: Wildfire
wildfire.desc: A natural recurring disturbance that renews the forest and opens jack pine cones. It creates young forest where aspen, berries and moose food thrive.

wildland fire.name: Wildland fire
wildland fire.desc: Shortleaf pine responds well to fire, which reduces competing trees and prepares soil for seedlings. Fire management is part of the park's work.

windblown sediment.name: Windblown sediment
windblown sediment.desc: Sediment blown in from the continent adds nutrients and organic matter to the shallow sea.

winter & monsoon rain.name: Winter & monsoon rain
winter & monsoon rain.desc: Two rainy seasons, winter rain and the summer monsoon, give this desert unusually rich plant life.

winter and monsoon rain.name: Winter and monsoon rain
winter and monsoon rain.desc: Two rainy seasons feed the desert, and water is one of the main reasons it holds so many species. Washes run only after storms and can flash flood.

winter burning.name: Winter burning
winter burning.desc: Park staff burn tall grass in winter, and animals gather on the burnt patches to eat new shoots.

winter cold.name: Winter cold
winter cold.desc: Joshua tree blooming depends on timely rain and a winter freeze.

winter ice.name: Winter ice
winter ice.desc: The lake is frozen for about four to five months, and the clear ice lets light in for under-ice algae. Seals dig dens in it.

winter rain.name: Winter rain
winter rain.desc: Most rain on the islands falls in the cooler months, which sets the growing season for scrub and wildflowers.

winter rain and flash floods.name: Winter rain and flash floods
winter rain and flash floods.desc: Rain is scarce because mountain ranges block moisture. Rare wet winters trigger wildflower blooms and brief shallow lakes on the valley floor.

winter rain and rain shadow.name: Winter rain and rain shadow
winter rain and rain shadow.desc: Rain falls mostly in winter and drops steeply from the Judean hills to the Dead Sea side, a rain shadow effect that makes the eastern slopes desert.

winter rain and snow.name: Winter rain and snow
winter rain and snow.desc: Most of the range's precipitation falls in winter; around 790 mm a year at Prodromos on the high slopes.

winter rainfall.name: Winter rainfall
winter rainfall.desc: Mediterranean climate with rain falling mostly in winter, which suits fynbos plants.

winter snow.name: Winter snow
winter snow.desc: Deep mountain snow covers the high meadows for months and pushes grazers down into the forest; meltwater feeds the slopes in spring.

winter snow and frost.name: Winter snow and frost
winter snow and frost.desc: Snowfall and hard frost shape the high plateau, and snowmelt feeds the streams and pools that supply water downstream.

winter snow and ice.name: Winter snow and ice
winter snow and ice.desc: Snow lies long on the high massif and pushes chamois and other animals down to forest in winter. A relict ice cave records past glaciation.

winter snow cover.name: Winter snow cover
winter snow cover.desc: Deep winter snow covers the ground plants and small mammals live under, and makes food hard to reach for grazers and ground-feeding birds.

winter snowpack.name: Winter snowpack
winter snowpack.desc: Crater Lake gets several metres of snow a year and it lingers for about eight months. It waters the slopes as it melts and feeds the lake.

woody lianas and saplings.name: Understory shrubs and vines
woody lianas and saplings.desc: Shrubs and woody vines are staple foods for okapi, which browse leaves and buds of many such plants.

xanthippus corallipes.name: Grasshoppers
xanthippus corallipes.desc: Chew leaves of shrubs and flowers through summer and feed lizards and birds.

xanthisma spinulosum.name: Cut-leaf ironplant
xanthisma spinulosum.desc: Cut-leaf ironplant (Xanthisma spinulosum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 79 times near the park in GBIF.

xanthocephalus xanthocephalus.name: Yellow-headed Blackbird
xanthocephalus xanthocephalus.desc: Yellow-headed Blackbird (Xanthocephalus xanthocephalus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 802 times near the park in GBIF.

xerospermophilus tereticaudus.name: Round-tailed Ground Squirrel
xerospermophilus tereticaudus.desc: Round-tailed Ground Squirrel (Xerospermophilus tereticaudus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

xestospongia muta.name: Giant barrel sponge
xestospongia muta.desc: A reef sponge that filters tiny particles from the water. Sponges are the main food of hawksbill turtles.

xyleborus.name: Ambrosia beetles
xyleborus.desc: Wood-boring beetles recorded in large numbers on the island; they tunnel into woody plants and farm fungus in the galleries.

xylocopa virginica.name: Carpenter bee
xylocopa virginica.desc: Carpenter bee (Xylocopa virginica): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

xylopia.name: Xylopia
