xylopia.desc: Pepper-fruit trees of the forest. GloBI records show Xylopia quintasii eaten by red colobus, Diana monkeys and mangabeys.

year-round rain.name: Year-round rain
year-round rain.desc: About 1,700 to 2,200 mm falls each year. The south has no real dry season.

young soils.name: Young soils
young soils.desc: Thin soils left behind by ice build up as plants grow and die and as nitrogen is added.

yucca baccata.name: Banana yucca
yucca baccata.desc: Banana yucca (Yucca baccata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 113 times near the park in GBIF.

yucca brevifolia.name: Joshua tree
yucca brevifolia.desc: The park namesake, dominant in the open Mojave areas. Pollinated by yucca moths, its seeds are moved by ground squirrels.

yucca elata.name: Soaptree yucca
yucca elata.desc: A tall succulent that stores water through hot summers and helps hold the dune edges in place. Yucca moth larvae bore into its trunk.

yucca glauca.name: Bear-grass
yucca glauca.desc: Soapweed yucca (Yucca glauca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

yucca schidigera.name: Mohave yucca
yucca schidigera.desc: Mohave yucca (Yucca schidigera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 148 times near the park in GBIF.

yushania alpina.name: Mountain bamboo
yushania alpina.desc: Forms a nearly continuous belt above the forest, thinner on the drier north side, and shades out most other plants.

yushania niitakayamensis.name: Yushan cane
yushania niitakayamensis.desc: A hardy bamboo of the high mountains that forms dense grassy stands in the subalpine and alpine zone, an open ground-level food source for browsers.

zaglossus bruijnii.name: Long-beaked echidna
zaglossus bruijnii.desc: An egg-laying mammal of hill and montane forest that feeds mainly on earthworms, unlike the ant-eating short-beaked echidna.

zalophus californianus.name: California sea lion
zalophus californianus.desc: Hunts fish around kelp forest edges and is a main target of white sharks off California.

zalophus wollebaeki.name: Galápagos sea lion
zalophus wollebaeki.desc: Eats mainly sardines plus squid, octopus and crustaceans. Sharks hunt it, and its numbers fall when El Niño drives away its prey.

zambezi floodwater.name: Zambezi floodwater
zambezi floodwater.desc: After the rains the floodplain becomes a set of lakes and pools. As they shrink, big animals gather near the water that is left.

zanda funerea.name: Yellow-tailed black cockatoo
zanda funerea.desc: A large cockatoo that feeds on seeds, including those of silver wattle.

zapus princeps.name: Western Jumping Mouse
zapus princeps.desc: Western Jumping Mouse (Zapus princeps): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

zea mays.name: Maize
zea mays.desc: A farm crop around the lake. GloBI records show wood mice and brown bears eating it.

zenaida asiatica.name: White-winged dove
zenaida asiatica.desc: One of the most commonly recorded birds in the park area. It eats seeds and fruit and is taken by coyotes.

zenaida auriculata.name: Eared dove
zenaida auriculata.desc: A seed-eating dove found in open country, and a common prey bird for small raptors.

zenaida macroura.name: Mourning Dove
zenaida macroura.desc: Mourning Dove (Zenaida macroura): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 588 times near the park in GBIF.

zephyranthes atamasco.name: Atamasco Lily
zephyranthes atamasco.desc: Atamasco Lily (Zephyranthes atamasco): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

zinnia grandiflora.name: Rocky Mountain zinnia
zinnia grandiflora.desc: Rocky Mountain zinnia (Zinnia grandiflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

ziziphus mauritiana.name: Indian jujube
ziziphus mauritiana.desc: A thorny dry-country fruit tree recorded in the area, offering fruit to birds and mammals.

ziziphus mucronata.name: Buffalo thorn
ziziphus mucronata.desc: A thorny savanna tree whose fruit and leaves are eaten by many animals.

zonotrichia albicollis.name: White-throated Sparrow
zonotrichia albicollis.desc: White-throated Sparrow (Zonotrichia albicollis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 338 times near the park in GBIF.

zonotrichia capensis.name: Rufous-collared sparrow
zonotrichia capensis.desc: A very common small bird that eats seeds, insects and fruit, including hedge cactus fruit.

zonotrichia leucophrys.name: White-crowned Sparrow
zonotrichia leucophrys.desc: White-crowned Sparrow (Zonotrichia leucophrys): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2,500 times near the park in GBIF.

zooplankton.name: Zooplankton
zooplankton.desc: Drifting animals that graze phytoplankton and feed small fish.

zostera japonica.name: Dwarf eelgrass
zostera japonica.desc: A seagrass recorded in GBIF near the bay. Seagrass beds shelter young fish and feed grazers, and have been lost to jetty building.

zostera marina.name: Eelgrass
zostera marina.desc: A flowering seagrass of sheltered flats. Meadows give young animals cover, and shore crabs eat its seeds.

zostera noltei.name: Dwarf eelgrass
zostera noltei.desc: Seagrass of sheltered intertidal flats; its beds shelter invertebrates and young fish, and its dead leaves enrich the sediment.

zosterops japonicus.name: Japanese white-eye
zosterops japonicus.desc: A very common introduced songbird that eats berries, nectar and insects. It is prey for cats and owls.

zosterops lateralis.name: Silvereye
zosterops lateralis.desc: A small bird eating fruit, nectar and insects. It is one of the most commonly recorded birds on the island.
